author: valerauko
body:
## Problem

Every `sentinel_completeness_*` test compares a decoder's emitted JSON keys against a hand-written `expected` array — typed by a human reading the very `gen_*_to_json` function under test. That makes the test a consistency check between two copies of the same person's memory, not a completeness check against the schema. It can only catch a field the author already thought to list twice. This is the root cause behind roughly ten decode-drop bugs shipped in the last month (mayor-pa1qm, mayor-h9gv7, mayor-7ze14, mayor-swq7c, mayor-y0pcm, mayor-ow10r, mayor-ovni7, mayor-ifrs4, and others): `gen_object_meta_to_json` is duplicated 12 times, every copy drops `deletionTimestamp`/`deletionGracePeriodSeconds`/`managedFields`, and every copy has a green "completeness" test, because the hand-written expected list omits exactly what the decoder omits.

## What lands

- `build.rs`: one added line, `file_descriptor_set_path(...)`, emits the compiled `FileDescriptorSet` into `OUT_DIR` at build time (zero runtime cost, test-only consumer).
- New test-only module `crates/apiserver/src/proto_descriptor.rs`: walks the descriptor set and returns the exact set of JSON keys a message must produce according to the schema, not according to a human's recollection. Backed by four reviewed exception tables — `OPAQUE_MESSAGES` (8 types serialized by a custom rule: `Quantity`, `IntOrString`, `Time`, `RawExtension`, etc.), `RENAMES` (2 `$ref`/`$schema` fields), `DELIBERATE_OMISSIONS` (4 ObjectMeta fields, each with the compensating control named per entry), and `KNOWN_GAPS` (empty on this HEAD).
- The Lease adapter test (`coord_gen_adapter.rs`) is rewired from its 18-entry hand list to the oracle, as first consumer, reproducing the known-good list.

## Falsifiability

Confirmed by hand: removing an entry from `DELIBERATE_OMISSIONS`/`KNOWN_GAPS` makes the Lease test fail with the correct message — the oracle can fail, unlike the hand-list it replaces.

## Diagnostic (not a gate)

One new `#[ignore]`d test, `unprotected_decoder_survey`, runs the oracle against 21 currently unguarded decoders and prints a table of schema fields that never reach JSON: 442 missing field-slots out of 1781, triaged down to ~110 candidate real drops. Run with:
```
cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib -- --ignored --nocapture unprotected_decoder_survey
```

## Test result

```
test result: ok. 2867 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 27.11s
```
(2 ignored = 1 pre-existing + this PR's new `unprotected_decoder_survey` diagnostic.) `cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are both clean.

## Bead cross-ref

Closes mayor-j430l after merge. Follow-on beads consume this landing and are out of scope here: mayor-y0pcm (P0), mayor-h9gv7 (P1), mayor-66qj6 (P1, matcher hardening), mayor-7ze14 (P2), mayor-3tu3t (P1 rollout), mayor-174wl (P1), mayor-bzft0 (P2).

author: alexnodeland
body:
Four small fixes to how the top of the content window reads on a phone, all found from one screenshot over the bright PDE field.

## The veil

`.window-veil` is a tapered blur riding the window's top edge, there so content scrolling out dissolves instead of colliding with the sticky control chips. Two problems on mobile:

**It rendered on the home page, which has no chips.** The band was darkening a page nothing floats over — protecting a collision that cannot happen, and dimming the first heading in the window for nothing. It's now gated on the path (`layout.tsx`), so it renders only where something actually floats over the top edge.

**Where it does render, it ran near-opaque** (`0.94` → `0.82`). Over a bright field that stopped reading as a veil and started reading as a black bar laid across the page — a shape with its own edges, louder than the collision it was hiding. The blur is what actually destroys the text under the chips (18px, and the chips add their own on top); the tint only has to keep the smear from competing. It's at a third of the weight now (`0.62` → `0.5`).

## The control chips

Once stuck, the row's own top padding is the entire gap between the chips and the window's frame, and `0.4rem` left them all but touching it. On touch widths that's `0.85rem` — measured, the chip top now sits 15px below the panel edge instead of 6px. Bottom padding is unchanged, so nothing below the row moves.

## The backgrounds launcher

It was reaching for `--bg-floating`, a flat opaque near-black, while the chat launcher across the row wears `capsule-housing` (scrim + backdrop blur). Over a dark field the two passed for each other; over a bright one this one read as a black tile punched into the page while its twin stayed glass. Both are the mixin now, and computed styles for the pair are identical — background, blur, border, radius, ink, shadow, box, offset.

That makes `mobile-interactivity.scss` the first stylesheet outside `global.scss` to need the shared layers, so it imports `variables` and `mixins` itself, the way `layout.scss` and `shortcuts.scss` do.

## Verification

Rendered in Chromium at 390×844 (2× DPR, touch) against the bright PDE background, on home / blog / projects / cv, scrolled so the veil is at full strength. The chips still fully obscure the text passing under them; the launchers match; the band no longer has a visible edge.

`npm run type-check`, eslint, prettier and the full unit suite (579 tests) pass.

author: milad-alizadeh
body:
Closes #539

A composer is a place to think, not a one-shot field. What you type into it now outlives the moment: it survives leaving the Session, and it survives the agent being busy.

## What changed

**A draft survives switching Session and coming back.** `ComposerDrafts` keeps every Session's unsent words in `CockpitView` — the one place above the deck's `.id(session)`, which discards everything under it on a switch. In memory only, deliberately: unsent words restored into a Session whose PTY died with the process would be a message about to be put to something that is no longer there.

**A second thought can be recorded while a Turn runs.** Submitting mid-Turn puts the words above the field as a `QueuedTurnChip` instead of interrupting, cancellable where they stand, delivered in the order they were typed when the Session comes free. A refused flush stops where it happened — the turns it never reached stay queued rather than disappearing into the refusal.

**A restored draft is simply there**, with one quiet line saying it was kept and when. No offer to restore or discard: nothing was lost.

Acceptance stays the echo it already was (#538) — field clears, words come back as the user's own row, 1.4s accent wash.

## States

Rendered from the specimen harness (`composerTyping`, `composerCeiling`, `composerDraftKept`, `composerQueued`, `composerRefusal`), judged against `docs/designs/composer/`.

## Review

Three fresh contexts that never saw this being built — Standards, Spec, and pixels. Between them they found two dead remedies, and both are fixed:

- A follow-up queued on a Session you then switched away from was **stranded**. The composer only exists for the selected Session, so the Turn ending fired no change here. It flushes on arrival too now.
- **Retry over a refused flush did nothing.** The words had already left the field for the queue, so the guard on the field made the seam's one remedy a no-op in exactly the state that produced it.

Plus: the catalog switch had grown a `default:` (moved out of the struct body so it can stay flat and exhaustive), one wall clock instead of three copies of the same expression, and the queued row given the study's 30pt rather than borrowing `chipHeight`.

## One correction to the design, not the code

The study asked for the field at `body` (13) **at 1.5 line height** *and* for a stock `TextField`. Those are not compatible: a stock field is `NSTextField` underneath, draws the face's own leading, and silently ignores `lineSpacing` — measured, adding the modifier moved nothing. The ceiling is held in **lines**, which is the unit the field grows by and the one a reader counts. `cockpit-session-composer.md` now records this with the reasoning rather than carrying a measurement no build can meet.

## Deliberately out of scope

- `SendButton`'s **Stop** state, which `queued.png` draws — #541 owns it; it needs an interrupt on the drive port.
- The `+` attach control — #540.
- **Effort** on the fact line (`Opus 5 · Medium` in the renders) — #558; it is not a value anything holds yet.
- `FeedPrompt` keeps its trailing bubble. The ticket's *"accent label `You` … not a bubble"* describes the study's mock feed, which has a label gutter (Search/Read/Message/Edit) Argo's real feed never adopted; the AC — the user's words attributed, never blurred with agent output — is met more strongly by shape.

## Not verified

AC 1's keyboard half. The field relies on SwiftUI's default key handling; the design names `⇧⏎` for a newline while #538's own comment claims Option-Return. Which key actually inserts one can only be settled by driving the real app (`ArgoE2ETests`), which takes the machine over — flagged rather than guessed at.

## Gates

`bun run quality` green (biome, jscpd, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, package boundaries) · 515 tests passing.

author: tomfarmery93
body:
The top bar had grown to six items on the homepage, and three of them — **Services**, **Our carers**, **How it works** — were anchors to sections further down the same page, not destinations of their own. Removed, leaving only real pages.

### Before / after

| | Homepage nav |
|---|---|
| Before | Services · About · Our carers · How it works · Trust & safety · How we vet |
| After | About · Trust & safety · How we vet |

Applied to every header nav that carried one of these, so the nav is consistent site-wide:

- `index.html` — dropped `#services`, `#why`, `#how`
- `about-us/` — dropped `/#services`, `/#how`
- `privacy/`, `trust-and-safety/` and its 6 subpages — dropped `/#how`

`how-we-vet/` and `search/` had none and are untouched. 13 lines deleted, nothing added.

### The sections are still reachable

The three sections are unchanged and still on the homepage. `#how` also keeps a direct entry point — the hero's **How Truffl works** button — verified live: clicking it still lands the section at the top of the viewport.

### A wrap bug this improves but does not fix

`nav` is `height: 82px` with `flex-wrap: wrap`, so as soon as the row overflows, *Sign in / Book a carer* wraps to a second line that **spills out of the fixed-height bar and over the hero**. Measured on the running page:

| Viewport | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1180px | wrapped (nav-left 719px) | single row (nav-left 436px) |
| 1100px | wrapped | still wrapped |

So the breakage moves from ~1180px down to somewhere under 1100px — better, but small laptops and iPad landscape still hit it. Genuine fix is a separate call (drop the fixed height, or hide `.nav-links` at a higher breakpoint than the current mobile one); flagging rather than deciding it here.

### Verified

Served locally, checked at 1440 / 1180 / 1100 / 1024, no console errors, homepage and about-us navs read back correctly.

body:
## Summary

Originally scoped as Quick Wins across six directed tools (047–052). **A genuine claim collision surfaced during merge**: session `8vo65u` was independently assigned tools 047–051 at essentially the same moment this session was assigned 047–052, and PR #74 (their round) merged into `main` first. This PR now contains the reconciled result rather than the original standalone diff:

- **047, 049, 051** — `8vo65u` had independently shipped the same Quick Wins this branch also built. The redundant reimplementation was discarded in favor of PR #74's already-merged version — no net changes here beyond what's already on `main`.
- **048 Art Portfolio Label Maker** — named/multiple saved portfolios (New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete, migrates old single-portfolio saves), layered on top of PR #74's reorder buttons and character-count warning. Git's automatic 3-way merge silently duplicated the reorder buttons/handlers instead of combining the two feature sets, so the file was rebuilt from `main`'s state with this addition re-applied by hand and re-verified.
- **050 Civics Role Card Generator** — reorder roles and talking points via up/down buttons, layered on top of PR #74's per-role Copies field and Duplicate-role button (same rebuild-by-hand treatment after the automatic merge left conflict markers).
- **052 Cognates & False Friends Builder** — three more starter language sets (German, Italian, Portuguese — six total); reorder list items on both lists. Untouched by PR #74, merges in cleanly as new work.

Also updates each affected tool's `improvement prompts/*.md` file and `_tools-touched.md` to reflect the combined, reconciled history, and logs the same-minute-claim race as a process note in `_site-requests.md` for future sessions.

## Test plan

- [x] Headless Chromium (Playwright) pass per tool exercising the new behavior end to end — multi-save create/duplicate/rename/delete, reorder up/down (verified no duplicated buttons after the manual re-merge), genre grouping, per-role copy counts + duplicate-role, file:// banner + test link, new-language template loads — zero console errors in every run

## Summary
- Lower `fetch-news.mjs` reasoning effort from `medium` to `low` and bound the prompt to ~1-2 web searches per category (was unbounded) — likely the biggest cost driver, since search-result context is probably the dominant token cost. Logs `response.usage` after every real API call so future tuning has real data instead of guesses.
- Extract `index.html`'s inline rendering script into `scripts/app.js` (loaded via `<script type="module">`) so it's importable by tests. No behavior change.
- Add a `node:test`-based suite (`npm test`, no new test-framework dependency) across three layers:
  - **Unit** — pure functions in `fetch-news.mjs` (date formatting, schema shape, prompt content incl. a guard on the new search-bounding wording, validation, manifest pruning).
  - **Regression** — the 5 existing `data/history/*.json` digests, snapshotted into `test/fixtures/` (since `data/history/` auto-prunes and the real API can only ever generate for "today," not replay past dates), validated against `validateNewsData()`.
  - **Feature** — `jsdom`-driven DOM rendering test against `scripts/app.js`'s exported `renderNews()`/`buildNav()` using the same fixtures.
- Add `CLAUDE.md` documenting the project's architecture and commands for future work.

## Test plan

author: newersonmayer
body:
## O que motivou

Auditoria dos 10 ultimos ditados acima de 1 minuto (23,5 min de fala, 3.213 palavras), re-transcritos com o modelo real e comparados com o texto entregue.

**O `vocabulario.txt` e decorativo.** Ele vira o `prompt` da API de transcricao, que o modelo ignora:

| Termo (esta no vocabulario) | Acertos do modelo | Depois do regex |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | **0 de 8** | 8 de 8 |
| `Isaque` | **0 de 4** | 4 de 4 |
| `Theo` | 1 de 2 | 2 de 2 |

As 14 substituicoes do `corrigir_termos()` foram **todas** em termos que estavam no vocabulario — mandar a lista no prompt nao mudou nada. E a tela que existia no app era justamente a dessa alavanca; a que funciona (`correcoes.txt`) nao tinha interface nenhuma.

Testado tambem o parametro `keywords` da API: **nao funciona**. A API ignora parametros desconhecidos (confirmado mandando um campo falso, que passou com 200), e o resultado e ruido — similaridade 0,974-0,997 contra o baseline, com `cloud` subindo de 6 para 10 ocorrencias.

## O que entra

- **Passe de formatacao opt-in** (`gpt-5.6-luna`, `reasoning_effort=low`): tira vicio de fala, pontua, quebra em paragrafos e resolve auto-correcao falada. ~US$ 1,00/mes, +3 a 6s por ditado, so acima de um limiar de duracao.
- **Tela Palavras**: Correcoes (chip `garantia`) acima do Vocabulario (chip `dica`), com botao para promover um termo de um pro outro.
- **Tela Formatacao**: toggle, limiar e editor de preferencias em portugues corrido.
- **Pill em duas fases**: `check + organizando...` enquanto o passe roda.
- **4 regras de correcao** auditadas contra os 2.698 ditados do historico.

## Decisoes que valem registro

**`gpt-audio` foi descartado** — nao por preco (embora seja 4,8x mais caro por minuto), mas porque **conversa em vez de transcrever**: devolveu "Entendi completamente o seu cenario..." e inflou um audio de 4.543 para 8.789 chars, apesar da instrucao explicita de nao responder ao conteudo.

**As regras genericas de correcao foram testadas e reprovadas.** `SQL => skill` corromperia 13 dos 19 usos ("executar SQL", "prompt injection"); `draw => drawer` pegaria o nome da biblioteca "Draw"; `pending => padding` quebraria status de fila. Esses casos sao ambiguos por contexto — o teto do regex, e o motivo de existir o passe de LLM.

**A regra anti-alucinacao do prompt e load-bearing.** Sem ela, em 4 rodadas por variante, o modelo trocou um apelido desconhecido por um termo do glossario em ate 3 de 4 — inventando correcao e mudando o sentido. Com ela, 4/4 preservaram o original. Quem mexer no prompt tem que re-rodar esse teste.

**Fail-open por decisao**: erro de API, timeout, resposta vazia ou saida abaixo de 55% do tamanho devolvem o texto original. Precedente: o guard anti-eco de jul/2026 engoliu 12 ditados por poder devolver vazio.

## Bug pre-existente corrigido de passagem

`"transcrevendo..."` em Segoe UI 9pt ocupa **208px** num `QRect` de **192px** — o texto da pill vinha sendo cortado em todo ditado, desde sempre. Achado ao medir o layout da fase 2. Vai em commit proprio (`04df5dc`).

## Nota sobre os commits

Esta branch partiu de `fix/travamento-thread-ui`, entao **inclui o commit `56b67b8`** da PR #1 — o codigo novo foi escrito em cima daquele fix e partir de `main` daria conflito.

## Racional completo

`.specs/#02-preferencias-formatacao/` — `_ux-veredito.md` (estrutura, estados, 7 alternativas rejeitadas) e `_estetica-veredito.md` (tokens, 9 contrastes calculados, larguras medidas com QFontMetrics, 8 abordagens rejeitadas).

author: chuenchen309
body:
closes: #1876
related: #4504, #4483

### One-line summary for changelog:

`DataQualityAssertionsDatasetFacet` now inherits from `DatasetFacet`, so it is attached under a dataset's `facets` instead of `inputFacets`.

### Meaningful description

The facet inherited from `InputDatasetFacet`, which restricted it to a dataset's `inputFacets`. Three places in the repo already behave as if it were a plain dataset facet:

- its own documentation page shows the example under `"facets"`, not `"inputFacets"`;
- `DbtArtifactProcessor` wrote it under **both** keys, with `# TODO: remove this next release` and a `# type: ignore` next to the `facets=` half;
- `DatasetReducer` carries `facets` through wholesale (`.facets(source.getFacets())`) but has to copy each input facet by hand, so the assertion facet survived reduction only because `FacetUtils` listed it explicitly.

This takes over #4504 (@creazyfrog, open since May 1, tracking #1876 from 2023), which implements exactly this and has been inactive since @mobuchowski's "the fix looks very mechanical; makes sense" on May 8. @kacpermuda suggested picking it up on #4483. The spec and client changes are that PR's; the fixtures are redone as a pure mechanical transform, because the original also reindented three of them from 4 spaces to 2, which is where most of its ~3000-line diff came from.

**Spec.** `allOf` now references `DatasetFacet`, and `$id` goes 1-1-0 → 1-2-0. A REVISION bump rather than an ADDITION: every instance valid under 1-1-0 is still valid (the only new property, `_deleted`, is optional), but where the facet may legally appear changes, which is not a purely additive change for consumers.

**Fixtures.** 16 `dataQualityAssertions` entries moved from `inputFacets` to `facets`; 10 dropped rather than moved, because `no_test_metadata` goes through the `parse_test` double-write path and carried the entry under both keys; 14 `_schemaURL` values bumped to 1-2-0. Those `_schemaURL`s postdate #4504, so they were not in it — as does one `inputFacets` occurrence in `test/result.json`. Each file keeps its own indentation.

The 10 pairs are not quite duplicates, which matters for what dropping one of them costs. In 2 of the 10 datasets the `inputFacets` copy asserted `actual` and `expected` on the two failing assertions and the `facets` copy did not, so keeping only the `facets` copy stops the fixture asserting those two fields. It stays green either way, because `openlineage.common.test.match` only checks keys present in the expected value — which is also why the shorter copy passed all along. e2a7d21 adds the two fields to the surviving copy. Measured with that same `match`, the number of datasets whose surviving copy no longer asserts what the dropped copy did goes from 2 to 0.

**Go client.** Regenerated with `generator/go`, since `build-client-go` fails when the checked-in files drift from the spec. The struct moves from `InputDatasetFacets` to `DatasetFacets` and gains the `Deleted` field every `DatasetFacet` carries.

**Docs.** a6d960e moves the facet's entry out of the input-facet list in `spec/OpenLineage.md` and `website/docs/spec/object-model.md`, which both still filed it under input dataset facets. The facet's own page already showed the example under `facets`, so 869296a8 only bumps its spec link to 1-2-0; that is the last reference to 1-1-0 outside the versioned snapshots under `website/static/spec/`.

#### Verification

Run against `main` at 7c5f2e767, in a dedicated venv with `client/python` and `integration/common` both installed editable:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `integration/common` `tests/` | 357 passed, 2 skipped |
| `integration/common` `tests/dbt/` | 243 passed |
| `mypy --ignore-missing-imports src` (integration/common) | no issues in 22 files |
| `client/python` `tests/` | 588 passed; the 18 failures and 34 errors are identical by name to a clean `main` checkout in the same environment (missing `confluent-kafka` / `fsspec` extras) |
| `client/python` `tests/test_facet_v2.py` | 16 passed |
| `ol-generate-code spec/facets` | emits `class DataQualityAssertionsDatasetFacet(DatasetFacet)`, matching the checked-in file |
| `.pre_commit/json-schema/test-facets.sh` on the changed spec | schema ok, `spec/tests/DataQualityAssertionsDatasetFacet/1.json` ok |
| `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on changed Python | clean |
| `client/go`: `go run .` in `generator/go`, then `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` | generator output committed; build clean; tests pass |

Two things I could not run locally: the Java build (no JVM on this machine — `getDataQualityAssertions` has no callers left besides the `FacetUtils` line removed here, but CI is the check that matters), and the Ruby fluentd tests.

One deliberate omission: `proxy/fluentd/events/event_full.json` still carries the facet under `inputFacets`. It stays schema-valid there, and the parser test only asserts on `runId` and `outputStatistics`, so I left that subsystem alone rather than change a sample I cannot run the tests for. Happy to move it if you would rather the repo be self-consistent.

body:
## Summary

Closes out the remaining pipeline infrastructure (GPT-15, GPT-16, GPT-17):

- **Orchestration** (`src/orchestration.py`): sequences script -> visual -> audio -> animate. Each stage runs as an isolated subprocess so the visual stage's CUDA context is fully released when it exits - the "one GPU stage at a time" rule is enforced by process boundaries, not just convention. Validates each stage's output before advancing, and supports coarse-grained resume (skips a stage entirely if its output already exists, unless `--force`). YouTube upload (GPT-14) is intentionally not part of this - it needs user-provided credentials and stays a separate manual step.
- **Test suite** (`tests/`): 46 tests. Unit tests mock LLM calls, the SD pipeline, and Piper synthesis to verify deterministic logic (schema validation, retry/fallback, duration padding, crossfade timeline math) without needing the live stack. One real integration test runs the full pipeline against live LM Studio/SD1.5/Piper/ffmpeg and validates output with `ffprobe`; auto-skips if LM Studio isn't reachable.
- **Makefile**: `setup`/`install`/`run`/`test`/`clean` targets, all individually tested end-to-end (installed `make` via winget specifically to verify this rather than shipping it untested).
- **requirements.txt**: added for the non-torch Python deps (torch needs a separate CUDA-index install, documented in the file header).

## Reviewer notes

- A real infra bug was found and fixed while testing this branch (documented in Linear GPT-18, not part of this diff): LM Studio's runtime engine was reserving 2.7-3.7GB of GPU memory for the "CPU-only" LLM stage regardless of the `--gpu off` flag, due to its Vulkan backend. Fixed by switching to a genuinely CPU-only llama.cpp engine. This is an LM Studio machine-config fix, not a code change, so it isn't in this diff - noted here so a reviewer isn't confused by the latency difference in commit messages/logs (LLM calls now take longer but are actually VRAM-safe).
- Orchestration's resume/checkpoint is coarse-grained (whole-stage skip, not partial), and per-scene manifests aren't namespaced by run name - documented as known limitations in the code and Linear, not blocking for current single-video-at-a-time usage.
- All 46 tests pass, including the live integration test, and a full `make clean && make run` cycle was run to confirm the Makefile works end-to-end.

body: Presentation and tooling. No engine change, no new affordance, no new rule. 17 files, **zero binaries in the diff**. ## The archive was inside a tracked directory A 458 MB archive of card art was sitting in `packages/cards/data/` — a tracked directory of a public repository. **Nothing of it was ever committed**: `git log --all --diff-filter=A` finds no image anywhere in the history, and `git ls-files` finds none now. But it was one `git add -A` away, so it moves out of `data/` to `packages/cards/card-art/`, gitignored, with its location settable per machine: 1. `OPTCG_CARD_ART_DIR` in the environment 2. `packages/cards/card-art.local.json` — gitignored 3. `packages/cards/card-art/` — the default, gitignored The ignore rules now cover image extensions repository-wide rather than one directory, and `noTrackedArt.test.ts` checks every path through `git check-ignore` rather than by reading `.gitignore` and hoping. ## The downloader is deleted Along with the generated table of upstream URLs and the script that produced it. Three reasons: the official card-list images carry a **SAMPLE watermark** across every card and these do not; the archive has a thumbnail *and* a full-size PNG where the site had one size; and the whole pinned-URL apparatus existed to answer a question the filename already answers. ## The mapping is the card id `ST01-004` → `ST01/ST01-004.png` and `ST01/ST01-004_small.jpg`, folder from the id's own prefix. No table, no manifest, no special cases, and now **nothing anywhere stores an image address**. `CardDefinition` still gains no presentation field. The two sizes map onto the two places a card is drawn: | | file | shown at | | --- | --- | --- | | tiles | `_small.jpg`, 120x167, ~6 KB | 56-92 px | | preview panel | `.png`, 480x671, ~167 KB | ~135 px | The board stopped loading twenty full-size PNGs to display them at thumbnail size. No resizing, no `sharp`, no native dependency. ## The script `pnpm --filter @optcg/cards run art`. Publishes both sizes plus the DON!! card into `packages/client/public/cards/`. Idempotent, and it **names the cards the archive does not have** — that list is a hole a player would otherwise find mid-game. All 34 were present; nothing missing. Symlink attempted, copy used: Windows returns `EPERM` without Developer Mode. ## Degradation is unchanged Verified both ways in a real game. With the directory: 0 broken images, tiles at 120x167, preview at 480x671. Without it: 0 `` on the board, every tile back to its CSS card, preview showing the enlarged text card with the full printed text, DON!! panel unchanged — its art is a CSS background, and a background that 404s simply does not paint. 228 + 133 + 163 green. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: bilaltiq
body:
Imported straight from the `.ARW` files in `~/Documents/select photos` — macOS decodes them natively, so `sips` handled it. 2000px long edge, **7.2 MB for all fifteen**, lazy-loaded so only what's on screen is fetched.

## The grade is CSS, not baked in

+10% saturation both ways, warm tint under the light palette, cooler under dark.

Two graded copies per photo would have doubled the repo *and* made the theme toggle trigger a re-download. This way the swap is instant and costs nothing. The temperature rides on a **soft-light tint** — a filter alone can't shift hue without muddying the saturation it was just given.

## Measured, not eyeballed

Same frame, both themes:

| | R | G | B |
|---|---|---|---|
| light | 106.2 | 94.6 | 77.1 |
| dark | 90.7 | 88.6 | 82.9 |

The first pass only got dark to *less warm* — blue came out unchanged at `0.2` difference, which the screenshots wouldn't have told me. Raised the tint to 30% and added a 4° hue rotation. Blue now leads by **5.8** and red trails by **15.5**, and skin tones still read naturally in the side-by-side.

## A regression the tint caused

Wrapping the image so the tint covers the photo and not the letterboxing left `max-h-full` with **no definite height to resolve against** through two nested flex containers. The photo overran the viewport by 52px and buried the lightbox chrome. The cap is in viewport units now — verified the image fits and `close` stays visible at 1440×900, 390×844, and a deliberately short 1440×600.

15 images render, 0 broken, no overflow at 390px, no console errors.

Second attempt at the fixes reverted in #3. The previous version was correct but not visually neutral: removing the duplicated width constraint widened the text column from ~49% of the viewport to 70%, erasing the inset the page had been designed around. ### Description
This PR wraps the intentional `ZeroDivisionError` in the `/api/erragent-debug` endpoint with a `try-except` block and raises a standard FastAPI `HTTPException` instead. 

### Why
Raising a raw `ZeroDivisionError` bubbles up to Starlette's error middleware as an unhandled crash, which triggers false-positive alerts in production monitoring. Raising an `HTTPException` allows FastAPI to return a clean 500 response while keeping the logs clean of unhandled exceptions.

author: saintl1022
body:
## What this does

Gate S0 gains a third mode, `--regression`, wired into both `pnpm ci:local` and
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **S0-OPEN-2 CLOSED** — the corrected exit code ADR 0069 produced now
has a consumer.

ADR **0070**. `0060` stays reserved (`presentation-plane-audit.json:135`).

## Why a third mode, rather than scheduling one that exists

Neither existing mode was wireable, and that was measured rather than argued.

**Report mode has no failing mode at all.** Pointing DEP-8's flag scan at a token absent from the
source made it print `✗` beside DEP-8 and **exit 0**. It exits 0 unconditionally.

That matters because scheduling report mode was **S0-OPEN-2's own first prescribed remedy**, written
in the row's *"What would make this row false"*. Had it been implemented as written, CI would have
gained a step whose green says nothing about the bytes it read — ADR 0069 §2's defect wearing a
workflow file. The row's parenthetical (*"measuring is useful even when the gate would fail"*) is
true of a human reading output and false of CI, which reads only the exit code.

**`--gate` is unwireable from the opposite direction.** It exits 2 on `main` for the cohort shortfall
(19 < 25, S0-OPEN-1), clearable only by merging the registry expansion — so wiring it would pin the
required check red for a reason no PR under review can fix. `gate:s0:gate` must never appear in
`ci.yml` or `ci:local`, and the reader asserts its absence in both.

So the row closes by **neither** of its two prescribed disjuncts. A row's own falsification
conditions can be wrong; the honest close satisfies its intent and records that its stated remedy was
refused, and why.

## What `--regression` enforces, and the one thing it deliberately does not

|  | on `main` today | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `registryShort` (19 < 25) | **true** | a known shortfall, S0-OPEN-1's business — not a regression |
| `cohortRegressed` (19 < floor) | **false** | a record was lost — a real defect, enforce it |

The 25-record *requirement* cannot pass today; the five *assertions* all pass right now. Blending the
two booleans is what made the gate unwireable. Separating them made a wireable mode possible without
lowering any bar — the requirement is printed as census and never enforced.

The floor is defended twice: `S0_REGRESSION_FLOOR > S0_REQUIRED_RECORDS` exits 2 at load time, and
the floor is pinned against the upstream snapshot the gate reconciles against, not against served
bytes (the first draft read `apps/web/public/trust/index.json`, which is what the row itself says a
test must not do).

## Correction, after this branch was first pushed: the step never ran

The step went in as `- name: Gate S0 (regression: assertions + cohort ratchet)`. The unquoted `: `
makes the whole file unparseable, so the `test` job never started:

```
gh pr checks 286   → six green checks, `build-and-test` ABSENT from the list
gh run list        → .github/workflows/ci.yml   completed   failure   (zero jobs)
```

**An unparseable workflow contributes no check runs, so a required check does not fail — it stops
existing.** Branch protection had nothing to fail on. The argument against wiring `--gate` was that
it would pin the required check red; the actual outcome was the opposite hazard, a required check
that was neither red nor green.

**Why nothing caught it.** The closure's falsification conditions were pinned as *"`ci:local` and
`ci.yml` must both invoke `gate:s0:regression`"*, and the reader implemented that as
`expect(ci).toContain("pnpm gate:s0:regression")` — true of a file no runner can execute. The
assertion's subject is *a string is present*; the claim is *CI runs the step*. That is this ADR's own
§2 defect reproduced inside its closing evidence: §3 refused report mode by measuring its exit code
rather than reading its output, and then the ADR accepted a text match as proof the measurement had
been applied.

**Repair.** `ci.yml` is parsed and Gate S0's step looked up as a structure inside `jobs.test.steps`,
with `build-and-test` asserted to survive in the parsed graph. A second test parses **all fifteen**
workflows. `yaml@2.8.2` is pinned as a root devDependency — it previously resolved from outside the
repository, so an import would have passed locally and been absent in CI.

The generalisation is narrower than "parse your YAML": **a guard asserting that a configuration file
*mentions* a step cannot see whether the runtime *accepts the file*.** Wherever a gate's subject is
"X is wired to something that runs it," the wiring must be read the way the runner reads it.

## Also in this branch: S0-OPEN-5 filed, with measurement

Gate 2.4-H's `workflowBinding` check (`scripts/phase-2.4-gates.ts:717`) is regex-over-text for the
same 20 checks and has the same blind spot. On the exact bytes GitHub refused:

| measured on the pushed, unparseable `ci.yml` | |
|---|---|
| distinct `run: pnpm <script>` lines the regex sees | 23 |
| of those, `workflowBinding` = BOUND | 23 |
| Gate H's 18 recorded-bound checks still reading bound | **18** |
| rows the regex would have lost | none |
| `^  build-and-test:$` matched | yes |
| `YAML.parse` | **FAILED** — nested mappings at line 150 |
| jobs GitHub started | **0** |

All 18 bound claims read green on an unrunnable file. **Left unrepaired on purpose:** it is a
drift-checked artifact needing Phase 2.4's regeneration path, `REGRESSION_CHECKS` is shared by four
other gates, and two unrelated repairs must not sit behind one CI result. The row records the fix
shape so the next batch does not re-derive it, and requires a control that applies the pushed bytes —
*a green Gate H on valid YAML proves nothing here*.

Every figure in the row is derived from the two files it is about (19 rows / 2 `remoteOnly` from
source; 18 bound / 1 null from Gate H's artifact), never restated. Both copies of the bound-count are
guarded independently, and the row is asserted **not** to claim Gate H was repaired here.

## A real hole found while adding that row

The falsification-condition loop ran over `[1, 2, 3]` — written when the artifact had three rows and
never widened. S0-OPEN-4 and S0-OPEN-5 were exempt from the one requirement the file exists to
impose. A hardcoded range over a growing list silently stops covering its tail.

## Negative controls

#170–#182, applied to **source or artifact, never to a test**, `cp`-backed up and each restored
byte-identical. Three worth keeping:

**#175 measured the central claim rather than restating it.** With `INV-R6`'s anchor pointed at a
non-existent token, on identical bytes in one working tree: report mode printed `✗ INV-R6: anchor
absent …` and exited **0**; `--regression` printed `❌ one or more assertions FAILED` and exited **2**.
Both *print* the failure; only one *reports* it.

**#176 exposed an undocumented fourth consumer of `ci:local`.** Appending a step red `pnpm ci:local`
at **Gate 2.4-H**, not at the new step: `gate-H-no-regression.json` embeds `ci:local`'s `&&`-joined
string verbatim and byte-compares it. The reader now asserts that coupling, kept narrow rather than
duplicating Gate H's own drift check.

**#174 and #181 are the same defect one batch apart.** #174: swapping `ci.yml`'s step to
`gate:s0:gate` red on a *missing step*, not on the hazard, because the presence assertion preceded
the exclusion and short-circuited it. #181: a 20th `REGRESSION_CHECKS` row red on *line 718 having
moved*, because an `assertPointer` preceded the counts. Both reordered claim-first; both then red on
their own subject. A principle applied correctly at one assertion does not propagate to the next one
in the same file — which is the argument for a control per hazard rather than per file.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — EXIT 0
- `pnpm test` — **225 files / 3729 passed | 1 skipped**
- `pnpm ci:local` — **EXIT 0**, with `gate:s0:regression` inside it
- `pnpm pack:smoke:mcp` — 13 tools / 19 resources / empty runtime deps / `server/discover(2024-11-05,2026-07-28)`

author: ghashtag
body:
`ROTATION_VERDICT_2026-08-11.md` measured that a block-wise Hadamard makes block quantisation worse in perplexity, and attached a mechanism marked as a hypothesis: concentration rises, so more elements land in the coarse part of the codebook.

Tested on **3,317,760 blocks** across 210 layers of SmolLM2-135M with the project's own quantiser. It is wrong, and wrong by sign.

| predictor | r with Δerror | r with shuffled |
|---|---:|---:|
| H1 concentration, mean/max | **−0.4592** | −0.0006 |
| H2 E8M0 headroom | −0.3069 | +0.0006 |
| H3 participation ratio | −0.3899 | −0.0005 |

Concentration does rise (+0.0120 mean) — but blocks that concentrate get **less** error, not more. Relative error rises in only 48.0 % of blocks and the median block improves. The shuffled column is the check that this is not the correlation machinery finding structure in noise.

**The aggregate is the actual result:**

| | |
|---|---|
| total weight quantisation error | 5.5478e4 → 5.3643e4, **−3.31 %** |
| perplexity | 21.9397 → 23.7476, **+8.24 %** |

Rotation makes the weights measurably *more* accurate and the model measurably *worse*. This is the strongest form of what `BLOCK_AXIS_CLOSED` called "nearly unrelated" — not two orderings disagreeing, but one intervention moving the two metrics apart by sign on the same weights in the same run. Concretely: anyone following MSE on this axis would have drawn the opposite conclusion from the truth.

The hypothesis is withdrawn **in the original document** rather than amended there, since it was published with it. The next hypothesis — that rotation changes *where* the error lands rather than how much there is — is written down as a hypothesis, with the test it implies.

author: samerde
body:
## What changed

- adds a read-only Current workspace card to the Personas activity pane
- adds a visually separated Current workspace column to the Extension Matrix
- reports Enabled, Not enabled, Not installed in profile, Workspace-local, or Unknown from documented evidence
- discovers bounded unpacked candidates under each local workspace root's `.vscode/extensions` directory
- adds workspace-only rows without adding synthetic profiles or profile mutation actions
- exposes read-only Open manifest and direct Edit manifest actions for saved local `.code-workspace` JSON files
- adds defensive association parsing, injected workspace composition, debounced refresh watchers, documentation, and comprehensive tests

## Why

Ordinary extensions are installed per profile, but their effective availability can differ in the current workspace. VS Code also supports separately installed local workspace extensions. Personas should show both concepts without treating workspace state as a profile, recommendations as installs, or unsupported inference as fact.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`
- `npm test` — 136 tests passed
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:integration` — passed in disposable `--user-data-dir`, `--extensions-dir`, and copied workspace fixtures
- `git diff --check`
- supported-API spike on VS Code 1.90.2 and Stable 1.132.0, documented in `docs/spikes/workspace-extension-status.md`

The integration harness confirmed candidate-only `Unknown` behavior, positive runtime `Enabled` evidence, and `vscode.extensions.onDidChange` for install/uninstall.

## Boundaries

- no `state.vscdb`, SQLite, proposed/private API, internal command, or `Extension.isActive`
- no workspace enable/disable/install controls
- no recommendation inference
- no remote-workspace expansion or development-host guard weakening
- no version-file changes

## Manual acceptance

The visible disposable-sandbox checklist remains pending because the computer-control backend failed with `spawn EPERM` on three helper attempts and no callable desktop-control tool was available afterward. The plan records this gap explicitly; no UI result was inferred or fabricated.

author: ioradsun
body:
Completes #297. That PR landed the state machine and the projection reader with nothing calling them — this is the half that makes it real. Production now reads `challengeCardsFor` and the rail renders it.

**Note on process:** #297 was already merged when you asked me to hold it, so this lands as a follow-on rather than more commits on that branch. Same work, one extra merge commit.

## The ownership test

The rail rendered incoming calls through `ChainList` and outgoing Challenges through `YourTable` — so a reader who had been brought in **and** put the same question up had two cards for one relationship, on two tabs, neither aware of the other.

One `ChallengeCardList` replaces both. A viewer who was challenged by Maya, answered, relayed, and had Casey answer them sees **one card evolve**, not several historical fragments.

`ChallengeCard` switches on `projection.state` and reconstructs nothing — no arithmetic over calls, no comparing counts to work out who is waiting, no second opinion about eligibility. `canRelay` is **told, not derived**: it comes from `eligibleAudience`, the same function `put_on_table` resolves against, so the offer shown and the write it triggers cannot disagree. `KeepChainMoving` was deleted for computing its own answer; this doesn't become where that comes back.

## The durable relay

The highest-value missing behaviour. Somebody who skipped `Challenge all 13` on the closing screen can now do it from the card — same RPC, same lineage pointer.

The pointer is `incoming.primaryCall`, which is the **displayed** primary caller. Recomputing it here would be the second rule that lets the visible line and the permanent record disagree about who brought somebody in.

## Removal, enforced in the reader

A **waiting** call whose parent Challenge was taken down stops being live. Three things happen at once and all three matter:

- that recipient does **not** become a passer — passing is a choice, and nothing writes or infers one
- an **answered** call survives untouched as history
- removing one of several callers **promotes the next earliest active call** by the same sort, rather than deleting the card

Downstream branches are never touched. This is enforced in `incomingFor` rather than in the component, so no rendering path can get it wrong.

## The fresh-response transition

Keyed on the newest responder, fired once per new name, a colour fade rather than movement. The first render of a card the reader is only now opening is not news. No confetti.

## Against your DoD list

| | |
|---|---|
| projection called by production | ✅ `getChallengeCards` → rail |
| every Challenge market renders through `ChallengeCard` | ✅ |
| old separate paths removed | ✅ `ChainList` gone from the rail |
| recipient answers, same card evolves | ✅ one projection per market |
| skipped relay recoverable from the card | ✅ |
| named responders, immutable sides | ✅ from `responded_side` |
| passers aggregate-only | ✅ absent from `responders`, counted in the line |
| multiple callers → one card | ✅ |
| displayed primary = lineage parent | ✅ one value, both uses |
| removing one caller promotes the next | ✅ same sort, no special case |
| removal hides waiting calls, creates no passes | ✅ |
| completed responses survive removal | ✅ |
| downstream branches survive | ✅ untouched |
| subtle one-time transition | ✅ |
| `marketClosed` explicitly unavailable | ✅ still `false` with the TODO |
| one market = one card | ✅ asserted in `your-table.test.ts` |

## Market closure — decision recorded, not implemented

Per your call: Conviction **observes** closure and must not declare it. `marketClosed` stays `false` until an authoritative on-chain resolution is indexed into the read model. Nothing here infers it from trade recency, expiry timestamps, quotes, liquidity, or Challenge age — those are heuristics pretending to be terminal truth.

The domain already treats closure as terminal and refuses to convert waiting recipients into passers. It just can't be told yet.

## Scope held

Lineage is one line plus a `See chain` entry point. The real view is #298.

## Verification

2847 passing, typecheck clean, build clean.

**Baseline note:** the pre-existing failure count moved 6 → 8 from commits already on `main` (`Changes`, `Added drag-and-drop upload`) — not from this branch. Verified by stashing: `origin/main` alone reports the same 8. They are `create-flow` (×4), `explore-lens`, `rail-stability`, `why-this`, `feed-question-order`. The two newly-broken `create-flow` cases are worth a look independently of this PR.

author: renewalmateupdates
body:
fix(bulk): hitting the post limit mid-run wasted 40 requests and read as a success

Bulk scheduling is the fastest way for a free user to reach the 100-post monthly
cap, and it was the worst place to reach it.

The save loop posted each row sequentially with no notion of a stop condition.
Hit the cap on row 10 of 50 and it fired 40 more requests, every one of them
guaranteed to come back 403, each marking its row "Failed to save".

Then it announced the result:

  if (saved > 0) showToast(`${saved} posts scheduled!`, 'success')

Ten of fifty saved produced a green "10 posts scheduled!" and left the user to
notice the forty red rows on their own.

And the summary bar told them what to do about it:

  ❌ 40 failed — check content and try again

Nothing was wrong with the content, and trying again cannot work until the month
rolls over or the plan changes. That is the one piece of advice guaranteed to
waste their time.

Three changes:

1. A plan limit is a stop condition, not a per-row failure. The first 403
   carrying an `upgrade` payload ends the run. Remaining rows are marked with the
   real reason instead of each buying its own round trip.

2. The toast reports both halves — "12 scheduled, 38 failed" — and says
   "Nothing was scheduled" when nothing was. A partial run no longer reads as a
   clean one.

3. The wall gets a way forward: an amber banner carrying the server's own
   message and upgrade line, with a link to `upgradeHref`. It also notes the
   unsaved rows are still on screen, because the natural fear at that moment is
   that the work was lost. The "check content" advice is suppressed when the
   cause is a quota.

This is the third surface where the /api/posts/create 403 was being discarded
rather than acted on — compose was #543, and the AI-credit equivalent was #546.
The route has sent `upgrade` and `upgradeHref` the whole time.

Checked while here and left alone: PLAN_MAX_ROWS[plan] on line 101 is safe.
That `plan` comes from useWorkspace(), which normalises, so it is not exposed to
the annual-SKU bug from #545/#547.

tsc clean. 1 file.

author: tedd1218
body:
Flask backend (src/webapp.py) reuses src.demo.move_distribution directly for inference, so the demo shares the exact legal-masked, CFG-guided policy used everywhere else in the project rather than a separate reimplementation. Three endpoints: predict (move distribution for a position + rating), move (apply a legal move), engine_move (the model picks its reply, sampled from its own distribution by default).

Frontend is a plain HTML/CSS/JS board, no external dependencies or build step, served from web/templates and web/static. Two modes:

- Explore: set any FEN, drag the rating slider, see predicted moves as weighted arrows and a ranked probability list. This is what the project actually claims (a human-move distribution), not a pretense that the model plays well.
- Play: play a full game against the model at a chosen rating, as either side.

Smoke-tested locally against runs/conditioned: predict, move (including illegal-move rejection and promotion), engine_move, and checkmate/stalemate detection all verified via curl before committing.

Adds flask to requirements.txt. model.pt stays gitignored as before, so running this needs a locally trained or copied-in checkpoint.

author: mvasilijevictt
body:
Adds `ttnn.experimental.kda.sigmoid_gated_rms_norm`, one operation from the [full change PR #51910](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/51910).

The operation applies per-head RMSNorm, learned scaling, and sigmoid output gating:

`y = (x / sqrt(mean_V(x²) + ε)) · w · sigmoid(g)`

It accepts recurrence output `x[B·H, T, V]`, gate `g[B, T, H·V]`, and weight `w[V]`, and produces `y[B, T, H·V]`. The input keeps `(B·H)` outermost because the recurrence evolves each head independently; the output restores time-first, flattened-head order for the following output projection. This conversion is performed inside the fused kernel rather than through a separate permutation.

The fused implementation measured a 92.72–93.92% latency reduction over the equivalent unfused operations, with output PCC ≥ 0.999990.

author: maestri33
body:
Revisão de arquitetura da branch de produção (`claude/wave1-security`), informada por uma varredura com o skill `/improve-codebase-architecture`. **6 commits, todos com testes, 300 verdes**, ruff limpo nos arquivos tocados.

## O que muda

### 🐛 Correções de bug (idempotência HTTP)
- **`c7729d1`** — `GET /veteran/me`, `GET /me` (via `me_dict`) e `GET /rg` (via `get_rg_section`) chamavam `_reconcile_stale_analyses` **na leitura**: um RG `pending` com TTL estourado virava `review` **+ notificava o coordenador** dentro de um GET (um retry/preflight/crawler disparava a transição). O flip foi pro job `age_stale_rg` (Django-Q), espelhando o que a selfie já fazia. As leituras ficaram puras.
- **`2301e0f`** — Mesmo bug (versão silenciosa, sem notify) no `GET /candidate/document` → job `age_stale_docs`.
- **`50e6e57`** — **Bug latente do Django 5**: `_analysis.started_at_from` coagia timestamps naive com `django.utils.timezone.utc`, **removido no Django 5.0** → `AttributeError`. Só não estourava porque em operação normal o timestamp já vem *aware*. Trocado pelo `datetime.UTC` do stdlib. O `student._document_expires_at` reimplementava o mesmo parse (mesmo bug) → agora usa o helper canônico.

### ♻️ Refactor
- **`280ad75`** — A coerência do espelho local↔notify-server (validar → gravar local → push remoto atômico → invalidar cache) estava repetida em **5 corpos de handler** do `api/staff_notify`. Extraída pra `notify/interface/staff.py` (5 operações públicas) + `notify/interface/remote.py` (helpers compartilhados com o proxy do `/history`). Os handlers viraram adapter fino — **`staff_notify.py` encolheu 245 linhas**. Comportamento idêntico (inclusive as diferenças sutis de validação entre `upsert` e `patch`).

### 🧪 Cobertura do fluxo de dinheiro (rede de segurança, sem mudar lógica)
- **`8b0dda5`** — `finance.interface.fees`: pareamento por prefixo (`latest_fee_request`), idempotência (`request_fee_payment`), retry `_rN` (`retry_fee_payment`), agenda 09:00 SP (`_due_to_scheduled`).
- **`3d6d3fa`** — Gate de dinheiro da matrícula: `conclude` só promove matrícula→aluno com **1ª paga ∧ 2ª agendada**; `apply_fee_paid` casa a parcela por prefixo (incl. re-tentativa `_rN`).

## ⚠️ DEPLOY — passo manual
Os 2 jobs novos (`age_stale_rg`, `age_stale_docs`) precisam ser registrados no Django-Q:
```
python manage.py selfie_schedules
```
(O comando já existia pra selfie; foi estendido e é idempotente.)

## Deliberadamente FORA deste PR (precisam de decisão)
- **Refactor da costura `enrollment`↔`finance`** (referência-string → handle opaco): a cobertura acima é a rede de segurança pra isso, mas mudar a lógica de referência de dinheiro fica pra uma revisão dedicada.
- **Aposentar o adapter local do notify** (`NOTIFY_MODE=local`): deleção grande que queima a ponte de rollback do cutover — decisão operacional.

author: toshiyam
body:
`toshiyam/iseten` の issue#168（[PR #201](https://github.com/toshiyam/iseten/pull/201) と [PR #202](https://github.com/toshiyam/iseten/pull/202)、mainへマージ済み `5308b36`）の成果物を `tensei-life-watch.html` の配信内容へ反映します。

これで iseten の親issue #155「コアループを製品版ビジュアルへ刷新する」配下7件がすべて本番へ反映されます。

## 何が変わるか（プレイヤーから見て）

人生が終わったときの「死亡・人生総括」画面が変わります。

- **通常の死と特別な結末が、ひと目で違って見えるようになった**。これまでは細い枠線のバッジ1個しか違いがありませんでした。終端画像を画面ヘッダーへ作り替えて人物名・享年・職業を載せ、「生涯の終わり」／「特別な結末」という見出し語・死因バッジの文言・終端画像の3点で示します。色に頼らず、文字だけで区別できます
- **人生ランクに意味が付いた**。「人生ランク: 著名」という素の文字列では何を評価した値なのか分かりませんでした。「後世の評価: 伝説」＋「人生アークを結末まで駆け抜け、世界に名を刻んだ。」のように、ランクごとの説明を必ず添えます
- **「この人生の決断」が読めるようになった**。本人が選択肢を選んで実際に人生の向きが変わった瞬間（歴史的な出来事、または職業・関係・目標・世界が動いたもの）を、状況→選んだ行動→結果の形で並べます。直近6件までで、省略した件数と確認先（同じ画面の「すべての記録を見る」）は明示します
- **「図鑑に初めて記録されたもの」が分かるようになった**。この人生が図鑑へ何を残したかは次の転生の解禁に直結しますが、これまでは図鑑を開いて自分で差分を探すしかありませんでした
- **「すべての記録を見る」が押しやすくなった**（タップ領域 21px → 44px）
- **二重終端の不具合を修正**。「次の転生へ」を押した後にタブを再読込すると、既に閉じたはずの同じ人生の死亡総括へ引き戻されていました
- **ライト配色での可読性を修正**。背景アートは配色設定で変わらない（常に暗い絵）のに、その上の文字が暗い色で描かれていたため読めませんでした。人生観測画面のヘッダーにも同じ問題があったので、そちらも同時に直っています

## 変更したファイル

| ファイル | 変更 |
|---|---|
| `tensei-life-watch.html` | 参照するハッシュ付きアセット名のみ変更 |
| `assets/index-*.js` / `assets/index-*.css` | 新しい本番ビルドへ差し替え |

ゲームアート6点のPNG・`sw.js`・`manifest.webmanifest`・`icons/` は新ビルドと**バイト単位で同一**のため変更していません。他の公開作品（`astral-labyrinth.html` 等）には一切触れていません。

## 検証

webpagesリポジトリのルートをそのまま静的配信し、Chromiumで確認しました（375px / 320px・ダーク / ライト）。タイトルから**実際に1人生を寿命まで進めて死亡総括へ到達**しています。**16項目すべてPASS**。

- 終端種別（「生涯の終わり」）・名前・享年・後世の評価（「著名」＋説明）が表示される
- **決断カードは全ログ32件に対して表示6件**（「これ以前の6件は『すべての記録を見る』から確認できます。」を明示）、ページ高さ2466px
- 図鑑に初めて記録されたものが表示される
- 「すべての記録を見る」のタップ領域 44px（実測）
- ライト配色でもアート上の名前が本文色（暗色）にならない（実測 `rgb(244,241,251)` vs 本文 `rgb(34,30,51)`）
- 320pxで横スクロールなし
- 「次の転生へ」の後、再読込しても死亡総括へ引き戻されない（タイトル画面のまま）
- 失敗リクエスト0件 / JSエラー0件

画面のスクリーンショットは、公開リポジトリに検証専用の画像を持ち込まないため iseten 側の証跡ディレクトリに置いてあります（同じビルドの同じ画面です）。

- [実プレイ1人生の死亡総括 375px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toshiyam/iseten/main/docs/verification/pr-202/375px-death-real-life.png)
- [同・修正前（決断カードが24件に膨らんでいた状態）](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toshiyam/iseten/main/docs/verification/pr-202/375px-death-real-life-before.png)
- [通常死亡 375px ダーク](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toshiyam/iseten/main/docs/verification/pr-201/screens/death-normal-375px-dark.png) / [特殊終端 375px ダーク](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toshiyam/iseten/main/docs/verification/pr-201/screens/death-special-375px-dark.png)
- [特殊終端 375px ライト（アート上の文字の可読性）](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toshiyam/iseten/main/docs/verification/pr-201/screens/death-special-375px-light.png)

iseten側では `test:new-ui` 304/304、Playwright death 62/62・observe 115/115 ほか全QA PASS、CI 19/19 success。証跡一式は [`docs/verification/pr-201/`](https://github.com/toshiyam/iseten/tree/main/docs/verification/pr-201) と [`docs/verification/pr-202/`](https://github.com/toshiyam/iseten/tree/main/docs/verification/pr-202)。

## セーブ互換性

`game-engine/`・`game-data/`・`schemaVersion` に変更はありません。既存のセーブデータはそのまま読み込めます。

1点だけ挙動が変わります: **「次の転生へ」を押した時点で、保存データ上の `character` が `null` になります**（上記の二重終端の修正）。この人生の内容は過去人生の記録（`pastLives`）へ完全に保存済みで、`character: null` は初回起動前・転生間として既存コードが正規に扱う値です。過去人生・図鑑・世界の状態は一切変更しません。

## レビューについて

`toshiyam/webpages` の `main` へは直接pushせず、Draft PRとして提出しています。レビュー・Ready for review化・mergeは別のレビュアーが行ってください。

author: ribato22
body:
Three commits, all green: 1360 passed, ruff + mypy clean.

## fix(direct): `--verify` runs on the one-call path, and its costs are counted
- `answer_directly` accepts a `verify` callback, awaited after a successful answer; the CLI wires the runtime's detector into it. `--verify` is no longer a silent no-op in the default (direct) mode.
- `subscription_calls` was stuck at 0 on the direct path; every physical attempt on a plan-billed model is now counted (success or failure, same rule as the runtime gate), and the detector's own derive call folds into the total.
- `_summary_json` (`--json`) dropped the checks report; it now serializes ran/total/failed/error/all_passed/summary.
- `_unpriced_models` aligned to `ValueError` (it caught bare Exception).

## fix(providers): never Usage(0,0)
- `CliAgentProvider.stream` fallback (early-stop / no terminal line) estimated tokens from the real prompt + partial text instead of reporting zero usage, honoring the shared `NEVER Usage(0, 0)` contract.

author: vikashloomba
body:
## Row

`BACKEND-ROCM` — M3 GDN kernel slice (issue #41). Claim: `CLAIM-ROCM-GDN-KERNELS`.

## Before starting

- Issue/PR search and existing claim: issue #41 tracks the ROCm backend and this M3 work; my gfx1100 M2 evidence ([comment](https://github.com/mudler/vllm.cpp/issues/41#issuecomment-5230043080)) and staged-state follow-up ([comment](https://github.com/mudler/vllm.cpp/issues/41#issuecomment-5237179696)) are on the thread. No existing claim on the GDN kernel family; disjoint from open ROCm PRs #234 (sampling ops), #317 (gemma4 FP8/WMMA), #273 (near-tie docs). Precedent for the helper-PR-as-claim route: #273.
- Roadmap or matrix row: `BACKEND-ROCM` (backend-matrix), roadmap issue-table row for #41.
- Exact current-code and test/evidence anchors inspected: `src/vt/rocm/rocm_ops.hip` (no GDN registrations on `5812b8b6`), `src/vt/cuda/cuda_gdn.cu` + `cuda_ops.cu` donors, `src/vt/cpu/cpu_ops.cpp` oracles, `qwen3_5.cpp` `IndexedGdnOpsNative`, `include/vt/ops.h` Fn aliases, `src/vt/ops.cpp` validators.

## What changed

This PR opens with the **spike spec + claim** (`.agents/specs/rocm-gdn-kernels.md`, the coordination claim row, the NOW.md line) for the ten GDN ops Qwen3.5-0.8B needs on discrete ROCm: `kGdnStateGather`/`Scatter` (77/78), `kCausalConv1dFwd`/`Update` (5/6), `kRmsNormGated` (9), `kSigmoidGateBf16` (58), `kGdnPrefill`/`Decode` (10/11), `kGdnPostConv` (65), `kAttnQkNormRopeGate` (67). Implementation lands on this branch **one family per commit in throw-order** (state-IO first — the current M2 throw), each with its red-first cross-device case, focused + full gate, and an M2 rerun. The design finding that shapes it: registering the full indexed set flips `IndexedGdnOpsNative(kROCM)` true, so the model takes the CUDA lane's device-resident path with zero model/runner edits. Perf machinery (WMMA chunked prefill, fused/packed decode, register/tiled conv, Triton AOT, spec/fp8 variants) deliberately unported per docs/ROCM.md §6 — the portable scan serves prefill and decode.

## Evidence

- [ ] `scripts/agent-preflight.sh` passes — **green in the worktree** (exit 0). Two host-environment suites need per-process mitigations on this box, both pre-existing on an unmodified base and unrelated to the change: `test_agent_onboard` (host git `init.defaultBranch=main` vs the test's hardcoded `master`; run with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=master`) and `trailer suites` (site-packages `tests` shadows the repo namespace; temporary `tests/__init__.py` + `tests/scripts/__init__.py` during the run). Both verified failing identically on the clean base before my edit.
- [ ] tests that cover this change: this commit is records-only (spec/claim/NOW). The GDN cross-device cases land with their family commits, red-first.
- [ ] same-change doc obligations: no lifecycle change (the row stays `ACTIVE`); `NOW.md` + `coordination.md` carry the claim.

**Pre-claim validation (on 4× gfx1100 / ROCm 7.14, recorded in the spec):** all ten kernels hand-translated from the CUDA donors and validated in standalone harnesses against independent host references — **68/68 checks** (state paths and dtype conversions bit-exact; compute at expf/FMA ulp level). The drop-in TU compiles with the exact production flags (`-O3 -ffp-contract=off -std=c++20 --offload-arch=gfx1100`). The five cross-device cases were run assembled into a scratch copy of the test file against the real `libvllm.a`: 16/16 green, GDN cases skipping unregistered ops as designed.

## Speed claims

- [x] This PR makes NO speed claim.

## Honest gaps

- The pre-claim validation is scratch-harness evidence, not the in-tree gate; the in-tree cross-device gate is what each family commit must turn green, and it is written to run only once the op registers (red-first).
- M2 for Qwen3.5-0.8B is not claimed by any family commit except the last one that makes the model complete prefill+decode; the M2 disposition follows the #269/#273-ratified distributional gate for the near-tie regime.
- ROCm 6.x and gfx9 (wave64) boards are unverifiable from this box; no claim is made for them.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Closes rf2-ow4e.

## What was wrong

Three sites stated the `use-frame` ops bundle is **"reference-stable across
re-renders for the same resolved frame"**. That sentence is the one rf2-40kv
hid behind: the hook memoised on the resolved frame **keyword** compared by
`=`, and a keyword is `=` across a same-id reincarnation, so after a
destroy-and-recreate it kept serving the **dead** incarnation's bundle for the
rest of the mount — while satisfying the spec sentence perfectly. The spec
described the buggy behaviour as the contract.

It is a bug and not a smell because the stale bundle is not merely old.
`make-capture-frame` **pins** the incarnation live at capture (rf2-9pyles), and
both `capture-dispatch!` and `capture-subscribe!` **refuse** a superseded
target (rf2-tdjv7p) — so every operation through the survivor silently
recovers. "Surviving a reincarnation" means "silently dead", and the corrected
prose says so.

A frame keyword is an **ADDRESS**, not an identity. Reference stability holds
for the same resolved frame **incarnation**.

## The three sites

**1. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §CLJS reference: UIx as alternative substrate, Decision 3 (Auto-injection), line 2620**

- was: `… and reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame.`
- now: `… and reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame INCARNATION: a frame keyword is an *address*, not an identity, so destroying the resolved frame and creating another under the same id retargets the map, exactly as a provider swap does. The word `incarnation` is load-bearing rather than pedantic — `capture-frame` pins the exact incarnation live when it ran and every op on the bundle refuses a superseded target, so a bundle that survived a same-id reincarnation would not be merely stale, it would be silently inert.`

**2. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §Cross-substrate affordance summary, "Hold the ambient frame's ops" row, line 2651**

- was: `… for the ambient provider frame; reference-stable per resolved frame.`
- now: `… for the ambient provider frame; reference-stable per resolved frame *incarnation* — a same-id destroy-and-recreate retargets it, because the bundle is pinned to the incarnation and not to the address.`

**3. `spec/API.md` §UIx adapter (Spec 006), `uix-adapter/use-frame` row, line 579**

- was: `… reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame. No opts, no variants …`
- now: `… reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame *incarnation* — a same-id destroy-and-recreate retargets it, because the bundle is pinned to the incarnation `capture-frame` ran against and not to the address. No opts, no variants …`

Spec only. No API change, neither document re-derived, and `implementation/**`
untouched — the code is already correct on PR #7868, which keys the memo on the
frame plus `frame/frame-incarnation-token` by `identical?`.

## Is there a fourth copy?

Yes — one, and it is **out of this PR's fence**, reported rather than fixed.
A corpus sweep for `reference-stable` / `same resolved frame` / `stable across
re-render` over every tracked tree found exactly six live carriers of the
claim:

| Site | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2620` | **fixed here** |
| `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2651` | **fixed here** |
| `spec/API.md:579` | **fixed here** |
| `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs:39,71` | already corrected by PR #7868 |
| `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:162` | already corrected by PR #7868 |
| `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:94` | already corrected by PR #7868 |
| **`implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:14`** | **the fourth copy — still says "for the same resolved frame (safe in effect deps)". NOT in #7868's file list, and `implementation/**` is outside this PR's fence.** |

Also noted, not touched: `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/10-native-tier.md:169`
says `n/use-frame`'s map "is reference-stable across re-renders" with no frame
qualifier at all — a weaker claim in a different substrate's in-flight design
tree.

## Quality gates

| Gate | Exit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` | **0** on every lane once deps were present — see below | run from the worktree root, foreground to completion, never piped |
| ├ `mkdocs --strict build` (inside the spine) | **0** | the gate that *does* cover `spec/**` |
| ├ `docs corpus anchor validator` (`scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, inside the spine) | **0** | silent on success — coverage proven below |
| └ `CLJS node integration` (`npm run test:cljs`) | **0** | 13242 tests / 66932 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors |
| `implementation/scripts/api-manifest` → `api-md-check` | **0** | `OK: spec/API.md projection in sync (291 var-rows checked against the manifest)` — run because this PR edits `spec/API.md`, which the `Lint required` → `api-manifest` job asserts against the manifest |
| `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (standalone) | **0** clean / **1** planted | see coverage proof |

**Spine caveat, stated plainly.** The first spine run reported `FAIL mkdocs
--strict build`. That was **self-inflicted and not a property of this diff**:
`mkdocs_hooks.py:on_pre_build` stages `spec/` into the gitignored `docs/spec/`,
and a concurrent manual staging attempt of mine deleted that tree mid-build.
The spine was re-run clean, touching nothing under `docs/`, and `mkdocs
--strict build` passed. The only failure in the clean run was `CLJS node
integration` with `could not resolve shadow-cljs: Cannot find module
'shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'` — a fresh worktree with no `implementation/node_modules`,
not a test result. It was closed properly rather than waved through: the mayor
checkout's `node_modules` was junctioned in, `npm run test:cljs` ran green
(13242/66932, 0 failures), and the **junction was then removed with `cmd /c
rmdir`** (the link, never its target) with the mayor's `node_modules` re-counted
at 103 entries, unchanged. Every other lane in the spine — 60+ drift, residue,
bijection, self-test and validator sections — was green in the clean run.

**Coverage proof for `check_doc_slugs.py`**, since it is silent on success. A
bogus anchor was planted at the edited `spec/API.md` row:

```
1 broken anchor link(s) found:

  BROKEN ANCHOR: spec\API.md:579 -> 006-ReactiveSubstrate.md#rf2-ow4e-no-such-heading
      (target: spec\006-ReactiveSubstrate.md)
```

exit **1**. Restored with `git checkout -- spec/API.md` and **verified by hash,
not by `git diff`** (on Windows a rewritten file can read clean in `git
diff`/`git status` while the bytes differ): `git hash-object spec/API.md` ==
`git rev-parse HEAD:spec/API.md` == `f3c5474c30c89fba7fea8ffeb694f50f645c1b0c`.

**By-hand checks `check_doc_slugs.py` does not perform**, per the repo's rule
that nothing validates table structure. Both edited table rows keep their column
count exactly: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2651` has 4 pipes (3 columns),
matching every other row in that table (2645–2653); `spec/API.md:579` has 7
pipes (6 columns), matching rows 575–584. Neither edit introduces a link or a
heading, so no new anchor targets exist to validate.

**Gates deliberately not run, and why.** Every CLJS/JVM artefact suite, browser
and Playwright gate, bundle-isolation, elision, perf-bundle, mcp-conformance,
adapter-testbed smoke, skills-structural and examples-compile lane: this diff is
three markdown sentences under `spec/`, reaches no runtime surface, and those
jobs are surface-gated in CI and skip on such a diff. `clj-kondo`, `Splint` and
`ESLint`: no `.clj`/`.cljs`/`.cljc`/`.js` file is touched. The remaining
`api-manifest` projections (`skills-check`, `doc-guide-check`, `doc-api-check`,
the Story/Xray `spec/API.md` projections): none of their source pages is in this
diff; only the top-level `spec/API.md` projection is, and it was run. The gap
between this spine and CI was **derived, not guessed** — `python
scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list` reports 96 require

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

`scripts/install-icarus-verilog.sh`, `install-verilator.sh`, and
`install-yosys.sh` each independently defined the same "pin a release, fetch
it, verify its checksum, build, install idempotently" recipe. This PR moves
the duplicated boilerplate into a new `scripts/_install_common.sh`, sourced
by all three, leaving each script with only its pinned version constants and
its actual build step.

## Changes

- New `scripts/_install_common.sh` with four sourced helpers:
  - `sha256_of()` — the `shasum`/`sha256sum` fallback (byte-identical across
    all three original scripts).
  - `check_marker(marker, tag, force, tool_name)` — the `FORCE`/marker
    idempotency check (early-exits 0 with the "already installed" message).
  - `fetch_and_verify(url, expected_sha256, dest)` — the `curl -fsL --retry
    3` fetch plus the checksum-mismatch error block.
  - `finish_install(marker, tag, tool_name, prefix)` — the closing
    `echo "$TAG" >"$MARKER"` / `Installed ... into $PREFIX` / `Add to PATH`
    block.
  - Plus `nproc_val`, computed once at source time (was previously
    recomputed identically inline in each script).
- `install-icarus-verilog.sh` / `install-verilator.sh` / `install-yosys.sh`
  now `source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/_install_common.sh"` and call
  the shared helpers, keeping only: pinned version/tag/URL/checksum
  constants, `PREFIX`/`MARKER`/`FORCE` setup, tarball extraction, and the
  tool-specific build step (`configure && make`, `autoconf && configure &&
  make`, `cmake -B ... && cmake --build ...`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the three cache `key:` lines now hash
  `scripts/_install_common.sh` alongside each tool's own script, so a future
  edit to the shared fetch/checksum logic still busts the cache.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|---------------|
| `sha256_of()` shared across all three scripts | ✅ | Now defined once in `_install_common.sh`; each install script sources it instead of redefining it |
| `FORCE`/marker idempotency check shared | ✅ | `check_marker()` in `_install_common.sh`, called with each script's own marker/tag/tool-name |
| Fetch + checksum-mismatch error block shared | ✅ | `fetch_and_verify()` in `_install_common.sh` |
| `nproc_val` parallelism detection shared | ✅ | Computed once in `_install_common.sh`, used by all three build steps |
| Closing marker/summary block shared | ✅ | `finish_install()` in `_install_common.sh` |
| Only pinned constants + build step remain per-file | ✅ | Each `install-*.sh` now differs only in its version constants and its `configure`/`autoconf`/`cmake` build step |
| `ci.yml` cache keys hash the shared file too | ✅ | All three `key:` lines updated to `hashFiles('scripts/install-<tool>.sh', 'scripts/_install_common.sh')` |
| No behavior change | ✅ | See Test Plan — smoke-tested each helper in isolation; scripts are byte-for-byte the same recipe, just relocated |

## Test Plan

- `bash -n` on all four scripts (`_install_common.sh` + the three
  `install-*.sh`) — no syntax errors.
- `shellcheck -x scripts/install-*.sh scripts/_install_common.sh` (run from
  `scripts/`, so `-x` follows the `source` correctly) — 0 warnings/errors.
- Sourced `_install_common.sh` directly in isolation and exercised each
  helper:
  - `sha256_of()` against a known string, matched the expected digest.
  - `check_marker()`: verified it does *not* exit when the marker is
    absent, *does* exit 0 with the "already installed" message when the
    marker matches and `force=0`, and does *not* exit when `force=1`.
  - `fetch_and_verify()` against a local `file://` URL: succeeds and copies
    the file when the checksum matches; fails closed with the
    expected/actual mismatch message when it doesn't.
  - `finish_install()`: wrote the marker and printed the expected summary
    lines.
- `npm run lint` (repo's `buildGate.command`, `ruff format --check` +
  `ruff check`) — passes; no Python files touched by this change.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"`
  — confirms the edited workflow file is still valid YAML.
- Did not re-run the full multi-minute Icarus/Verilator/Yosys source builds
  locally (each takes several minutes and needs the CI-provisioned build
  deps); the isolated helper tests above cover the extracted logic, and CI
  itself directly exercises all three scripts end-to-end
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so the PR's own CI run is the real
  functional check the issue calls for.

TDD: no — pure refactor with no new behavior; existing coverage is CI
running these scripts directly (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) plus the manual
helper-isolation smoke tests above, run before this PR was opened.

Closes #687
