author: ankit-arora
body:
Fixes a live failure introduced by the CLI bump in v1.9.2.

## What happened

```
Bedrock: assumed arn:aws:iam::...:role/dr-bedrock-... ; agent will use Bedrock in eu-west-1.
[agentbox] using opencode-ai@1.18.16
[agentbox proxy] denied:models.opencode.ai: host "models.opencode.ai" not in allowlist
✗ opencode reported an error
```

opencode **1.18.x fetches its model + pricing registry from `models.opencode.ai`**, not `models.dev`. The allowlist had only `models.dev`, which sat there unused while the run died.

## Severity

Not a partial degradation. opencode cannot resolve a model id without the registry, so this failed **every** opencode run regardless of provider or model — including the whole Bedrock lineup added in deployment-runner-kit#61.

## Why both hosts stay

Which host is used depends on the opencode version, and that version is **pinned in the Dockerfile** — so a version bump alone can break this, which is exactly what v1.9.2 did (1.17.9 → 1.18.16). An unused allowlist entry opens no connection, so keeping both costs nothing and survives a rollback.

Verified `models.opencode.ai` serves the same registry shape and the **identical** `amazon-bedrock` ids, so the declared Bedrock ids in drk#61 are unaffected — all seven present.

## Follow-ups this exposed, not fixed here

- The Task error read `opencode opencode reported an error` — duplicated binary name, and no trace of the actual cause. The `denied:` line was only in the job logs.
- The runner logs `qwen3-coder-480b has no Bedrock profile prefix; leaving the model unchanged`, which reads like a problem. It is correct behaviour — that model uses a declared id — but the wording invites the wrong conclusion.

author: allanice001
body:
swaggo/swag generates the OpenAPI spec that both SDKs are generated from, so
it sits in the build path of the shipped artifact. Two things were wrong with
how it was resolved:

- go.mod required swag/v2 v2.0.0-rc5, but no package imports it, so `go mod
  tidy` deleted it outright — 10 go.mod lines and 43 go.sum lines, including
  golang.org/x/tools. That is the same dependency whose missing go.sum hash
  broke `make vet` on every bot PR for two days.
- The Makefile ignored that pin anyway and ran `go install ...@latest` when
  swag was absent from PATH, so the spec was built by whatever version
  resolved that day.

A `tool` directive fixes both: tidy now retains swag (it moves to the indirect
block rather than being dropped), and `go tool swag` runs exactly the pinned
version. Verified: tidy keeps swag and x/tools, `go tool swag --version`
reports v2.0.0, and `make swagger` regenerates the spec unchanged at
OpenAPI 3.1.0 with 66 paths and 75 schemas.

Signed-off-by: allanice001 <alanis.swanepoel@glueops.dev>

Follow-up to the dependency audit's supply-chain section, which flagged the
unpinned `OGC_WRAPPER` (fixed in #1041) but missed this second unpinned
`@latest` in the same codegen path.

author: cpwaters
body:
## Summary

Reported: "when a job is created the map doesn't show the route."

## Root cause

`acceptLoad` only denormalizes the route onto the new `Job` if the load was **already** enriched (`load.route` set) at acceptance time:

```ts
...(load.route !== undefined ? { route: load.route } : {}),
```

The drain enriches a freshly-posted load's route on its own schedule (up to ~1 minute later, in production). If a carrier accepts the load inside that window — very plausible, especially when testing/demoing where posting and accepting happen back-to-back — the job is created with no route at all, and **nothing ever revisits it afterward**. The driver's map (`MapView.tsx` reads `job?.route`) shows "No Active Route" for that job permanently.

## Fix

When the drain enriches a load's route (`recordEnrichment` in `packages/actions/src/drain.ts`), it now also looks up any job that already references that `loadId` and backfills the route onto it (if it doesn't have one yet) — in the same transaction as the load/listing update. Whichever order acceptance and enrichment happen in, the job ends up routed either way.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 196 green. Two new tests: the backfill fires for a job accepted ahead of enrichment (the reported bug, reproduced deterministically), and an already-routed job (the normal ordering) is left untouched.
- [x] `pnpm test:rules` / `pnpm test:contract` — green (drain writes go through the Admin SDK like every other system-sourced write; `jobs/{jobId}`'s `allow write: if false` already covers this, no rules change needed)
- [x] `pnpm seed` / `pnpm check:web` / `pnpm build` — clean

author: saivenu-hydradb
body:
Three bottlenecks in the client.mutate write path were invisible in traces because they fell inside shard.write_txn with no sub-spans:

- write.permit_acquire: the graph_write_gate semaphore acquire.  Queue time here means the shard's write concurrency limit is saturated before any transaction work begins.  Without this span, a slow shard.write_txn is indistinguishable from a write that was queued.

- write.lane_lock: the per-cell mutex that serialises concurrent writes to the same cell.  Contention here does not appear in turbolay.writer.retries (which counts SlateDB conflicts, not mutex waits) and was completely invisible.  Hot cells accumulate wait time here silently.

- write.fence_validate: two remote reads on every write attempt — the cell drop marker and pending-drop marker.  These fire on retries too, so a retry-heavy workload multiplies the round-trip cost. error.class on this span pins a CellDropped failure to this specific check rather than the root.

All three spans are added at every entry point that flows through client.mutate: write_edge (scalar), import_relationships_batch and write_edge_mutations_batch (both UNWIND batch paths).

Also adds turbolay.query.kind = scalar | batch on the client.mutate root span, recorded after parse_opencypher_unwind_batch determines the shape.  Without this, a slow client.mutate trace gives no indication which execution path was taken.

author: copilot
body:
The app exposed learner-management logic/data in the public frontend and trusted client-side checks for sensitive updates. This change moves learner-wide management behind admin auth, restricts public data to anonymous assignment state, and enforces server-side phone ownership checks for modifying existing assignments.

- **Public/Admin surface split**
  - `/` continues to serve the public experience.
  - `/dafdaf` now serves `admin.html` and requires existing Basic Auth (`BACKUP_PASSWORD`).
  - Removed all “all learners” UI/logic from `base.html` so admin flows are not shipped to public clients.

- **Server-side authorization for existing assignment changes**
  - `PUT /api/assignments/:id` and `DELETE /api/assignments/:id` now require:
    - admin auth, or
    - matching `X-User-Phone` to the assignment owner phone.
  - Prevents unauthorized edits/deletes even if requests are crafted directly.

- **Data exposure minimization**
  - `GET /api/assignments` returns:
    - full records for admin-authenticated requests,
    - anonymized records for public requests (`masechet`, `daf`, `daf_end`, `learned`, `is_full_masechet` only).
  - Added `GET /api/my-assignments` scoped by `X-User-Phone` for user-owned views/edits.

- **Phone identity consistency on create**
  - Phone values are normalized server-side.
  - New assignments with an existing phone automatically inherit existing identity details for that phone (name/dedication), ensuring consistent ownership mapping.

```python
# app.py (authorization gate for existing assignment mutation)
verified_phone = self._get_verified_phone()
owner_phone = store.normalize_phone(assignment.get("phone"))

if not verified_phone:
    self._send_json({"error": "Phone is required"}, status=400)
    return False
if verified_phone != owner_phone:
    self._send_json({"error": "Forbidden"}, status=403)
    return False
```

body:
## Summary

- proves complete conditional two-open detection in the aligned common-two-row, projectively constant `q=0,r=5` cell
- uses the upstream `p_a>=2` row quota to exclude four/five `B` defects, then exhausts all residual four- and five-defect `R/B` words
- reconstructs arbitrary-ratio collision kernels, the all-regular reciprocal cofactor graph, `RRRBB` exceptional cases, and the basis-free `3|2` Hall bridge to the exact two-singleton `P_5` obstruction
- adds a focused SymPy verifier, an independent no-import recursive-permanent audit with exact `Q(omega)` arithmetic, a durable hostile review, and ledger/frontier updates

## Falsified strengthening preserved

The initial claim that the `RRRRT` full common kernel survives only at equal ratios is false. A `2+2` reciprocal primitive-cube-root divisor also survives. Its kernel is still exactly one-dimensional, so the detector proof uses only the corrected dimension bound.

## Scope

This proves detector closure only. It does **not** prove witness exclusion, fixed-root injectivity, arbitrary permanent nonrestriction, extraction/gluing, or global resolution. `q=0,r>=6`, `q>=1`, and unfactorized cells remain UNKNOWN/OPEN. The global Krenn--Gu conjecture remains UNRESOLVED.

## Exact local validation

- `uv run --with sympy python -B claims/arbitrary-order/verify_projectively_constant_lift_complete_aligned_five_cell_detector.py`

author: yukimemi
body:
`yaiba gcal login` opened a Google error page instead of the consent screen, on Windows, every time. Found by @yukimemi running it on the release that had just shipped.

```
'redirect_uri' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
'response_type' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
'scope' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
...
```

and in the browser: **エラー 400: invalid_request — Required parameter is missing: response_type**.

## What happened

`cmd` treats `&` as a command separator, and an OAuth URL is mostly `&`. `cmd /C start "" <url>` therefore ran `start "" https://…?client_id=…` and then took `response_type=code`, `scope=…`, `code_challenge=…` and the rest as separate commands. Google got a URL carrying only `client_id` and answered, accurately, that `response_type` was missing.

The launcher had been correct for as long as it existed, because the only URL it was ever handed was `http://localhost:8188` on startup — no `&`, no problem. Moving it into `browser.rs` to share with `gcal login` handed it a kind of URL it had never seen, and the precondition it had been quietly relying on was written down nowhere. It is in the function now.

## The fix

Quote the URL — and the quotes have to go into the **raw** command line. `Command::arg` quotes an argument only when it contains a space or a quote, and a URL has neither, so it reached `cmd` bare no matter how it was passed. `raw_arg` is how to state what the command line actually is.

A URL containing a `"` is refused rather than escaped. Nothing yaiba builds contains one — every query value goes through `gcal::escape` first — and leaving it printed for the person to open is a perfectly good outcome, whereas inventing an escape for a case that cannot arise is how that case starts arising.

## What kept it from being fatal

The URL is printed *before* the browser is opened. That was written down as being for SSH, containers and headless boxes; it turned out to be for this. The consent screen was reachable the whole time by copying the line above the error.

## Tests

`windows_command_line` is one function, used by both the launch and the test, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing about the quoting — the second-list-to-keep-in-step problem this repo has been bitten by before. The test reproduces the actual failure: the query must survive `&` intact, the URL must be one quoted argument, and the empty `""` title must come first or `start` takes the URL as a window title and opens nothing.

`cargo make check` green.

## Ships in

v0.23.0 has already merged and tagged, so this is 0.23.1 material.

author: angel-manuel
body:
## Why

Kaniko was [archived upstream in June 2025](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko) — "no longer developed or maintained". The deploy path for all three images depended on it, and the exit-137 OOM that #526 and #527 chased was a symptom: Kaniko keeps a compressed copy of every snapshotted layer in memory, and our builder-stage dependency layer is the whole multi-GB `target/release` tree. `--compressed-caching=false` tuned around one instance of that; this removes the class.

**Supersedes #526 and #527** — both patched the Kaniko step that no longer exists. #527's still-valid one-liner (why the API build stays on `E2_HIGHCPU_8`: the default pool's non-increasable E2 CPU quota) is kept as-is. Rebased on #528, and the new comments follow the one-liner style its second commit established for these modules.

## What

**Builder → `docker buildx`.** All three Cloud Build triggers (`cloud-build`, `-shortener`, `-metrics-exporter`) build with `docker buildx` under the `docker-container` driver, exporting and importing layer cache via `--cache-to/--cache-from type=registry,mode=max` against a `<image>/cache:buildcache` ref in the same Artifact Registry repo. BuildKit diffs layers incrementally instead of snapshotting the whole filesystem, so the OOM failure mode is gone rather than tuned around. `--provenance=false` keeps the pushed artifact a plain image manifest, exactly what Kaniko produced and what Cloud Run consumes.

A preceding step mints an AR access token for an explicit `docker login`: buildx hands auth to a separate BuildKit container, so Cloud Build's own docker credential wiring isn't enough to rely on. The token lives in `/workspace` for one step and is deleted right after the login.

**Dependency layer → cargo-chef.** `cargo chef prepare` distills the workspace into a `recipe.json` of dependencies only, `cargo chef cook` compiles it, and the real `cargo build` follows a plain `COPY . .`. This retires:

- the hand-maintained eleven `COPY crates/*/Cargo.toml` lines and the matching `echo "fn main(){}"` stub block, in all three Dockerfiles plus `Dockerfile.dev`. Their cost is in the history: aad3d8d4, 9b3b059c, c19ccc96, eb06cb78 — four separate "copy X manifest" fixes, one per new crate, each found by a broken build. cargo-chef derives the list from the workspace, so a new crate needs no Dockerfile edit.
- `find crates/ -name "*.rs" -exec touch {} +`, which forced every workspace crate to rebuild on every build just to defeat the stub fingerprints. `cook` drops the workspace's own artifacts when it finishes, so it isn't needed.

**Contexts are whole-repo now**, so `.dockerignore` — not a `COPY` allow-list — decides what reaches the image. `tests/mock-target/src/` comes back in: a workspace member with no discoverable target fails manifest parsing, which is what the stub used to paper over.

## Why not `RUN --mount=type=cache`

A cache mount would keep `target/` out of the image entirely, which is the tidier shape — but BuildKit's registry cache exporter does not carry cache-mount contents, and Cloud Build runs every build on a fresh VM, so a cache mount there is cold every time. Worse, mounting over `target/` masks the cooked dependency layer, so deps would rebuild on every build. The dependency cache has to *be* a layer to survive the trip through a registry. Recorded in D54.

## Verification

Built all three images locally (podman/buildah):

| image | result |
|---|---|
| `overslash-api` | builds; after `COPY . .` the final `cargo build` compiles **only** the 6 workspace crates in 1m27s — every third-party dep including `pg_query` served from the cook layer |
| `oversla-sh` | builds; final build recompiles only `oversla-sh`, 3.23s |
| `overslash-metrics-exporter` | builds |

Also checked on the API image: injected `OVERSLASH_GIT_SHA` is baked into the binary, version still reports `0.7.0-dev` with `OVERSLASH_RELEASE` unset, `services/` (24 files) and the entrypoint are in place. All three build scripts pass `bash -n` with the Terraform heredoc rendered; `tofu fmt` clean.

## Notes for the reviewer

- `infra/` is never auto-applied — this is inert until `make tofu-apply` runs per env. The first build after apply is cold (no cache ref yet); `--cache-from` warns and continues.
- The `docker-container` driver pulls `moby/buildkit` from Docker Hub per build. We already have an optional AR pull-through mirror (`enable_docker_hub_remote`); if rate limits ever bite, `--driver-opt image=` pointed at it is the fix.
- `bin/deploy-cloudrun.sh` and `make shortener-deploy` stay on plain `docker build` — still correct, just not sharing the CI cache. Adding `--cache-from` there is a small follow-up, complicated only by the script's `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman` support.
- Artifact Registry cleanup-policy comments were written around Kaniko's `--cache-ttl` and are updated: the live `cache:buildcache` version is re-pushed every build, and `keep-recent` protects it through a quiet month.

author: yuolel
body:
Updates `changelog/media/README.md`, which still described the old full-width image rendering. Documentation only — no page changes.

Brings it in line with the agreed entry-image standard:

- **Image goes after the entry text**, not before it — the reader gets the point in words first, then the illustration. It sits outside the `.a` body div, as the last child of the `<article>`.
- **`max-width:600px`** — roughly two-thirds of the ~916px content column. The page's CSS defaults entry images to full width, which is too dominant for a UI screenshot, so the inline cap is required; using the same cap everywhere keeps the images a consistent set.
- **Capture at 1000px or wider** so the screenshot downscales into the cap rather than upscaling (upscaled captures look visibly soft).
- **Landscape only** — a portrait capture becomes a tall block that swamps the entry.
- **Check the `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL loads** before merging.
- Alt text should use the app's real labels — "Settings → Connections", not "the Integrations tab".

Also cross-references the matching standard in `scripts/release_comms/PROMPT.md` (`vidtao/bratrax`), so the weekly routine and anyone adding an image by hand follow the same rules.

author: osobytes
body:
The Rust + TypeScript tree becomes the game. `v2/` is gone as a directory and as an
idea: `v2/rust` → `rust/`, `v2/ts` → `ts/`, `v2/tools` → `tools/`, `v2/README.md` →
`ARCHITECTURE.md`. The LÖVE/Lua implementation and everything whose only subject was
it are deleted. **Native support is dropped; the browser is the only target.**

Docs under `docs/` are deliberately untouched — this is a code change. See
*Deliberately not done* below.

## The gate

`scripts/check_v2.sh` is now `scripts/check.sh`. Its own header predicted this
cutover would be "a small diff — delete the Lua-specific steps, keep this script and
its two call sites", and that is what happened. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` goes from
thirteen jobs to one, and that job calls the same script, so the two still cannot
drift (AGENTS.md §9).

Green on this branch:

```
1545 Rust tests passed, 0 failed
Tests  1191 passed | 3 expected fail | 9 skipped (1203)
wire enum parity: OK (11 enums)
presentation parity: OK (19 mappings)
final_hash=bfbb106aea5480f8 sequence_digest=0bfd0ed355f87322 (matches the pinned OMP-1 fixture)
GATE OK
```

`./scripts/check.sh --self-test` also passes, so the gate is still demonstrably able
to go red. **The determinism digest is byte-identical to before the migration** — the
simulation this ships is the simulation that was tested.

## Comments

Every comment framing this code as a port of a Lua original is gone. A new reader
should never learn a Lua version existed. What was kept, deliberately:

- **Engineering knowledge.** Where a comment carried a real why — a determinism
  rationale, an invariant, a dated incident — the knowledge survives and only the
  Lua framing was dropped. Issue numbers and bug histories are preserved verbatim.
- **The frozen reference vectors, and the tests asserting them.** The
  `*_lua_reference.txt` fixtures and the differential tests around them pin bit-exact
  behaviour and **cannot be regenerated now that the implementation they were
  captured from is gone**. `tools/lua_reference/README.md` and
  `tools/render_reference/README.md` are rewritten from how-to-capture recipes into
  provenance documents that say exactly that: a failing differential is a finding
  about the code, not a stale fixture to refresh. Their names were left alone on
  purpose — the provenance is accurate and renaming ~20 `include_str!` paths is churn
  with risk and no benefit.

## Two things that were quietly broken

Found while sweeping, both fixed here:

- `gc_sim::tripwire::serialize` and `gc_sim::outfield_ai_baseline::serialize`
  generated **Lua source** (`-- comment` lines, `return { ... }`) for baselines that
  are now Rust consts. Nothing could load their output. They now emit the Rust their
  target files actually hold, pasteable verbatim, and the round-trip tests were
  strengthened to assert the emitted field names are real fields of the target struct.
- Both baselines' headers told you to refresh with `love . --tripwire write` /
  `--ai-baseline write --refreeze-ack`. Those entry points died with `main.lua`. The
  instructions now say what is true (see the follow-up below).

Two scripts were also over-deleted and restored: `scripts/web_serve.py` (generic WASM
header serving, no Lua in it) and the generic Selenium launch/teardown helpers that
lived inside the deleted `browser_determinism.py`, now `scripts/browser_launch.py`.

## Coverage this removes — read this part

The deleted CI jobs were real evidence. Their harnesses measured the LÖVE build, so
they die with it, but the guarantees they asserted do not stop mattering.

- **OMP-1 browser determinism** ran the build through headless Chrome *and* Firefox
  twice each on every push, asserting bit-identical replay across two engines. **Not
  covered.** The surviving gate asserts a wasm determinism digest twice, but
  single-process and single-engine. `browser_online_peers.py` proves two wasm
  instances agree over real WebRTC, but same-engine only, and that is peer agreement,
  not cross-engine replay determinism.
- **OMP-2 rollback campaign** — native shards, a Chrome/Firefox matrix, hour-long
  soaks, PR-triggered stress runs, impact-scoped reuse, an auto-filed issue on
  regression. **Not covered by name.** `gc-netcode`'s own `cargo test` suite still
  runs, so rollback *logic* is tested; there is no browser-driven stress/soak/matrix
  campaign against the shipped artifact, and no long-running evidence mechanism.
- **OMP-3 fault harness** — a dedicated job injecting faults and requiring the harness
  to catch every one. **Not covered.** No equivalent exists for the new stack.
- **The fun tripwire (#468).** `gc_sim::tripwire` and `gc_data::fun_baseline::BASELINE`
  both survive, but nothing calls `tripwire::measure()` against real seeded matches --
  `tests/tripwire.rs` only exercises `compare`/`serialize` on synthetic signatures. So
  the tripwire can fail on a bug in itself but **not on gameplay drift**. Wiring it is
  a feature rather than a migration, so it is tracked separately.
- **The frozen Outfield AI baseline (#59, #148/#149) is NOT lost** -- correcting an
  earlier draft of this description. `gc-sim/tests/outfield_ai_baseline.rs`'s
  `outfield_ai_baseline_reproduces_the_frozen_fixture_exactly` runs a live 60-seed
  `measure()` and asserts it equals `frozen::RECORD`, inside `cargo test --workspace`.
  That is a real gameplay-drift gate, running today, on every PR.
- **Browser artifact smoke** — *superseded, not lost.* `gate_app_bundle` builds the
  real browser wasm target and byte-compares it against the shipped bundle, a stricter
  check of the same concern.
- The remaining Lua gates (`stylua`, `lua-language-server`, `love . --test`,
  snapshot headroom #209, shader hoist #391, the Babylon/native-shell/love.js refusal
  self-tests #341/#328/#329/#360, embed manifest #343) are **moot rather than
  missing** — their subjects no longer exist in this repository.

Still asserted, unchanged: wire-enum parity (#433), presentation-content parity
(#447), Rust fmt/clippy/test on both native and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with floors
on pass counts, TypeScript typecheck and vitest with floors, the twice-checked wasm
determinism digest, the byte-identical browser-bundle check (the 2026-08-07 stale
artifact), the match-harness Python/TypeScript mirror self-test, and the two-browser
WebRTC peer agreement check.

## Deliberately not done

- **`docs/` is untouched**, as scoped. Several documents now describe a tree that
  does not exist and reference deleted scripts.
- **`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `THIRD_PARTY.md` are
  untouched** for the same reason — but flagging loudly that `AGENTS.md` is the file
  agents load automatically, and it still names LÖVE 11.5 as the engine, StyLua as
  law, and `stylua --check . && lua-language-server --check . && busted` as the
  pre-commit command. None of that is true after this merge. It should be the next PR.
- **No identifiers or fixture files renamed.** Test names like
  `match_driver_differential_matches_the_lua_reference` describe what they assert
  accurately.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md` corrects two claims** rather than restating them: the
  `MatchStateView` duplication debt is resolved (verified in the source), and two-bone
  IK is not implemented at all rather than "hand-written" (open as #318).

## Merged with main

#464 (the rig3d knee bend) landed on main after this branch moved `v2/ts` to `ts/`,
so it is merged in here. Git's rename detection carried all twelve files across; the
two new `rig3d/crouch` files needed placing by hand. Verified rather than assumed,
because a rename-heavy merge can drop work silently:

- The merged sources are **byte-identical to main's for all twelve files** once
  comment lines are excluded — so nothing of #464's behaviour was lost to the move or
  to this branch's comment cleanup.
- Reverting the six implementation files to their pre-merge state **fails 20 of the
  incoming tests with real assertion err

author: anoop-narang
body:
`./scripts/release.sh prepare minor` fails outright on macOS:

    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib'

tomllib is stdlib only from 3.11, and `python3` on macOS is 3.9. Every helper
in the script -- get_version, get_pkg_name, set_version, bump_version, the
changelog update, and the publish-time changelog check -- hardcoded `python3`,
so releasing this package was impossible on such a machine. The error names a
missing module, which reads as a broken checkout rather than a too-old
interpreter.

Resolved once at load time instead of per call site: `python3` when it can
actually import tomllib, else `uv run`, else a message that says what is
needed and what was found. uv is the right fallback because this repo already
builds and tests through it, so a machine that can run the suite can run the
release.

The two `need python3` guards are dropped as redundant -- resolve_python has
already exited with a better message by then.

Verified under bash, which is how the script runs:

    PY_BIN=uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python
    version=0.10.0   pkg=hotdata-framework
    minor=0.11.0     patch=0.10.1        major=1.0.0

and with no usable interpreter on PATH:

    error: need python3 >= 3.11 (for tomllib) or uv; python3 is Python 3.9.6

No behaviour change to what a release does -- only which interpreter runs it.

Note the same hardcoded `python3 - <<PY` + tomllib pattern is in sdk-python's
and hotdata-marimo's copies of this script, so both are latently broken the
same way on a pre-3.11 `python3`. Not touched here.

author: nirvanach7
body:
## Summary

The "explore unseen models" routing toggle picked a random unmeasured model purely by sample count and pushed it to the front of the routing chain. For requests with request-level capability gates (vision / tools / structured output) it could promote a model the main routing loop would immediately skip — e.g. an image request randomly probing a text-only model, wasting a fallback hop and (in the worst case) surfacing the wrong model to the client.

## Change

`routeRequest` exploration candidates are now filtered by the same gates as the main loop:

- models ruled out earlier in the request (`skipModels`)
- text-only models when the request requires vision
- models without structured tool-call support when the request uses tools
- platforms that drop `response_format` when structured output is requested
- models whose context window or per-minute token limit can't hold the request

So an exploration pick is always a model that can actually serve the request; the loop still falls through to the scored order when the explore pick fails.

## Tests

Added a regression test in `router-bandit.test.ts` asserting an image request (requireVision) never routes to a text-only model even with exploration enabled. Full `router-bandit`, `router-key-bandit` and `fallback` suites pass; `tsc` clean.

author: tfalohun
body:
Found while re-reading a letter before sending it. The phone number was correct and the draft lint was clean. **The route was wrong.**

## What Oklahoma actually says

From [the state's own How to Apply page](https://oklahoma.gov/okdhs/services/cap/advantage-services.html), in this order:

> "**Before you begin the online application below**, please review the Provider Search tool. Choose the Home Care and Case Management providers you would like for the county where you live. **This information will be needed when you call to do the medical eligibility assessment.**"

> "Click to complete an **online application** for in home assistance."

> "**If you are unable to complete the online application**, you may call the Medicaid Services Unit at 1-800-435-4711..."

So the phone is explicitly the **fallback**, not the front door, and the first real step is choosing providers.

## What our record said

| | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `applicationGuide.steps[1]` | "Contact your local county OKDHS office" | Choose providers from the state provider search |
| `method` | `multiple` | `online` |
| `urls` | program page only | + online application, + Provider Search |
| visible documents | SSN cards, birth certificate, proof of residency | chosen providers, rough income/savings, daily tasks |

"Contact your local county OKDHS office" is not a route Oklahoma publishes for this waiver at all. And with only the program page in `urls`, a family had no way to reach either the online application or the provider search from their plan page — while the letter told them to call.

**The provider pre-step is the one families never anticipate.** Skipping it means arriving at the assessment call unable to answer the question being asked. It is now the first visible document, because that is genuinely what you need before you start.

The old document entries are kept further down the list, since they do matter later for the SoonerCare financial side.

## The letter

Patched in the database to match: provider pre-step, then online, then phone as the backup. Also removed "Here is one step you can take", which stopped being true once the pre-step was named.

## Why the lint did not catch this

Exactly as its header warns. The letter was internally consistent, the phone number was right, and the snapshot matched the pipeline. What was wrong was the *route*, which no consistency check can see. This is the same class as the SoonerCare finding earlier today and it took reading the operator's page.

Worth noting the letter and plan page would also have disagreed on documents: the letter said income, savings, and daily tasks while the plan page still listed birth certificate and proof of residency. That is the deploy-boundary problem from #1552 showing up in a different field.

author: spiralocean
body:
Reported: the "Which platforms" figures are larger than the number of devices actually running.

## Cause

The chart plotted update-feed requests and printed `~${(r.v / 12).toFixed(1)} machines` — a guess from a polling cadence, sitting two sections below the real fleet count and disagreeing with it.

It reads high for three compounding reasons:

1. **`FEED_PER_DAY = 12` is a floor, not the rate.** The real figure is 12 scheduled checks plus one per launch — the constant's own comment says so.
2. **Releases restart every machine that updates**, and each restart fires another check. So release days — exactly when this page gets looked at — inflate most. The feed metric gains ~8% per launch against ~4% for the changelog-derived "running installs" (48/day + 2 per launch), which is why the two drift apart.
3. **Anything else touching a 2 KB file at a stable URL** lands in the same bucket: crawlers, uptime probes, and measurably today, the release-verification sweep in `DEPLOY.md`.

That third one also breaks the property the chart advertised. Its subtitle claimed the split was exact *"even when the headcount isn't"* — but a sweep hitting `latest-mac.yml`, `latest.yml` and `latest-linux.yml` equally manufactures Windows and Linux traffic on a fleet that may have neither. With ~15 all-time downloads, six stray requests aren't noise; they're the reading.

## Fix

The page already had the right number and wasn't using it here. `stats.js` derives fleet composition from **versioned installer fetches** — one per machine per release, no cadence assumption, and nothing incidental downloads 100 MB. Its own comment says why that source is the trustworthy one:

> each machine fetches it exactly once when it takes a release, so counting versioned artifact fetches counts computers, with no cadence assumption and nothing inflated by restarts

New `totals.platform` sums `r_mac`/`r_win`/`r_linux`, so it agrees with `totals.fleet` by construction. `totals.feed` stays, relabelled as request volume — which is what it honestly is.

## Verification

Replayed the fleet-composition step on a realistic cumulative tally:

```
per-version running: 0.1.84: 2, 0.1.83: 2, 0.1.82: 1
platform: { mac: 3, win: 1, linux: 1 }
platform sum: 5   fleet: 5   ✓ agree by construction

old chart, with today's six verification curls in the window:
  mac:   32 checks -> ~2.7 machines
  win:    2 checks -> ~0.2 machines
  linux:  2 checks -> ~0.2 machines
  ...including Windows and Linux machines that do not exist
```

Both changed files syntax-checked (`stats.js` as ESM; the inline `<script>` extracted and `node --check`ed). Empty state handled: with no installer fetches recorded the chart says so rather than drawing three empty bars.

## Follow-up in DEPLOY.md

Documents that the verification sweep shows up in request volume and **cannot** be filtered out — the analytics dataset groups by `clientRequestPath` with the query string stripped, so a `?verify=1` marker lands in the same bucket. Rather than invent a filter that wouldn't work, the note records that the machine figures no longer care.

author: bastianhagedorn
body:
## What changed

Disable `REUSE_GATHER_INDICES` in the four MXFP4 MoE selector entries that explicitly enabled it, for expected slice sizes 36, 64, 416, and 896. All other tuning choices remain unchanged.

## Why

Index reuse avoids repeated gather-index loads, but it also retains the cached slice state and a `BLOCK_M`-element offset vector in the activation producer. On B200, that retained state and control overhead costs more than the saved loads for every selector entry that currently enables reuse.

## B200 results

Fresh run on SM100, 148 SMs, using 11 randomized rounds and 100 ms per variant per round:

| Expected slice | Reuse | No reuse | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 36 | 61.150 us | 60.739 us | 0.67% |
| 64 | 64.424 us | 63.902 us | 0.81% |
| 416 | 120.832 us | 120.123 us | 0.59% |
| 896 | 138.133 us | 134.955 us | 2.30% |

The geometric-mean speedup is 1.09%. No-reuse wins 42 of 44 paired rounds. Every comparison changes only `REUSE_GATHER_INDICES`, and all outputs are bit-identical.

body:
Moves every dependency to its latest release: quic 1.7.0 to 1.8.0, ws 0.4.0 to 0.5.0, webtransport 0.4.3 to 0.4.4, instrument 1.1.4 to 1.1.5, hackney 4.7.0 to 4.7.3 and barrel_mcp 2.2.4 to 2.3.0. mimerl, h1 and h2 were already current. The test and bench profiles follow with cowboy 2.18.0, cowlib 2.19.0 and ranch 2.2.1, and the tooling with erlfmt 1.8.0 and rebar3_lint 5.0.4.

rebar3_lint 5.0.4 pulls elvis_core 5.x, so the elvis config moves to the new format: dirs and filter become a single files glob, god_modules becomes no_god_modules, invalid_dynamic_call becomes no_invalid_dynamic_calls and line_length becomes max_line_length. Four strict rules are new. prefer_strict_generators is disabled because `<:-` needs OTP 28 while the quickstart promises 27 or later, and prefer_sigils is disabled because it would restyle every binary literal in the tree. strict_term_equivalence turned up one real weak comparison, fixed in livery_req:has_header/2; livery_openapi_validate keeps `==` since it compares a float against an integer on purpose and `=:=` would never hold. consistent_ok_error_spec is ignored for livery_body, livery_req_proc and livery_ws, whose `{ok, _}` returns are the shape those entry points promise.

Adopting sigils and strict generators is a separate sweep and would mean dropping OTP 27.

Implements the first safe Flow smart-buy-list layer while preserving the existing manual Buy List and current Flow commands.

- "create/make/build/generate list" asks before generating anything.

- Accepts a budget such as ₦100,000 or ₦20,000 and fits the same scoring/allocation logic to that cap.
- After Accept, persists the generated list through the existing Purchase Order/Buy List store and gives the existing PO import code.
- The chat response tells the merchant to review the list before ordering.

- Normal Buy List remains manual; nothing is auto-generated merely by opening Buy List.

- Existing Flow restock confirmation and new-money path are preserved.

body:
Adds `cf pages` porcelain for the wave-2 pages shard, following `internal/cli/dns.go` and docs/STYLE.md.

## Commands

| Command | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `cf pages project list` | `GET /accounts/{a}/pages/projects` (auto-paginated) |
| `cf pages project get <project>` | `GET .../pages/projects/{name}` |
| `cf pages project create <name>` | `POST .../pages/projects` |
| `cf pages project delete <project>` | `DELETE .../pages/projects/{name}` |
| `cf pages deployment list <project>` | `GET .../deployments` (`--env production\|preview`) |
| `cf pages deployment get <project> <deployment-id>` | `GET .../deployments/{id}` |
| `cf pages deployment rollback <project> <deployment-id>` | `POST .../deployments/{id}/rollback` |
| `cf pages domain add <project> <domain>` | `POST .../domains` |
| `cf pages domain remove <project> <domain>` | `DELETE .../domains/{domain}` |

Paths and request/response fields were checked against the pinned spec revision (`4e2f140437b8`).

## Notes

- Account scope comes from the global `--account-id`/env/profile chain; no per-command account flag. Missing account produces an actionable error.
- `list` renders a table and honors `--output`/`--query`; everything else defaults to JSON. All results funnel through `g.renderResult`/`g.renderValue`.
- Every command works under `--dry-run` (no network, confirmation skipped).
- `project delete` and `domain remove` confirm on a TTY and require `--force` otherwise. `rollback` does the same: it changes what visitors see.
- List commands use `DoAutoPaginate` and leave `per_page` at the API default; the Pages list endpoints report `result_info.total_pages`, which the paginator follows (covered by a two-page test).
- Path segments are `url.PathEscape`d, and empty/whitespace positional args are rejected before any request is built.

## Tests

`internal/cli/pages_test.go`: pure-helper tests (body building, `--env` validation, timestamp formatting, path escaping), dry-run request construction for all nine commands, and `httptest` coverage for table rendering, pagination, `--output json`/`--query`, rollback/domain-add/create request shape, API error surfacing, `--force` requirements, stray args, and help examples.

`make check` is green (vet + style lint + tests + build).

## Scope

Only `internal/cli/pages.go`, `internal/cli/pages_test.go`, and a one-line `AddCommand` in `internal/cli/root.go`. No kernel files touched.

body:
## Summary

Initial commit of a complete single-page landing site for Diósdi Méhes, a premium single-origin raw honey brand. The site features a luxury aesthetic with a quiet, brass-on-near-black design system, no external frameworks or build tools, and a focus on elegant typography and generous whitespace.

## Key Changes

- **HTML structure** (`index.html`): Ten-section layout including entrance gate, sticky navigation, hero, story, process/traceability, products (light section), markets, email signup, contact form, and footer. All copy in Hungarian with semantic markup and ARIA labels for accessibility.

- **Design system** (`styles.css`): 
  - Comprehensive CSS custom properties (design tokens) for colors, spacing, and easing
  - Signature visual motif: a glowing radial-gradient orb used as a decorative element
  - Luxury typography stack: Fraunces (display), Work Sans (body), IBM Plex Mono (labels/UI)
  - Scroll-reveal animations with `IntersectionObserver` support
  - Responsive breakpoints (900px, 560px) with mobile-first adjustments
  - Full support for `prefers-reduced-motion` to disable all animations

- **Behavior** (`main.js`):
  - Entrance gate with staggered CSS animations and keyboard focus management
  - Sticky navigation with scroll-triggered translucent background
  - Scroll reveal system using `IntersectionObserver` for one-time section animations
  - Front-end-only form validation and inline confirmation for signup and contact forms
  - Centralized brand name management via `BRAND` constant for easy rebranding

- **Documentation** (`README.md`): Setup instructions, file structure overview, and notes on brand name swapping and form behavior.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **No build step**: Pure HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript—serves directly from the filesystem or any static host.
- **Accessibility**: Semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus management, and keyboard navigation throughout.
- **Brand agility**: Brand name (currently "Diósdi Méhes") is defined in one place (`BRAND` object) and propagated via `data-brand-*` attributes, allowing instant rebranding.
- **Graceful degradation**: Forms validate client-side only; animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; scroll reveals fall back to immediate visibility if `IntersectionObserver` is unavailable.
- **Luxury aesthetic**: Hairline dividers, generous padding, single accent color (brass), and the recurring orb motif create a cohesive, high-end visual identity.

body:
**What.** The platform takes no commission on vendor sales. The Stripe Connect application
fee now defaults to zero in code and in the Terraform variable for both environments, with
tests holding it there.

**Why.** DEC-009 gave the platform a cut of every sale. The only vendor who has ever paid for
this stays for two stated reasons: it is cheaper than the alternatives, and it takes no
commission on checkouts. Those cannot both be true. Taking nothing per sale is also the one
thing a marketplace structurally cannot match, since commission is its entire revenue model,
and the vendors we are aiming at are currently paying 20 to 42 percent of a first order
elsewhere. Revenue is the subscription instead. Recorded as DEC-014.

The code default alone would not have held: `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT` comes from a Terraform
variable that defaulted to `"5"` in both prod and staging, so the environment would have
overridden it.

The mechanism stays in place and an explicit percentage is still honoured, so the decision is
reversible without code. It just cannot come back by accident.

**Testing.** All gates green: typecheck, lint, 280 tests, 5 acceptance scenarios, coverage.
Mutation checked through both doors that could reintroduce a fee: restoring the code default
to `'5'` turned it red, and restoring the Terraform default to `"5"` turned it red separately.
Both restored to green.

author: andymai
body: Answers a user request: design an organizer in the layout planner and export it as a single bin with dividers, instead of designing each bin individually. They were round-tripping through Bento3D to get there. Behind the `merge_bins_to_design` labs flag (experimental). ## How it works A layout layer and a `CompartmentConfig` describe the same structure from opposite ends: rectangles tiling a uniform grid. `planMergedBin` converts one into the other, saves a design, and opens the designer on it, so labels, wall patterns, bed splitting and every export format come along without reimplementing any of them. - **Scope**: the selection when there is one, the active layer otherwise. Entry points are the multi-select context menu and a header button (the header covers the whole-layer case, which a selection-scoped menu cannot reach). - **Non-destructive**: the layout is never modified. No CQRS command, no undo entry. - **Cell size is the GCD of every bin edge on that axis**, so whole-unit layouts stay at one column per unit rather than burning two. Selections needing more than `MAX_COMPARTMENT_GRID` (12) rows or columns are refused with the numbers involved. - **Labels carry across** as `compartmentTexts`, remapped in lockstep with the renumbered cells, and turn on label tabs. No labels means no tabs. - **Height takes the tallest bin**, which is only meaningful because the merge is scoped to a single layer — `bin.height` is measured from that layer's own base plane. - Gridfinity base by default, with a flat-bottom toggle for a plain drawer insert. Split connectors turn on automatically when the piece overruns the print bed, checked per axis against `printBedDepth`. ## The constraint that shaped this The original plan used a `cellMask` so a ragged selection could keep its exact footprint. A spike found that **a masked bin exports with no dividers and no label tabs at all**: `featuresStage` runs only builders declaring `supportsCellMask`, and neither `compartmentWallsFeature` nor `labelTabsFeature` does. No error, no warning. The existing L/T-shape coverage in `compartmentBuilder.scenario.manifold.test.ts` passes *because* of this — an undivided shell is trivially watertight, so those tests confirm manifoldness while the compartments they pass in are inert. So the merge never emits a `cellMask`. A ragged selection squares off to its bounding box and the uncovered cells become their own compartments (merged into maximal rectangles, not one per cell), with the count stated in the dialog before anything is written. Dropping the mask also raises the size ceiling from 10 to 16 grid units. ## Drive-by fixes Both are what made the limitation look supported: - `pipeline/context.ts` claimed masked bins "still use the additive-fuse path" and pointed at a skipped `"polygon-mask gap"` scenario that does not exist in this repo. - The masked cases in the manifold suite now say their compartments are inert, so nobody reads them as evidence dividers survive a mask. `compartmentBuilder.scenario.polygonGap.test.ts` locks the real behaviour in, comparing triangle counts within a run so it stays kernel-agnostic. Its first test is a positive control proving the rectangular path genuinely honours both features — without it, the other three would pass vacuously. ## Verification - Full suite: 21,670 passed, 0 failures - `pnpm quality`: 0 errors - All four i18n gates pass; 15 keys across 15 locales ## Known limits - Rectangular footprints only, per the above. Giving `compartmentWallsFeature` and `labelTabsFeature` polygon support is the follow-up their own code comment anticipates, and label-tabs-on-masks is where the #1753 T-junction bug lived. - One height for the whole piece. Per-compartment floors would force the additive divider path. - The 12-cell ceiling will block half-bin layouts past 6 units wide. If that turns out common, raising `MAX_COMPARTMENT_GRID` with `BASE_TIMEOUT_MS` is the lever #1871 measured but chose not to pull. --- ## Summary by cubic Merge a selection of bins or an entire layer into one printable insert with dividers and carried-over labels, saved as a bin design and opened in the designer. Now shows a plan-view preview of the compartments in the merge dialog; scope is explicit per entry point and requires at least two bins. - **New Features** - Behind `merge_bins_to_design`: merge selection (context menu) or whole layer (header overflow); single-layer only. - Rectangular footprint; gaps become compartments; labels map to `compartmentTexts`. - Uses tallest bin height; grid cell size is the GCD of edges; rejects grids over 12 rows/cols and any scope with fewer than 2 bins. - Gridfinity base by default; optional flat-bottom insert; auto split connectors if it overruns the print bed. - Non-destructive: layout stays unchanged; design is saved then opened in the designer. Mobile menu supported. - Merge dialog adds a footprint-proportional plan view of compartments, built from the same `cells`; gap compartments are distinguished. - **Bug Fixes** - Scoped the merge to its entry point (no global inference), preventing a stray selection from hijacking the whole-layer action. - Blocked single-bin “merges”; dialog now names its scope and counts gap compartments inside the total; replaced raw checkbox with `CheckboxRow`. - Kept the merge dialog open on a failed save; it now closes only after a successful save. - Corrected docs and pipeline comments about masked bins dropping dividers/tabs; added `compartmentBuilder.scenario.polygonGap.test.ts` and updated manifold tests to reflect real masked behavior. Written for commit 457015f3090183dd7ad4ddf8e4971a8b2926e760. Summary will update on new commits.

Closes #70

## Summary
- add durable free text and sticky-note overlay kinds with bounded nested `Y.Text` bodies, world geometry, optional semantic anchors, and orphan fallback
- apply incremental local-human edits with composition-local IME drafts, relative-position commits, per-peer undo, and same-note CRDT convergence
- support select, edit, move, resize/wrap, color, duplicate, delete, z-order, keyboard operation, and an accessible semantic overlay list
- create notes at the measured unobscured viewport center and clearly label them as ArielCharts overlays excluded from Mermaid export
- normalize concurrent/offline text overflow to one UTF-8-safe authoritative Yjs state explicitly broadcast to every replica and persisted
- preserve Mermaid source/copy/export byte-for-byte across Flowchart, Sequence, ER, and generic Mermaid families

## Exact-head evidence
Head: 8d4bcdf21bab4222584a26c248a229c363a0d03b
Tree: 9ee474c350d455e13a8fbf3d381e1c51417501a2

- shared build: passed

- production build: passed
- protected collaboration E2E: passed
- workspace UX E2E: 39/39 passed on the UI/runtime head; final delta is server-only repair fanout
- diff check: passed

## Review
Broad review closed IME peer-edit deletion, offline overflow replica forks, and offscreen fixed-point creation. Focused review then exposed observer-delta truncation during normalized repair; the final path suppresses that partial observer fanout and explicitly sends the complete repaired state to sender and peers. Real WebSocket tests prove sender/peer/server/reload convergence with bounded fanout. No P0/P1/P2 findings remain.

## Architecture
Annotations remain versioned overlay objects independent of Mermaid source. Their bodies are nested `Y.Text`; local draft/composition and selection stay browser-local. Overlay history snapshots project safe plain text and reconstruct `Y.Text` on restore. No raw HTML or arbitrary embeds are accepted.

author: gyuminlee-repo
body:
릴리스 절차 문서에 두 가지를 넣었다. 2026-08-11 에 v0.16.21 라벨 경합으로 개번·리베이스를 한 바퀴 돈
사례에서 나온 것이다(#297 을 닫고 #298 로 다시 올려 머지).

## 1. 라벨 경합 판정을 API 실측으로 바꿨다

`git fetch --all` 후 `git log origin/main` 만 보고 라벨이 비어 있다고 판정하면 안 된다. 그 조합이 실제로
원격 진행분을 놓쳤다. 로컬은 `origin/main` 을 `4c07cdf5` 로 보았고, 원격은 이미 `403280a4`(#296,
v0.16.21 선점)였다.

증상을 문서에 그대로 적었다. 로컬에서 `git merge-base --is-ancestor` 가 통과하고 `git merge-tree` 가
충돌 0 을 내는데 `gh pr merge` 만 `Pull Request has merge conflicts` 로 거부되는 형태다. 이때 로컬이
낡은 것이므로 API 를 믿는다. PR 을 닫고 다시 열어도 해소되지 않는다는 것도 적었다(mergeability 재계산
문제로 오진하기 쉬워 실제로 그 경로를 한 번 시도했다).

## 2. 경합이 확인된 뒤의 복구 순서를 5단계로 적었다

라벨만 올려서는 안 된다. CHANGELOG 최상단과 로케일 10개의 `whatsNewDialog` 가 같은 자리를 놓고 충돌한다.
백업 브랜치 보존, 코드 커밋만 리베이스, 새 라벨로 CHANGELOG 재작성, 9개 로케일 재스탬프, force-push 대신
새 브랜치 순서다. 특히 **코드 커밋과 릴리스 메타 커밋을 분리해 두면 리베이스가 충돌 없이 끝난다**는 점을
적었다. 한 커밋에 섞으면 그 리베이스가 로케일 충돌을 그대로 떠안는다.

`careful-check.sh` 가 force-push 를 차단하며 우회하지 않는다는 것과, 닫힌 PR 의 head 브랜치는 자동 삭제
대상이 아니어서 직접 지워야 한다는 것도 같이 넣었다.

## 곁들여 정정한 것

`version-sync` 검사 대상이 3곳이라고 적혀 있었으나 실제로는 6곳이다(`pyproject.toml`,
`src-tauri/Cargo.lock`, `kuma_core/shared/version.py` 추가). 손으로 맞추지 말고 `vX.Y.Z:` 제목 커밋으로
`scripts/sync-version.sh` post-commit 훅이 쓰게 하라는 지시를 붙였다. 매니페스트를 먼저 손으로 올리면
`gen-whatsnew.mjs` 가 "CHANGELOG 최신 섹션이 현재 버전을 언급하지 않는다" 며 거부하는데, 이번에 실제로
그 순서로 한 번 막혔다.

## 검증

문서 전용 변경이다. 제목에 `vX.Y.Z:` 를 쓰지 않아 `scripts/sync-version.sh` 가 매니페스트를 끌어올리지
않은 것을 확인했다(`version-sync` 여전히 0.16.22 aligned, working tree 깨끗). 추가한 줄에 em dash 0.

author: jrmoulckers
body:
## Summary

#843 shipped in #845 and immediately paid for itself: the very first job summary named four skips, and **all four were false diagnoses**. Three claimed "No seeded database" in a job whose own log reports `3 recipes (1 adaptation), 3 versions, 7 timeline events` seeded.

This PR fixes the four, and drops `EXPECTED_SKIPS` from 4 to 0.

## The root cause: #775 destroyed the helper's oracle

`gotoSeededRecipe` treated `status !== 200` as "no database". Measured against a fresh `postgres:16-alpine` with a production build:

| path | status | title | recipe content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/recipes/nonnas-sunday-gravy` | 200 | `Heirloom · Family recipes, kept alive.` | **absent** |
| `/recipes/home-cook/nonnas-sunday-gravy` | 200 | `Nonna's Sunday Gravy · Heirloom` | present |
| `/recipes/does-not-exist-zzz` | 200 | `Heirloom · Family recipes, kept alive.` | absent |

Two facts, both contradicting the helper's docstring:

1. **The flat legacy path does not redirect.** The docstring claimed it "now 308s to the canonical one (#666)". It renders the not-found page, byte-equivalently to a slug that never existed.
2. **Status is not an oracle for existence anywhere in `(main)`** — that is #775, pinned by #841.

So the helper returned a **non-null** path pointing at the not-found page, and every caller then failed against the wrong document and blamed the database.

Fixed by resolving through `/sitemap.xml` — the app's own canonical statement of what exists, unpaginated, and free of any hardcoded cook slug — then confirming with the recipe's `h1`. Both docstring claims corrected in place.

## The other two skips

**`share-print.spec.ts` pre-dates #81.** `ShareButton` lives inside `<RecipeActionsMenu>`, a Radix `Popover` whose content is absent from the DOM until opened. The test skipped on "Share control not rendered" — meaning **deleting Share entirely would have kept this test green**. It now opens the overflow menu and asserts.

**`authoring.spec.ts` waited for a URL shape #666 removed** — single-segment `/recipes/<slug>`. It burned its full 15 s timeout every run, then blamed the database. Now completes in **1.8 s**.

## Fixing the guards unmasked a real race

With the skips repaired, `offline.spec.ts` failed for the first time:

```
Received string: "Rested overnight 1786432900282"
```

`co-creator.spec.ts:334` overwrites the first step of the **shared** seeded recipe that `offline.spec.ts:97` asserted on, and the two run in parallel on CI. The defect has existed since #776 and was invisible solely because the broken helper skipped before reaching the assertion.

Fixed by capturing the step title online and comparing it offline. Not circular: one render came over the network and the other from the service-worker cache, which is precisely the property under test.

## A vacuous guard is worse than a missing one

A missing test announces itself as a gap. These four announced themselves as *satisfied preconditions* — and one of them fired on exactly the condition it exists to catch, phrased as housekeeping. Skip reasons are prose, and prose is the weakest artifact class in this repo: nothing checks it, and a false diagnosis in it reads as established fact to the next person.

## Why a zero baseline is safe

`serial` mode cascades skips when an earlier test fails. That cannot produce a spurious failure here, because a cascade only occurs on a run that is **already red**. Documented at the constant.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- [x] `format:check` · `lint` · `typecheck` · `copy:check` · `audit:ci` — all exit 0
- [x] `pnpm test` — **3436/3436 across 340 files**
- [x] `db:generate` + `git diff --exit-code -- drizzle` — no drift
- [x] `check:bundle` — all tracked routes within budget
- [x] E2E on a clean seed, serial: **15 passed / 4 skipped → 16 passed / 0 skipped**; each of the four passes in isolation
- [x] **Confirmed in CI, not just locally.** This PR's E2E job reports `E2E skip check (#843): 0 skipped of 23`, against `main` at `eb5a7350` reporting `4 skipped of 23` from the same script. That is the check added by #843 doing the job it was written for, on its first real subject.

## Known, and not caused here

`co-creator.spec.ts` › "a co-creator edit is visible under both namespaces" times out at 120 s on "save changes". Verified pre-existing rather than assumed — it reproduces **identically with every change in this PR stashed**, and it appears on `main` at `e8cfcaa3` (`1 flaky`, same test, same timeout) before this branch existed.

I first wrote this up as "Windows-environmental". **That was wrong and this PR''s own CI falsified it**: it flaked on Linux CI here too, passing on retry. It is a genuine flake in that spec, not a platform artifact, and it is now more visible because the suite does real work — `main` runs E2E in **35.8 s with 4 skipped**, this branch in **2.9 m with 0 skipped**. The old runtime was fast because four tests were doing nothing.

Not fixed here: it is a different defect in a file this PR does not touch, and folding it in would mix a flake investigation into a skip fix. Recorded on #849.

`co-creator.spec.ts` still mutates shared demo content. It should own a dedicated fixture recipe via `seed-e2e.ts`, the way #783 gave the e2e identity its own user. Recorded on #849 as follow-up rather than expanded into this PR.

## Issues

Closes #849

author: wmadden-electric
body:
Composer's `deploy` command does its real work by running `alchemy` — a full-screen, interactive, terminal-owning program. Today no engine command can express that. This is what it looks like after this change:

```ts
const child = await ctx.spawn({
  command: alchemyBin,
  args: ["deploy", stackFile, "--yes", "--stage", stage],
  env: containerEnv,
});
if (child.signal !== null) return exitWithChildStatus(child); // Ctrl-C: abort, not failure
if (child.exitCode !== 0) {
  return exitWithChildStatus(child, {
    nextActions: [reproduceHint(stackFile, stage)],
  });
}
present(readDeploymentResult()); // the handler picks up after the child
```

While the child runs, the user is talking to alchemy, not to us: its output arrives unframed on the real stdio, Ctrl-C reaches it natively from the terminal, and when it exits the handler resumes with `{exitCode, signal}` in hand — free to print a summary, error structurally, or exit with the child's code verbatim.

## The decision

The engine gains one affordance for commands whose work is performed by another program: `ctx.spawn`, a terminal handoff.

- **The child owns the terminal.** Inherited stdio, same process group (shared console on Windows), no detach — the terminal delivers Ctrl-C to the child exactly as if it were run directly. The engine's job during the window is to *not interfere*: it records signals rather than acting on them, forwards SIGTERM (which has no native path to the child), always outlives the child, and on child exit replays what the user pressed into its normal ladder — one Ctrl-C aborts `ctx.signal` so handler cleanup runs; a second escalates. Programmatic aborts terminate the child with TERM → 5s grace → KILL.
- **Nothing interleaves.** Engine commentary reported during a live child is buffered and flushed after it exits; presenting or settling mid-child is a construction error, as is a second concurrent spawn.
- **Exit codes pass through honestly.** `exitWithChildStatus` settles the run with the child's code verbatim — including codes the engine reserves for itself — through the same settlement path server commands already use, because a foreign program's exit status is not a statement in this CLI's code space. A signal-killed child settles 128+signal. Commands that may spawn reject `--json` at parse time: delegated terminal output cannot be framed, and pretending otherwise would corrupt the stream mid-run.
- **Credentials are injected, never handled.** A command declares that its child needs the platform session; the engine resolves it and sets `PRISMA_SERVICE_TOKEN` / `PRISMA_WORKSPACE_ID` in the child's environment — the same variables every Prisma tool already reads, so a child that is itself a Prisma tool authenticates with zero wiring. Handler code never sees token material. A session expiring within five minutes refuses the run up front with a re-auth hint rather than launching a deploy that will die mid-flight. This required one narrow, documented exception to the credential-manager rule that the engine never reads the credential storage itself — the single call site is the spawn path, recorded in the design doc against the current (rev 6) surface.
- **Spawning is a `Runtime` seam.** The engine never imports `node:child_process`; the bin supplies the adapter, and the test harness substitutes a scripted fake that records the invocation (env *keys*, never values). The real-child test suite drives a trivial fixture program through a genuine engine host process to prove the things fakes can't: group-native Ctrl-C delivery, unframed passthrough, the kill ladder, and the engine outliving its child.

## How it lands

This PR is the engine leg of the Composer-adoption slice, complete and reviewable on its own: the affordance is generic (no composer knowledge) and fully tested, including a real-child suite driven through a genuine engine host process. Composer's command family (built on `ctx.spawn`) lands in the composer repo against this engine; mounting that family in the `prisma` bin follows as its own PR. The slice contract, inventory, and dispatch plan ride along under `.drive/projects/prisma-cli-v8/`.

## Alternatives considered

- **A declarative "delegated command" kind** (no handler at all): rejected — composer's commands have real work on both sides of the child (config evaluation and preflight before; result reading and summaries after). A kind with nowhere to write code cannot express the actual commands.
- **Signal forwarding with a detached child**: rejected for native delivery — detaching removes the child from the terminal's foreground group, making forwarding the only delivery path and re-creating on POSIX the problem Windows already has. Same-group spawning lets the terminal do its job and needs no forwarding machinery for Ctrl-C at all.
- **Letting commands read TTY state and spawn directly**: rejected on standing ruling — interactivity policy and process management are engine concerns; hand-rolled spawns are how the legacy CLI accumulated three incompatible exit-code schemes.

author: s-heppner
body:
Previously, the SDK had no logo in its documentation. The original PyI40AAS logo was left behind when the project moved to the Eclipse Foundation, so the README carried no visual identity. This change restores it for recognition value.

The logo is taken from the archived ACPLT PyI40AAS repository and added as `etc/logo.svg`, stripped of the Inkscape and sodipodi editor attributes, including an export path that leaked the original author's home directory. The CC0 dedication and the attribution to Michael Thies are kept.

The `README.md` shows the logo centered above the title. GitHub draws a full-width rule under every `h1`, which would cut straight through a logo placed beside the heading, so the logo goes above it instead. The title is written as an `<h1 align="center">` tag rather than as a Markdown heading, because centering needs the `align` attribute.

A separate dark variant of the logo is not needed, as it stays legible on both the light and the dark GitHub theme.

Fixes #230

## 实现范围（按 issue 讨论中维护者收窄后的方案）

- [x] `RemoteRef` 增加 `via: Option<RouteSnapshot>`（profile 名、user、host、port；`serde(default)` 兼容旧 session 文件）：创建时写入、每次（重）打开经 `claim_remote` 时用 config 实时值刷新；显示时 profile 还在则优先用实时值。快照只服务标签，不参与相等性/哈希（`RemoteRef` 手动实现 `PartialEq`/`Hash`，忽略 `via`），否则刷新会把一个条目劈成两个
- [x] 删除 SSH 配置时**级联清除**引用它的远程工作区条目（单一动作，不做三选）：走 `forget_workspace`（`tree_sync::forget` + `WorkspaceStore::remove` + `release_unused_hosts`），**永不发 `WorkspaceRemove`**（链路活着时那会真删远端 pane）；持有活链路或正在连接中的条目排除——条目忘了会把活链路从还在用的窗口底下释放掉
- [x] 删除确认框报出端点（`user@host:port`）+ "将一并清除 N 个条目，不影响远端会话"；0 个关联条目时维持现状文案
- [x] 停泊态：路线缺失（`Profile` id 不在 config / `Alias` 不在 ssh config，同一谓词 `RemoteTarget::resolvable`）的条目不自动重试、不弹错误（`RemoteStatus::RouteLost`，supervisor tick 直接跳过）；行内动作 [移除条目][关闭] + "新建配置连上该机器后可在工作区列表中找回"
- [x] 标签 fallback：profile 实时值 → 快照 → "已删除的配置" 占位，任何分支**不落地裸 UUID**（含无快照的老条目）；supervisor 每 250ms 跑一次谓词，`~/.ssh/config` 解析按 mtime 缓存，不在 tick 上重复读盘

## 测试

纯函数（tty7-core）：

- 快照 serde 往返 + 无 `via` 字段的旧 session 文件兼容加载
- 路线可解析性谓词：`Profile` 悬空与 `Alias` 悬空同一判定
- 标签 fallback 任何分支不落地 UUID（钉住本 issue 的真正症状）
- 引用统计覆盖且仅覆盖该 profile 的条目

GUI（`#[gpui::test]`）：

- `claim_remote` 创建时写快照、profile 改名后再打开刷新快照且条目不重复、profile 删除后再打开保留最后的名字
- 级联统计恰好等于被删 profile 的无链路条目
- **级联路径不发 `WorkspaceRemove`**：经 machine mirror 观测（它在 op 上线前一定会记录）——`forget_workspace` 后 mirror 仍列着该工作区（远端会话不动），`delete_workspace` 后消失（对照组）

CHANGELOG + docs/remote（workspaces 新增 "Deleting a profile" 一节，ssh 页指向它）已同步。`cargo test --locked`、`cargo fmt --check`、host-boundary 检查全绿。

## Summary

- extract PSim slave CLI parsing into package-private `SlaveCommandLineParser` and immutable `SlaveLaunchArguments`
- extract deterministic host/port/thread resolution and MATSim config mutation into package-private `SlaveConfigPreparer`
- add nine characterization tests covering precedence, fallbacks, diagnostics, and config side effects
- ratchet the PSim suite to 88 tests, 48.29% line coverage, and 46.39% branch coverage

## Design decisions

- Missing and unreadable config termination remains in `SlaveControler`; extracted components do not call `System.exit`.
- Legacy diagnostics and fallback values are preserved, including the hard-coded `12345` message and `MasterControler` help wording.
- Raw numeric option values remain strings until config preparation so invalid-value fallbacks retain their existing behavior.
- Socket retry, object-stream construction order, handshake decoding, memory exchange, strategy substitution, scenario loading, and MATSim runtime construction remain in `SlaveControler`.
- All new types are package-private and no public API is expanded.

- Blocking connection and wire-protocol responsibilities intentionally remain in the controller for the next characterized bundle.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Fixes #7568

Showcase **authoring** fix. The global-filter engine is untouched — it did exactly what the metadata told it to.

## What was wrong

`showcase_ops_dashboard` declared its dashboard-scoped filter as a bare `field: 'status'` carrying the **task** vocabulary (`backlog / todo / in_progress / in_review / done`), and the project-bound widgets declared no `filterBindings`. A widget with no bindings inherits a dashboard filter on its own object's like-named field, and `showcase_project` also has a `status` — with a disjoint vocabulary (`planned / active / on_hold / completed / cancelled`).

So the inherited binding was **field-valid and value-empty**: the query was well-formed, the backend answered `200 OK`, and the widget rendered a zero. `packages/lint`'s `dashboard-filter-field-unknown` rule cannot see this — it checks that the effective field *exists*, which it does.

## Which fix, and why

Both admissible options were considered:

| | shape | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A | per-widget `filterBindings` on the project widgets | **chosen** |
| B | scope the filter with `scope: 'widget'` + `targetWidgets` | rejected |

**A, for three reasons.**

1. **It is the mechanism this repo has measured working.** Revenue Pulse maps `region` on the invoice widgets to `sales_region` on the account widgets through `filterBindings`, verified on the wire and in the echoed SQL in the same QA run. `targetWidgets` is described in `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts` as the **legacy** allow-list that `filterBindings` overrides, and the browser bundle that would implement `scope: 'widget'` is not vendored here (`packages/console/dist` is absent) — so option B could not be driven, only asserted. Demoing an unmeasured capability in the showcase is precisely what Prime Directive #10 forbids.
2. **It is what the Studio widget inspector authors** (objectui#2586), so it is the shape a showcase reader should be taught.
3. **The two status vocabularies are disjoint**, so there is no project field to re-target onto. The honest binding is an opt-out, not a mapping.

The filter is also given the explicit name `task_status`. A bare `status` made the opt-out read as "ignore *project* status" rather than "this control is about *tasks*"; with the name, the metadata says what the filter governs and every widget it does **not** govern says so on its own line. `dateRange` stays inherited everywhere on purpose — projects do carry `created_at`, so that filter is meaningful on both sides.

## A fifth widget

The issue names four. `table_spend` is a fifth project-bound widget with the identical defect; it is fixed here too. It went unnoticed because an emptied *table* reads as "no data", not as a broken filter — a zeroed KPI tile at least looks wrong.

## Verification — driven, not read

The dashboard renderer reads published metadata, resolves each dashboard filter to a field **per widget**, ANDs it with the widget's own `filter`, and issues one `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` per widget. A harness did exactly that against a live showcase backend (`pnpm dev -- --fresh`, seeded data, sqlite), reading the metadata from `GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/showcase_ops_dashboard`.

**Scope of the drive, stated plainly:** the per-widget resolution is transcribed from `effectiveFilterField` / `dashboardFilterDefs` in `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts` — this repo's own executable mirror of objectui's `resolveBoundField`. Everything downstream of that (metadata → wire → SQL → number) is the real server. The browser bundle itself is not in this repo and was not exercised; the objectui half remains a checklist item (`dashboards.global-filters-rescope`).

Widget totals, `dateRange` held unset in every capture so the status selection is the only variable:

| widget | dataset | before: pristine | before: `status=in_review` | after: pristine | after: `task_status=in_review` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kpi_active_projects` | project | 2 | **0** | 2 | **2** |
| `kpi_at_risk` | project | 1 | **0** | 1 | **1** |
| `kpi_total_budget` | project | 1090000 | **0** | 1090000 | **1090000** |
| `col_health` | project | 5 | **0** | 5 | **5** |
| `table_spend` | project | 5 | **0** | 5 | **5** |
| `kpi_awaiting_review` | task | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `bar_status` | task | 10 | 2 | 10 | 2 |
| `donut_priority` | task | 10 | 2 | 10 | 2 |
| `line_created` | task | 10 | 2 | 10 | 2 |

The SQL the server echoed tells the same story. Before, under a selection:

```
kpi_active_projects: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" WHERE (status = $1 AND status = $2)
kpi_at_risk:         SELECT COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" WHERE (health = $1 AND status = $2)
col_health:          SELECT health AS "health", COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" WHERE status = $1 GROUP BY health
```

After, under the same selection — the project side carries no `status` predicate at all, and the task side still composes both filters:

```
kpi_active_projects: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" WHERE status = $1
kpi_at_risk:         SELECT COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" WHERE health = $1
col_health:          SELECT health AS "health", COUNT(*) AS "project_count" FROM "showcase_project" GROUP BY health
kpi_awaiting_review: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "task_count" FROM "showcase_task" WHERE (status = $1 AND status = $2)
bar_status:          SELECT status AS "status", COUNT(*) AS "task_count" FROM "showcase_task" WHERE status = $1 GROUP BY status
```

The QA checklist's Delivery Operations clause — "the global status filter composes with per-widget filters" — still holds, on the side where it is coherent.

## The test pins the consequence, not the key

`examples/app-showcase/test/dashboard-filter-vocabulary.test.ts`, generic over every showcase dashboard:

1. **every value a global filter offers must be a value its effective field can hold** on each widget it reaches — otherwise that selection returns zero rows by construction;
2. **a filter must still reach at least one widget** — otherwise the repair for (1) is "opt everybody out", which leaves an inert control on the header bar;
3. the #7568 case named in intent terms: `task_status` governs the task widgets and no project widget.

**Reverse verification**, direction predicted before running: revert `ops-dashboard.dashboard.ts` to `main` and (1) and (3) go red, (2) stays green — the broken filter *did* reach widgets, it just could not answer them. Measured exactly that. (1) named all five affected widgets individually, including `table_spend`:

```
showcase_ops_dashboard > kpi_active_projects: filter "status" binds to showcase_project.status,
whose values are [planned, active, on_hold, completed, cancelled] — selecting
[backlog, todo, in_progress, in_review, done] can only ever return zero rows.
```

Restored, all three green.

## Gates run locally

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase verify` (= `os validate` + `tsc --noEmit` + `vitest run`) — green; **18 files / 171 tests passed**. The `validate` step is what runs `validate-widget-bindings`, the rule family this card sits next to.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on both changed files — clean.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` — OK, 7046 files scanned.

No changeset: `@objectstack/example-showcase` is `private: true` and absent from the `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`, so this PR releases nothing. Labelled `skip-changeset`.

No `packages/spec` change was needed, and no platform behaviour was altered.

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary
- recursively unwrap zero-dimensional NumPy wrappers before validating goal-state numeric parameters
- reject booleans and non-scalar arrays even when hidden inside object-backed 0-D arrays
- guard against self-referential 0-D wrappers instead of recursing/coercing indefinitely
- add regression coverage at the model scorer, transition-matrix helper, and benchmark-config entry points

## Bug
The existing validation checked only the outer array. A 0-D object array containing another NumPy array could therefore bypass both the boolean and scalar checks. NumPy then coerced a nested boolean to `1.0` (and a nested singleton array to its scalar value), contradicting the validator's explicit contract to reject bool and array-like parameters.

## Validation
- reproduced the pre-fix coercion locally with NumPy (`nested True -> 1.0`, nested singleton array -> scalar value)
- syntax-compiled the modified source and focused test module
- added focused pytest regressions; repository CI should exercise the full suite on this PR

No existing open PR found for this goal-state nested-scalar validation hole.
