## 왜

PR #1276 은 "공개 화면에서 AI Planner / AI itinerary / CocoTrip AI 가 서비스 행위자로 남지 않을 것"을 목표로 했다. 머지 후 라이브 4언어 읽기전용 검증(`PROD-VERIFY-1276-FINDINGS-2026-08-11`, origin/main `eade4d0e`)에서 **목표 미달 3곳**이 남아 있었다. 전부 #1276 이 건드리지 않은 문자열이다.

| | 화면 | 라이브 문구 (4언어 전부) |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | `/map` 로그아웃·빈 상태 | `AI 일정의 경로는 계정에 저장돼 있어요` · `Your AI itinerary routes are saved…` · `AIプランのルートは…` · `AI行程的路线已…` |
| F2 | `/region/:id` SEO 본문 + FAQ | `AI 일정 만들기 — …자동으로 짜 줍니다` · `AI itinerary — get a plan…` (FAQ 는 JSON-LD 로 구글에도 나감) |
| F3 | `/tours` 카드 배지 | `AI-CURATED` ×2 (4언어 모두 영어 원문) |

## 무엇을

### F1 · F2 — 문구 (ko/en/ja/zh)

AI 를 행위자로 쓰지 않고, `docs/DESIGN-EDITORIAL-CONCIERGE.md` §5 "Name the capability, not the implementation" 과 `pageMeta.planner.description`(#1275/#1276 이 세운 포지셔닝)을 따라 **한국 현지 데이터 · 실제 지하철/버스/도보 경로 · 도시/날짜/여행 조건 → 일정 자동작성**으로 바꿨다. 라벨은 `nav.planner` SSOT(`여행 플래너` / `Trip planner` / `旅行プランナー` / `行程规划`).

🔴 **가격 `$9.90` · 무료 개요 · 취소/환불/포함사항 등 결제·상품·법무 의미와 숫자는 한 글자도 바꾸지 않았다.** 회귀 테스트가 4언어 각각에 대해 이 문자열들을 잠근다.

### F3 — 배지 (근본원인)

#1276 은 `TourCard` 안에 `UNGROUNDED_BADGE_TAGS = new Set(['Popular', 'Best Value'])` 를 뒀다. `AI-Curated` 가 빠진 게 표면 원인이고, 근본원인은 필터의 **위치와 형태** 두 가지다.

1. **위치** — 필터가 카드 컴포넌트 안에 있었다. 같은 배지를 그리는 두 번째 카드(`MobileHomeV2` Smart Picks, 라우트 `/preview/mobile-home`, prod 번들 포함·DEV 게이트 없음)는 아무 필터 없이 `tour.tags[0]` 을 그대로 찍고 있었다.
2. **형태** — 정확 문자열 `Set` 이라 `AI Curated` / `ai-curated` / `Best  Value` 같은 변형은 그냥 통과한다. 태그 값은 상품 데이터와 어드민 입력(`ProductEditor/BasicInfoTab`)에서 온다.

→ `src/data/tours.ts` 에 `publicBadgeTag()`(소문자·비영숫자 제거 후 비교)를 두고 **두 카드가 같이 쓴다**.

**태그 값 자체는 지우지 않는다.** `/tours` 필터 칩·검색·어드민 편집은 그대로 동작한다 — 공개 카드 배지에서만 뺀다. Firestore 상품 데이터와 어드민 운영 데이터는 읽지도 쓰지도 마이그레이션하지도 않았다(어드민 태그 목록은 존재 여부만 읽기 감사).

### 배선 추적 중 같이 발견해 고친 것

`/preview/mobile-home` 의 meta description 이 `AI travel planner, private tours & charter across Korea` 였다. 홈(`/`)의 같은 문구는 #1276 이 정리했는데 이 라우트만 남아 있었다. 같은 포지셔닝으로 맞췄다.

## 회귀 테스트 — 구현 문자열이 아니라 렌더 결과

신규 `tests/unit/public-ai-actor-copy.component.test.tsx` (27 케이스). **F3 은 기존의 구현 문자열 검사(`UNGROUNDED_BADGE_TAGS = new Set([...])` 정규식)를 그대로 통과했었다** — 상수는 맞는데 그 상수를 안 쓰는 카드가 있으면 화면에는 그대로 나온다. 그래서 화면에 뭐가 찍히는지로 잠근다.

- **TourCard** — `AI-Curated`/`Popular`/`Best Value` 및 대소문자·공백·하이픈·언더스코어 변형이 배지로 안 나오는지, 정당한 `History`/`Nature`/`Multi-City` 는 그대로 남는지, 배지가 사라져도 제목·가격은 남는지, 그리고 **실제 상품 목록 전체를 렌더**해 AI 배지 0 인지(라이브 재현)
- **RegionSeoInfo** — 4언어 본문 + FAQ JSON-LD 에 AI 행위자 표기 0, 한국 현지 데이터/실제 경로/여행 조건 의미 유지, `$9.90`·무료 개요 문구 보존, 플래너 미대상 도시(else 분기)까지
- **MapPage** — 로그아웃 / 플랜 0건 두 분기를 4언어로 실제 렌더

기존 두 테스트는 새 동작에 맞춰 갱신했다(`public-promise-truthfulness` 의 TourCard 블록은 구현 정규식 → 실제 반환값, `region-seo-info` 의 분기 판별 문구 교체).

**red 증거** — 이 브랜치 테스트를 origin/main 소스(`git stash push -- src`)로 돌리면 `24 failed | 77 passed`. 되돌리면 `101 passed`.

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | ok (tsc -b + vite build, exit 0) |
| `npm run test:unit` 전체 | **573 files · 7196 passed · 7 todo · 0 failed** |
| `npm run check:i18n` | PASS (4 locale × 2174 keys) |
| `node scripts/lint-mistake-patterns.mjs origin/main` | 202 OK · 0 warning · 0 violation |
| 변경파일 ESLint | **신규 오류 0** (before/after 동일 3건 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, 전부 내가 안 건드린 줄) |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| pre-push 5 checks | passed |

**로컬 preview 실물 검증 (read-only, 로그인·AI 호출·결제·운영 쓰기 0)** — `vite preview` + Playwright chromium, 390/768/1440 × ko/en/ja/zh × `/map`(로그아웃)·`/region/seoul`·`/tours` = **36 로드**

- HTTP 200 36/36 · pageerror **0** · console error **0** · 폰트 외 4xx/5xx **0**
- `scrollWidth > innerWidth` 가로 넘침 **0**
- AI 행위자 표기 **0** (en 은 단어 경계, ko/ja/zh 는 `AI` 그대로)
- 새 문구 4언어 전부 실제 렌더 확인 · `$9.90` 보존 확인
- 카드 배지 실측 전체 집합 = `NIGHT` / `NIGHT TOUR` / `NATURE` / `HISTORY` / `MULTI-CITY` — **`AI-CURATED`·`POPULAR`·`BEST VALUE` 0건**

## 남은 것 (이 PR 범위 밖)

- **P2 F4** — `/tours` 신뢰 배지 레일에서 `Weekdays 10am–6pm · English Support` 가 en 390px 첫 화면에 42%만 보임(#1276 이 만든 부작용, 가로 스크롤로 도달은 가능). 미수정.

- **P3 F8** — `/tours` 테마 필터에 `Popular / 인기 / 热门` 칩 잔존. 배지는 숨겼지만 필터 칩은 그대로 — 의도한 동작(태그 값 보존)이자 일관성 갭.
- **P3 F7/F9** — ko/ja/zh 영어 누출(`NIGHT`·`✓ Tolls` 등), `/region` 조사 붙임 공백(`서울 을`). 기존 결함, 이 PR 문구도 같은 보간 스타일을 유지했다.

author: jackalcooper
body:
## What changed

- add a per-runtime lifecycle gate with explicit idle/executing/destroying transitions
- enforce one execution owner, epoch-bound internal worker tokens, and owner/worker role separation
- make process reset one-shot for explicit executions and result creation owner-bound and quiescent
- preserve runtime state on lifecycle failures and document the ABI contract

## Why

Forgejo issue #59 identified that worker counts alone did not provide a stable execution barrier. Concurrent enters, resets, and result publication could observe ambiguous ownership and failure cleanup could implicitly destroy a runtime.

This is stack 1 of 2. It establishes the execution state machine; the follow-up layers arena pins and import/export/destroy linearization on top.

- `zig test native/term_runtime.zig -lc` — 36 tests passed

## Summary

Implements the reframed approach for #2715: expand the summary layer so frontends can consume pre-aggregated, JSON-serializable DataFrames instead of adding `return_data=True` to plot methods.

- Add **11 new `mmm.summary` methods**: `waterfall`, `channel_share_hdi`, `prior_predictive`, `residuals_over_time`, `residuals_distribution`, `prior_vs_posterior`, `saturation_scatterplot`, and sensitivity trio (`sensitivity_analysis`, `sensitivity_uplift`, `sensitivity_marginal`)
- Add **`BudgetSummaryFactory`** (`allocation_roas`, `contribution_over_time`) for stateless budget-sample summaries
- Add **`cv.summary`** (`MMMCVSummaryFactory`) with `predictions`, `param_stability`, `crps`
- Organize summary code in **`mmm/summary/`** package (mirrors `plotting/`): `factory.py`, `helpers.py`, `budget.py`, `cv.py`, `sensitivity.py`; `__init__.py` re-exports the public API
- Extract shared xarray utilities into **`xarray_utils.py`**; refactor matplotlib plot methods to use summary as single source of truth
- Extend **`plot_interactive`** with `waterfall()` and `channel_share()` backed by summary DataFrames

Target consumer API:

```python
records = mmm.summary.contributions().to_dict(orient="records")
```

Closes #2715.

## Package layout

```
pymc_marketing/mmm/summary/
  __init__.py       # MMMSummaryFactory, BudgetSummaryFactory, MMMCVSummaryFactory, helpers

  helpers.py        # shared computation + dataframe_to_json_records
  budget.py         # BudgetSummaryFactory
  cv.py             # MMMCVSummaryFactory
  sensitivity.py    # sensitivity_* summaries
```

Public imports are unchanged, e.g. `from pymc_marketing.mmm.summary import MMMSummaryFactory`.

author: nelljerram
body:
**Cherry-pick history**
- Pick onto **release-v3.32**: projectcalico/calico#13080

Two unit-test-discovery files were calling eventlet.monkey_patch() at module import time:

 - networking_calico/agent/dhcp_agent.py:22 (production code, but imported by test_dhcp_agent and test_subnet_watcher);
 - networking_calico/tests/test_fv_etcdutils.py:29 (the FV tests).

Either was enough on its own to contaminate the entire test process with eventlet.  Under that contamination, subunit's runner -- which writes binary subunit-protocol status messages to stdout via os.fdopen(fileno, 'wb', 0) -- ends up parked indefinitely in epoll_wait() on an empty FD set partway through `tox -e py38`.  Symptom: `make -C networking-calico tox-caracal` hangs forever after "_run_testr called".

A note on reproducibility: this hang started appearing reliably on my own laptop, _today_, despite the structural problem above having been latent in the repo for a long time.  I am confident I've not noticed a hang like this before today.  CI has continued to pass throughout; and rebooting my laptop (to eliminate any accumulated process / kernel / monitoring-agent state) did not change the behaviour -- the hang still reproduces from a clean boot.  We do not have a satisfying explanation for the timing trigger that made the latent pathology suddenly become a deterministic hang on one machine; venv contents, package versions, and freshly-checked-out upstream state were all investigated and none of them looked like an obvious cause.  The fix below addresses the root structural issue (module-level monkey_patch contaminating the test process), so we're unblocked regardless of what tipped the balance.

Untangling without breaking production:

 1. Move dhcp_agent's monkey_patch into a new wrapper module networking_calico/agent/dhcp_agent_main.py, and re-point the `calico-dhcp-agent` console_script in setup.py at it.  The wrapper does monkey_patch() before importing the dhcp_agent module, so every subsequent module-level import in dhcp_agent (etcd3gw, neutron, eventlet.event, eventlet.queue, ...) still happens under a fully patched interpreter in production -- identical effective behaviour to today.  Unit tests that just want to import CalicoDhcpAgent no longer trigger the patch.

 2. Gate test_fv_etcdutils' monkey_patch and the whole TestFVEtcdutils class behind CALICO_RUN_FV_TESTS=1.  These are FV tests that spawn a real etcd subprocess and require eventlet; they were never safe to autodiscover into the unit-test sweep.  Without the env var the module imports cleanly (no monkey_patch), and the class skips via @unittest.skipUnless.

 3. Provide a deterministic way to run the FV tests:
    - tox.ini grows a [testenv:fv] env that reuses the standard [testenv] config (deps, passenv), sets CALICO_RUN_FV_TESTS=1, and invokes the FV tests under unittest directly (not subunit / coverage).
    - Makefile grows `tox-fv` and `tox-fv-<release>` targets that mirror the existing `tox` / `tox-<release>` pattern, so e.g. `make tox-fv-caracal` runs the FV tests against caracal pins.
    - The Semaphore "OpenStack: Unit and FV tests (tox) on Caracal" job (which already named FV tests in its title but didn't run them) is extended to invoke both make targets sequentially: unit tests first (fast, gates the FV run on failure), then FV tests against the same .tox/py38 venv on the host.  Source in .semaphore/semaphore.yml.d/blocks/40-openstack.yml; .semaphore/semaphore.yml and .semaphore/semaphore-scheduled-builds.yml regenerated via `make gen-semaphore-yaml`.

After these changes:
 - `python -m subunit.run discover -t . networking_calico/tests` completes in seconds (was: indefinite hang).
 - `make tox-caracal` finishes cleanly.
 - `make tox-fv-caracal` runs the 4 FV tests in ~65s.
 - Production `calico-dhcp-agent` daemon behaviour is unchanged: the new wrapper monkey-patches before importing the agent module, so all module-level imports still happen under a patched interpreter.

author: macrozone
body:
## Why

Every pnpm caching mechanism catladder had lost its measurement. Each configuration below ran as jobs **in the same pipeline/run**, so they shared fleet conditions — an earlier cross-pipeline comparison was thrown away after the same job's cache throughput varied 3× between afternoons.

### node_modules cache — [gitlab 338067](https://git.panter.ch/manul/wea/food-2050/-/pipelines/338067)

| | restore | install | save | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| with node_modules cache (hit) | 169s | 6.4s | 1s | **176s** |
| store-only | 44s | 12.8s | 1s | **57s** |
| writer (hit + save) | 182s | 8.2s | 187s | **377s** |

1.29 GB / 348k files to save 6s of install.

### store cache — [gitlab 338153](https://git.panter.ch/manul/wea/food-2050/-/pipelines/338153) / [github](https://github.com/panter/food-2050-catladder-test/actions/runs/31539879149)

| | GitLab | GitHub |
|---|---|---|
| no cache at all | **35s / 50s** | 64s / 65s |
| store cache (hit) | 74s / 76s | **56s / 65s** |
| — restore | 53s / 54s | 21s / 25s |
| — install | 16.2s / 16.4s | 28s / 32s |

GitLab zips the store file by file (53s for 186k files); GitHub streams one zstd tarball (21-25s). Two effects compound on GitLab: slow cache transport *and* faster runners, so a cold install (30-42s) beats a warm restore.

### store inside docker images — [github](https://github.com/panter/food-2050-catladder-test/actions/runs/31543067266)

| | store copied in | no store | no store + in-layer rm |
|---|---|---|---|
| docker build | 339s / 146s | 27s | **25s** |
| in-image `--prod` install | 28.4s (`reused 441`) | **9.6s** (`downloaded 442`) | 10.8s |
| final image | **3.35 GB** | 0.73 GB | **0.66 GB** |

The store lands in a layer *below* `node_modules`, so pnpm cannot hardlink across the overlay boundary and copies every package — making the install slower than downloading it, while shipping the payload twice in a single-stage image.

## What

- `getYarnCache` / `getNodeModulesCache` return nothing for pnpm — pnpm projects generate no `cache:` blocks at all
- jobs install with plain `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; the `--store-dir` pointing at a project-local `.pnpm-store` is gone (nothing to cache, and nothing to leak into a docker context)
- the docker job no longer does `mkdir -p .pnpm-store` or `COPY .pnpm-store /app/.pnpm-store`
- the in-image prod install uses `--store-dir /tmp/pnpm-store` and `rm -rf`s it in the same `RUN`, so packages ship once
- yarn caching byte-identical

## Trade-off

CI now pulls dependencies from the registry on every install job (~50 per food-2050 pipeline). Worth a registry proxy if that load matters; it buys back roughly 2 minutes per reader job, 5 per writer, and ~2.7 GB per image.

## Verification

- 278 tests green; only the two pnpm example snapshots changed
- the store removal is validated in a real image: `node_modules` reads back identically to the store-copying variant (same 3000 files / 136,828,468 bytes, 0 unreadable, `@node-rs/argon2` natives present)

author: 78w8yz8kfr-spec
body:
## Worum es geht

Entnahme auf eine Baustelle und Rückgabe von dort ins Lager.

**Die Rückgabe verlor die Baustelle.** Die Entnahme konnte eine tragen, die Rückgabe nicht — im Journal stand dann eine Entnahme auf die Baustelle und daneben ein Zugang aus dem Nichts. Wer später fragte, was eine Baustelle wirklich verbraucht hat, bekam die ausgegebene Menge statt der verbauten: der Rest, der abends zurück ins Regal ging, fehlte in der Rechnung. Die Rückgabe trägt die Baustelle jetzt mit. Eine Umlagerung weiterhin nicht, die geht von Lager zu Lager.

**Die Auswahl war für den Falschen gebaut.** Sie kannte nur die Baustellen aus dem eigenen Tagesplan. Für den Monteur stimmt das, für den Lageristen nicht: der gibt Material für Baustellen heraus, auf denen er selbst nie steht, und sah deshalb überhaupt kein Auswahlfeld. `/api/v1/stock/contexts` liefert die laufenden Baustellen des Betriebs jetzt mit; die eigenen stehen oben, der Rest darunter. Abgeschlossene, abgebrochene und archivierte fehlen — auf sie soll nichts mehr gebucht werden.

**Die Wahl bleibt stehen.** Zwischen zwei Buchungen wie der Lagerplatz, denn wer eine Baustelle rüstet, bucht zehn Artikel nacheinander; sie jedesmal neu zu wählen wäre der sichere Weg zu Buchungen ohne Baustelle. Unsichtbar wird sie dadurch nicht: sie steht im Feld und noch einmal in der Bestätigung („Für Baustelle …" / „Zurück von Baustelle …"). Über einen Neustart der App trägt sie bewusst nicht.

## Änderungen

- `api/src/stock.mjs`: `loadSites()`, Baustellen im Lagerkontext
- `frontend/core/stock-management.js`: `BAUSTELLE_BUCHBAR`, `baustellenListe()`, `baustelleNochWaehlbar()`, Auswahlfeld mit zwei Gruppen und Richtungshinweis, Baustelle in der Bestätigung
- `frontend/core/stock-module.js`: Baustellen offline gemerkt, Wahl über `neuerVorgang()` weitergetragen, abgeschlossene Baustelle fällt aus dem Zustand
- `database/migrations/116_release_version_0_44_16.sql` samt Abnahmetest, der beide Richtungen wirklich bucht und nachrechnet
- Fassung 0.44.16, Zwischenspeicher `schaefchen-online-v98`, CHANGELOG, PROJECT_STATUS, Modulhandbuch, Demoseite

Keine Datenbankänderung: `stock_movements.construction_site_id` steht seit Migration 107.

## Geprüft

- SQL-Kette auf frisch aufgebauter Datenbank grün bis 116; der Abnahmetest bucht Entnahme 12 und Rückgabe 8 und prüft, dass vier Meter auf der Baustelle und 96 im Lager stehen — und rollt sich selbst zurück
- API: 185 Tests inkl. PostgreSQL-Integration, Abdeckung 89,60 / 75,97 / 95,47
- Frontend: 233 Tests, PWA-Smoke
- Im echten Chromium gegen eine laufende Datenbank: Auswahl zeigt beide laufenden Baustellen mit Nummer und nicht die abgeschlossene; Entnahme 12 m → „Für Baustelle Sanierung Rathaus", Bestand 100 → 88; Wahl übersteht den Weg über die Startseite; Rückgabe 8 m → „Zurück von Baustelle …", Bestand 96. Ohne Netz: Liste aus dem Gerätespeicher, Buchung mit `constructionSiteId` in der Warteschlange, bei Netzrückkehr nachgetragen und in der Datenbank bestätigt

author: darakhamia
body:
Follow-up to #806, which is merged. New branch off `master`, one commit.

## What the live page showed

The first production screenshot showed what the local stand-in could not: the GOO wordmark and the legal links sit on the column's real left edge, while the form is inset about 2rem to the right of them. The "Don't have an account? / Secured by Clerk" strip also still carries its own fill, spanning the full column width.

Measured off that screenshot: the footer strip spans the whole 400px column, and the form content sits ~38px inside it on each side. So the wordmark is where it should be — Clerk's own `card` padding is what moved the form.

## Why the previous pass did not catch it

`elements` classes are **appended** to Clerk's own classes, and Clerk paints with emotion, which injects into `<head>` *after* the app stylesheet. A plain utility of equal specificity therefore loses. Colour and type classes won anyway — which is why the theming looked correct in both themes — but box geometry and fills did not, so `card`'s padding and the footer's background survived being told otherwise.

## The fix

Tailwind v4's important modifier (`!` **suffix** — checked against this toolchain, not assumed) on exactly the properties that have to beat Clerk:

| Element | Marked | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cardBox` | `border-0! bg-transparent! shadow-none! px-0!` | outer box fill and frame |
| `card` | `border-0! bg-transparent! shadow-none! px-0! pt-0!` | the padding that caused the offset |
| `main` | `px-0!` | second possible carrier of the inset |
| `scrollBox` | `bg-transparent! shadow-none! px-0!` | third |
| `footer`, `footerAction` | `bg-transparent! border-0! px-0!` | the strip's own fill |

Horizontal padding is zeroed on **all** the boxes Clerk nests rather than guessing which one holds the inset — padding cannot go negative, so zeroing one that had none is a no-op, not an overshoot. In Clerk v6 the footer is a *sibling* of `card` inside `cardBox`, not a child, which is why it needs its own treatment instead of inheriting the card fix.

Everything else stays a plain class, so Clerk keeps its internal vertical rhythm.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on the touched file | clean |
| Important declarations reach the bundle | read out of the emitted CSS: `.px-0\!{padding-inline:…!important}`, and likewise for `pt-0`, `bg-transparent`, `border-0`, `shadow-none` |
| Suffix-vs-prefix syntax | determined empirically through this project's own build, not from memory — the v3 prefix form emits nothing here |

**Not verified: the live result.** This container has no working Clerk keys and clerk-js cannot load, so the card cannot be rendered here at all. The geometry above was derived from the production screenshot. Worth one more look at `/login` on production after deploy — and at a second step such as email verification or password reset, where Clerk renders a different card body.

author: aterga
body: # Motivation Internet Identity has one piece of user-owned shareable info today — verified emails — and it is textual. This adds a second: a profile picture. Each identity may carry zero or one picture of up to 100 KiB, and apps can request it as an Identity attribute under the key `profile_picture`. It is offered exactly where `verified_email` is offered: on `/manage/shareable-info`, and as a row in the continue-to-app consent screen. Nothing is shared without consent. This is a sketch — the vertical slice is complete and tested, but there are open questions at the bottom worth settling before it ships. # Changes **Storage — its own stable map, not the anchor.** `StorableProfilePicture` lives in a `StableBTreeMap` at memory id 33. Mechanically the anchor record could hold it (`StorableAnchor` is `Bound::Unbounded`), but it must not: `activity_bookkeeping` rewrites the whole anchor on every authenticated call, and the record is sized against `DEFAULT_ENTRY_SIZE` (4 KiB) with a realistic ceiling of ~6–10 KiB. A 100 KiB blob there would tax every unrelated operation. The per-anchor MCP config is the existing precedent for exactly this, and its comment says so. **WebP only, and the bytes are never trusted.** WebP subsumes the alternatives: it encodes both lossily and losslessly and carries alpha in either mode, so it covers everything PNG and JPEG would have been kept for, while being smaller than both at equivalent quality — which buys real picture quality under a 100 KiB cap. With one format the media type stops being data, so it is absent from the candid surface, the stored record and `identity_info`; `PROFILE_PICTURE_MEDIA_TYPE` is a constant that both sides derive their `data:` prefix from. `validate_profile_picture` bounds the size and checks the full RIFF container header including the coding chunk — `VP8 ` lossy, `VP8L` lossless, `VP8X` alpha/animation — so both compressed and uncompressed pictures are storable while a RIFF container that merely claims to be WebP is not. Nothing is taken on the caller's word, because a caller-supplied media type would end up in a `data:` URL that relying parties feed to an `` tag; that is also why SVG is rejected, being a script-execution vector in an `` on some consumers. No image decoding happens on-chain. **Transport — a `data:` URL in the existing `Icrc3Value::Text` slot.** Relying parties receive `data:image/webp;base64,…`, which drops straight into an ``. The cost is base64's 4/3 inflation. **Per-attribute-name value bound.** `ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_MAX_BYTES` is 50 000 — below 100 KiB, so it had to move. `AttributeName::max_value_bytes()` now returns a per-name bound rather than raising the global one, which would have widened what every `email` and `name` may carry. Both enforcement sites go through it. **Unscoped only, ICRC-3 only.** The picture is II-native user data, not a claim an identity provider can vouch for, so it has no `openid:`/`sso:` form — those arms report it as unavailable. The legacy attribute flow does not gain it: it is deprecated and serves `openid:`-scoped keys exclusively. **Consent integrity.** A `spec.value`, when the caller sends one, is an equality pin. The consent screen round-trips the exact bytes the user saw, so a picture changed between listing and certification fails the call rather than silently certifying an image the user never approved. **Frontend — the consent flow needed a real change, not another text row.** `AvailableAttribute.displayValue` is `TextDecoder`-decoded bytes, and it is rendered as text in five places, lowercased into a Map key for deduplication, and interpolated into `{#each}` keys. A ~137 KB data URL belongs in none of those. Image-valued attributes now carry the URL in a separate `imageSrc` field that the picker renders as a thumbnail, while `displayValue` holds a short content fingerprint that keeps its role as the option's identity. `getProviderName` also had to learn that "unscoped" no longer implies "verified email", or the picture row would have been tagged with the email provenance label. **Frontend — convert and resize before upload.** A 100 KiB cap is unusable against phone camera output, so a picked file is decoded, centre-cropped to a 512 px square and re-encoded as WebP, stepping down a quality ladder until it fits; the first rung is near-lossless so a flat-colour avatar or logo keeps crisp edges. The picker still accepts PNG, JPEG and WebP — converting is the client's job, and narrowing what a user may *choose* would be gratuitous. None of this is a security boundary; the canister re-checks size and header. `canvas.toBlob` needed care here: it does not fail on a media type the browser cannot encode, it silently falls back to PNG, and Safari before 16.4 does that for WebP. Those users would have hit an opaque "not WebP" rejection, so `encodeWebp` checks the produced `blob.type` and raises a distinguishable error, which the panel turns into "this browser can't save pictures in the required format". **`identity_info` reports metadata, not bytes.** That call runs on every `/manage/*` load. It gains `profile_picture : opt ProfilePictureMetadata` (size, upload time); the panel fetches the bytes separately, so users with a picture don't pay 100 KiB on every page load. `StorableProfilePicture::metadata` reads those fields off the stored record rather than going through the API shape, which would clone the bytes only to discard them. **Attribute calls only load the picture when asked.** Both `prepare_icrc3_attributes` and `list_available_attributes` gate the stable-memory read behind a predicate, so an identity with a picture doesn't pay a 100 KiB read and clone on attribute flows that never mention it. Relatedly, the data URL is rendered once per request rather than per spec — `MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_REQUEST` is 100, and the duplicate-key check fires only *after* resolution, so a ~2 KB authenticated request naming `profile_picture` a hundred times would otherwise have triggered a hundred encodings of the same picture. **Archive operations carry no payload.** `set_profile_picture` / `remove_profile_picture` follow the email operations' privacy rationale: the anchor and timestamp on the surrounding entry answer "who changed their picture when?" without handing an archive consumer a size it could match against a picture it already has. **Drive-by fix.** `ATTRIBUTE_NAME_MAX_BYTES` named the Rust variant identifier (`VerifiedEmail`, 13 bytes) while the wire name `verified_email` is 14, so the bound it fed was one byte short. It now names the wire form, with a test that fails if a longer variant is added without bumping it. Candid bindings are hand-written to match `didc bind` output, including its field ordering by candid name hash. `didc` is version-pinned and sha-verified via `.didc-release`, and the CI regeneration step no longer commits, so these ship as written. # Tests Run locally against this branch's HEAD, all green: - `cargo test -p internet_identity --bin internet_identity` — 660 passed. author: hvejsel
body:
Closes FIR-4933 (internal tracker).

## Problem

Two field lists that had to agree, kept apart by hand:

- The hook editor's suggestion list was a hand-written copy. It **missed** fields the platform's own managed hooks match on — so those hooks rendered as broken rows with `<redacted>` values (FIR-4933's screenshots) — and it **offered** fields the server gates never send (`actor.type`, `message.channel_id`, `message.body`, `wakeup.fire_at`, `retry.pending`, ...), letting users build rules that look fine but can never fire, with no warning either way.
- The hook journal's retention allowlist was a third vocabulary that dropped exactly the fields those conditions use (whole `message` section, `continuation`, `chain`, `failure`, the `wakeup` keys), so replaying a journal event through Test almost never matched — and `RecordTestEvidence` needs a match, so conditional hooks could not clear the publish gate that way. `before.issue.assigned` was not retainable at all.

## Fix

One server-owned manifest — `server/internal/cerebro/workflows/hook_field_manifest.json` — declares, per condition-visible event, each field's path, label, input widget and sensitivity. `go generate` emits `hook-field-catalog.generated.ts`; `hook-validation` and `hook-ux` read the generated catalog instead of hand-written lists. Same provenance pattern as the action catalog (`hook-action-catalog.generated.ts`).

Behaviour changes:

- A condition field outside the manifest renders with an explicit **`(unknown field)`** marker instead of the old "<redacted>"-as-unfamiliar behaviour — honesty, not borrowed security semantics. Known fields redact only when the manifest marks them sensitive.
- `event.Actor` is merged into the condition context, so `actor.type` / `actor.id` resolve on every event (one-line engine change).
- Journal retention now keeps condition-visible fields and `before.issue.assigned` events, so Test/replay and publish evidence work on these hooks.
- `before.issue.assigned` is selectable in the editor.
- Templates repaired: `require-continuation` uses `continuation.present`; `no-silent-failure` uses `failure.attempt >= $event.failure.max_attempts` (`retry.pending` never existed server-side).

Drift locks so the gap cannot reopen:

- Go test: the generated TS must byte-match the manifest (mirror of the action-catalog test).
- Go test: every managed policy condition and every `$event.*` value must resolve in the manifest for its events.
- Go test: the engine's base condition context may not grow fields the manifest does not declare.

## Scope notes

Not in this PR (tracked as follow-ups from the FIR-4933 review): `before.issue.status_change` firing only for issues with an active chain, project/workflow bindings silently never matching on `before.message.send`, `fail_mode` open→warn normalisation on save, the 2s catalog-timeout fail-open on `CanBlock` events, and removing structurally-always-true managed conditions (`chain.active eq true`, `issue.terminal eq false`).

## Test plan

- `go test ./internal/cerebro/workflows/` — green (new manifest/drift tests included).
- `go build ./...` — green.
- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/cerebro-workflows` — 154 tests green (incl. updated UX-contract expectations for the new `(unknown field)` marker and boolean Yes/No rendering).

author: hudsonmp
body:
## What changed

- Replaces the skill-driven copy/paste `/compact focus ...` handoff with one bare `/compact`, an unanchored precommit, a same-terminal editable ledger, and automatic continuation of the original compaction.
- Reconstructs user prompts, assistant conclusions, tool calls/results, file deltas, and relevant attachments with stable provenance IDs and exact one-to-one coverage validation.
- Separates type, status, retention, confidence, and contested interpretation; supports edit, split, merge, move, class rules, rival views, and per-prompt context costs.
- Makes demotion recoverable through project-local SQLite/FTS and distinguishes omission feedback from misconstrual feedback.
- Adds deterministic cold proposals, cancellable background enrichment, stale-proposal rebasing, terminal/process watchdogs, private atomic state, and a conservative post-compaction adherence audit.
- Removes the obsolete shell/skill/browser/external-terminal workflows and tracked bytecode.
- Packages v0.19.0 as a public Claude marketplace plugin and standalone Python CLI with install, privacy, troubleshooting, contribution, changelog, license, and CI documentation.

## Acceptance evidence

- Warm live run: a prepared proposal opened from bare `/compact`, accepted seven edits, emitted the reviewed contract, and the same compaction continued. Its resulting summary retained all five test claims.
- Cold live run: with background analysis disabled, precommit/editor opened in the same timestamped second; no proposal model or second command ran.
- Cached-install run: `compact-focus@papert-tools` v0.19.0 opened the editor from Claude's marketplace cache in under two seconds; `q` blocked compaction cleanly.
- Proposal benchmark exposed 92.5 s / $0.069 latency, motivating the deterministic foreground and preemptible background architecture rather than hiding a slow cold path.

## Verification

- `python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 34 passing
- `python3 -m py_compile compact-focus/compact_focus/*.py`
- `claude plugin validate . --strict`
- `claude plugin validate ./compact-focus --strict`
- wheel build and isolated venv install (`claude-compact-focus==0.19.0`)

## Deliberate limits

- Inline terminal ownership currently supports macOS/Linux, not native Windows.
- Context percentages distinguish attributable transcript evidence from hidden system/tool context; unknown model windows never receive a fabricated denominator.
- The post-compaction audit is lexical triage, explicitly not semantic verification.

author: lunev51
body:
Живая жалоба с макбука: при выделении мышью в буфер ничего не уходит, Cmd+C тоже молчит, правой кнопкой копируется только одно слово.

## Причина — не буфер обмена, а выделение

Claude Code включает отслеживание мыши: в потоке pty лежат `CSI ?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1003h`, `?1006h` (прочитано из кольцевого буфера вкладки). С этого момента xterm отдаёт мышь приложению и своё выделение не строит — протяжка не выделяет ничего, копировать нечего. Оба «сломанных» пути честно выходят вхолостую: `copyOnSelect` не получает текста, ветка Cmd+C видит пустой `getSelection`.

Правый клик копирует слово, потому что xterm на macOS по умолчанию выделяет слово под курсором (`rightClickSelectsWord`) и подменяет им выделение.

Пробить перехват можно только форсированным выделением, и клавиша зависит от платформы: `isMac ? altKey && macOptionClickForcesSelection : shiftKey`. На Windows Shift работает всегда, на маке нужна опция с дефолтом `false` — кокпит её не выставлял, то есть **на макбуке выделить текст было нельзя ничем**.

## Что сделано

- `terminal.js`: xterm получает `macOptionClickForcesSelection: true`.
- `hotkeys.js`: строка про Option (мак) / Shift (ПК) — без неё фича необнаружима.

## Живая проверка

Пробный экземпляр (отдельный каталог данных), браузер по сетевому адресу, платформа подменена на `MacIntel` через CDP — xterm определяет мак именно по `navigator.platform`. В терминале работающий TUI Claude Code.

| Условие | Протяжка | Shift | Option |
|---|---|---|---|
| опция выключена | нет | нет | **нет** — выделить нечем, маркер в буфере цел |
| опция включена | нет | нет (так и задумано на маке) | **выделение есть, буфер получил текст** |

На Windows Shift+протяжка выделяет и копирует независимо от опции. В PowerShell-вкладке (мышь не перехвачена) работает обычная протяжка.

## Тесты (+2)

`terminal-selection`: опция передана именно в объект опций xterm; шпаргалка объясняет, чем выделять. Комментарии вырезаются перед проверкой — разбор бага написан прямо над опцией и содержит её имя, страж по всему файлу остался бы зелёным после удаления самой опции.

Мутации, все четыре краснеют: опция удалена; опция `false`; опция закомментирована; строка шпаргалки удалена.

1080 тестов.

Разбор целиком — `RESEARCH_mac-clipboard.md`, ограничение записано в `PROGRESS.md`.

## Осталось за кадром (отдельно)

- Провал копирования нигде не виден: `copyText` возвращает `false`, а `terminal.js` результат не смотрит.
- Правый клик без выделения по http падает с TypeError на `navigator.clipboard.readText` — тот же баг, что чинили в #30, только для чтения.

## What it solves Resolves: four post-migration defects found while auditing recently migrated components, plus the shared `FiatChange` duplication they exposed. 1. **Double navigation in `usePreventNavigation`** — when a tx flow opted out of the discard warning, clicking a link navigated twice: the hook performed the navigation itself *and* the guard called `proceed()`. 2. **`AddCustomAppModal` swallowed validation messages** — `Input.error` was wired to `errors.appUrl.type === 'validUrl'`, so the `required` error never surfaced (and `required: true` had no message to show in the first place). 3. **`FiatChange` treated `"0"` inconsistently** — the falsy check `if (!fiatChange)` rendered "n/a" for a genuine zero change, while `"0.00"` (truthy) rendered "0%". Same bug in the mobile copies. 4. **Four near-identical `FiatChange` implementations** — web + three mobile components each re-derived direction, colour, sign and parsing inline. ## How this PR fixes it **1. Navigation guard contract** `requestDiscard` now tells its action *how* it was invoked. `usePreventNavigation` owns the navigation when the guard returns `true` synchronously, so the guard replays `proceed()` only when the navigation was actually blocked and later confirmed: ```ts requestDiscard((deferred) => { closeFlow() if (deferred) proceed() }) ``` The hook's JSDoc now states the contract explicitly: a guard returning `true` must not call `proceed` itself. **2. `AddCustomAppModal` errors** `required: true` → `required: 'URL is required'`, and the `error` prop inverted to `type !== 'alreadyExists'`. `alreadyExists` stays excluded on purpose — it renders as a positive "This Safe App is already registered" confirmation with a share URL, not as an error. **3 + 4. Shared fiat-change helpers** New `packages/utils/src/utils/fiatChange.ts`: - `parseFiatChange(value)` — backend string (`"-3.00"` = -3%) → decimal fraction; `null` only when absent or non-finite, so `"0"` is preserved as a real zero - `getFiatChangeDirection(change)` → `'up' | 'down' | 'none'` Platform styling stays platform-local: `apps/mobile/src/utils/fiatChange.ts` maps direction → Tamagui token + sign. Each call site drops its inline `getColor()` / `changeSign()` closures. The protocol total in `ProtocolSection` was extracted into a `ProtocolFiatChange` component, and `calculateProtocolFiatChange` now guards against a non-finite ratio. ## How to test it **Double navigation** 1. Open a tx flow that opts out of the discard warning (`shouldWarn: false`), e.g. a flow with no unsaved input. 2. Click any sidebar link. → Navigates once, no discard dialog. 3. Repeat with a flow that has unsaved progress. → "Discard this transaction?" appears, the flow stays mounted, nothing navigates until you confirm; then it navigates exactly once. **AddCustomAppModal** 1. Apps → My custom apps → Add custom Safe App. 2. Focus and blur the URL field empty. → "URL is required". 3. Enter garbage (`not-a-url`). → invalid-URL error. 4. Enter a URL already in the default list. → no red error; the "already registered" confirmation with share link shows instead. **FiatChange zero** 1. Web assets table and mobile assets list with a token whose `fiatBalance24hChange` is `"0"`. → renders `0%` in the neutral colour, not "n/a". 2. Non-numeric / missing change → still "n/a" (web) / `0%` placeholder (mobile). **Unit tests** ```bash yarn workspace @safe-global/web test src/hooks/__tests__/usePreventNavigation.test.ts src/components/tx-flow src/components/safe-apps/AddCustomAppModal src/components/balances/AssetsTable/FiatChange.test.tsx yarn workspace @safe-global/mobile test fiatChange FiatChange ProtocolFiatChange ProtocolDetailSheet yarn workspace @safe-global/utils test fiatChange ``` ## Affected flows - Closing a tx flow via the dialog close button (with and without unsaved progress) - Navigating away from an open tx flow via an in-app link or browser back - Adding a custom Safe App (validation feedback on the URL field) - Reading 24h fiat change on the web assets table, the mobile assets list, mobile position rows, and mobile protocol sections/detail sheet ## Blast radius **Shared packages (web + mobile):** - `packages/utils/src/utils/fiatChange.ts` — new module, no pre-existing consumers. Consumed by 4 components across both apps. **Web:** - `usePreventNavigation` — sole consumer is `TxModalProvider`; the JSDoc change codifies the `proceed`-ownership contract for future callers. - `TxModalProvider.requestDiscard` — signature widened to `(deferred: boolean) => void`. Internal to `components/tx-flow/index.tsx`; the `setTxFlow` / `TxModalContext` public API is unchanged, so no call site of the ~dozens of tx flows needs touching. - `AssetsTable/FiatChange` — used by the assets table and inline balance displays. - `AddCustomAppModal` — self-contained; no shared form utilities changed. **Mobile:** - `apps/mobile/src/utils/fiatChange.ts` — new, Tamagui-token-only. - `ProtocolFiatChange` — new component; `ProtocolSection` and `ProtocolDetailSheetHeader` now render it instead of inlining the markup. - `calculateProtocolFiatChange` — now returns `null` instead of `NaN`/`Infinity` for degenerate totals; consumers already handled `null`. **Not touched:** no RTK Query endpoints, slices, feature flags, chain configs, persisted state, or routes. ## Risks / not checked - The mobile changes are covered by unit tests but were **not** run on a device or simulator — no visual confirmation of the Tamagui colour tokens. - Did not verify the `beforePopState` (browser back) path manually in a browser; it is covered by the `usePreventNavigation` unit tests only. - Did not verify `beforeunload` / tab-close behaviour — unchanged by this PR, but it shares the guard. - No E2E test added for the tx-flow discard gate; coverage is unit-level. - `AddCustomAppModal` error copy was not reviewed by design. - Did not audit remaining migrated components for the same falsy-`"0"` pattern beyond the four fiat-change call sites. ## Visual summary Navigation guard — the double-navigation fix: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant H as usePreventNavigation participant P as TxModalProvider participant R as Router Note over U,R: Before — flow opted out of the warning U->>H: mousedown on link H->>P: guard(proceed) P->>P: closeFlow() P->>R: proceed() ❌ P-->>H: true H->>R: router.push() ❌ Note over R: navigated twice Note over U,R: After U->>H: mousedown on link H->>P: guard(proceed) P->>P: closeFlow() P-->>H: true (deferred = false, no proceed) H->>R: router.push() ✅ Note over R: navigated once ``` Fiat change — before/after structure: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before W1[web FiatChange] --> I1["inline: Number(v)/100
falsy check, direction,
getColor, changeSign"] M1[mobile FiatChange] --> I2[same inline logic] M2[PositionFiatChange] --> I3[same inline logic] M3[ProtocolSection] --> I4[inline ternaries] end subgraph After W2[web FiatChange] --> S[parseFiatChange
getFiatChangeDirection
packages/utils] M4[mobile FiatChange] --> S M5[PositionFiatChange] --> S M6[ProtocolSection] --> PC[ProtocolFiatChange] PC --> S M4 --> T[getFiatChangeColor / Sign
mobile, Tamagui tokens] M5 --> T PC --> T end ``` ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 - [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 — no analytics impact - [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻 - [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯 --- ## CLA signature With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Ag

author: lmontigny
body:
[docs/cpu.md](docs/cpu.md) has said the AMX investigation was **never repeated on Arm**, and that the benchmark could not be pointed at it unmodified because it looks for `BRGEMM` and `avx10_1_512_amx`, both x86 names. Repeating it on a GCP Axion N4A (Arm Neoverse N3, 8 vCPU, `torch 2.13.0+cpu`, oneDNN v3.12) found the names were the smaller problem.

## The method does not transfer, not just the strings

Swapping `amx` for `acl` looks like the fix and is wrong. oneDNN routes FP32 **and** BF16 matmuls to the same `gemm:acl` — that names Arm Compute Library, not an instruction — and the dispatch log is identical for both dtypes too. Neither log can say whether the BF16 instructions ran.

So `matrix_matmul` is now three-valued: a list on x86, `None` where the log cannot answer. Recording "the matrix unit never ran" beside a 2.42x BF16 speedup would be false, and that is exactly what the old field did here.

## The two workloads disagree, which is the finding

Synthetic MLP, eager — BF16 wins everywhere, including where AMX lost:

| rows | FP32 | BF16 | | x86 AMX |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.442 ms | 1.264 ms | 1.14x | **0.77x — slower** |
| 8 | 1.324 ms | 0.546 ms | 2.42x | 2.22x |
| 64 | 3.851 ms | 2.119 ms | 1.82x | 4.87x |
| 512 | 25.728 ms | 8.136 ms | 3.16x | 3.16x |

SmolLM2-135M, same host, same benchmark — it reverses:

| prompt | eager FP32 | eager BF16 | inductor FP32 | inductor BF16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 43.59 ms | 40.36 ms | 32.01 ms | **27.46 ms** |
| 64 | 94.28 ms | 302.52 ms | **76.95 ms** | 281.02 ms |

At 64 tokens BF16 is **3.2x slower**, against 1.82x *faster* for the MLP at the same row count. The MLP does not predict the model on this part — which is what the x86 section had been using it for.

## What the dispatch log is good for

| implementation | why oneDNN skipped it |
| --- | --- |
| `matmul:brg:sve_512` | `unsupported isa` |
| `matmul:lowp_gemm:acl` | `unsupported datatype combination` |
| `matmul:lowp_gemm_sq:acl` | `unsupported datatype combination` |

oneDNN calls this core `AArch64 SVE (128 bits)` and its Arm BRGEMM path wants 512-bit vectors, so that path is unreachable here — a wider-SVE part (Graviton 3/4, Neoverse V-series) could land elsewhere. The `lowp_gemm` rows are the INT8 kernels, declined only for want of INT8 operands.

## Also in this PR

- **Renamed** `cpu_amx.py` → `cpu_matrix_unit.py`; the file no longer asks an Intel question.
- **Flags are tokenised**, not substring-matched — `sve` is a prefix of `svebf16`.
- **Fixes a memory bug this PR introduced.** `ONEDNN_VERBOSE=all` on a 30-layer model at 512 tokens emits enough output to exhaust a 31 GiB host when `subprocess.run` buffers it; it wedged the machine. The log is now streamed and line-capped.

## Limits

- **512-token prompts are not measured.** Each BF16 call runs into seconds and the sweep was cut for cost, so the comparison stops one length short of where AMX looks best.
- **Absolute latencies are not comparable across the two hosts** — different host, different `transformers`. The within-host FP32/BF16 ratios are.

The x86 conclusion survives and gets stronger: a dtype policy has to be per-host. The policy that is right on Emerald Rapids (BF16 above 16 rows) is wrong on Neoverse N3 in *both* directions at once.

author: copilot
body:
The `Deploy` GitHub Actions job failed because `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages` could not push to `gh-pages` using a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` (403). This update scopes the required write permission to the deploy job so publishing can proceed on `main` pushes.

- **Root cause**
  - Deploy job token had `contents: read`, but deployment requires pushing commits to `gh-pages`.

- **Workflow change**
  - Added explicit job-level permissions in `.github/workflows/main.yml`:
    - `deploy.permissions.contents: write`
  - No trigger or build/deploy step changes.

- **Resulting behavior**
  - `build` remains unchanged.
  - `deploy` retains existing conditions and artifact flow, now with sufficient permission to publish.

```yaml
deploy:
  needs: build
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
  permissions:
    contents: write
```

author: yong076
body:
## Why

The daemon reads whichever provider home its environment named when launchd froze that environment at install time. A second profile (`$CODEX_HOME` / `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointed elsewhere) or an app-managed runtime home is invisible to it — and when such a home is a mirror that quietly stops receiving new sessions, nothing looks wrong, because the lifetime total it already holds stays plausible.

Measured on a dev machine: the home the daemon reads holds 8,058 sessions while `~/.codex` holds 8,526, and its state DB is 905 KB against 50 MB.

## What this does

**Discovery is automatic; adoption is not.** A discovered home is reported by `agentcat doctor` and only counted after `agentcat homes --adopt`. Auto-absorbing would eventually swallow a backup dir or a test fixture and inflate every number the product shows — worse for trust than the gap it closes.

**Deduplication is the correctness precondition, not a refinement.** Mirrors hardlink their sessions, so naive multi-home scanning would have counted 8,058 files twice. Three layers: `realpath`, then `(st_dev, st_ino)` for hardlinks `realpath` cannot see, then session identity from the filename for true copies (longer file wins). Layers 1–2 always run since two paths to one inode are the same bytes; layer 3 only with multiple homes, where `sessions/` and `archived_sessions/` sharing a UUID means a move in progress rather than a duplicate.

Deduping at file *selection*, rather than re-keying cursors to inode, gets the same guarantee without invalidating every stored offset or forcing a multi-thousand-file re-parse.

**New diagnostics:** `untracked_home`, `stalled_home` (the home we read went quiet while an unread one keeps growing), `env_drift` (the launch job pins a path the current shell no longer agrees with).

**New CLI:** `agentcat homes` — list / `--adopt` / `--exclude` / `--forget`.

**Snapshot:** additive, tilde-relative `homes` block behind capability `homes.discovery`.

## Audit fixes ridden along (agent-cat #38/#43/#45)

Every connector-side claim was re-verified against current main first; several were already fixed and only the issues were stale (#45-1 CODEX_HOME limits, #45-9 antigravity limits mirroring gemini, #16-1 events retention, #16-3 port bind, #16-4 hardcoded personal path). What was still live:

- **#43** — the OTEL telemetry log had no rotation and reached 8.9 GB. Now truncated once it passes a threshold **and** has been read to the end, so no unread record is ever destroyed.
- **#45-4** — a full rebuild triggered on a gap the rebuild itself could not close, re-parsing up to 10k files every 60s forever. Now marked, with the marker expiring as soon as either total moves.
- **#45-10** — Windows took `HOME` over `USERPROFILE`, so Git Bash/MSYS pointed every provider path at a shell home with no provider dirs under it.
- **#38-4** — API-key/Bedrock/Vertex installs reported `token_missing`, which reads as "Claude detection is broken". Now detected and reported as expected-no-subscription-quota.
- **#45-13** — deleted 111 lines of dead antigravity day-filter code.

**Not done, deliberately:** automatic Claude OAuth refresh, the headline ask in #38. Claude Code stores one credential set with a short-lived access token and a rotating refresh token; refreshing it out from under Claude Code risks invalidating the refresh token it holds and logging the user out of their CLI. Expiry is already surfaced as `token_expired`. The safe version needs a decision about writing back to the user's Keychain.

## Back-compat

Verified, not assumed: the app decodes with an explicit `CodingKeys` list where only `generatedAt` and `providers` are required, so an unknown `homes` key is ignored by installed builds. `SCHEMA_VERSION` deliberately stays at 4. A snapshot generated with this code removes zero established top-level keys and adds exactly one.

## Verification

- Suite 217 → 289 green.
- Mutation-checked: disabling dedup fails 6 tests, auto-adopting every home fails 8, disabling stall detection fails 1.
- Real dedup on this machine: 16,584 naive → 8,526, i.e. the mirrored 8,058 collapse onto the copy already counted.
- Test isolation hardened — the suite previously reached the developer's live install (it truncated a real 8.9 GB log). `tests/sandbox.py` now redirects every module path, asserts none escape, and blocks outbound HTTP. A full run changes zero mtimes under `~/.agentcat`.

author: asafaviv-devops
body:
## Summary

JIRA: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SPRE-6549

Adds two new Prometheus alerts to improve cert-manager monitoring coverage:

- **CertManagerIssuerNotReady** (warning) - monitors namespace-scoped Issuers. Needed as teams migrate from service-ca to per-namespace selfsigned-issuers.
- **CertManagerControllerSyncErrors** (warning) - detects cert-manager controller sync failures that may prevent certificate issuance or renewal. Uses a 15m increase window with 5m persistence.

Also modifies the existing **CertManagerCertificateExpiryCritical** alert: removed the `>= 0` guard from the expression so it now fires for both certificates expiring within 7 days AND certificates that have already expired. Previously, expired certificates were excluded by the `>= 0` condition, creating a monitoring gap. A separate CertManagerCertificateExpired alert was initially added to cover this gap but was replaced by this simpler fix to the existing alert.

## Metrics used

All metrics are confirmed in the federation endpoints-params allow-list:
- `certmanager_issuer_ready_status`
- `certmanager_controller_sync_error_count`

## Testing

- Positive and negative promtool test cases for both new alerts
- Added test case for expired certificate on CertManagerCertificateExpiryCritical
- `make check-and-test` passes

## Context

Part of the ongoing migration from OpenShift service-ca to cert-manager across Konflux clusters. As teams create per-namespace selfsigned-issuers, we need monitoring coverage for namespace-scoped Issuers (not just ClusterIssuers). SOPs for all alerts will be submitted separately to the sop repo.

## Summary
"파라미터가 잘못되었다"는 `CO400` 오류가 재현됐습니다. 처음엔 스펙 문서의 Content-Disposition 언급 때문에 multipart/form-data로 "mail" 파트에 JSON을 실어 보내도록 구현했는데, 실제로 성공한 참조 코드(`requests.post(url, headers=header, data=json.dumps(payload), proxies=proxy, verify=False)`)를 확인해보니 JSON 문자열을 그대로 body에 담아 보내는 방식이었습니다 - multipart가 아니었습니다.

- 참조 코드가 `verify=False`로 호출하는 것도 확인해서, `CONFLUENCE_VERIFY_SSL`과 동일한 성격의 `MAIL_API_VERIFY_SSL` 옵션도 함께 추가 (기본값 `true`)

## Summary

Upgrade the Android build toolchain to the newest compatibility intersection currently supported by the upstream matrices: AGP 9.1.0, Kotlin 2.4.10, Gradle 9.5.0, and AndroidX Activity 1.13.0. Regenerate the pinned wrapper, strict dependency lock, and additive verification metadata, including Linux and Windows AAPT2 hashes. Fix the Kotlin 2.4 warning-as-error exposed in the tile service lifecycle. This is the reviewed replacement for Dependabot PR #12.

AGP 9.3/Gradle 9.7 were intentionally not retained: Kotlin 2.4.10 documents full support through AGP 9.1 and Gradle 9.5, while the newer Lint toolchain called Java 21 collection APIs under the repository's required JDK 17 CI runtime.

## Change scope

- Platforms: Android / Android TV
- Outputs: Build and packaging toolchain for VPN / SOCKS5 / HTTP
- Security or privileged-state impact: No network-policy change. Supply-chain verification remains strict and the Gradle distribution is SHA-256 pinned.

## Validation

- [x] Relevant format, lint, and unit tests pass.
- [x] Protocol or parser changes include malformed-input/interoperability coverage. (Not applicable: no protocol change.)
- [x] Privileged network changes include isolated cleanup and leak-prevention evidence. (Not applicable: no privileged network behavior change.)
- [x] UI changes cover English/Chinese, themes, focus, scaling, and TV navigation as applicable. (Not applicable: no Flutter UI change.)
- [x] New logs, errors, and diagnostics were reviewed for sensitive data.
- [x] Documentation, wrapper, lockfile, and verification metadata are updated.

Local repository policy, 21 policy/tool tests, Android host tests, ktlint, Lint, metadata XML parsing, and diff checks pass. A local arm64 Release/AOT APK also passed ABI/debug-artifact/signature structure checks. GitHub PR Check, CI on JDK 17, and arm64 Release Build remain the authoritative clean-environment validation.

## Not tested

No VPN/TUN/WFP runtime test was run on the development host. No MSI was installed. Runtime networking is unchanged by this toolchain-only migration.

## Checklist

- [x] The PR title follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] No signing key, WARP Secret, token, license, device ID, endpoint pin, diagnostic bundle, or generated package is committed.

author: lichtbaer
body:
## Worum es geht

Die Standortbewertung lief auf `horizonProfile()` in `data.js`: drei Sinusterme, im Diagramm als gefüllte Geländesilhouette gezeichnet, mit **0,42 im Score** gewichtet und als Satz mit Nachkommastelle ausgegeben („Die Sonne steht im Maximum 4,3° über der Horizontlinie — sicher frei").

Der Rauschterm war bei null geklemmt und konnte deshalb konstruktionsbedingt gar nicht verdecken. Ergebnis: **alle zwölf Standorte bekamen „sicher frei"** — auch der Hohe Peißenberg, wo die Sonne 1,92° hoch steht und laut `README.md:89` schon eine 5-m-Hecke in 150 m reicht (1,9°). Die Seite behauptete dabei in `Sofi.dc.html:376`, die Profile stammten aus DOM1/DGM, ausgewertet mit HORAYZON. Beides existierte nicht — im Backend gab es keinen Horizont-Endpunkt.

## Datenquelle

**Copernicus DEM GLO-30** (ESA), offen über S3 ohne Anmeldung. Eine Quelle, ein Format, eine Lizenz — statt sechzehn Landesportalen.

Entscheidend war eine Messung, nicht eine Annahme: **GLO-30 ist ein Oberflächenmodell und enthält Bewuchs.** An der Kachel N50/E008 liegt der Frankfurter Stadtwald bei 122 m, das Vorfeld des Frankfurter Flughafens 4 km entfernt bei 105 m — bei gleicher Geländehöhe der Rhein-Main-Ebene. Das sind **17 m Kronendach**; ein Transekt über die Waldkante zeigt Sprünge von +7 m auf 60 m Strecke. Gebäude fehlen dagegen weitgehend (Commerzbank-Tower, 259 m, liest sich als Bodenniveau).

Für einen Westhorizont im Freien ist das die passende Asymmetrie: dort limitieren Baumreihen, nicht Hochhäuser.

## Änderungen

| Datei | Inhalt |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/geotiff.py` | Minimaler Kachelleser, Motiv wie `grib2.py`: Deflate mit Fließkomma-Predictor (Byte-Ebenen + Differenzbildung). Hält GDAL aus dem Image, wie `README.md:108` es festlegt. Gegen rasterio bit-identisch geprüft. |
| `backend/app/services/dem.py` | Kacheln holen, zu einem 1″-Mosaik verrechnen (int16, Dezimeter, memmap, 2,85 GB). |
| `backend/app/services/horizon.py` | Ein Strahl je 0,25° über 240°–330°, bis 40 km, mit Erdkrümmung und Refraktion (k = 0,13). |
| `backend/app/api/routes.py` | `/api/v1/horizon`, `/api/v1/elevation`, `terrain` in `/health`. |
| `backend/app/worker.py` | Prüft beim Start, ob das Raster vollständig ist, holt sonst nach. |
| `frontend/` | Mock entfernt, an die API angeschlossen, Urteilstexte und Datenherkunft korrigiert. |

**Rund 25 ms je Punkt** — deshalb Punktabfrage on demand statt vorberechneter Spalte. Das ist der Grund, warum der Klick auf eine beliebige Kartenstelle funktioniert; ein Ortsmittelpunkt hätte das nicht abgedeckt.

## Der Fehler bleibt einseitig — und die Oberfläche stellt ihn einseitig dar

Was GLO-30 fehlt (Gebäude, alles unter 30 m Rasterweite), verdeckt **zusätzlich, nie weniger**. Daraus folgt eine Semantik, die keine der beiden Richtungen gleich rendert:

- **`blocked`** → eine **Aussage**. Genauere Daten können den Horizont nur anheben.
- **`clear`** → eine **Obergrenze**, mit bezifferter Reserve. `tight` markiert alles unter 2°, wo eine einzelne Baumreihe genügt.

Jede Näherung im Backend ist so gewählt, dass sie den Horizont eher zu niedrig ansetzt — Standhöhe, Strahlreichweite, Rasterrand. Ein zu strenges Urteil wäre der teurere Fehler, weil `blocked` als Tatsache erscheint.

Fehlt der Horizont ganz, gibt es **keinen Score, sondern einen Strich**. Die übrigen drei Faktoren umzugewichten ergäbe wieder eine Zahl, die wie eine Bewertung aussieht und die entscheidende Größe nicht kennt — genau der Zustand, den dieser PR beseitigt.

## Fallstricke, die im Code dokumentiert sind

- **Die Längenabtastung wechselt bei genau 50° N** von 1″ auf 1,5″, und die Grenze läuft mitten durch Deutschland (Frankfurt: 50,1°). Ein naives Mosaik verschiebt die halbe Republik, ohne dass die Zahlen unplausibel aussähen. Deshalb einheitliches 1″-Gitter mit exakter Nearest-Neighbour-Aufweitung.
- **Mindestabstand 90 m.** Bei 30 m Rasterweite ist die Nachbarzelle das eigene Rauschen; ohne die Sperre meldet fast jeder Punkt in Deutschland 3–4° Horizont.
- **Standhöhe aus dem Zellwert, nicht aus dem Umfeldminimum.** Das Minimum greift auf einem Gipfel die Hangschulter — am Hohen Peißenberg 26 m — und erzeugt ein falsches `blocked` auf einem Rundblick-Gipfel.
- **Reine Seekacheln existieren nicht** (S3 `NoSuchKey`), das ist kein Fehler, sondern die Auskunft „hier ist nur Wasser".

## Standortkoordinaten korrigiert

Vier Koordinaten in `SITES` lagen neben dem Gipfel. **Hesselberg** lag 93 m tiefer am Hang und wurde deshalb als „verdeckt" bewertet — bei einem freistehenden Zeugenberg, dessen eigener Zugangstext zwei Zeilen weiter „Rundumsicht" sagt. Kalmit lag 141 m daneben.

Gegen das Höhenmodell nachgezogen; alle vier treffen jetzt ihre angegebene Gipfelhöhe. Das Sinusprofil hat solche Fehler nie auffallen lassen, weil es die Koordinate gar nicht benutzt hat.

## Betrieb

Der Worker zieht beim ersten Start rund 3 GB Kacheln und verrechnet sie — **wiederaufnehmbar**, Kachel für Kachel, jede wird nach dem Eintragen gelöscht (Spitzenbedarf 2,85 GB statt 6 GB). Läuft neben der Wolkenschleife, nicht vor ihr: eine fehlende Wolkenprognose am Ereignisabend wäre der teurere Ausfall.

`api` und `worker` teilen sich `fielddata:/data` bereits — **keine Compose-Änderung nötig**. Bis das Raster steht, antworten beide Routen mit `503` und `/health` meldet `terrain: false`.

## Geprüft

- **96 Tests grün** (`backend/tests`), davon 27 neu: GeoTIFF-Leser gegen einen aus der Spezifikation geschriebenen Encoder, Horizontgeometrie gegen synthetische Raster (Wand, Kuppe, Krümmung), Routenvertrag inklusive 503-Verhalten.
- Kachelleser **bit-identisch zu rasterio** über eine vollständige Kachel.
- Fernfeld gegengerechnet: Taunus vom Niddapark aus 2,98° bei 300° aus 12,8 km — Handrechnung für den Altkönig ergibt 2,7°.
- Seite im Browser gegen die laufende API geladen; alle drei Urteilsvarianten rendern korrekt. Die Scores differenzieren jetzt von 87 (Feldberg) bis 41, vorher bekamen alle zwölf „sicher frei".

## Nicht in diesem PR

Das Nahfeld unter 30 m Rasterweite — die einzelne Hecke, das Gebäude. Nächste Kandidaten wären OSM-Gebäudeumrisse und eine 10-m-Kronenhöhenkarte, beide bundesweit aus je einer Quelle. Als Notiz im README vermerkt.

`pvlib.iotools.get_pvgis_horizon` wurde geprüft und **nicht** übernommen: dahinter steckt SRTM-3 (~90 m Gelände), also gröber als GLO-30, plus eine Laufzeitabfrage mit der Besucherkoordinate an einen Dritten — gegen die Architektur in `api-spec.md:6-9`. Als unabhängige Gegenprobe auf einzelnen Stützstellen bleibt es sinnvoll.

author: aryangorde8
body:
Fixes #4489

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`AsyncPQExecutor.shutdown_async` cancelled the worker futures and *then* awaited
`queue.join()`. A sentinel is pushed per worker just above that, and `_worker`
calls `task_done()` when it consumes one — so a worker cancelled before it
reaches its sentinel leaves the queue's unfinished count above zero and the
join waits forever.

`AsyncPQThreadPoolExecutor.shutdown_async`, in the same file, already does this
in the correct order: drain first, cancel after, with a separate `else` branch
that cancels immediately when `wait=False`. This PR makes the base class match
its own subclass.

`S3Connector.close()` separately awaited the **synchronous** `shutdown`, which
calls `run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` — blocking the very loop the
coroutine needs in order to make progress. It now awaits `shutdown_async`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

@zhengfeihe — kept small as asked: +16/−8 across two source files, plus a test
file. No behaviour change beyond the ordering.

The hang is timing dependent, which is worth knowing when reading the test.
Against the unfixed executor the two `wait=True` tests pass on Python 3.10,
3.11 and 3.12 and **fail on 3.13** (10s timeout, 5/5 runs), where cancellation
lands before the workers drain. The CI matrix covers 3.13, so this is reachable
from CI — it is how the bug was found, via a fixture teardown in #4484.

Note this touches `s3_connector.py`, which #4484 also modifies, in a different
region. They should merge cleanly; whichever lands second I will rebase if
needed.

#4484's test fixture currently works around this by shutting down with
`wait=False`. I left that as is rather than have that PR depend on this one.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

author: eshmis
body:
Blast-radius: none — no CODEOWNERS path is touched (`.gitignore`, `apps/web/lib/repository/map-eligibility.ts`, `scripts/check-layer-graph.mjs`).

## The gap the owner asked about has a number, and nothing printed it

Owner, tonight: *expand the repository and the map until they match, and then beyond*. That target is already measurable in this repo and has been since `map-eligibility.ts` was written. `auditAnchors` returns `unanchored` — the map-eligible corpus records that no layer node reaches — and that file calls it "the most concrete statement this repository can make about what the map does not yet cover".

Nothing ever printed it. The checker printed its *length* and threw the list away, so the only way to read it was to edit the checker. A list you have to patch a script to see is one nobody consults.

**Measured at HEAD:** `9 of 62 map-eligible records anchored — 53 algorithm records no node reaches`.

**And the prose describing it had drifted.** `map-eligibility.ts` said "61 of the 70 algorithm records have no node"; its role table said `benchmark-circuit 112 / algorithm-reference 70`. Live: `benchmark-circuit 120 · operator 62 · algorithm-reference 62 · gate-primitive 27 · state 12`. Eight records were reclassified from `algorithm-reference` to `benchmark-circuit` at some point, which moves the eligible denominator — the exact number that file's argument is about — without touching a line of it. The total (283) is the invariant; the split is not, and only the split was written down.

## What this changes

- `node scripts/check-layer-graph.mjs --unanchored` prints the 53 records with their titles, plus the role census the denominator comes from. A bare slug does not tell you whether a record is a method the map is missing or a survey no node could honestly anchor, and that judgement is the whole of the work.
- Drifted counts replaced by measured ones, dated, each beside the command that re-derives it. Where a count was load-bearing for an *argument* rather than for the reader — "It has never fired — all 9 anchors are `algorithm-reference`" — it is now stated without the number, which is what the sentence meant.
- `.gitignore`: `node_modules` **without** the trailing slash, in addition to the existing line. A trailing slash matches directories only, so a `node_modules` *symlink* — the cheap way to give a fresh worktree deps so a checker can run in it — is not ignored and `git add -A` tracks it as a symlink. That happened to me on #389 an hour ago and cost an amended commit.

No behaviour change. Rules, errors and exit status are untouched; the new output is behind a flag that defaults off.

## What the list says, and why it is the next piece of work

38 of the 53 are `vqe-*`. The rest are the textbook set — QFT, Grover, Shor, teleportation, superdense coding, phase estimation, quantum counting, quantum walk, QAOA, adiabatic evolution, QITE, quantum-kernel SVM.

The map's 82 nodes are one pipeline: linear-ODE solving and Hamiltonian simulation. There is no region a variational method could hang from, so those 38 are not missing cross-links — they are a family the map has no shape for. Which is the owner's standing principle exactly: *"if the map can't hold something that literature truly has, then the map needs restructuring not a workaround the literature."*

Two prior rulings bound whatever comes next, and neither blocks it:

- **D98.1 (2026-08-08)** names VQE as the motivating case for `closure` — *"iteration loop type algorithms, like vqe and some integrators, which run iteratively over several states/processes"*. A VQE region is the canonical `closure: "measured"` loop, and that vocabulary already exists.
- **2026-07-19** deliberately left VQE and QAOA prose-only for *comparison metrics*, being heuristics without a proven worst-case speedup. That constrains cost fields — no invented complexity — and says nothing about map presence.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-layer-graph.mjs --quiet` → `✓ layer graph valid (82 nodes)`, exit 0.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/repository-map-eligibility.test.ts` → 0 fail.
- `--unanchored` output inspected; role census sums to 283, matching the census line's own denominator.

author: frolyo
body:
Closes #4150.

## The problem

The iOS share extension's contact picker lets you select several chats at once, but nothing summarized the selection — only the per-row checkmarks, which scroll out of view. You could tap Send without knowing whether you'd armed two chats or five.

## The change

**`ShareUI` had no count to show.** Selection was tracked as a bare `MutableState<bool> CanSend`, so "how many" wasn't observable. That's now a `GetSelectedCount` compute method over `_selectedIds`, invalidated alongside `IsContactSelected` on each toggle — mirroring the pattern already in the file rather than making the set itself a state. That keeps per-contact granularity: toggling a row still recomputes only that row's `ContactView`, while the badge picks up the new count.

**`CounterBadgeView`** is a `UILabel` that hides itself at zero and overrides `IntrinsicContentSize` to add horizontal padding with an 18pt floor, so "1" renders as a circle and "12" grows into a pill. It's `SystemBlue` to match the button's tint — this is a confirmation of intent, not an alert, so the unread-badge red would have read wrong.

**Placement.** The badge sits inline, 6pt to the left of the title, vertically centered on the button. A corner badge was the first attempt and didn't survive the device: the header leaves only ~23pt between the sheet's top and the button, so it collided with the sheet's rounded top-right corner and sat ~4pt from the screen edge.

`ContactSelectionView` drives both `Enabled` and the badge from one `UpdateSendButton(model)`, shared by the initial render and later state changes, so the two can't drift.

## Trimming

`CounterBadgeView` needs a `CodeKeeper.Keep<>` entry in `IosShareExtAotSource`: it's a `UIView` subclass whose `IntrinsicContentSize` override is dispatched from ObjC, so Release would otherwise trim it and the badge would size itself wrong.

## Verification

Built and deployed to a physical iPhone (15 Pro Max), confirming the rebuilt appex carried the new type. The screenshot that caught the corner-badge collision is what drove the inline placement; the current position was re-verified on device.

author: setilanaji
body:
Docs only. No code, no version change.

> **Stacked on #9** (which is stacked on #8), so the diff shows only the Track I doc change. Base retargets automatically as those merge.

## What this settles

`docs/ROADMAP.md` said Track I had an "open question worth settling first: whether the scope fix justifies the risk". The plan named `Socket`'s interface width as **the main cost** and the reason to hesitate.

Measured against the Dart SDK in this repo (3.41.9), that estimate is **roughly 6x too pessimistic**.

`Socket implements Stream<Uint8List>, IOSink`, and `Stream` alone declares ~119 members. But `dart:async` ships `class StreamView<T> extends Stream<T>` (`async/stream.dart:2309`), which implements every one of them by forwarding to an inner stream and needs only `listen`. So:

```dart
class _ThrottledSocket extends StreamView<Uint8List> implements Socket
```

leaves ~**21** members to hand-write, not ~140:

- `Socket`'s own (10): `destroy`, `setOption`, `setRawOption`, `addError`, `port`, `remotePort`, `address`, `remoteAddress`, `close`, `done`
- `IOSink` (11): `add`, `write`, `writeAll`, `writeln`, `writeCharCode`, `addError`, `addStream`, `flush`, `close`, `done`, `encoding`

Both hooks confirmed present as the plan described: `connectionFactory` (`_http/http.dart:1547`) and `HttpOverrides.global` (`_http/overrides.dart:44`).

And this is not new ground for the repo — the same decorator shape already ships twice in `jala_websocket`: `_CapturingWebSocketSink implements WebSocketSink` and `JalaWebSocketChannel extends StreamChannelMixin`.

## What stays risky

Narrower than "wide interface", and all three are testable:

- The **adapter/socket double-charge trap** already named in I2 — both mechanisms pacing one call. One flag checked in two places, with a test asserting total elapsed time matches a single application of the cap. This is the real correctness hazard.
- **`jala_core` is currently `dart:io`-free** — needs a conditional import following the `file_jala_mock_store_io.dart` / `_stub.dart` pattern.
- `setOption` / `setRawOption` semantics on a wrapped socket, which have no analogue in the existing WebSocket decorators.

## Changes

- Records the measurement under the plan's Open question 1
- Corrects **I1**, which still asserted the claim this disproves
- Updates the roadmap line that repeated it

**Starting Track I is now a scheduling call rather than a feasibility one.** This PR does not decide whether to schedule it.

body: ## Summary Verified and hardened server-side idempotency for `POST /api/chats/{chatId}/messages` keyed by `(chat_id, sender_id, client_id)`. ### Already in place - Unique index `idx_messages_client_id` on `(chat_id, sender_id, client_id)` (migration 018) - `SendMessage` pre-insert lookup + unique-violation fallback - Handler skips WS/push when `created=false` and still returns the existing message ### Fix On unique violation, the insert TX is **rolled back before** re-looking up by `clientId`. With SQLite `MaxOpenConns(1)`, querying while the failed TX still held the only pool connection deadlocked concurrent duplicate retries. ### Tests - First send / duplicate send - Lost-ACK retry (same `clientId` → same message id, one row) - Equal ciphertext with different `clientId`s → two rows - Scope: same `clientId` across different chat/sender does not conflict - Concurrent race on one `clientId` - HTTP-layer coverage in `TestSendMessageHTTPIdempotency` ### DoD Duplicate POST with the same chat + sender + `clientId` cannot create a second logical message row.

author: naveenkumarsp
body:
## Summary
Grafana can be deployed behind a reverse proxy at a sub-path  exposed through `config.appSubUrl`.  This plugin's `fetch()` calls that used hardcoded absolute paths bypassed that sub-path, breaking every request in that deployment topology. Grafana SDK's own `getBackendSrv().fetch()`  already resolves sub-paths correctly, so this only touches the raw `fetch()` call sites. 

  ## Changes
  - Add `src/utils/subpath.ts`: `pluginUrl()` for this plugin's own resource routes, `withSubpath()` for other-origin routes (Grafana core, other plugins).
  - Route `agentClient.ts`, `agentTopologyClient.ts`, `backendSessionClient.ts`     through `pluginUrl()`.
  - Route `llmModels.ts` (grafana-llm-app) and `useEmbeddingAllowed.ts`  (Grafana core `/api/health`) through `withSubpath()` instead — these aren't this plugin's own resource route, so `pluginUrl()` would double the path prefix.
  
  ## Test plan
  - [x] `tsc --noEmit`
  - [x] `eslint` on changed files
  - [x] `jest` — new `subpath.test.ts` plus existing suites for the touched clients (23/23 passing)
  - [x] Manual verification using sub-path based grafana deployment (I tested this locally; happy to share repro steps if
  useful for review)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches all frontend HTTP entry points for the agent and sessions; mis-prefixing would break requests in sub-path installs, though behavior at root is covered by unit tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes broken **raw `fetch()`** calls when Grafana is served under a reverse-proxy sub-path (`config.appSubUrl`).
> 
> Adds **`src/utils/subpath.ts`** with `getSubpath()`, `withSubpath()` for Grafana core and other plugins, and `pluginUrl()` for this plugin’s resource routes. **Agent, topology, session, LLM model, and embedding health** clients now build URLs through those helpers instead of hardcoded absolute paths. **`subpath.test.ts`** covers root and `/grafana` prefix behavior.
> 
> **`package.json` overrides** bump transitive deps (`js-yaml`, `fast-uri`, plus new pins for `ip-address` and `nanoid`); **`package-lock.json`** reflects those versions.
>

author: xdyasser
body:
## The name

`Hub` → **Devotions** / **الأوراد**.

`المفاتيح` was never the Arabic for "hub" — it is the plural of "key", and in an app that ships *Mafātīḥ al-Jinān* it names one of the books on the shelf rather than the door they sit behind. What is behind that door is the Qur'an read, the dhikr counted, the duʿāʾ said, the fast marked: **الأوراد**, the portions of worship a person keeps to daily. The English moves with it — `Devotions` is the word the code has used for this all along (`DevotionRepository`, `container.devotions`).

## The sweep

The table was complete. What was not was the reaching of it — 21 files' worth of strings that never went through `t()`.

**Domain words with translations nobody was calling.** The madhab list and the school note beside it, the branch (`Sunnī`/`Shīʿī`), the fasting calendar's day labels, the sixteen points of the compass, the two reciter traditions. All of them already had Arabic sitting in `DOMAIN`; every call site printed the raw string.

**The four tiers.** `AppTier.FAVORITE.name.lowercase().take(4)` gives `favo` and `allo` in English and four letters of nothing in Arabic. Replaced with `tierName` / `tierPill` in `Localization.kt`.

**Every duration.** `45m`, `2h 30m`, `30s` — the h and the m and the s are English words cut to one letter, and they appear at the gate, in the budgets, on the friction knobs and on every pending change. Now `45 د`, `2 س 30 د`, `30 ث`.

**Every queued change.** `RuleMutator` wrote its fifteen descriptions in English, and the pending-changes screen showed them verbatim.

**Everything Android reads rather than draws.** A new `values-ar/strings.xml` for the app name, the device-admin warning, the notification channels and the accessibility-service description — the fourteen strings the system reads off resources on screens the app never sees.

**Singles that had slipped the net.** The strip heading in appearance; the āyāt count under the gate; the adb instructions; three `queued — takes effect at` notices written three different ways in three files; the prayer-times listing, which named prayers by lowercasing the enum and so read `asr` and `isha` in both languages; and one sentence about handoff that was half translated and half not, because the app's name was concatenated into the middle of it.

**Two bugs found on the way.** `SupplicationCollection.MAFATIH.attribution` had drifted from its table key (`· complete` vs `· a selection`), so it fell through to English. And `BackLine` put a chevron in front of a label that already carried one, pointing the one direction Arabic does not read — nothing called it, so it goes.

## Verification

The Android Gradle Plugin cannot be resolved from this environment (Google Maven is blocked by the proxy), so **the build was not run locally** — CI on this push is the first compile. What was checked instead:

- Every `t("…")` literal in `app/src/main` cross-checked against the table: **0 call sites without Arabic**.
- All 491 table entries checked for duplicate keys, placeholder-count mismatches between key and value, untranslated values, and values with no Arabic in them: **0 problems**.
- Two new tests in `LocalizationTest` lock in the tier words and the duration units in both languages.

---
