author: gradkh
body:
## The problem

Three instances of the same failure mode: a Postgres-gated suite that reports `ok` forever without executing.

| | Cases | Why it never ran |
|---|---|---|
| `pgvector_span_instrumentation.rs` | 3 | The `pgvector-spans` lane ran `cargo test -p cognee-vector --test pgvector_span_instrumentation` with **no `--features`**. The target is `#![cfg(feature = "pgvector")]` and `cognee-vector` declares no `default` features, so the file compiled away: `running 0 tests`, exit 0, green — since the day the lane was added, while paying for an idle `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` container. |
| `pgvector_integration.rs` + 2 inline adapter cases | 26 | No job ever set `PGVECTOR_TEST_URL`. |
| `provenance_batch.rs` (2 of 3), `pg_shared_db_single_stack.rs`, `pg_full_stack_e2e.rs` | 4 | No job ever set `TEST_POSTGRES_URL`. |

Verified on `4db8bbf3`, before any change:

```
$ cargo test -p cognee-vector --test pgvector_span_instrumentation -- --nocapture
running 0 tests
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; ...
```

`git log -S '#![cfg(feature = "pgvector")]'` confirms the gate has been there since the initial commit and `pgvector` has never been a default feature — broken from the start, not a regression.

## Real defects the newly-running tests found

**1. The three span cases were missing a precondition (test bug).** All three failed on their first ever execution:

```
thread 'upsert_emits_pgvector_span' panicked at crates/vector/tests/pgvector_span_instrumentation.rs:51:10:
upsert: StorageError("Query Error: error returned from database: relation \"DocumentChunk_text\" does not exist")
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed;
```

They call `index_points` without creating the collection. **Concluded: the test is wrong, not the adapter.** Every `VectorDB` impl in the workspace requires the collection to exist first — `BruteForceVectorDB` returns `CollectionNotFound`, LanceDB fails to `open_table`, pgvector's INSERT hits a missing relation — the entire shared `tests/common` conformance suite calls `create_collection` first, and the production callers in `cognee-cognify` all do `has_collection` → `create_collection` before indexing (`tasks.rs:2870`). Python's `create_data_points` auto-creates instead (`PGVectorAdapter.py:278`), but that is a difference in *where the responsibility sits*, not in observable pipeline behaviour. Fixed by establishing the precondition in `make_adapter()`, with `expect` rather than `.ok()?` so a create failure fails the test instead of degrading into the skip path this lane exists to detect.

**2. `reset()` orphaned collection tables and poisoned the next run (test-hygiene bug).** The two inline `shared_db_migration_tests` cases shared the `PGVECTOR_TEST_URL` database and called a `reset()` that dropped `_vector_collections` and the `seaql_migrations*` tables — but not the collection tables it did not know about. `UUID_f`, `Meta_f` etc. survived, invisible to `list_collections`, so the integration suite's cleanup could not delete them:

```
thread 'test_uuid_round_trip' panicked at crates/vector/tests/common/mod.rs:197:48:
StorageError("Execution Error: error returned from database: relation \"UUID_f\" already exists")
```

Only reachable once both targets run in one lane against one server — i.e. it was latent until this PR. Fixed by giving each case its own throwaway database via `create_temp_postgres_db` (the #136 pattern), which also removes the `#[serial]` attributes. Proven idempotent by running the whole lane sequence twice back-to-back.

**3. `pg_full_stack_e2e` required a model no CI job downloads.** It demanded `COGNEE_E2E_EMBED_MODEL_PATH` + `COGNEE_E2E_TOKENIZER_PATH` (BGE-Small ONNX). Nothing in `scripts/` or `.github/` fetches it, and the workspace moved to OpenAI embeddings by default. The ONNX pair is now optional; without it embeddings come from the same OpenAI-compatible account as the LLM (`Settings::resolve_embedding_inputs` already falls endpoint/key back to `llm_*`). **No assertion was weakened** — the test asserts ComponentManager wiring plus non-empty graph/vector output, and nothing depends on which backend produced the vectors. It also now uses a throwaway database: its "non-empty" assertions were satisfiable by leftovers from an earlier run, and its cleanup ran `delete_graph()` against whatever database `TEST_POSTGRES_URL` named — destructive on a developer's own instance.

Two smaller finds: `cargo test -p cognee-database --features postgres` fails the file's third (SQLite) case with `has no supporting driver`, because that crate declares no default features — the lane passes `--features sqlite,postgres`. And the span tests' skip message (`DB_PROVIDER!=postgres — skipping …`) did not match the guard's variable-agnostic `[A-Z_]+ not set .* skipping` glob, so it is reworded.

## Proof the suites execute

All six targets, locally against `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`:

```
--test pgvector_integration          -> running 24 tests   test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed;
--lib                                -> running 34 tests   test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed;
--test pgvector_span_instrumentation -> running 3 tests    test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed;
--test provenance_batch              -> running 3 tests    test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed;
--test pg_shared_db_single_stack     -> running 1 test     test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed;
--test pg_full_stack_e2e             -> running 1 test     test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed;
```

Named cases, zero `... not set — skipping` lines:

```
test upsert_emits_pgvector_span ... ok
test search_emits_pgvector_span ... ok
test delete_emits_pgvector_span ... ok
test pgvector_adapter::shared_db_migration_tests::pgvector_coexists_with_relational_migrator_in_shared_db ... ok
test pgvector_adapter::shared_db_migration_tests::pgvector_purges_legacy_row_from_default_table_on_upgrade ... ok
test postgres::upsert_batch_with_duplicate_ids_dedups_keeping_last ... ok
test postgres::temp_database_supports_back_to_back_initialize ... ok
test relational_pgvector_pggraph_coexist_in_one_database ... ok
test pg_full_stack_add_and_cognify ... ok
```

**33 cases that had never executed once now do.** CI job logs are linked in the first review comment.

## The guard: generalized, not copied

`assert_pggraph_suite_ran.sh` → `scripts/ci/assert_pg_suite_ran.sh`, with `--label` / `--log … --min-tests N` (repeatable) / `--require-test NAME` (repeatable). **Generalized rather than copied** because its skip-marker matching was already variable-agnostic — only the count floor and the inline test names were hard-coded, so parameterising two things was a smaller change than a third 130-line copy, and one script cannot drift across six YAML call sites. All three lanes call it; the pggraph invocation is behaviour-preserving.

Every check was exercised against captured logs, positive and negative:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| pggraph real run (**nextest** format, 32 + 24) | passes — no regression for the existing lane |
| pgvector real run (**libtest** format, 24 + 34 + 3) | passes |
| single-database real run (3 + 1 + 1) | passes |
| `--features` dropped → `running 0 tests`, cargo exits **0** | `::error::only 0 tests passed in zero.log, expected at least 3` |
| URL unset → 24 skips, cargo exits **0** | `::error::PgVector tests skipped — the suite never reached a live Postgres` |
| `DB_PROVIDER` unset (interleaved mid-line: `test delete_… ... DB_PROVIDER not set to postgres — skipping …`) | caught — confirms the unanchored match is load-bearing |
| log missing / unreadable | `::error::… is missing or empty` (grep's exit 2 must not read as "clean") |
| required test name absent | `::error::required test … did not run (or did not pass)` |
| `--min-tests` not following its `--log`, or a `--log` with no floor | usage error, so a misordered invocation cannot leave a log unchecked |
| `--require-test 'a.*b'` | rejected — a bare name, never a pattern |

## Lane structure

**`pgvector-spans` →

author: turtton
body:
## Summary

Replace `ShuttlePub/workflows/.github/workflows/<wf>.yml@main` self-references in `coverage.yml` and `bench.yml` with the workspace-relative `./.github/workflows/<wf>.yml` form already used by `check.yml`, `test-psql.yml`, and `test-consumers.yml`.

## Why

Renovate's `github-actions` manager treats `owner/repo/path@ref` as an external dependency. These self-references caused Renovate to repeatedly open PRs re-pinning `@main` to the latest commit SHA — an unbounded stream of patch PRs for references that are always in the same repository.

The `./` form is not recognized as a remote dependency, so Renovate stops emitting PRs for them. It resolves to the same repository at the same ref, which is exactly the desired behavior.

## Why not `$/` (self-repository syntax)

The [2026-07-30 changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-reference-same-repository-actions-with-self-repository-syntax/) introduces `$/` as the recommended syntax. Runtime support is confirmed (all consumer tests passed in a trial PR), but **actionlint v1.7.12 does not recognize `$/`** (issue [rhysd/actionlint#711](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/711) open, author inactive per [#719](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/719)). The Lint workflows gate fails, blocking merge.

This PR uses `./` which actionlint already accepts. Migration to `$/` can happen once actionlint adds support.

## Changes

| File | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `coverage.yml:11` | `ShuttlePub/workflows/.github/workflows/read-toolchain.yml@main` | `./.github/workflows/read-toolchain.yml` |
| `bench.yml:17` | `ShuttlePub/workflows/.github/workflows/read-toolchain.yml@main` | `./.github/workflows/read-toolchain.yml` |
| `bench.yml:19` | `ShuttlePub/workflows/.github/workflows/detect-workspaces.yml@main` | `./.github/workflows/detect-workspaces.yml` |

## Verification

- `Lint workflows` (actionlint + zizmor) must pass.
- `test-consumers` exercises `check.yml` and `test-psql.yml` (which already use `./`) — confirms the pattern works at runtime.
- `coverage.yml` and `bench.yml` are `workflow_call`-only; their `./` resolution uses the identical mechanism already proven by `check.yml`.

author: matejgomboc
body:
## Description

Addresses the three AI review findings on `src/util.rs` and `src/mcp/tools/maintenance.rs`. Each was verified against the code before applying — one turned out to be a trap:

### 1. `sanitise_file_name` — applied the safe half only
The `bytes()` micro-optimisation is applied (and the redundant `is_empty` check folds into it, since `all` on an empty iterator is `true`). The finding's *main* suggestion — tracking `has_non_underscore` during the map pass to skip the second scan — was **rejected as incorrect**: an input like `"<>."` maps to `"__."` and trims to `"__"`; the dot would set the flag and the suggested code returns `Some("__")` where the current code correctly returns `None`. The usability check must run on the *trimmed* string. Regression tests now pin this (`"<>."` and `"__ ."` → `None`) so the suggestion can't be applied later by accident.

### 2. `generate_unique_id` — applied as suggested
Per-call `Vec<char>` replaced with `const ALPHABET: &[u8; 26]`.

### 3. `parse_layer` — applied, but further than suggested
The finding proposed extracting the three ~100-line numbered-family tables into a helper — which would keep the duplication it complains about. Instead the aliases now delegate to `Layer::parse` via the canonical Altium name (`"mechanical17"` → `Layer::parse("Mechanical 17")`), making the `Layer` enum the single source of truth: new variants are picked up automatically and out-of-range numbers (`Mechanical33`, `MidLayer31`, `InternalPlane17`) fall out as `None` — now covered by tests alongside the family range boundaries.

Net: **+39 / −99 lines.** Full suite passes locally (720 unit + integration), clippy clean under `-D warnings`.

author: archeltaneka
body:
## What changed

- Added 13 deterministic repository-local Phase 4 reference cases covering eligibility validation, descriptive statistics, continuous randomized analysis, binary randomized analysis, invalid inputs, and expected abstentions.
- Added structured reference-accuracy, abstention-correctness, diagnostic-completeness, uncertainty-completeness, status-semantics, determinism, and row-order-invariance evaluation.
- Added authoritative JSON and derived Markdown baseline reports with explicit per-field tolerance rationale and provenance.
- Extended the existing ExperimentOS evaluation CLI, centralized quality policy, CI reporting, artifact conventions, and GitHub Actions orchestration instead of introducing parallel Phase 4 infrastructure.
- Extended randomized-analysis observability with low-cardinality aggregate metadata, eligible-row counts, provider-failure isolation, and explicit privacy tests.
- Included the completed descriptive-statistics surface required by the Phase 4 baseline because it was not present on `main`.
- Documented evaluated capabilities, policy semantics, telemetry privacy, CLI usage, CI behavior, artifacts, and current limitations.

## Reliability behavior

- Expected invalid and abstained outcomes remain distinct from quality failures.
- Successful inference cannot pass without point estimates, standard errors where required, confidence intervals, confidence metadata, p-values where required, method/estimand metadata, and sample counts.
- Blocking rules cover reference regressions, incorrect abstention behavior, incomplete uncertainty, missing diagnostics, nondeterminism, incorrect statuses, and non-finite results.
- Advisory rules do not fail CI.
- Statistical count fields are parsed as strict non-negative integers.
- Telemetry never emits raw outcomes, covariates, rows, credentials, prompts, private payloads, or arbitrary analysis IDs.

## Offline command

```powershell
uv run python -m packages.evals.cli statistical-baseline
```

The command writes:

- `reports/phase4/statistical_baseline.json`
- `reports/phase4/statistical_baseline.md`

It exits 0 for a blocking-policy pass, 1 for a blocking quality failure, and 2 for an infrastructure or malformed-dataset failure.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q` — **1027 passed**, with one existing LangChain deprecation warning.
- `uv run ruff check .` — **passed**.
- `uv run mypy` — **passed (40 source files)**.
- `uv run python -m packages.evals.cli statistical-baseline` — **passed; 13/13 cases passed**.
- Phase 3 offline verification — **all 14 stages passed**.
- Existing centralized quality-policy command — **passed**.
- Independent review — **no Critical or Important findings remaining**.

## Migration and environment notes

- No database migration.
- No dependency or lockfile change.
- No new environment variable or secret.
- No live LLM, external judge, network service, database, or hosted telemetry provider is required.
- No synthetic experiment generator change.

## Scope limitations

This does not add CUPED, sequential testing, Bayesian inference, Difference-in-Differences, propensity methods, observational treatment-effect estimation, DML, HTE, EconML, DoWhy, business-impact estimation, or product-intelligence workflow integration.

Closes #92

body:
### Motivation
- Ship the approved TradeBuilt V2 assessment (version `tradebuilt-contractor-health-check-v2.0`) as a standalone Contractor Health Check product with deterministic V2 engine contract compatibility and a clear free/paid boundary. 
- Replace legacy V1 UI/score plumbing where required, preserve frozen V1 interpretation for completed legacy results, and remove benchmark/action-plan leakage from free outputs.

### Description

author: jakechampion
body:
One call — `tagof(o.v)`, after the loop — cost the struct local `o` its **entire** reclaim credit. `fieldmove_expr` (the NODEEP field-move scan) reads every non-scalar field read in a direct call argument as a move, so the local was marked `NODEEP:` and `__field_reclaim_S` was never called at all, nor `__struct_drop_S`. Every superseded box and the `xs` buffer it owned stranded per ITERATION.

Ten calls, x86-64, `FERN_LEAKCHECK=1`:

| k | before | after | native |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1840 B | **880** | 0 |
| 8 | 10240 B | **880** | 0 |
| 32 | **98560 B** | **880** | 0 |

Flat instead of growing with k; the exits (60 / 2 / 50) never moved and match `fern -interp` and native throughout.

## The verdict this needs was already computed, and already trusted for more

`borrowable_params_of` admits a param only when the callee provably never returns, stores, slices or captures it. `expr_unsafe_for` already consults it for this exact shape one level up — its Level-2 rule, where a bare-ident argument at a borrowable position is a borrow rather than an escape — and that rule licenses caller-side **frees**. Keeping a deep drop is strictly weaker than freeing, so the same registry settles the question here.

Free calls only: method-param borrowability is not in the free-function-keyed registry, so a method argument keeps marking.

## What identified it was the k curve, not the count

Rewriting the call as `var vv: V = o.v; tagof(vv)` — a `var` init, which the same scan already treats as a borrow — restores the credit and lands on 480 B. Both numbers look like "a leak"; only the curve says one is per-iteration and the other per-call. The remaining flat 880 B is the enum payload's shallow-drop model (`k_enum` frees the box, not the payload array), a separate matter, and it is what the new k-sweep holds constant.

## Tests

New `TestSelfHostBorrowedFieldArgReclaimX86_64`:

- **k-sweep** at 1 / 2 / 8 / 32 — byte count must be flat, exit checked per k. Fails on the parent, where the count tracks k.
- **`retaining-callee-still-marks`** — `keep(v: V): V { return v; }` is refused by `borrowable_params_of`, so `var kept = keep(o.v)` keeps `o` marked. The probe reads `kept` back after the rebind loop, so an over-release there is a wrong exit rather than a quieter number. Verified it measures identically on the parent and on this branch, i.e. the exemption does not reach it.

## Verification

- `TestSelfHostBorrowedFieldArgReclaimX86_64` green (70.6 s, 0 skips).
- Whole-compiler self-build with the patched `irlower.fern` succeeds; every probe's exit agrees with `fern -interp` and with native.
- **Still in flight**, running alongside this PR: `TestSelfHostPerModuleEmitAllFixpointX86_64` — the gate that matters most for this change, since it widens deep-drop eligibility across the compiler's own sources. I will report it here and drive CI to green.

Log entry: `docs/RC-PERCEUS-SELF-HOST-PORT.md` §9. Refs #6653, #4451 (native-convergence debt tracker — goal 2).

author: mengwong
body:
**Replaces eight `aug2026` PRs that cannot land separately:** #245 `lang-syntax-typecheck`, #241
`lang-eval-ledger`, #240 `ladder-viz`, #243 `lang-printer`, #246 `lsp`, #244 `lang-sets`, #242
`lang-imports-stdlib`, #230 `actus-archive`.

## Why those eight had to be consolidated

The `aug2026` split is by **file**, but several of the changes are atomic at the **type** level.
`jl4-core/src/L4/Syntax.hs` removes the `Expr` constructor `Exponent`, widens `MkAssume` 4→5,
`MkTypedName` 4→5 and `MkOptionallyTypedName` 3→4 (the `TYPICALLY` default), adds
`Record` / `ReadCell` / `RecallMode` and `unqualifiedNameToText`, and adds strict fields to
`MkCheckState` and `MkCheckEnv`. `L4/EvaluateLazy` widens `MkEvalDirectiveResult` 3→4.

Every consumer of those types must change in the *same commit*, and the consumers are spread across
six packages: `jl4-core`, `jl4-lsp`, `jl4-mlir`, `jl4-repl`, `jl4-service` and
`jl4-actus-analyzer`. The dependency runs **both ways** — land `Syntax.hs` alone and other modules
name a constructor that is gone; land any of those alone and it meets `main`'s unchanged types.
No ordering, and no amount of rebasing, resolves that.

None of this is visible to import-level dependency analysis, because every one of those types lives
in a module `main` already has. It was found by building.

Two members would not have been found by reading at all:

- **`actus-archive`.** `jl4-actus-analyzer` is on `main` and in `main`'s `cabal.project`, so
  `cabal build all` compiles it, and `FeatureExtractor.hs:519` matches `MkTypedName` with 4
  arguments. CI on any single PR never reaches it — the build dies inside `jl4-core` first.
- **`lsp`.** `LSP/L4/Inspector.hs` matches `EL.MkEvalDirectiveResult` with 3 arguments in five
  places, behind the same wall.

## How it was built — no hand-written intermediate code

Start from #245 + #241; build; take **unstable's** version of whatever the compiler rejects; repeat
to a fixed point. Six rounds.

Every file here is byte-identical to `origin/unstable`, with exactly two classes of exception:

1. the four shared build files — `cabal.project`, `jl4-core/jl4-core.cabal`, `jl4/jl4.cabal`,
   `jl4/tests/Main.hs` — which are the union of their per-slice edits, as in every other `aug2026` PR;
2. one golden, noted below.

An earlier attempt hand-wrote minimal repairs instead (add a `_`, delete a case arm). It was
abandoned at ~60 repair sites across five packages, still not building. It also surfaced a trap
worth recording: **`MkTypedName`'s new field is inserted at position 4, not appended**, so
`MkTypedName _ a ty Nothing` must become `_ a ty _ Nothing`. The naive append *compiles* and
silently matches the wrong field.

### One file the fixed point could not see — added 13 August

`jl4-wasm/app/QueryPlanWasm.hs`. `jl4-wasm` is **not in `cabal.project`** — the WASM target builds
under its own project and compiler — so `cabal build all` never reached it, and the six-round loop
above could not converge on a file it never compiled. The partition had left it with
[#252](https://github.com/legalese/l4-ide/pull/252), which made these two PRs a **cycle rather than
an ordering**: this branch carried `unstable`'s `VizExpr` (`UBoolVar` widened 5→6) against `main`'s
five-argument pattern match, while #252 carried the updated call site against `main`'s `VizExpr`. The
WASM job failed on both, in mirror image — `should have 6 arguments, but has been given 5` here,
`does not export ‘boolPriorsFromBody’` there — and no merge order cleared it.

The file now sits here, alongside the `VizExpr` and `jl4-query-plan` modules it is compiled against,
and #252 falls back to `main`'s copy, which matches the `VizExpr` #252 ships against. It is
byte-identical to `origin/unstable`, so it does not join the exception list above. Found by CI, not
locally; the table below is unaffected, because none of those suites build this target.

## Verification (local, GHC 9.10.3)

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `cabal build all` | clean |
| `cabal test all` | **7 / 7 suites pass** |
| `jl4-test` | **2039 examples, 0 failures** |
| `jl4-core-test` | 269 / 0 |
| `jl4-service-test` | 341 / 0 |
| `l4-cli-test` | 20 / 0 |
| `jl4-lsp-test` | 10 / 0 |
| `jl4-mlir-test` | pass |
| `jl4-websessions-test` | 1 / 0 |

## Goldens

Twelve goldens that the partition had assigned to `dmn-export`, `service-cli` and
`corpus-legal-new` turn out to belong here: this tree reproduces `unstable`'s version of each
**byte-for-byte**, so they are taken verbatim rather than re-blessed. They had been mis-attributed
by `partition.mjs`'s pass-3 fallback, which assigns an orphaned golden to "the theme of the PR that
last touched the file".

One — `jl4/examples/legal/tests/promissory-note.ep.golden` — is a genuine intermediate state and is
re-blessed here. **#234 `corpus-legal-new`** re-blesses it again later (an earlier revision said
`dmn-export`, which was wrong): an exactprint golden reproduces its source *including comments*,
this PR carries the repaired printer against the old source, and #234 lands a comment sync in
`promissory-note.l4` together with the final golden — measured, the delta between the two versions
is byte-for-byte that comment sync. So the order is this PR first, then #234. **It is the only file
in this PR that differs from `unstable` on purpose.**

## What this leaves for the other PRs

| PR | keeps | which is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #252 `service-cli` | 13 files | the `l4` CLI subcommands (its `jl4-service`, `jl4-query-plan` and `jl4-core` library modules move here, and `jl4-wasm/app/QueryPlanWasm.hs` followed on 13 August) |
| #247 `mlir` | 48 files | the parity harness, runtime, probes and docs (its 4 source modules, `app/Main.hs` and `test/Main.hs` move here) |
| #236 / #232 / #250 | unchanged | the DMN, BPMN and OpenFisca exporters |
| #249 `proleg` | unchanged | — |

Everything downstream of this PR is a one-way dependency: a genuine DAG that can be toposorted and
reviewed PR by PR.

## Reviewing this

It is large — 1,036 files — but it is one thing, and nothing in it is new. Every line has already
been through review on `unstable` as one of the 39 upstream PRs listed in the commit message. The
useful review question is therefore not "is this code correct?" but "is this the right *boundary*?"
— and the answer to that is mechanical and reproducible: it is the least fixed point of "what does
the compiler demand", which anyone can re-derive by building.
---

# What is actually in here

The eight PRs this replaces are **closed, not deleted** — each remains readable in full, and is
linked below for its file-by-file inventory. What follows is the part a reviewer cannot reconstruct
from the diff: what each theme does, why, and the measurements its source PRs recorded.

Two things to read past. Where a theme's text says a sibling "must land with this" or describes a
one-line interaction with another theme, that coupling is now **internal to this PR** — it is
preserved because it explains *why* the boundary falls where it does. And the `Independence`,
`Risk if rejected` and batch-roster sections are dropped throughout: they answered a question
("can this land alone?") that consolidation has settled.

---

## `lang-syntax-typecheck` — front end & typechecker

*Was #245; see it for the full file-by-file inventory.*

**What this adds**

This is the L4 compiler front end: lexer, parser, annotation attachment, name resolution, unification and the typechecker, together with the corpus of `.l4` fixtures and goldens that pin their behaviour. After it, a library can declare operator precedence and associativity (`@infixl 6` on `UNION`) so unparenthesized word-operator chains re-associate GHC-style instead of failing on arity; deeply nested outlines can be written with `•` bullets that desugar to `LIST`; a multi-clause pattern-matching `DECIDE` is analysed as a clause *matrix* so incomplete decision tables are reported instead of silently nulling at runtime; unqualified nam

author: xiaodoudou
body:
The outline drawn while the trigger key is held is now opt-in, under **Outline what would be translated** in the popup, and off by default.

The key is held for a moment before every single translation, so an outline that is always on is a box drawn on the page nearly every time the user reaches for the shortcut. It is worth having while you are learning what a tap takes, and worth turning off once you know.

### What changed

- `aimOutline: false` in `DEFAULTS`, with the other trigger settings.
- `onAim` resolves the block only when the setting is on, so with it off the hold costs nothing it did not cost before the outline existed. It is still called, so an outline drawn before the setting was switched off is cleared by the same press rather than left on the page.
- A `No` / `Yes` select in the popup, next to the trigger key.

### Docs

The README's Use table and the store listing now say the outline is optional. The README also drops a line that had it backwards: it said to "let go if it is the wrong one", which is exactly what translates the wrong one. Moving off it, or pressing any other key, is what cancels.

### Tests

The e2e holds the key twice. First on the default, where nothing may be outlined, ended by typing Ctrl+C so that press fires nothing; then with the setting on for the shape checks that were already there. 190 checks pass, and `package.test.mjs` is green.

Use a combination approach that cannot be reset by a rooted later segment. The best fix is to normalize the base directory first and then append the filename with `Path.Join` instead of `Path.Combine`. `Path.Join` concatenates path segments without the rooted-path reset behavior of `Path.Combine`, which directly addresses the CodeQL concern while preserving current functionality (`<base>/settings.json`).

In `example.csharp.greeter/GreeterPlugin.cs`, replace the static `SettingsPath` initializer (lines 8–10 in the snippet) so it uses `Path.Join(...)` with the same base-directory expression and `"settings.json"`. No new imports, methods, or dependencies are required.

body:
Part 4/4 of the offline-delegation split (replaces #1815). Based on #1820.

Wires `DIAL_NATIVE` into on-behalf-of retrieval: redemption requires an administrator's consent record (only one the consent endpoint wrote counts), then acts through the owner's offline credentials, refreshed via the offline client of the issuing identity provider. Failures stay distinguishable: missing/rejected owner credentials → permanent 409, unreachable IdP → retryable 502, lost provider config → 503. Status becomes honest for DIAL-native services: app level reflects consent, user level reflects the caller's offline credentials (`ExternalServiceStatusEnricher`).

The final state of this stack matches #1815 (verified e2e on Keycloak and Entra ID) except for review-driven cleanups made during the split.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The installer runs, the shortcut appears, and clicking it does nothing. Two independent faults, both of which kill the process *before* `createWindow()` — so none of the careful error dialogs in `main.js` ever get a chance to render.

**1. The SQLite binary in the installer is built for the wrong runtime.**
`better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers@13.x` started shipping prebuilt N-API binaries, and its `binding.gyp` skips compiling when it finds one. So `electron-rebuild` prints `✔ Rebuild Complete` having produced nothing but a stamp file:

```
build/Release/            <- 13.0.3, after electron-rebuild
  obj.target/better_sqlite3.stamp   # no better_sqlite3.node anywhere
prebuilds/win32-x64.node            # ...this is what gets packaged
```

`openLocalDatabase()` runs before the window opens, and loading that prebuild inside Electron **segfaults** — no window, no dialog, no log. Reproduced here: `new Database(':memory:')` dies with SIGSEGV under Electron 33 (and under plain Node 20/22 on this machine too). Pinned to `12.11.1`, exactly, which has no prebuilds, so the rebuild genuinely happens and produces a binary matching Electron's ABI. Also stopped `postinstall` swallowing a failed rebuild with `|| echo`.

**2. A shared file was in no packaging rule.** `net/prepare.js` requires `../../lib/offline/package-token`, which lives at the repo root, outside `desktop/`, and so outside everything in `build.files`. `registerIpc` therefore threw `Cannot find module` and the app quit during startup. It is now copied in as `extraResources` to `resources/lib/offline` — the exact path `../../lib/...` resolves to from inside `app.asar`, so dev and packaged stay identical with no code change.

**Guards**, since both faults were invisible to a build that merely produced an `.exe`:

- `prepack:check` (now run by every `dist:*`) adds `native:check`, which opens an encrypted database *using Electron's own runtime* (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`) and fails if the module ships prebuilds or will not load.
- `npm run smoke` starts the packaged binary and fails if it exits during startup. Added to the Windows workflow after `dist:win`.

## Verification

On this Linux box, packaged with `electron-builder`, installed the `.deb` and ran `/opt/TERECO Collect/tereco-desktop`:

```
[tereco] ready — API https://tereco.vercel.app, loading .../app.asar/renderer/dist/index.html
```

Before the fix, the same binary: `exited with signal SIGSEGV`, then (once SQLite was fixed) `Cannot find module .../lib/offline/package-token`. `npx vitest run desktop` passes 61/61.

Note the Windows installer still has to be built on Windows (existing workflow) — the fix is not platform-specific, but the `.exe` in front of the lab needs a rerun of `Desktop installer` from this branch.

author: jeffreysanford
body:
Follows #53. That PR bounded growth; this one makes the store survive a restart and moves access to it behind the platform.

## The gap

Governance is described throughout this repository as authoritative for job, policy, provenance and audit records. Its only persistence dependency is `spring-boot-starter-data-redis` — there is no relational store behind it. Neither compose file mounted a volume for Redis, while `postgres` and `minio` in the forge stack were both given one.

It surfaced concretely: a job store measured at **2,044,218 keys and 767 MB** disappeared with no purge ever run against it, because removing the container removed the data.

## Persistence

Named volume plus `--appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec`.

Not the RDB defaults — those can leave an hour between saves on a quiet stack, which would silently discard audit history on an unclean stop. `everysec` bounds loss to about a second without paying an fsync on every write, which would land on the ingest path.

**Ordering was the constraint.** Before persistence, an oversized store cleared itself whenever the container was recreated. A volume removes that accidental safety valve, so #53's retention window and memory ceiling had to land first. Doing this in the other order would have made the 767 MB permanent.

## Access through the API

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/admin/job-store` | records, log keys, artifact keys, keys carrying retention, indexed jobs |
| `POST /api/v1/admin/job-store/purge` | `{keepRecent, dryRun}` — **dry run by default**, audited when it deletes |

`scripts/redis-purge-jobs.sh` is now a client of those. Its previous form shelled into `redis-cli`, which bypassed the auth filter, the audit trail, and any record of who ran a destructive sweep over provenance records.

The server-side purge streams the key space rather than collecting it, unlinks in batches so large deletes are freed off the event loop, and trims the createdAt index alongside the records — #44 records that an index entry pointing at a missing record consumes a slot in every listing window and returns nothing for it.

## ADR-008

Records that Redis is the system of record **for now**, what that costs, and two falsifiable triggers for revisiting:

1. Eviction reaching operator-submitted records — the ceiling hit with only unexpiring keys left.
2. Provenance queried as history rather than status — joins across jobs, datasets and source attribution, or retention in months.

`volatile-lru` deletes data under pressure. A store that evicts is not a system of record in the full sense however well it is persisted, and the ADR says that rather than treating the volume as settling it. The relational target already exists and is already persisted — the forge stack's `postgres` — but governance would gain a relational dependency it does not have today, which is why that is not done here.

## Deliberately not changed

The forge stack's Redis stays ephemeral. `FORGE_REDIS_URL` appears **only** in `cosmic-forge-compose.yml` and has no consumer anywhere in the codebase, so persisting it would persist nothing. Possibly dead infrastructure, worth its own look.

## Verification

- Full `java-governance` suite: **24 test classes, 0 failures, 0 errors**.
- `docker compose config` resolves the redis service with the volume and AOF flags.
- `scripts/check-docs.sh` passes; the DECISIONS.md diff is **purely additive — zero deleted lines** (an earlier attempt reflowed three lines of the already-merged ADR-007 and was reverted).
- Purge script fails with an actionable message when governance is absent.

One bug caught in testing worth naming: the script originally defaulted to port `8080`, where an unrelated service answers `200` with HTML — it would have reported against something that was never governance. Governance publishes on **8082**, and the probe now checks for the endpoint's own payload rather than just a 2xx.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: masalasev-ops
body:
Phase 2 builds the compute layer, runs it against real data, reviews it in a session
that did not build it, and corrects what the review found. 27 commits, 2.1 to 2.15
plus the sign-off pass.

`ci.ps1` green at `7f97a92`: `guards.ps1` 5 checks over 84 files, 0 warnings and 0
errors, 5 migrations applied from an empty server, nothing to apply on the second,
**Passed 227, Failed 0**.

## What it builds

Five components, migrations `0004` and `0005`, ten config keys.

| | Component | Writes | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| C08 | IndicatorEngine | `indicator_daily` | 15 technical, ticker-partitioned |
| C09 | ValuationEngine | `valuation_daily` | 13 of which 12 computed |
| C35 | SentimentEngine | `sentiment_derived_daily` | 3 |
| C10 | MarketContextEngine | `market_context_daily` | 4 of which 3 computed |
| C11 | PercentileEngine | 30 `_pctile` columns across 4 tables | date-partitioned |

`run-night 2026-08-10` completed over twelve stages in 14m31s. The compute layer is
14.4 seconds of that; the rest is ingest, 579 seconds of it C05.

## What the phase found by running rather than by reading

**Two components had never executed and both were broken at the write.** C08 read back
a `percentile_cont` result as `decimal?` where the aggregate returns a double, and C10
wrote a `jsonb` column through binary COPY as `text`, which Postgres refused with
"unsupported jsonb version number 123". Both had thorough tests and every one passed,
because neither defect is reachable by an arithmetic test: one is the type an aggregate
returns, the other is the format byte a COPY stream carries.

## The sign-off review

Ran at `4ccf342` in a session with no commit in this repository, per `CLAUDE.md` §3. It
reproduced step 1 rather than taking it on trust and then went past it. Committed
separately as `a0bb916` with its attribution stated, so the section was written by a
session that had not committed here.

**It recomputed rather than re-read.** All 15 indicator columns and all 12 computed
valuation columns, rebuilt from the raw bars in a separate program over seven names
chosen so the adjustment has something to do: `NFLX.US` (10-for-1 split), `BKNG.US`
(25-for-1 plus dividends), `KLAC.US` (10-for-1 plus dividends), `OHI.US` (a dividend
inside the 20-bar dollar-volume window), `NOKBF.US` and `TBNK.US` (interior gaps),
`MH.US` (a zero-priced bar). 105 indicator cells and 93 valuation cells all agree, worst
relative difference 1.10e-7 against float32's own 1.2e-7.

It also computed each column **the wrong way**, because agreement proves nothing unless
the wrong reading gives a different answer. `KLAC.US` `adx14` is 18.02 adjusted and
45.71 raw. `NFLX.US` `dist_52w_high` separates the adjusted high (-0.41488, stored) from
the adjusted close used as the high (-0.41310), which is the plausible wrong-column
error. `MH.US` and `TBNK.US` have no corporate action and every counterfactual
coincides, which is the control behaving as a control.

**It reproduced the determinism claim independently**, recovering the digest expression
by trial because it was recorded nowhere, then re-running the compute layer from its own
binary. All five digests unchanged. It went further than 2.12 by re-running all four
metric engines with nothing after them, so D-77's split property is now observed live on
all four tables rather than on `indicator_daily` alone.

**It demonstrated that the 2.9 fix had no regression test.** Reverting
`MarketContextEngine.cs:82` left all 221 tests passing while the same binary died
immediately against the store. Three of six compute components had no test that ran the
stage.

**It corrected the denominators.** The alphabetical head reaches one recorded figure,
`fcf_yield`'s 464, and not the table: `ev_ebit`, `roic`, `accruals` and `cash_on_hand`
all span 26 initials. And "482 names running contiguously" is contiguous over the
**active universe** (483 members sort at or before `CCBG.US`, 482 carry the field), not
over `fundamental_snapshot`, where 856 of the 1,338 filers in that same span carry no
capital expenditure.

## The correction pass

Two of the findings were rules rather than defects. Both were settled by measurement
with the threshold written down before the number existed [`CLAUDE.md` §11].

**D-81, `cash_on_hand`.** The zero-coalesce ran in both directions and only one of them
is a zero. The justified case occurs 5 times; the mirror case 1,644 times, writing the
short-term investments figure alone. `NFLX.US` carried 28,678,000 against a reported
`cash` of 9,099,232,000. Which line should stand in was measured: over the 8,411
quarterly rows where the two candidates can be told apart, `cash` equals
`cash_and_equivalents` 6,710 times exactly and equals their sum 13 times. Rule is now
`coalesce(cash_and_equivalents, cash) + coalesce(short_term_investments, 0)`. On the
blessed date: 2,253 unchanged, 1,639 corrected, 5 nulled.

**D-82, EBIT. The pre-registered threshold failed and the substitution was refused.**
Substitute if the median relative difference against `operating_income` is under 2
percent and the 90th percentile under 10. Measured: median 1.01 percent, 90th **63.9**
percent over 380,281 rows, and 4.90 / **84.3** over the latest readable quarters. The
tail fails by six to eight times, which is exactly what that threshold was set to catch.
`ev_ebit` stays at 2,203 of 3,897 and the selection effect stays open rather than being
closed by a worse answer.

**The three write paths.** `StageWritePathTests` runs C09, C35 and C10 through their own
`ExecuteAsync`. The C10 case was verified against the defect rather than assumed to
cover it: reverting the fix now gives 226 passed and 1 failed, where the same edit gave
221 and 0 before. Every compute component now has a test that runs the stage.

**Authored documents.** `ARCHITECTURE.html` §3's C11 row and `METRICS.md` §6.1 both
stated the fallback as fewer than 15 members where the code counts non-null values, and
the two disagree on 18 cells and 110 names on the blessed date. `METRICS.md` §5 named
regime labels the `CHECK` rejects. All corrected with prior wording verbatim in
`CHANGELOG.md`.

## Digests

`valuation_daily` moves with D-81 and the other four do not, which is C09's write
ownership observed rather than declared. A second run reproduces the new digest, so
determinism holds across the change.

| Table | At 2.12 and at the review | At HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| `indicator_daily` | `26097aef9ce89c71962764dbb8217c24` | unchanged |
| `valuation_daily` | `52105e24c2f92b271e9812e5513eb91b` | `e08ce4c0db02d594da278dc413191409` |
| `flow_daily` | `0bf8e067a4d1b2860c5428417ae2d794` | unchanged |
| `sentiment_derived_daily` | `8e3978a1e5f0205f3a5a42f16ba653ef` | unchanged |
| `market_context_daily` | `03ecf62da6ed7a555bfa4908031dc821` | unchanged |

## Left open, deliberately

- **`METRICS.md` is still the 2.1 draft** and its nine PROPOSAL entries are still
  PROPOSAL. D-81 changes one of its rules and D-82 settles another, so promotion is one
  act after those land rather than nine entries authored alongside two amendments.
- **Half the phase 2 prompt archive is missing and is named as absent.** The first
  session's prompt, which produced 2.1 to 2.6, 2.9, 2.14 and 2.15, exists nowhere.
  Reconstructing it would be a paraphrase, which is the one thing a spent prompt must
  not be [D-63].
- **`prompts/BuildPlans/` is a third kind of file** and `prompts/README.md` describes
  two.
- **`ev_ebit_vs_own_5y` computes for no name** and `dist_52w_high_20d_change` for none
  either. Both need more history than thirteen months and resolve at phase 3.
- **`ci.ps1`'s intermittent failure**, third occurrence, one candidate ruled out.
  Evidence at `docs/evidence/phase-1/`.

author: scnplt
body:
Part of #15 — the cheap floor named in that issue, not the whole fix.

## Why

`go test` prints a test's SKIP and its reason **only** under `-v`. Without it, a package whose tests all skipped reports a bare `ok`, indistinguishable in the log from one that ran and passed them. A green run silently implies coverage it may not have.

That is not hypothetical here. PR #13 was the first time the `e2e` job ever ran, and it now skips `TestContainerListReportsHealth` on every CI run — GitHub's runners speak Docker API 1.48 and the field under test arrived in 1.52. Nothing in the log says so; the package line just reads `ok`.

This is the argument `DEVMON_E2E_REQUIRE=1` already makes one level up, applied to the skips that flag deliberately does *not* convert into failures. An unreachable Engine is a hard failure in CI. A Linux-only group on a non-Linux Engine, an endurance test behind an opt-in, and an Engine too old for a field are all legitimate skips — and each has to be readable rather than inferred.

## What changed

`-race -count=1 -v` moves into a shared `E2E_TESTFLAGS`, used by `e2e`, `e2e-container` and `e2e-endurance`. That matches how the Makefile already treats `MODULE`, `COVER_PKGS` and `E2E_PKGS` — its header says these are "defined once here so it is never retyped". Timeouts stay per-target, since they differ by design (15m vs 45m).

README gains a paragraph explaining that the `-v` is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. It also corrects a claim that was subtly untrue before this change: the existing text said skips appear "visibly, in `go test` output", which was only true under `-v`.

## Verified

`make` is not available on this Windows host, so the expanded command was run directly. Without an Engine, all 76 tests skip — and every one now names its reason:

```
--- SKIP: TestStreamEnduranceThirtyMinutes (0.00s)
    contract_endurance_test.go:195: skipping long-running test: set DEVMON_E2E_ENDURANCE=1 to run it
--- SKIP: TestContainerListAllParameter (0.00s)
...
76 skips
```

Before this change that same run printed one `ok` per package and nothing else.

## What this PR does not prove

`e2e` only runs on PRs into `main`, so **this PR cannot exercise the target it edits** — it runs `test` alone. The Makefile change is plain variable substitution and was verified by expanding it by hand, but the first real execution of `make e2e` with these flags will be the next `dev` -> `main` PR. Same caveat as #14.

No Go code changed.

author: patrikbak
body:
The site header and every dialog, drawer and menu all sat on `z-50`, so which one covered which was decided by nothing but where they landed in the document. Safari has been seen resolving that the other way round after a tab sits idle, leaving the header painted over the top bar of an open modal until the page is reloaded.

`globals.css` now holds a stacking ladder, one `@utility` per rung: `z-sticky` (page chrome under the header, and a mobile sheet's scrim), `z-sheet`, `z-header`, `z-overlay` (dialogs and drawers), `z-floating` (anything anchored to a trigger, so it clears the dialog it was opened from), `z-notification` and `z-tooltip`. Page content keeps plain `z-0`/`z-10`/`z-20` below the ladder's floor. The rung belongs to the primitive, so `Modal`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Select`, `Tooltip` and the drawers carry it and the call sites stop picking numbers. The two sticky bars pinned under the header (the guide's tab strip and the review queue's filter bar) share a `sticky-below-header` utility instead of repeating the same three classes at two different z-indexes. A `no-restricted-syntax` rule rejects a raw z-index in a class list and names the rungs.

The header's user menu and language switcher were each hand-rolling a Radix panel, with one chrome recipe copied between them and neither going through the shared `DropdownMenu`. That recipe is now `FLOATING_PANEL_CLASS` on `DropdownMenuContent` and `PopoverContent`, so the menus on the shared primitives wear the same translucent panel, and the two header menus pass only what actually differs.

Verified in WebKit against a production build: header 40, drawer 50, anchored panel 60, the guide strip sticky at `top: 80px` on 30, the ToC scrim 30 under its sheet 35 under the header. With a drawer open, `elementFromPoint` inside the header band lands in the dialog rather than the header.

author: tannevaled
body:
**Horodate: 2026-08-11 15:08 CEST**

## Summary

Completes the `Marshal` module toward MRI 3.4/4.0 byte-exact fidelity by replacing the previous scalar-only converter binding (which only handled nil/bool/int/float/symbol/string/array/hash) with a self-contained, **MRI-4.0.5-byte-exact** Marshal 4.8 encoder/decoder living in the VM (`internal/vm/marshal_codec.go`). Living in the VM lets it dispatch the user hooks and reconstruct the full object model under one shared symbol table and object-link counter, so shared and cyclic structures encode/decode exactly as in MRI.

## Implemented (byte-exact vs `ruby 4.0.5`, verified with `p Marshal.dump(x).bytes`)

- Scalars: `nil`/`true`/`false`, Integer (Fixnum + Bignum), Float (incl `inf`/`-inf`/`nan`/`-0`), Symbol (+ symlink refs).
- String: UTF-8 / US-ASCII / ASCII-8BIT / named-encoding (`I`-wrapped `E`/`encoding` ivars).
- Array, Hash (+ default value), Range, Regexp (+ encoding option bit), Struct, Object (ivars), Class/Module refs.
- Rational/Complex via the `marshal_dump` (`U`) form; Time via `_dump` (`u`) packed `time_mdump` form + `zone`/`offset` ivars.
- Custom hooks: `#marshal_dump`/`#marshal_load` and the class `_dump`/`_load` protocol.
- Object references / cyclic structures preserved (shared identity → object links).
- `Marshal.dump(obj, io=nil, limit=-1)` (String or IO destination) and `Marshal.load`/`Marshal.restore(src, proc=nil, freeze:)` (String or IO source, load-proc invoked per object, `freeze:` deep-freeze). `Marshal::MAJOR_VERSION`/`MINOR_VERSION` = 4.8.
- Errors match MRI class + message: `TypeError` (unmarshalable / incompatible version / anonymous class / hash default proc), `ArgumentError` (`marshal data too short` / `dump format error(0xNN)` / `undefined class/module X`).

## Deferred (noted)

- Time sub-microsecond precision (MRI `submicro` ivars) and non-UTC **zone-name** restoration — the instant is preserved (loaded as UTC).
- Depth-limit enforcement (the `limit` arg is accepted for arity, not enforced).
- `freeze:` on Array/Hash — rbgo has no frozen flag for those (applies to String/Object/Regexp).

`pstore` / `sinatra_session` keep the standalone `go-ruby-marshal` engine for their scalar payloads (unchanged).

## Verification

- **Byte-exact**: every dump asserted against captures from `ruby 4.0.5 (arm64-darwin25)`.
- `GOWORK=off go test ./...` — exit 0 (no regressions).
- **CI-exact whole-package coverage gate** — every added/touched function 100% (incl. error branches); only the pre-existing tolerated partials remain.
- `gofmt` + `go vet ./internal/vm/` clean.
- **ruby/spec ratchet**: 13678 passing (floor was 13520); FLOOR bumped to 13648 (measured − 30, Linux ≥ macOS).
- `prelude.rb` untouched (no `freeze-prelude` regeneration needed).

author: jbailes
body:
First installment of moving the economizer out of C, per the directive that this belongs in Go. **This is a foundation, not the finished port** — see *Status* below for exactly what is and is not done.

## What is ported

Three leaf units, in dependency order, with every test carried over one-for-one from the C suite so the port is pinned to the behaviour it replaces:

| C source | Go | cases |
|---|---|---|
| `fold_register.c` (91 ln) | `register.go` | 5 → 5 |
| `fold_recall.c` (147 ln) | `recall.go` | 6 → 6 |
| `coord_closet.c` (651 ln) | `closet.go` | 15 → 15 |

26 tests, `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean, whole `server-go` tree builds.

## A real test hole, found by mutation

`test_coord_closet.c` asserts `contains(out, "src/modules/git")` for the two-slashes-no-extension path case. That substring is satisfied by `"src/modules/git/retry.c"`, which is conserved via the **dot** rule — so the extensionless branch of `match_path` was never actually covered. Forcing that branch to always reject leaves the C-shaped assertion passing.

The Go test asserts on a whole rendered line instead, and now fails under that mutation and passes when restored. **The equivalent C assertion is still vacuous** — worth fixing in the C suite whether or not this port lands.

## Design decisions

- **One bus stage, not many.** `coord_closet`, `fold_recall` and `context_fold` are internal to a reduction, not separately callable, so they stay internal Go packages. Only `economizer-reduce` needs to be on the wire.
- **The module can be stateless.** `reduce_state_t` is already persisted by the C side via `db1_economizer_state_save/_load`, so state travels in and out with the request rather than the module owning a store.
- **Ordinal 27**, appended to the optional inventory, is the only safe slot: `principal_ref` must equal the inventory ordinal, so inserting mid-list renumbers every later module and changes event kinds on the wire. That gives event kind `4096 + 27*256 + 1 = 11009`.

## Status — what is NOT done

Not yet cut over, deliberately. The migration contract says a rule must never live in two languages. Nothing dispatches to this package yet — no descriptor, no stage, no bus wiring, no caller — so it is **inert code beside the live C**, not a second live implementation that can diverge. The cut-over debt is real and must be paid before anything routes here.

Remaining, roughly in order:

1. `context_fold.c` (643 ln) — including the freeze fix from #2552, which must survive into Go.
2. `context_reduce.c` (607 ln) — the orchestrator, plus the composed prefix-stability test.
3. `tool_condense.c` (1,179 ln), `economizer_json.c` (544), the provider shims (`economizer_openai/anthropic/proof`, ~1,000), `task_rail.c` (245), `episode_seal.c` (165), the gateway wire files (~370).
4. Module wiring: canonical inventory, `process-contracts.json`, `module.yaml`, `docs/modules/economizer.md`, dispatch table, registry-vs-contracts test.
5. Cut C over and delete it.
6. `compact_body()` lives in `src/compact.c`, OUTSIDE the module, and `context_fold` depends on it — that dependency needs a decision (port it, or keep it in C as shared substrate) before the fold can move.

That is ~5,000 further lines of C plus the wiring. It is a program of work, not a single change.

## The two production bugs

Both were held back from C hotfixes per the decision to do this in Go only, and both are therefore **still live in production**:

- **Cache telemetry is blind for every OpenAI-family model.** Root cause found: `aimee_backend_openai.c:412` and `aimee_backend_responses.c:298` parse only the top-level token counts and never read the `*_details.cached_tokens` sibling that is already in the response. The IR fields (`usage_cache_read`/`usage_cache_write`) and all downstream accounting already exist — Anthropic populates them. This is why delegate traffic reports `cache_read: 0` across 3.1M prompt tokens; the provider sends it, aimee discards it.
- **The fold freeze never engages under `economizer.mode=aggressive`** (#2552, green, unmerged) — every turn pays a cache write where the freeze exists to buy a cache read.

author: ghaith
body:
## Problem

On Windows, linking a real-sized project through the `clang` driver fails with `no such file or directory` for **every** object:

```
clang: error: no such file or directory: 'C:bachmannSolutionCenterworkspace...mainProg.st.o'
```

Every backslash has been stripped: `C:\build\obj\mainProg.st.o` arrives as `C:buildobjmainProg.st.o`.

## Cause

`write_response_file` assumed a single tokenizer for all linkers. Its comment stated *"an unquoted backslash is literal in this format"* — true for `lld` and binutils, but a **compiler driver treats a backslash as an escape**. Object paths were written bare, so the driver consumed the separators.

The defect needed two conditions that could not co-occur on Windows until recently:

1. A command line over the 30,000-byte threshold, routing args through a response file. Small projects never reach it.
2. A **driver** linker consuming that file. Windows always fell back to a direct `ld.lld` link, which reads backslashes literally — so the existing behaviour was correct for the only linker that could be selected.

Including the sysroot in the driver probe (#1852) made `clang` selectable on Windows and switched on condition 2, exposing the writer's assumption. The bug was latent in the writer the whole time; nothing on Windows could reach it.

## Fix

Choose the escaping from the linker family where the file is written:

| Linker family | Style | Backslash |
|---|---|---|
| `clang`, `cc`, `gcc` | `EscapedBackslash` | doubled |
| `ld.lld`, `ld.bfd`, `gold` | `LiteralBackslash` | literal |

Quoted arguments (those carrying whitespace) already double backslashes under both families, so that path is unchanged.

## Verification

Forcing a response file with `PLC_LINKER_RESPONSE_FILE=1` on a Windows host:

| Linker | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `clang` (driver) | fails on every object | links |
| `ld.lld` (direct) | links | links |

## Tests

30 linker unit tests pass, three of them new and each failing without this change:

- `response_file_quoting_escapes_backslashes_for_driver_linkers`
- `write_response_file_escapes_object_paths_for_driver_linkers` — asserts the emitted lines and that each unescapes back to the original argument
- `driver_linker_response_file_round_trips_windows_paths` — goes through `CcLinker` so the style is derived the way `finalize` derives it, rather than asserted against a hand-passed constant

**No lit test.** A lit case could force a response file with a driver linker, but lit runs on Linux where paths carry no backslashes, so the defect cannot reproduce — it would pass for the wrong reason. The unit tests are the real guard.

author: mviale13
body:
## What becomes better for the investor?

**MOVRvest can now say something useful from imperfect evidence instead of falling silent.** PR #116 made committee judgments visible and showed internal vocabulary leaking to the surface as though it were an investment conclusion. `CONFLICTED` is a fact about two readings; *"we cannot tell you anything"* is a fact about the investor's question, and they are different sentences.

## Measurement before abstraction

**The ETH forcing case — and it did not force a verdict.** Supply Governance stays `evidence_insufficient`, which is correct for that committee's remit. The assessment now says:

```
Circulating supply  [precise]     120.68 million, agreed by 3 sources
Value Capture       [structural]  measured activity is captured...
                                  — via the stated mechanism: amount of
                                    ETH burned, base fees plus blob fees
Supply Governance   [insufficient] still open: no mechanical issuance rule
                                   is held — a statement about what this
                                   platform has read, not about the protocol
Nothing useful is held about: Maximum supply.
```

**One mismatch reported rather than papered over:** the ruling's illustrative *"ETH has no fixed maximum supply"* is **not supportable from stored evidence**. The CoinGecko adapter maps a null `max_supply` to `None`, so *the vendor states there is no cap* and *the field was absent* are indistinguishable. Reported as unknown, not asserted.

**Where disagreement actually lives**, measured across the corpus:

| asset | spread | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| TAO | 9.9% | two credible estimates → **range** |
| ADA | 2.2% | two credible estimates → **range** |
| HYPE | 77.6% | one reading exceeds the maximum → **uncertain** |
| ARB | 80.7% | one vendor frozen at TGE float → **uncertain** |

## The type the measurement produced

Six shapes, each observed live before being declared, and **not ordered**:

```
1INCH   precise x2, range x1, structural x2
ADA     insufficient x1, precise x1, qualified x1, range x1, structural x1
ARB     insufficient x1, precise x1, qualified x1, structural x1, uncertain x1
BTC     precise x3, structural x2
ETH     insufficient x1, precise x2, structural x1
HYPE    insufficient x1, precise x2, structural x1, uncertain x1
SOL     precise x2, structural x2
TAO     precise x1, qualified x1, range x1
```

**`DIRECTIONAL` was specified and not built** — nothing produces one yet, since ETH's burn is held and its reward side is not read.

## Two boundary fixes

**A prose failure is a presentation failure.** The validator is untouched — every out-of-remit word still refused, the rejected sentence still reaches no reader — but the refusal is recorded in `wording_refused` and the committee falls back to its own deterministic account. **HYPE's Fee Capture now answers `mechanism_evidenced`** where the word *buy* previously erased a complete structural judgment.

**A guard the corpus forced.** *"Tokens in existence is 21.00 million"* for Bittensor is faithful to the evidence and irresponsible to print: the same vendor puts the maximum at 21 million, and S5 measured that substitution across 83 of 145 capped assets. Exact equality **qualifies** rather than rejects — Arbitrum genuinely is fully emitted — which is the difference between reporting a number and vouching for it.

## What it refuses

**No canonical figure is ever invented.** 480m and 530m produce a bound naming both; a test asserts `505` appears nowhere — not in the sentence, not in the readings, not in any method.

**No verdict is reinterpreted.** A committee's answer is quoted, never translated.

**Nothing about the asset** — no score, rank, recommendation, aggregate, agreement, favourable/adverse — checked over the surfaces *and* the source of both modules.

## Recorded, unsolved

- `max_supply: null` vs *field absent* — an acquisition question.
- `MATERIAL_SPREAD` is one constant (25%) doing work across every quantity; two committees' corpus is not enough to say whether supply and market cap deserve the same threshold.
- **Asset Quality's absolute bands are untouched**; the mismatch with a range-shaped assessment is recorded, and whether market significance belongs in relative share, percentile or descriptive evidence is deliberately not decided.

## Gates

2077 tests, mypy clean, ruff clean. HEAD verified in isolation — which caught the gitignored-cache trap on its **fifth** outing.

No frontend work, for the same reason as #116.

body:
Documentation only — no code changes. Closes out the v0.75.0 milestone.

## The status table had gone stale mid-milestone

"WHERE v0.75 STANDS" and the open-defects list under it were written before the SMP work and never revised, so this document had been arguing against its own later sections:

- **Tier 2 item 6** listed *"not started"* — it is done (#68).
- **The intermittent `-smp 4` page-fault panic** listed as an open defect. Fixed in #63.
- **`g_net_lock` re-entrancy** listed as open, with the note *"which is why `main` does not currently meet the release gate"*. Fixed in #64/#65.
- *"The next milestone-shaped piece of work is Tier 2 item 6"* — finished.

Corrected rather than deleted: the closed items stay, struck through and pointed at the PR that closed them, because the list records what this milestone **found** as much as what is outstanding.

## Release gate, run as the gate

Baseline `main` at the step 6 merge. Build **0 errors, 35 warnings** — the same count this milestone started with, held across every change in it.

| configuration | boots | result | suites | failures | rank faults |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniprocessor        | 1  | OK | 45 | 0 | 0 |
| `-smp 4` SeaBIOS    | 10 | **10 OK / 0 HANG / 0 PANIC** | 45 | 0 | 0 |
| `-smp 4` q35 + VT-d | 5  | **5 OK / 0 HANG / 0 PANIC**  | 47 | 0 | 0 |

All three configurations reach the prompt at 0 FAIL — the first time this milestone can say so.

## A gate configuration that was not actually running

The third config had to be written out by hand. `make qemu-iommu` expands `$(QEMU_IOMMU)`, and **that variable is not defined anywhere in the Makefile**. An undefined make variable expands to nothing, so the target has been booting with no `intel-iommu`, no `intremap`, and no q35 machine type — silently degrading into roughly the plain SMP configuration beside it. Every "smp4-iommu" result from that target since the variable went missing should be read with that in mind.

The runs above use the configuration spelled out explicitly. **The Makefile is deliberately not repaired here** — the flags a gate target carries are a choice to make on purpose, not something to infer from old logs and quietly commit under a docs change. Left as an explicit open item.

## What a v0.75.0 tag would not be claiming

Recorded so the tag is not read as more than it is:

- **Tier 1 step 3 is still not satisfied** — the original fork race has never been reproduced uninstrumented, so clean runs do not distinguish "fixed" from "did not fire".
- PBKDF2 is not memory-hard; Argon2/scrypt remains open.
- Lockout state does not survive a reboot.
- No confidentiality for the stored database.
- The suite set is not idempotent across boots on a re-used volume (2 suites fail on a second boot; pre-existing, confirmed by negative control).
- Toolchain suites' wall-clock budgets still break on a loaded host.
- `make qemu-iommu` is still broken.

author: nealcaren
body:
Closes #695.

Adds **`Wordshoal`** (Lauderdale & Herzog 2016, *Measuring Political Positions from Legislative Speech*, Political Analysis 24(3):374-394), the multi-domain extension of `Wordfish` and the newest member of the ideal-point family.

## What it is

A single Wordfish fit over a whole corpus of legislative speech is dominated by *what* each debate is about, not *where* a speaker sits ideologically. Wordshoal removes the agenda by scaling each debate separately and then combining:

- **Stage 1** runs Wordfish independently on each externally-known **domain** (debate), giving every speech a within-debate position. Each debate's axis is oriented arbitrarily — absorbed downstream.
- **Stage 2** is a one-dimensional linear factor model over the stacked within-debate positions, `psi = alpha_j + beta_j * theta_i + noise`, fit by the reference's conditional-ML coordinate ascent. `theta_i` is the actor's cross-domain position; the domain loading `beta_j` absorbs each debate's arbitrary sign and scale.

```python
m = topica.Wordshoal()
m.fit(docs, speakers=speaker, domains=debate,   # one speech per row; both labels required
      anchors={"Sanders": -1.0, "Cruz": 1.0})    # orient the sign of the shared axis
m.author_positions   # (N, 1) cross-domain actor scale
m.position_se        # (N,) standard error per position
m.domain_scales      # (M, 2) per-debate [intercept, loading]
m.author_components  # (N,) component id — actors in different components are NOT comparable
m.word_scores("health-2019", n=10)   # discriminating words within one debate
```

`domains` are trusted metadata, not inferred topics. Reach for Wordshoal over `Wordfish` when speeches carry debate labels and you want a scale comparable *across* debates; over `TBIP` when the domains are known rather than to be learned.

## Faithfulness & validation

Faithful to the `kbenoit/wordshoal` R package (GPL-3, read for algorithmic understanding only; implemented from the paper's equations, used purely as a parity oracle). The reference's stage-2 updates are a conditional-ML coordinate ascent, not a strict EM (the actor update omits `tau_i`, the precision update uses a partial residual); we replicate the published behavior exactly — a tau-weighted "correction" agrees on `theta` to |r|=0.9995, so nothing scientific is lost.

Validated against an R reference oracle (`quanteda.textmodels` Wordfish per debate + the paper's stage-2 ascent) on a fixed two-stage synthetic corpus (`parity/wordshoal_r_compare.py`):
- actor positions vs oracle: **|r| = 1.0000**; sign-aligned **value** agreement max|Δθ| = 0.017, `position_se` within <1%;
- both topica and the oracle recover the planted positions at |r| = 0.998;
- fit is **deterministic** (bit-identical across seeds; no RNG in either stage);
- **14-52x faster** than the R reference across corpus sizes (0.02-0.23s vs 0.97-3.26s).

Edge cases: a domain with < 2 speeches errors; a disconnected speaker-domain graph warns and is surfaced via `num_components` / `author_components`.

## Dual-review gates

Both gates from the `add-topic-model` workflow ran (fixed reviewer roles across gates).

**Gate A (plan).** *Reviewer A — faithful (Codex; fell back to Claude `opus` when Codex stalled)*: faithful-with-documented-deviations. *Reviewer B — adversarial (Gemini)*: flagged the reference's non-strict-EM stage 2 (resolved: empirically immaterial, replicate faithfully), the orientation β-flip, sorted-order init, and failed-domain zero-fill — all folded into the design. One blocker (a stage-1/stage-2 `beta_prior_sd` name collision) resolved by renaming the stage-2 knobs (`loading_prior_sd`/`intercept_prior_sd`) and hardwiring the stage-1 Wordfish priors.

**Gate B (pre-PR).** *Reviewer A — faithful (Codex)*: 2 blockers — (1) |r| alone is thin evidence → strengthened the parity check to full-vector (θ values + SE) agreement; (2) stage-1 capped at 100 iters → made tolerance-bound (cap 1000). *Reviewer B — adversarial (Gemini)*: 1 blocker — the connected-components union-find bridged speakers through failed domains and counted domain nodes as roots → fixed (union only scaled domains, label over actor nodes) + regression test. *Reviewer C — comparative (Claude `opus`, isolated worktree)*: APPROVE, no blockers. On poliblog (`speakers=blog`, `domains=day`) Wordshoal recovers the known `rating` labels at |corr| 0.917 and cleanly separates the parties, vs 0.564 for single-domain Wordfish and 0.470 for TBIP; it sits 2nd in family speed (~6x a single Wordfish, ~580x faster than TBIP) with trivial memory. Noted the multi-domain advantage is directional on a 6-actor corpus (folded into the docs) and that domains need >=2 documents. *Reviewer D — sample-user on poliblog (Claude)*: recovered the known `rating` labels at corr 0.917; T1-a (disconnected matrix looks comparable → added `author_components`), T4-a (non-string labels → coerce via `str()`), T4-c (domain_names lexicographic → documented); T1-b (arbitrary sign) documented and consistent with Wordfish.

## Tests / docs
- `src/wordshoal.rs` core (5 Rust tests: recovery, determinism, anchors, disconnected + failed-bridge components) + `tests/test_wordshoal.py` (11 tests). Exempt from the topic-health invariant suite (no topics), like Wordfish.
- Registry (`REGISTRY` + `IMPL`), `_topica.pyi`, README/docs roster regenerated; `docs/guides/models.md` prose; CHANGELOG.
- `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean, `scripts/preflight.sh` green, full `pytest` green, `mkdocs --strict` clean.

author: vertexprotocol
body:
The 42195 entry in a runner's Strava account had no icon, and every icon surface in the app itself — favicon, iOS touch icon, installed PWA — still showed v0's placeholder logo. This draws a mark from the `DESIGN.md` "Tartan" palette and puts it in both places.

## The mark

A stadium lane with a single ember lead arc: the runner's position on the track, which is the one thing the app is for. Clay ground under light chrome, espresso under dark, `--primary` for the arc. It survives 16px, which is the constraint that decided it.

A lettered alternate — `42` in Figtree ExtraBold over an ember lane rule — ships alongside it in `public/brand/` for the Strava listing, where the numerals can read better beside the app name.

Strava's guidelines forbid third-party icons carrying their logo or wordmark, so neither mark does; Strava orange stays confined to `components/strava-brand.tsx`.

## In the app

| File | Surface |
|---|---|
| `public/icon.svg` | Browser tab; switches ground and lane on `prefers-color-scheme` |
| `public/icon-{light,dark}-32x32.png` | 32px favicon fallbacks already wired up in `app/layout.tsx` |
| `public/apple-icon.png` | iOS home screen, 180px |
| `public/icon-{192,512}.png` | Installed PWA, now listed in the manifest with real sizes |
| `public/icon-maskable-512.png` | Android adaptive icon, scaled to clear the maskable safe zone |

`icon.svg` and the 32px pair use a heavier lane and a tighter box than the large sizes — at 32px the standard stroke thins out and the lead arc stops registering.

Two changes that ride along because the icon depends on them:

- `manifest.json` had `background_color`/`theme_color` at `#f5f3ef`, which is neither the light `--background` nor the `#e0d9d1` the layout already declares for light chrome. Now `#e0d9d1`, so the splash does not flash a different white behind the icon.
- `sw.js` caches `/icon.svg` in `STATIC_ASSETS` and serves static assets cache-first, so installed clients would keep the placeholder forever. `CACHE_NAME` goes `42195-v4` → `42195-v5`.

## In `public/brand/`

Versioned sources for both marks, in both grounds, plus a README covering what to upload to Strava (`app-icon-track-light-124.png`, at https://www.strava.com/settings/api), the palette table, and how to re-export.

Numerals are outlines rather than `<text>`, so the SVGs render without a webfont. All icons are full-bleed squares with no corner radius baked in.

## Not done here

`public/placeholder-logo.{png,svg}`, `placeholder-user.jpg` and `placeholder.{jpg,svg}` are also v0 leftovers, but nothing in the app references them — dead files, worth a separate sweep.

author: claudeleet
body:
Found while building and testing a diff/apply helper against real live state: every `routines/*.yaml` used `prompt: |` (clip chomping), which YAML always resolves to exactly one trailing newline. None of the original live routine prompts end with one, so every file carried a one-character diff against live that the initial seeding verification masked by `.rstrip('\n')`-ing both sides before comparing.

Switched to `prompt: |-` (strip chomping) so the parsed value matches live exactly. No content change — chomping only affects trailing whitespace.

author: davidtorcivia
body:
Separates multipart completion, cheap metadata observation, and full-body readback behind `MultipartObjectStore`. `AwsS3Store` maps these operations to completion POST, `HeadObject`, and streaming `GetObject` requests. Only matching full readback evidence advances `ObjectCommit` through at-rest verification and publication.

Retains the expected key, length, and CRC32C across ambiguous completion recovery. Confirmed completion retries only readback, potentially applied completion reconciles by reading before retrying completion, and all backend evidence is compared with the locally derived expectation. Terminal success or failure releases only the exact retained multipart recovery state.

Replaces the unpublished `S3Compatible`, `S3Adapter`, and misleading `head` surface before the supported SDK facade is established. Tests pin the POST, PUT, POST, HEAD, GET request transcript, transient and applied ambiguity recovery, field-by-field evidence rejection, canonical receipt validation, and exact cleanup behavior.
