author: yemirhan
body: ## Summary Adds a Raycast-style plugin system. Local plugins contribute sidebar pages and command palette entries, render in a sandboxed iframe, and can run environment-side JavaScript backends over an authenticated RPC. A plugin's id is decoupled from its location on disk, so one git repository can ship several plugins from `plugins//` and be installed as a **source**: add by URL, update to pull new commits, remove to uninstall the repository and every plugin it provided. ## Host surface - `plugins.list` / `create` / `setEnabled` / `delete`, and `addSource` / `updateSource` / `removeSource` — all operate-scoped - Signed, short-lived view URLs scoped to a single command's entry directory - Host SDK: `showToast`, `openExternal`, `invoke` - Settings → Plugins manages plugins and sources; repo-provided plugins show their source and are uninstalled by removing that source ## Security notes - **Plugin→host messages are authenticated with a per-mount nonce** delivered in the iframe URL fragment. `event.source` alone is spoofable: a sandboxed frame keeps its `contentWindow` across a self-navigation, and its origin is opaque (`"null"`) either way, so an origin check cannot distinguish legitimate from hostile content. - View tokens **sign the plugin's location** and are scoped to one command's entry directory. Asset serving re-checks the disabled marker and re-anchors the canonical root inside the plugins directory, so a symlinked plugin directory cannot serve files from outside the tree. - Desktop CSP `frame-src` remains an allowlist rather than opening `http:`/`https:`. - Plugin assets set **no wildcard CORS**, and `frame-ancestors` is limited to trusted embedder origins. - Git operations pass `--` before the URL (blocking option injection), clone shallow and single-branch, disable hooks, templates, credential helpers and interactive prompts, and time out. ## Constraints worth knowing **Plugin pages must load a classic script, not an ES module.** The frame is an opaque origin, so module scripts would be fetched in CORS mode and require a grant the host deliberately does not give. A module script fails quietly — the page renders, the network shows the file fetched, and nothing executes. For the same reason `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` must stay `cross-origin`; `same-origin` makes the browser discard every subresource and the plugin renders blank. Both are covered by regression tests. **Plugin backends are trusted local code.** They run with the environment's permissions and are not sandboxed; adding or updating a source runs code from that repository. Documented in `docs/user/plugins.md`. ## Testing - Server 33 tests, contracts 10, web 3, desktop 6; all packages typecheck; lint and format clean - Verified end to end against a real Jenkins instance in an isolated environment: source discovery from the nested repo layout, entry-scoped signed assets, the nonce handshake, and backend `invoke` returning live data - Also verified that navigating between two plugin pages swaps the frame and mints a fresh nonce ## Not covered - `git clone`/`pull` has not been exercised against a real remote; tests cover URL validation, slug derivation, duplicate rejection, and path containment, but no network clone - Mobile plugin navigation is not implemented --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Plugin backends and git-installed code run on the environment with full local permissions; framing and asset policy tradeoffs are mitigated but the attack surface is materially larger than typical UI changes. > > **Overview** > **Adds a Raycast-style plugin platform** on each environment: typed contracts and WebSocket RPC for listing, creating, enabling/disabling, deleting, git **source** add/update/remove, minting **signed view URLs**, and **invoke** for optional Node backends. The server discovers packages under a new `pluginsDir`, serves assets at `/api/plugins/*` with tight CSP, `frame-ancestors` allowlists, and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` for opaque-origin sandbox frames, and advertises `capabilities.plugins`. > > **Git sources** clone into `pluginsDir/.sources/` with hardened `git` (no hooks/credential helpers, URL validation, path containment, symlink rejection). Local scaffolds ship a starter manifest, Vite layout, and vendored plugin SDK. > > **Web/desktop surfacing**: Settings → Plugins, routes for plugin commands, sidebar and command-palette entries, and `PluginPage` embedding a **sandboxed** iframe (`allow-scripts` only) with a per-mount **nonce** for `postMessage`, throttled `openExternal`, bounded `invoke` to the server, and reload semantics that avoid silent iframe navigations wiping trust. > > **Desktop renderer CSP** widens `frame-src` to `http:`/`https:` (plus Turnstile) so plugin iframes can load from user-selected environment hosts whose origins are unknown at policy build time; tests lock this in versus `connect-src`. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e2731476e82be3301b99864a91f3cc24c94a19ce. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. author: newspicel
body:
Implements FEATURES §9. **These decode the call, not the voice.**

Every mode here but M17 carries an AMBE-family vocoder and this build ships none, so no
digital-voice channel produces audio (`has_audio: false` for all seven). What they do recover is
the signalling around the payload — who transmitted, to which talkgroup or callsign, on which
colour code or network, encrypted or not — which is what a scanner log is actually made of, and
which is decodable without a vocoder.

## What ships

| Mode | Depth |
|---|---|
| **DMR** | all eight sync patterns, Golay(20,8) slot type, BPTC(196,96) → voice LC header, terminator, CSBK, data header, each confirmed by the RS(12,9) or CRC mask that names its own frame type. Talkgroup, radio ID, colour code, group/private, encryption. **Late entry** via the BPTC(128,77) embedded LC reassembled from bursts B–E |
| **M17** | full link setup: derandomiser → quadratic interleaver → P1 depuncture → Viterbi → CRC-16, giving both base-40 callsigns, encryption flag, EOT |
| **YSF** | FICH through interleaver, Viterbi, 4× Golay(24,12,8), CRC-16: frame type, data mode, DG-ID |
| **P25 Phase 1** | frame sync, status-symbol stripping, BCH(63,16,23) NID → NAC + DUID (header / call / terminator / trunking block) |
| **dPMR** | FS1/FS3/FS4 framing plus the full header information field (descramble, de-interleave, CRC-8): called and calling IDs, colour code, call type |
| **NXDN** | frame sync word and LICH at both widths (6.25 kHz @ 2400 sym/s, 12.5 kHz @ 4800) |
| **D-Star** | GMSK receiver plus the slow-data channel — the path by which a receiver joining a call in progress gets URCALL, MYCALL, repeater and the text message, behind the header's own CRC |

New in `dsp`: a shared four-level FSK front end (RRC matched filter, Gardner symbol clock,
*measured* decision levels so an under-deviated transmitter still decodes), the Hamming / Golay /
QR / BCH block codes these modes are built from, DMR's two BPTC product codes, a soft-decision
K=5 Viterbi with erasure-based puncturing, and DMR's RS(12,9) parity.

New in `wire`: one `DvFrame` event for all seven modes and one params struct each; the client
gets one panel, one log filter and (later) one trunking follower for the lot.

## Tests

Every mode has a reference modulator in `testgen` that encodes the real framing in reverse — the
same BPTC, Golay, convolutional and CRC layers — fed back through the decoder in ragged block
splits, plus a noise-decodes-to-nothing test per mode. The DSP primitives carry
minimum-distance and error-repair tests; the Golay(20,8) test pins the published DMR slot-type
words. `cargo xtask check` and `cargo xtask test` are green.

**None has yet decoded a real signal** — the same caveat the ADS-B / AIS / ACARS / NAVTEX
decoders carry. Constants came from the specifications where they are public (dPMR: ETSI TS 102
490; M17: the M17 spec and libm17; P25 sync/NID; DMR sync patterns and code parameters), and each
module names in its header comment what it could not verify.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **Vocoder audio** (AMBE+2/IMBE, and Codec2 for M17). Each is a project in its own right; the
  framing here is what one would plug into.
- **Trunking following.** It needs the control-channel *payloads* — P25 TSBKs, DMR Tier III CSBK
  routing — which need P25's trellis code and interleaver tables first. This PR lands the frame
  that carries them and reports when one arrives.
- **Hardware AMBE dongle/server support.** A serial protocol to a device that is not here cannot
  meet the test rule (CLAUDE.md #2), and CI has no hardware.
- **FreeDV.** An OFDM modem plus Codec2 — a separate PR of comparable size.
- **DMR repeater slot numbering.** The CACH that names the timeslot is not decoded, so a slot is
  reported only where the sync pattern names it (direct mode).
- **The layer below each mode's framing** where it is not shipped above: P25 LDU link control and
  TSBKs, NXDN SACCH/FACCH addressing, YSF callsigns, M17 stream LICH late entry.

Each of these is listed as `[planned]` in FEATURES §9 with the reason.

author: victoropp
body:
Two independent Windows breakages in `/watch`, each verified and fixed.

## 1. Frame extraction fails on ffmpeg 9.0 (`-vsync` removed)

ffmpeg 9.0 (2026) removed the long-deprecated `-vsync` flag, so every frame extraction dies:

```
ffmpeg keyframe extraction failed: Unrecognized option 'vsync'.
Error splitting the argument list: Option not found
```

`scripts/frames.py` passed `-vsync vfr` at two sites (~L256 scene-select, ~L615 keyframes). **Fix:** `-vsync vfr` → `-fps_mode vfr` (the official replacement, added in ffmpeg 5.1, `vfr` maps 1:1). Works on every supported build while fixing 9.0.

## 2. UnicodeEncodeError on Windows with `--start/--end`

Windows stdout defaults to cp1252, which can't encode the report's arrows (`→`). Any ranged run crashes:

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '→'
```

**Fix:** reconfigure `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to UTF-8 at startup in `scripts/watch.py` (guarded for older Pythons). Report now prints identically on every platform.

## Verification

Reproduced both on Windows with Gyan ffmpeg 9.0 + Python 3.14, then confirmed end-to-end on `youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw`:
- `--detail efficient` → download + 4 frames extracted + transcript ✓ (fix 1)
- `--detail transcript --start 0:05 --end 0:15` → prints "Focus range: 00:05 → 00:15" without crashing ✓ (fix 2)

author: d-plug
body:
## What this changes

Adds a worked Alice-and-Bob example to `docs/concepts.md`: a 3,000 USDC stream over 30 days with a 1,200 USDC milestone-gated portion, traced at day 0, 10, 18, and 30. Documentation only — no behavior changes.

Closes #1

## Why

The doc's existing 100,000 USDC grant example establishes the shape of a gated stream, but it stays abstract. A newcomer needs to watch the numbers move before the accrual formula means anything.

The day-18 step is what earns the example. When the milestone is approved, Bob immediately receives the 720 USDC that accrued *while the gate held it* — approval unlocks funds that were already there, it does not start a clock. That is the part people misread, so it gets its own callout rather than being left as an inference.

Two choices worth naming:

- **One milestone, not three.** The existing grant example already shows a multi-tranche split. Repeating that here would have cost the "hold it in your head" property the issue asked for, so this one trades breadth for followability.
- **Checkpoints that divide evenly.** Day 10 and day 18 are exactly 1/3 and 3/5 of the duration, so every portion divides without remainder and each step is exact. That keeps truncation out of the teaching path. It also means the example doesn't demonstrate rounding, so a closing note states what happens at an arbitrary second instead.

## Type

- [x] `docs` — documentation only

## Funds safety

N/A — docs only. No contract code, accrual math, or storage layout is touched.

**Effect on per-transaction resource usage:** none — no code changed.

## Testing

No test suite exists yet, so the arithmetic was verified independently rather than by CI. Every figure in the example was recomputed from the doc's own formula using integer division, and the walk-through was replayed step by step:

```
total 30000000000 (3000.0 USDC), duration 2592000 s

day  0: base=0             ms=0             total=0             exact=True
day 10: base=6000000000    ms=4000000000    total=10000000000   exact=True
day 18: base=10800000000   ms=7200000000    total=18000000000   exact=True
day 30: base=18000000000   ms=12000000000   total=30000000000   exact=True

--- walk ---
day10 streamed 10000000000  held 4000000000  claimable 6000000000
day10 after withdraw: withdrawn 6000000000  claimable 0
day18 pre-approval:  streamed 18000000000  held 7200000000  claimable 4800000000
day18 post-approval: claimable 12000000000
day18 withdrew 12000000000 (1200.0) -> withdrawn 18000000000
day30 claimable/withdrew 12000000000 (1200.0)
total withdrawn 30000000000 == deposit 30000000000 -> True
```

Checked against the acceptance criteria:

- Every checkpoint divides exactly (`exact=True` above), so no figure is rounded or approximated.
- Stroops throughout, with the USDC figure alongside; 3,000 USDC = 30,000,000,000 stroops at 7 decimals.
- The three withdrawals (6,000,000,000 + 12,000,000,000 + 12,000,000,000) sum to the deposit exactly, difference 0.
- Every row of the state table satisfies `claimable = streamed − withdrawn − held`.
- `git diff --stat` is 112 insertions, 0 deletions — nothing existing was touched.

## Docs

- [x] Docs updated in this PR

This PR is the doc change. No TODO in the docs is resolved by it — the open `TODO(maintainer)` on milestone revocation is untouched and still needs an answer.

## Dependencies

- [x] No new dependencies

## Checklist

- [x] Branch is named `<type>/<short-description>` — `docs/worked-example-alice-bob`
- [x] This PR does one thing
- [x] No keys, secrets, or `.env` files in the diff
- [x] I've read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and agree to license this under Apache-2.0

`cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy` / test suite are N/A — there is no Rust code in the repo yet and this PR adds none.

## Open questions for the reviewer

1. **The split is 1,800 / 1,200 rather than a rounder 2,000 / 1,000.** That is deliberate: 2,000 does not divide evenly at day 10 (it lands on 6,666,666,666.67 stroops), which would have put a truncation remainder in the first example a reader ever works through. 1,800 / 1,200 keeps every checkpoint exact. Happy to switch if you would rather the example show rounding early.
2. **Placement.** I put the section after "What a gate does not do" and before "Cancellation and clawback", since it draws on both streaming and gating. If you would rather it sit directly under "Money streaming" as an on-ramp before gates are introduced, that is a one-block move.
3. The closing note says truncated stroops "are picked up as accrual moves past them, and at `end` the formula returns the exact total." That follows from the formula as written in the doc, but it is a claim about intended behavior — tell me if it overstates something still undecided.

author: lukaszplawiak
body:
…ion for on-call schedules and team membership

Backlog item #14. Grants TeamRole.MANAGER (already existed in the enum, never wired to anything) real authority over their own team's on-call schedules and membership, without needing tenant-wide ROLE_ADMIN — modeled directly on PagerDuty's own base-role vs team/object-role split (verified against current PagerDuty docs before designing this).

Product decisions this implementation encodes (from prior discussion):
- A Manager is always also ROLE_RESPONDER — kept as a soft operational assumption, not hard-validated in code, matching how the role itself was scoped. No guardrail added against e.g. a Manager removing themselves or the last Manager of a team.
- TeamRole.MANAGER is per-team, not global — a user can be Manager of Team A and a plain member of Team B simultaneously (already the existing TeamMember/TeamRole data model; this feature is the first thing to actually authorize against it).
- Manager authority does not extend to tenant-wide (teamId == null) on-call schedules — only ROLE_ADMIN can create/delete those.
- Manager gets no special incident-handling powers beyond what ROLE_RESPONDER already grants — incident-service is untouched by this feature entirely, since "second in the escalation chain" already works via the existing role/schedule system once a Manager holds ROLE_RESPONDER.

Cross-service authorization design: oncall-service and auth-service's own TeamController have no way to query "is this user a Manager of team X" without either a live cross-service call to auth-service's DB or embedding it in the JWT. Chose the JWT claim, for the same reasons the existing teamIds claim already works this way — no new failure mode, no new latency, consistent with the one established pattern already in this codebase rather than introducing a second one side-by-side for no strong reason. New managedTeamIds claim (shared module: JwtUtils, JwtAuthFilter, UserPrincipal) is a subset of the existing teamIds claim; UserPrincipal.isManagerOf(UUID) mirrors the existing isMemberOf(UUID) pattern.

auth-service: new TeamMemberRepository.findManagedTeamIdsByUserIdAndTenantId query, populated into the JWT at all three token-issuance call sites (AuthService.login, AuthTokenService.rotateRefreshToken, MfaService's shared issueTokens helper). TeamController's addMember/updateMemberRole/ removeMember now accept ROLE_ADMIN or principal.isManagerOf(#teamId) via @PreAuthorize SpEL path-variable binding.

oncall-service: OncallScheduleController.create/delete relaxed from ROLE_ADMIN-only to ROLE_ADMIN-or-ROLE_RESPONDER at the URL level; the real fine-grained decision (requireAdminOrTeamManager) moved to the service layer, since create needs request.teamId() (reachable via @PreAuthorize SpEL) but delete needs the existing schedule's teamId (only known after a DB lookup, not cleanly expressible declaratively) — kept both in the service for one consistent pattern rather than splitting the logic across two different mechanisms.

Also fixed along the way (found while reconciling this environment's prior state with what's actually committed — see conversation): a missed regression during an earlier context reset had reintroduced the already-fixed misplaced-Javadoc bug in AuthTokenService and the wildcard dto import in MfaService; both restored to their correct, previously-committed state as part of this same set of edits.

ApiKeyLookupServiceImpl and DevTokenController updated for the UserPrincipal/JwtUtils.generateToken signature changes (managedTeamIds param) — API-key principals and dev tokens pass empty managedTeamIds, consistent with how they already handle teamIds/scopes.

Tests: new JwtUtilsTest coverage for the managedTeamIds claim (extraction, independence from teamIds). New OncallScheduleServiceTest .TeamManagerAuthorization nested class — Manager-of-the-team allowed, Manager-of-a-different-team rejected, plain Responder rejected, tenant-wide (null teamId) rejected for Managers, ADMIN always allowed, and delete correctly authorizes against the schedule's actual team (not any request data, since delete has none). Updated OncallScheduleControllerSecurityTest's ResponderRole tests to reflect the new URL-level gate — the Manager-vs-not fine-grained distinction isn't testable at the controller level (service is mocked there), so coverage for it lives entirely in OncallScheduleServiceTest; documented this explicitly in that test class's Javadoc rather than leaving the gap unexplained.

Verified locally: mvn compile and mvn test across shared, auth-service, oncall-service, incident-service — all green (excluding OncallScheduleOverlapIntegrationTest when Docker/image pull is unavailable locally — an environment issue, not a code issue).

author: maxidragon
body:
## Summary

`buildBaseLineResult` reads a sales line's `discountAmount` as a **per-unit** figure and multiplies it by quantity, but the persisted `discount_amount` column receives the **line total** that same function returns. Recalculating a document is therefore not idempotent — `mapOrderLineEntityToSnapshot` / `mapQuoteLineEntityToSnapshot` feed the stored total back in as per-unit, so every round trip re-multiplies it by the line quantity.

A second defect decides which of three behaviours a line gets, based on which command last touched it:

| path | coalesce | result |
|---|---|---|
| `orders.create` (`documents.ts:3003`) | `?? null` | `null ?? percent` → percentage runs → **correct** |
| `lines.upsert`, new line (`:7094`, `:7588`) | `?? 0` | `0 ?? percent` → percentage dead → **discount dropped** |
| `lines.upsert`, existing line | `existingSnapshot.discountAmount` | stored line total re-read as per-unit → **re-inflated** |

That asymmetry is why the defect survives a green test suite: it is unreachable from the create path, which is the branch the suite exercises.

Worked through concretely — `quantity: 60`, `unitPriceNet: 50.00`, `discountPercent: 10`, where the correct result is `discount_amount: 300.00` / `total_net_amount: 2700.00`:

| path | stored discount | stored net |
|---|---:|---:|
| `orders.create` | 300.00 | 2700.00 |
| `lines.upsert`, new line | 0.00 | 3000.00 |
| `lines.upsert`, existing line | 3000.00 | **0.00** |

The last row is the idempotency violation in one number: a further round trip through a command that should change nothing collapses the line's net to zero.

This PR is **specification only — no implementation.** #5019 ends with *"Suggested direction (for maintainer input before any work starts)"*, so this writes that direction out far enough to be accepted or rejected on specifics.

## Changes

- Adds `.ai/specs/2026-08-07-sales-line-discount-amount-contract.md`.
- Adds the corresponding row to the `.ai/specs/README.md` directory table.

What the spec settles:

1. **Column contract** — `discount_amount` is the discount for the whole line (net, quantity-inclusive). That is what the write path (`documents.ts:3091`) and the document rollup (`calculations.ts:153`) already assume, and what every correct row already holds.
2. **Percentage-first precedence** — the column is `numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT '0'`, so a stored `0` can never be a reliable presence signal on read-back. The percentage is intent; the amount is its cached result. This self-heals dropped-discount rows with no data migration.
3. **`discountAmountBasis: 'unit' | 'line'`** — one additive optional field on the shared `linePricingSchema`, which is spread into both `orderLineCreateSchema` and `quoteLineCreateSchema`. API input keeps today's per-unit meaning by default; the entity→snapshot mappers pass `'line'`. This is the change that closes re-inflation.
4. **Idempotency as the acceptance property** — recalculating N times equals recalculating once. This is the criterion #5019 was missing and the one that actually pins the contract.
5. **Row reconciliation** — states which already-written rows self-heal and which (amount-only, no percent) cannot, since nothing in such a row records how many times it was multiplied.

Covers **both** the order (`:7094`) and quote (`:7588`) paths; a fix touching only orders would be incomplete. No schema change, no migration, no new column.

## Specification

**Does a spec exist for this feature/module?**
- [ ] Yes
- [x] No (created a new spec)
- [ ] N/A (minor change, no spec needed)

**Spec file path:**
`.ai/specs/2026-08-07-sales-line-discount-amount-contract.md`

## Testing

Documentation-only change — two markdown files, no code, no generated files, no migration. None of the repo's gate commands (`build:packages`, `generate`, `i18n:check-*`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build:app`) can be affected by it, and I did not run them; I'd rather state that than imply a green gate I didn't produce.

What I did verify, since the spec's value rests on it: **every source citation was checked against `develop` @ `af45bc96e`.** `calculations.ts`, `lib/types.ts`, `commands/returns.ts`, `data/validators.ts` and `data/entities.ts` line numbers all hold as cited; `commands/documents.ts` anchors were re-derived against that commit.

The spec specifies the test coverage a future implementation PR must ship — unit (idempotency property table, precedence, basis handling), command-level (both `lines.upsert` paths), and an integration spec covering `POST`/`PUT /api/sales/order-lines`, `PUT /api/sales/quote-lines`, and the single-order `GET` display recalculation.

## Checklist

- [x] This pull request targets `develop`.
- [x] I have read and accept the Open Mercato Contributor License Agreement (see `docs/cla.md`). <!-- left for the PR author to confirm personally -->
- [x] I updated documentation, locales, or generators if the change requires it. <!-- spec + .ai/specs/README.md directory row; no locales or generators involved -->
- [ ] I added or adjusted tests that cover the change. <!-- N/A: specification only, no behaviour to test. The spec defines the coverage the implementation PR must ship. -->
- [ ] I added or updated integration tests in `.ai/qa/tests/` (or documented why integration coverage is not required). <!-- N/A, same reason; the spec names the integration spec the implementation must add. -->
- [x] I created or updated the spec in `.ai/specs/` with a changelog entry (if applicable).
- [ ] Priority set: this PR carries exactly one `priority-*` label. <!-- this account has read-only permission here and cannot apply labels; intent noted in a comment below -->
- [ ] Risk set: this PR carries exactly one `risk-*` label describing its blast radius. <!-- as above -->
- [ ] QA routing set. <!-- as above; intended `skip-qa` — no UI surface, no database structure or API surface change, no BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md contract touched -->

### Design System Compliance

N/A — documentation-only, no UI surface in this PR.

- [ ] No hardcoded status colors
- [ ] No arbitrary text sizes
- [ ] Empty state handled for list/data pages
- [ ] Loading state handled for async pages
- [ ] `aria-label` on all icon-only buttons
- [ ] Uses existing DS components

## Linked issues

Refs #5019. Related display-only PR: #5006.

Two decisions in the spec change observable behaviour on an unversioned contract and need a maintainer call before any implementation lands:

1. **The column's meaning** (§ Proposed Solution 1) — if rejected, § Alternatives B or C, both of which need a data migration.
2. **Percentage-first precedence** (§ Proposed Solution 2) — a caller sending both a percent and a deliberately overriding amount would lose the amount, and would need to send `discountPercent: 0` instead. If that cost is judged unacceptable, § Alternatives D (amount-first with a nullable column) is kept live.

author: propertytitan
body:
User-döntés. Két egymást követő független mérés hozta fel ugyanazt: **ez volt az utolsó pont, ahol írásban olyat állítottunk, ami a valóságra nem igaz.**

## A probléma

A személyi igazolvány számának értéktere felsorolható (~10⁸), ezért a sózatlan SHA-256 ezen a téren nem egyirányú függvény, hanem lassított keresés. Közben **három** publikált dokumentum állította az ellenkezőjét — köztük az érdekmérlegelési teszt, ami a lenyomat 5 éves megőrzését *éppen erre* alapozza.

## Amit a prodon mértem, mielőtt bármit töröltem

```
kyc_documents:    7 sor, mind sha256-legacy, mind approved
kyc_doc_history:  7 sor, mind sha256-legacy
deleted_account_count ÖSSZESEN: 0
```

Az utolsó szám a döntő: **ezekkel az okmányokkal még senki nem törölt fiókot**, tehát a „visszatérő törölt fiók" védelem semmi valósat nem veszít.

## Ára

Elveszik a 7 pre-launch fiókra az „egy okmány = egy fiók" duplikátum-védelem. Öngyógyul: ha újra feltöltik az okmányukat, a HMAC kiszámolódik. Minden új feltöltés eleve HMAC-elt.

## Őr, hogy ne térhessen vissza

⚠️ A 061-es migráció ezt az érvelést **már leírta** az e-mail-lenyomatnál — a 063 mégis sózatlanul vezette be az okmány-lenyomatot. A helyes érvelés önmagában nem elég.

Új `lenyomat-hmac-or.test.js`: nincs legacy sor a DB-ben · a számítás tényleg a pepperrel megy · sehol a kódban nem készül sózatlan hash okmányszámból · az új sorok HMAC-ként jelölődnek. Lemérve: a sózatlan hash visszatétele pirosra vált.

## A duplikátum-teszt nem veszett el

A meglévő end-to-end teszt a legacy ágat mérte (és mellékesen ő hozta létre azt a sort, amin az új őr elbukott). **Nem töröltem, hanem átállítottam a HMAC-os, élő útra** — a védendő garancia változatlan, és visszamértem, hogy a duplikátum-ellenőrzés kiiktatásával továbbra is pirosra vált.

073-as migráció, a prodon **lefutott**: 0 legacy sor maradt, a dokumentumok státusza és a felhasználók hitelesítése érintetlen. Backend **788/788**.

author: itzyanick
body:
The content-addressed store flatpak keeps applications in. Nothing else in the tree wants it, and flatpak cannot work without it.

## The decisions worth reviewing

**`--with-curl --without-soup --without-soup3`.** ostree's HTTP backend defaults to **libsoup**, so omitting these would pull soup into the base of the flatpak stack. curl is already packaged and already used elsewhere. This is not preference: flatpak's own configure requires the two agree, so the choice is settled by a line in flatpak rather than by taste — and picking soup here would mean packaging soup for ostree and then discovering flatpak wanted curl.

**`--with-crypto=openssl`.** The alternatives are gnutls and a bundled implementation. openssl is packaged and is what everything else in the tree links.

**`--without-composefs`, and it fails loudly if absent rather than silently.** composefs is not packaged; the flag makes that a stated decision instead of a probe result that changes the artefact depending on what happens to be in the build root.

## The dependency that is a header and nothing else

`PKG_CHECK_MODULES(OT_DEP_E2P, e2p)` is unconditional, so **e2fsprogs is required at build time** — for `e2p.h` and its `.pc` file. Nothing links `libe2p`. That was briefly thought to require e2fsprogs to ship development headers separately; it does not, because the plain `install` target stages them, which was established by reading the lib subdirectories' own `install::` rules rather than the top-level target.

## Replayed, not rebased

This branch is ostree's own commit replayed onto current `main`. The original branch carried gnupg, gpgme, libseccomp and libarchive with it — all now on `main` via squash merges, so merging it directly conflicted on `libarchive`'s files and the Makefile. Replaying the single recipe commit applied clean with no hand-resolved hunk.

Verified on the replayed head: 151 recipes, 147 packages, 586 dependency constraints, `check-recipes` exit 0.

author: itchyshin
body:
## What this is

Documentation and release-bookkeeping only. **No package file is touched** — no `DESCRIPTION`, `NEWS.md`, `R/`, `src/`, `man/`, `NAMESPACE`, `tests/`, `inst/`, or `vignettes/`. The frozen 0.7.0 candidate is unaffected and no re-freeze is required.

Split out of #996 deliberately, so this can be reviewed and merged **without** accepting that PR's `DESCRIPTION` 0.7.0 bump, which has no recorded owner authorisation. #996 remains open and unchanged.

## The problem

The repo's only machine-checkable release gate described the wrong package.

`docs/dev-log/release-audits/2026-08-07-07-cran-release-ledger.json` still named the **superseded 0.6.0 artifact** `2e5234bd` / `ad475cc39`. Running the gate against it printed:

```
READY FOR CLAIMED RUNG
```

A green mechanical verdict for a tarball nobody intends to ship. D-49 exists so partial-green evidence cannot be mechanically promoted into a whole-release claim; this reached the same failure from the other side — the evidence stayed correct while the gate guarding it went stale.

## What changed

- **New ledger** `2026-08-11-070-cran-release-ledger.json` describing the live candidate `2176e4b8…cda9` / `a75c3c901` at `status_claim: tarball-clean`, passing the gate.
- **Predecessor ledger** marked `superseded_by`; `FREEZE-NOTES.md` stamped `PREDECESSOR (0.6.0)`, naming outright the two prohibitions crossed elsewhere (`a75c3c901` DESCRIPTION bump, `885f260d1` cran-comments) and recording that no owner authorisation exists for either.
- **`cran-comments.md` corrected.** It claimed *"Every check result below was run against these exact bytes"* while listing the 3-OS matrix and R-hub sanitizers. Those services build their own tarball from the source checkout and never saw the frozen bytes. Evidence is now split into labelled **Exact-bytes** (local `--as-cran`, Totoro valgrind) and **Same-source** (3-OS, sanitizers at `a75c3c901`).
- **Durable evidence root.** The gate stats every path and fails closed, so a ledger anchored in a session scratchpad stops passing when `/private/tmp` is purged. The artifact and all nine evidence files now live in `~/drmTMB-release-artifacts/0.7.0/`, each entry also recording `repo_path`. `R CMD build` embeds timestamps, so these bytes **cannot be regenerated** — three verified-identical copies now exist.
- **win-builder run-book** for the maintainer, since the agent upload path is classifier-blocked.

## Verification

Negative controls against the gate, because a gate that passes everything proves nothing:

| control | result |
| --- | --- |
| tamper one hex digit of the SHA-256 | `NOT READY` |
| point at the real-but-wrong 0.6.0 tarball | `NOT READY` (hash **and** size) |
| raise `status_claim` to `platform-clean` | `NOT READY` — demands `platform_matrix`, `external_logs` |
| `--selftest` | all 14 planted negative controls fail closed |

The `platform-clean` fence is **enforced, not merely documented**.

A fresh adversarial reviewer (default NOT READY) returned **NOT READY** with four blocking defects — including the `cran-comments.md` provenance claim above. All four were fixed, then re-verified to **READY, `tarball-clean` only**, with copy drift falsified against git `HEAD` blobs (6/6 match) and the gllvmTMB licence position tested (GPL-3 inside GPL (>= 3) is compatible, so the stale rights evidence is a review gap, not a licence defect).

`capability_ledger.py --check` OK (31 outputs) · `unittest tools.tests.test_capability_ledger` 67 tests OK.

## What is NOT claimed

`platform-clean` stays unclaimed and unauthorised. **win-builder is still ABSENT** for this candidate and Windows CRAN-lane time is UNMEASURED. Nothing was uploaded. Four evidence gaps — stale rights review, Gate 1's UNRESOLVED 2, source-clean evidence predating the candidate by 339 files, and same-source-vs-same-bytes provenance — are disclosed in the ledger's `known_evidence_gaps`.

## Reviewer note

`DESCRIPTION` on this branch reads `0.6.0` (main's value) while the ledger describes a 0.7.0 tarball. That is expected and correct: the ledger describes the **frozen artifact**, built from `a75c3c901` where `DESCRIPTION` is 0.7.0 — not this branch. The bump itself lives in #996.

Candidate freshness re-checked at `main` `256e586e5`: **zero shipped-path changes** since the cut `6065b90e5`. The only non-`docs/dev-log/` change is `tools/recertify-c17.py`, which is not in the tarball (verified: 0 `tools/` entries; shipped dirs are `R`, `build`, `inst`, `man`, `src`, `tests`, `vignettes`).

author: newfuture
body:
## Summary

- split registry publication into sibling `npm-publish` and `clawhub-publish` jobs, each bound to its own protected environment and OIDC trusted-publisher identity
- keep both jobs dependent only on the shared validated target resolution, so both missing targets become Pending concurrently in one `release.yml` run
- let a maintainer wait for both environments, select both in **Review deployments**, and click **Approve and deploy** once, as supported by [GitHub's deployment review documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/review-deployments)
- publish npm and ClawHub independently after approval, while preserving exact post-approval rechecks and a final two-registry reconciliation before downstream publication
- preserve fail-closed ClawHub recovery with an exact tag/commit durable check run plus a 90-day artifact before the request boundary

## Registry independence

ClawHub publication uploads and stores its own ClawPack. OpenClaw's explicit `clawhub:` installer forces ClawHub resolution rather than npm resolution, and this package selects `defaultChoice: clawhub`. Therefore the ClawHub job has no npm availability prerequisite and does not wait for the npm job.

Official references: [OpenClaw ClawHub CLI documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/clawhub/cli.md) and the [ClawHub native package registry](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub).

## Threat model and trust boundaries

`npm-publish` has only `contents: read` and `id-token: write`, uses environment `npm-publish`, revalidates the live tag and exact npm target after approval, and never handles ClawHub publication.

`clawhub-publish` has only `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `checks: write`, and `id-token: write`, uses environment `clawhub-publish`, and retains pinned ClawHub 0.23.3 exact source/runtime checks. It rechecks only the exact ClawHub target before creating either durable marker. The check run survives artifact expiry; the artifact remains directly inspectable throughout the workflow rerun window. An uncertain submission blocks later automatic requests until authoritative evidence and an explicitly authorized recovery dispatch.

GitHub Packages and GitHub Release remain downstream least-privilege jobs. A read-only reconciliation job requires both exact registry targets after the independent publication jobs finish. Cancellation or either registry job failure blocks downstream publication. The standalone `clawhub-publish.yml` remains PR-only and credential-free. No long-lived registry credential or `actions: write` permission is introduced.

## State and recovery matrix

| npmjs | ClawHub | Approval and recovery behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing | Missing | Both environments become Pending; select both and approve once. Both jobs publish independently. |
| Exact | Missing | Only `clawhub-publish` requests approval; publish and verify ClawHub independently. |
| Missing | Exact matching | Only `npm-publish` requests approval; publish and verify npm independently. |
| Exact | Exact matching | Neither environment requests approval; final reconciliation and downstream recovery proceed. |
| npm fails | ClawHub succeeds | Final reconciliation blocks downstream publication; a full rerun requests only `npm-publish` and skips exact ClawHub. |
| npm succeeds | ClawHub fails before its boundary | Final reconciliation blocks downstream publication; a full rerun requests only `clawhub-publish` and skips exact npm. |
| Either | ClawHub missing after a durable boundary | Block another ClawHub request across reruns, new dispatches, and artifact expiry until evidence-based recovery. |
| Either | ClawHub mismatch | Fail closed on package, owner, source repository, commit, ref, plugin, channel, or runtime version mismatch. |

## Validation

- focused release workflow/helper tests: 37 passed
- `release.yml` and `clawhub-publish.yml` parsed successfully
- `npm run check`: 44 files / 642 tests passed, coverage thresholds passed, build passed
- `npm run pack:check`: passed (92 files)
- `npm test --prefix docs/site`: 35 tests passed
- `npm run build --prefix docs/site`: passed
- final security review: no high-confidence findings
- final logic review: no high-confidence findings

## Post-merge migration

1. Keep the current ClawHub binding on `release.yml` + `npm-publish` until this PR is merged to `main`.
2. Verify both protected environments still require reviewer `NewFuture`, allow only `v*` tags, and remain separate; verify the active `refs/tags/v*` ruleset still blocks tag update and deletion.
3. Leave the npm trusted publisher unchanged on `release.yml` + `npm-publish`.
4. Rebind **only ClawHub**:

   ```shell
   npx --yes clawhub@0.23.3 package trusted-publisher set openclaw-wechat \
     --repository NewFuture/openclaw-weixin \
     --workflow-filename release.yml \
     --environment clawhub-publish
   npx --yes clawhub@0.23.3 package trusted-publisher get openclaw-wechat --json
   ```

5. Verify npm is still `release.yml` + `npm-publish` and ClawHub is exactly `NewFuture/openclaw-weixin` + `release.yml` + `clawhub-publish`.
6. Retain both protected environments permanently. Do not merge, rename, or delete either environment.

No external environments, trusted publishers, tags, packages, releases, or workflow runs were mutated by this PR.

body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stack: #14855 -> #14856 -> #14769 -> #14857 -> #14858. Top of the chain.
> Review only the last commit.

Gives `nodes.ItemDefinition` the `collect()` protocol, so a non-Python collector
can have its test definitions parametrized through `pytest_generate_tests`:

```python
class YamlDefinition(nodes.ItemDefinition):
    parametrize_argnames = ("value",)

    def make_item(self, parent, *, name, callspec, nodeid, context):
        return YamlItem.from_parent(
            parent, name=name, nodeid=nodeid, spec=dict(callspec.params)
        )
```

Ids, `pytest.param(...)` marks and node-id selection work as they do for Python
tests. Attaching the callspec, its marks and its id to the generated item is done
by the protocol rather than left to each `make_item()` — the callspec drives
reordering and high-scoped param caching, so it is not optional.

`ParametrizeContext` moves into `_pytest.parametrize` as the collector-agnostic
base of `Metafunc`, which overrides four seams (`_infer_scope`,
`_validate_argnames`, `_register_direct_params`, `_introspection_target`).

**Not included:** fixture resolution for non-Python items — no `indirect=True`,
no scope inference, no requesting fixtures.
`doc/en/proposals/generic_fixture_closures.rst` writes up the four couplings in
the way and a three-step path.

Requires #14855: `test_ids_and_marks_from_pytest_param` hits the skip-location
`INTERNALERROR` without it. Relevant if the chain is reordered.

author: lin-snow
body:
Follow-up to #2864, which merged one commit before this fix landed on the branch. Raised by Copilot on that PR.

## Problem

`continue-on-error` covers the staging upload but not the step that reports its failure. That step calls `gh api …/commits/{sha}/comments`, so a 403 on the comment API, a rate limit or a transient 5xx fails it and turns red a matrix job whose **production publish already succeeded**.

That is precisely the outcome the step exists to avoid: a red merge workflow invites a re-run, and here the production upload carries no `-f`, so the re-run 409s and fails again.

## Change

The report step is `continue-on-error` too, and no longer depends on the token to be useful: the message goes to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` first, which needs no permissions, and the commit comment is best-effort after it.

Verified by running the step's script with a `gh` stub that exits 1 on a simulated 403 — the script exits 1, `continue-on-error` absorbs it, and the summary still carries the full report. `actionlint`: 4 → 4 findings, all pre-existing.

author: allmight2002
srid
body:
Running a dev or e2e padi beside the production one is the normal shape on any developer's machine — and it used to stop every flag-less `kolu` command dead: *more than one padi daemon is running on this host — set $PADI_SOCKET or pass --socket to pick one*. Fine for a human at a shell. **Fatal for a headless MCP client**, which has nobody to type the `export`: `kolu mcp` exits 1, and the agent session silently gets no kolu tools while the production padi is up and healthy the whole time.

**The tie was never real.** Every extra daemon is keyed to an *explicit* `--state-root` / `KOLU_PADI_STATE_DIR`, so at most one live daemon serves the root **this environment** names — `namePadiStateRootForDiscovery()`, which the production `kolu` wrapper already exports as `$HOME/.local/state/padi` (`default.nix`'s `exportPadiStateDirRun`). That daemon is the **primary**, and resolution now picks it. Reading it back out of the `state-root` manifest the daemon wrote about itself is not a guess between equals; it is the same identity both sides already agreed on.

Reported by olai's orchestrator, which embeds kolu's MCP server by spawning `kolu mcp` from a systemd user service. Zero client change — a bare `kolu mcp` just works now.

### What decides "primary"

```
--socket ─┐
--state-root ─┤
$PADI_SOCKET ─┤
              └─→ discover live daemons ─┬─ exactly one → dial it (unchanged)
                                         ├─ several, one serves $KOLU_PADI_STATE_DIR
                                         │            (else ~/.local/state/padi) → PRIMARY  ← new
                                         └─ several, none does → refuse, naming the root
```

### Three deliberate non-shortcuts

| Tempting | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Exclude contract-skewed daemons from the count | If the **primary** is the stale build, excluding it silently attaches you to a dev daemon and drives another workspace's terminals. A skewed primary is still selected, then fails with the honest upgrade line — a stale build is a reason to upgrade, never a reason to guess. |
| Add a `kolu mcp detect` verb for clients to pre-resolve | Still needs all of the above defined first, then adds a verb, a two-step spawn protocol in every embedding client, and a JSON schema — to deliver a reason string the #2148 startup probe already writes to stderr. |
| Make the sole-daemon arm require a primary too | A dev box running only its dev padi has always worked flag-lessly. Left alone on purpose. *Worth a look, reviewers: a dev-shell `kolu` with only production up still dials production — pre-existing, not introduced here.* |

### What the review gauntlet changed

The original change was ~1 function. Most of the diff is what four review passes then found, and all of it is in the same blast radius:

- **`padi-tui` kept its own copy of the refusal sentence** (lowy ∥ hickey both landed on it) — and adding the primary concept made the two copies drift: padi-tui's never told users `$PADI_SOCKET` picks a padi. Hand-rolling only the `many` arm also let **`none` fall through to a success**, dialing a socket nothing serves instead of saying no daemon is running. It now delegates to `localPadiSocket`; there is no second sentence left to drift.
- **The sole-daemon test was vacuous** (grok, debate round 1). Driven through the real registry it can never assert the `one` arm on a machine that runs a padi of its own — the exact hosts this policy exists for. `classifyLivePadis` now takes the live daemons as a *list*, so every arm including `none` is pinned hermetically.
- **A blank `--socket` silently resolved to the primary** (altitude pass, then code-police). `--socket "$SOCK"` with `$SOCK` unset reads as "no socket given", so it fell through to discovery — which *used* to refuse and now succeeds. The user who named one padi would drive another workspace's terminals. `localPadiTargetOf` in `@kolu/padi` now owns argv→target for both faces, blank-checked *before* mutual exclusion (my first attempt had that order backwards, and the test I wrote for it passed under either branch).

### Honoring the design philosophy

- **Fail fast, no fallbacks** — a genuine no-primary case still refuses loudly (and now says which root it looked for, so *"kolu is down"* is distinguishable from *"none of these is yours"*); an environment that cannot name a root throws rather than defaulting; nothing degrades to "whichever daemon I found first".
- **Volatility boundaries** — no new package and no new receptacle. This is a leaf refinement of the one place `(host, state-root)` identity is spelled (`@kolu/padi/stateRoot`), beside the discovery it narrows. Both faces consume the same `PadiSocketResolution`, and after this PR neither formats a sentence of its own.
- **Reuse the source of truth** — no new env var and no second formula: `namePadiStateRootForDiscovery()` was already the naming rule, and the `state-root` manifest was already the identity record. `daemonServesStateRoot` is extracted so the adopt path and the dial path cannot classify the same daemon differently, and the tests use `@kolu/daemon-test-gate`'s canonical locator scrub rather than hand-picking env vars.

### Known debt, not fixed here

`kaval-tui`'s `resolveSocketPath` has the **identical `none` fall-through** that this PR fixes for `padi-tui` — with no kaval running it dials a socket nothing serves instead of saying so, and its `many` message likewise never mentions `$KAVAL_SOCKET`. It predates this branch, lives in a face this PR otherwise doesn't touch, and wants a `localKavalSocket` sibling to fix properly. Recorded in `kaval/src/socketPath.ts`'s docstring rather than left to be rediscovered. The kaval resolution deliberately does **not** get the primary rule: a kaval is spawned by a padi and every kolu PTY carries `$KAVAL_SOCKET`, so nothing headless reaches a flag-less `kaval-tui`.

### Verified against the live host

This machine had two live daemons while developing, so the reported failure reproduced verbatim — and the same command is green on the same host after:

```
# before
$ kolu mcp </dev/null
kolu mcp: more than one padi daemon is running on this host — set $PADI_SOCKET or pass --socket to pick one:
  PADI_SOCKET=/run/user/1000/padi-7cf24532456b0b94/padi.sock
  PADI_SOCKET=/run/user/1000/padi-8a396aeaf04a23d3/padi.sock
EXIT=1

# after
$ kolu mcp </dev/null
EXIT=0        # resolution: { kind: "primary", socket: ".../padi-7cf24532456b0b94/padi.sock" }
```

`padi-7cf24532456b0b94` is the digest of `/home/srid/.local/state/padi` — confirmed against that daemon's own manifest, not computed by hand.

Unit coverage: padi 713, padi-tui 25 (was 19), kolu-cli 67, kaval 112. The pure `classifyLivePadis` cases pin every arm; three real-registry cases cover the discovery→liveness→manifest wiring and the refusal text. *Those are hermetic despite discovery also unioning the real `/tmp` and `/run/user/$UID` drawers: each pins a `$HOME` inside a fresh temp dir, so a real daemon can join the candidate list but can never win the match nor drop the count below two.*

### Try it locally

```sh
nix run github:juspay/kolu/padi-primary -- mcp
```

author: jkitchin
body:
Closes #981.

## What was wrong

A `Constraint` body may be **array-valued**: `k * x - b == 0` on a 3-vector is
*one* `Constraint` object standing for *three* scalar equations. This is the same
one-object-many-rows distinction #908 fixed in the incumbent verifiers, and the
NLP evaluator, the modeling layer and the Rust IR all already handle it.

The relaxation engine did not. `build_uniform_relaxation` emitted one LP row per
`Constraint` object, so its interval walk hit a numpy array where it expected a
float, raised `TypeError: only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python
scalars`, and the caller degraded to building **no relaxation at all**. The dual
bound then fell back to the trivial objective floor -- exactly `0.0` for a sum of
squares -- and the *relative* gap against zero can never close, so no time limit
could certify.

Sound (dropping relaxation rows only enlarges the feasible set), but it silently
disabled global optimality for every vectorized model: DAE collocation, the `nn`
layer formulations, and any numpy-style user model. The term classifier had the
same blind spot from the other side -- a vectorized product classified whole
matches no scalar pattern, lands in `general_nl`, and its variables never become
partition candidates, so spatial branching had nothing to branch on either.

## The fix

`python/discopt/_relax/scalarize.py` (new):

- `static_shape(expr)` recomputes an expression's shape **bottom-up**. It
  deliberately does not start from the cached `_known_shape`, which is `None` on
  any node built over a matmul (matmul is outside the M8 shape guard) and
  therefore reports "unknown" for the entire DAE collocation body.
- `scalar_elements(expr)` rewrites an array-valued expression into one scalar
  expression per flat element, in `np.ravel` order, using numpy's own
  broadcasting index arithmetic so the rewrite is value-preserving by
  construction.
- Returns `None` -- never `[]` -- when static scalarization is not possible.
  `None` means "caller keeps its previous behaviour"; `[]` would drop rows
  silently, which is exactly how this stayed invisible.
- `MAX_SCALAR_ELEMENTS = 200_000` refuses an accidental huge broadcast at
  WARNING rather than truncating.

`canonicalize()` now emits one canonical node per **scalar row**, with a
`constraint_index` row map back to the owning `Constraint` and a
`constraint_exprs` tuple that pins the fresh element expressions (the
stale-`id()` hazard `cnode_of` documents). `uniform_relax` and `term_classifier`
consume the expansion.

## Verification

**Regression test** -- `python/tests/test_981_vectorized_relaxation.py`, 5 smoke +
2 slow. Five of the seven fail on the pre-fix tree, measured by stashing the
source change with the test file in place:

```
FAILED test_vectorized_bilinear_matches_its_scalar_transcription
FAILED test_vectorized_constraint_expands_to_one_canonical_row_per_element
FAILED test_scalar_model_canonicalization_is_unchanged
FAILED test_dae_collocation_certifies_a_real_bound
FAILED test_dae_bound_survives_a_narrowed_parameter_box
E       AssertionError: assert 0.0 > 0.0
E        +  where 0.0 = SolveResult(status='feasible', obj=0.0171, gap=0.0171, time=120.0s, nodes=8639).bound
5 failed, 2 passed in 240.84s
```

All 7 pass after. The bound assertion is the load-bearing one: `optimal` alone
would not discriminate, since a small enough objective satisfies the *absolute*
gap tolerance against a zero bound.

**Value preservation** -- every element of every supported node type is evaluated
against the whole array through the same DAG compiler the solver uses, at 3 random
points each: 132 element comparisons, and the count itself is asserted non-zero
(CLAUDE.md §6).

**The reported instance** -- `tutorial_dae`'s parameter-estimation cell:

| | status | bound | gap | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | `feasible` | `0.0` | never closes | 493 s |
| after | `optimal` | `0.00155805` | 1.5e-07, certified | ~10 s |

Same estimate (`k=0.4837`, 3.27 % relative error). The `time_limit=20.0` stopgap
and the `{note}` admonition explaining it are reverted, and the notebook is
re-executed.

**Bound-neutrality for scalar models** (CLAUDE.md §5, bound-neutral regime). Every
row in the in-repo `.nl` corpus is scalar, so `scalar_elements` returns the body
object itself and nothing downstream can differ. Measured rather than argued:

- *Canonicalization identity*, all 66 instances: the row map is the identity, the
  row count is unchanged, and every `constraint_exprs[i] is model._constraints[i].body`.
  3835 assertions, count asserted non-zero.
- *A/B solve panel* at a 20 s limit, both arms gated on a version marker
  (`fix-marker-present` asserted True on one arm and False on the other, per
  CLAUDE.md §8). Of the **50 instances that terminate in both arms, status,
  objective, bound, node_count and gap_certified are exactly equal on all 50**.
  Of the 16 that hit the limit, 15 match on status and bound; `tanksize`'s bound
  differs in the 5th decimal (1.2668572 vs 1.2668921) at 10208 vs 10285 nodes --
  a node-throughput artifact of a wall-clock limit, and `tanksize` is one of the
  66 instances whose DAG was proved identical object-for-object, so no code path
  differs there.

**Required suites**

author: wprhvso
body:
A command that takes an argument often has its continuation arrive as an ordinary message, which matches no command filter and so never reaches the buffer at all. There was no way to ask "are you already collecting for this message?" — _batches is private and pending is a global count.

MessageBuffer.is_buffering answers it using the buffer's own key builder, so a second entry can be registered into the same buffer for continuations. It is true only while a batch actually holds messages: a dispatched batch stays in the dictionary for one more idle window and must not count as open.

It lives on MessageBuffer rather than BufferedRouter because buffers may each carry a different key builder, so a router-level answer would be about a different question.

author: niravshah2705
body:
## Context

`GET /api/settings-policy/settings/org` **403'd real org admins** — the root cause behind #109's client stopgap. The org service and settings service keep **separate Firestore user namespaces**, so a user who is `ORG_ADMIN` in the org service is org-less (`org_id=None`) in the settings service, and `require_org_admin` always failed. PR #109 disabled the org-policy card (`ORG_POLICY_MANAGEABLE=false`) as a stopgap; this fixes it at the root and re-enables the feature.

## Approach

Propagate org membership from the **authoritative** org service via the **gateway** — the only browser-facing origin, and one that already pulls `org_id`/`org_role` from org `/api/v1/me` for billing.

- **`services/gateway/src/proxy.js`** — add an `injectHeaders(req)` hook to `createProxy`. The proxy builds headers from `{}`, so it never forwards client-supplied headers → injected values can't be spoofed.
- **`services/gateway/src/index.js`** — a `resolveOrgMembership` middleware on the **org-scoped** settings-policy mount resolves `{org_id, org_role}` via `callJson(orgUrl, '/api/v1/me')` and injects `x-org-id`/`x-org-role`. Fail-safe: any miss injects nothing → settings stays org-less (403), never a false grant. Keyed off the authenticated bearer, never client input.
- **`services/settings/app/middleware/auth.py`** — when a forwarded user token is present, the gateway's `x-org-*` headers override the org-less local record when building the `Principal` (validated against the `OrgRole` enum; absent/invalid → keep the local record).
- **`public/js/views/settings.js`** — re-enable the org-scope policy card + vault for org admins (revert #109's stopgap); keep the `deriveIdentity` `has_organization` bug fix.

## Security (reviewed `cross-tenant-isolation`, `header-trust-abuse`, `api-security`)

The trusted-proxy exception holds: the settings service is **IAM-gated to the gateway SA only** (`deploy/gcp/terraform/settings_service.tf:63,196-202`), and the gateway builds proxy headers from `{}` so client-supplied `x-org-*` are never forwarded. A browser can neither reach settings directly nor smuggle these headers through the gateway. Org identity is derived from the authoritative org service keyed by the authenticated bearer. Resolution is per-request (fresh), so a role change/removal takes effect immediately (no cache staleness).

## Tests

- Settings authz matrix (`test_authz.py`) gains: header-granted `ORG_ADMIN` → 200; forwarded `MEMBER` → 403; malformed `x-org-*` ignored → 403 (no escalation).
- [x] Gateway unit tests green (67); all JS/Python syntax valid.
- [ ] End-to-end on staging: an org admin manages org policy (200); a non-admin/org-less user sees it disabled; a browser-sent `X-Org-Role: ORG_ADMIN` still 403s (stripped at the gateway).

## Notes

- Conceptually follows #109 (this reverts the client stopgap it added).
- The org `/me` pull runs per org-scoped settings-policy request; a short-TTL gateway cache is a possible future optimization.
- The still-absent project-membership sync can later ride this same trusted-header channel.

body:
| 🚥 Resolves RM-17863 |
| :------------------- |

> 🎨 UI is awaiting confirmation from Ryan.
> 🔗 Part of a 3-PR chain: [ai-cli-runner#109](https://github.com/readmeio/ai-cli-runner/pull/109), [readme#20253](https://github.com/readmeio/readme/pull/20253)

## 🧰 What's changing

`importDocs()` for website-URL imports now returns a `sources` array — one entry per source URL — recording how the CLI resolved it: the requested URL, any redirect, the adopted docs-route base, the final URL, and which discovery route produced the skeleton (`llms` / `mintlify` / `archbee` / `scrape` / `sitemap` / `none`, plus a `scrapeDiscarded` flag when the coverage gate threw the scrape away).

## 🧬 Why

The import runner needs this signal to decide whether a submitted URL actually resolved to a documentation site. Strong routes (llms.txt, Mintlify, Archbee) are docs sites by construction; weak routes (scrape/sitemap) trigger an AI docs-site check downstream that can surface a soft "this might not be a docs site" warning (slug `non_docs_site`) on the import progress screen. The import itself is never blocked.

Pure metadata bolt-on — no behavior change to discovery, staging, or zipping.

author: osocordobes
body:
Cuatro agujeros de la misma familia. El repo **ya tenía** `limitByIp`/`limitByKey`
(`lib/security/rate-limit.ts`) y `verifyTurnstile` y los usaba en **todas** las
acciones anónimas menos en estas.

## 1. Login sin freno propio

El intento sale del server, así que el rate-limit por IP de GoTrue contabiliza
la **IP de egress de Vercel**, no la del atacante. Su 429 le caía al **usuario
legítimo** —y encima disfrazado de "Email o contraseña incorrectos"— mientras el
atacante seguía probando passwords gratis.

Ahora: **20/h por IP** (tolera el wifi compartido de una clínica con varios
profesionales) y **10/h por email** (credential stuffing distribuido en N IPs
contra una misma cuenta), consumidos **antes** de tocar Supabase.

## 2. Captcha progresivo, no permanente

El plan pedía Turnstile en el login. Al implementarlo apareció un problema
serio: **el widget de Turnstile solo existe en la vista de signup**, así que
exigirlo en el login habría **roto el login entero en producción** — y este PR
convive con el fix del loop de login, que es justamente el bug que reportó el
cliente.

Además, un captcha en cada login es fricción diaria sobre un profesional que
entra a su consultorio todas las mañanas, y con los límites de arriba ya puestos
su valor marginal contra el atacante es bajo.

Solución: se pide **recién a partir del 6º intento de la hora para ese email**
(`LOGIN_CAPTCHA_AFTER = 5`, leyendo el `remaining` que ya devuelve el
limitador). El server responde `code: "captcha_required"`, el formulario monta
el widget y reintenta con el token.

- Uso normal (1-3 logins por hora): **nunca ve un captcha**.
- Barrido sobre una cuenta: tiene que resolver un captcha para los intentos 6 a
  10, y después se topa con el corte duro.

El token de Turnstile es de un solo uso, así que tras cada fallo el widget se
resetea (si no, el reintento siguiente falla por token consumido).

## 3. El oráculo de enumeración

El branch "Esta cuenta entra con Google" confirma la existencia de una cuenta y
dispara un query `service_role` por intento. Quedó **detrás** de los límites de
arriba: cada sondeo consume cupo de las dos ventanas.

## 4. `requestPasswordReset` sin límite

Cada llamada gatilla un mail de Supabase Auth, y el SMTP built-in da **2-4
mails/hora por proyecto**: unos pocos requests anónimos dejaban sin mails de
auth a **todo el producto**, incluido el **portal del paciente, que es
magic-link-only** — sin mail no entra nadie.

Mismos números que `resendSignupConfirmation` (10/h por IP, 5/h por email), que
comparte exactamente el mismo recurso escaso.

De paso: el botón "Enviar link" tenía un `void pending;` con un comentario que
mentía sobre por qué no se deshabilitaba. Ahora se deshabilita de verdad y dice
"Enviando…".

## 5. `signUpForInvitationAction` no miraba la invitación

Creaba la cuenta con `service.auth.admin.createUser({ email_confirm: true })`
—service-role, salteando GoTrue— **sin mirar la invitación**: la action ni
siquiera recibía el token. Cualquiera con su URL podía crear cuentas
auto-confirmadas y **anular el "Confirm email" que está ON en producción**. Y si
el email ya existía, **forzaba `email_confirm: true` sobre la cuenta ajena antes
de validar la password**.

Ahora:

1. exige una invitación **PENDIENTE, vigente y del mismo email** — las mismas
   condiciones que `accept_member_invitation` (M49). Si divergieran se podría
   crear una cuenta que después no puede aceptar la invitación;
2. da de alta por `supabase.auth.signUp`, el camino canónico del repo, que
   **respeta el toggle** "Confirm email";
3. **nunca** toca el estado de confirmación de una cuenta ajena.

Con "Confirm email" ON el alta no abre sesión, así que la pantalla ahora dice
"revisá tu email" en vez de refrescar una página que se vería igual (`.au-ok`,
el hermano afirmativo de `.au-err`, con los mismos tokens).

El token crudo solo se hashea (`sha256` hex, idéntico al
`encode(digest(p_token,'sha256'),'hex')` de la RPC): no se persiste ni se
loguea.

Todos los caminos de error responden el **mismo mensaje genérico**: no se
distingue "token inválido" de "email que no coincide" ni de "la cuenta ya
existe".

## Cómo se verifica

`tests/unit/invitation-guard.test.ts` cubre la lógica pura del gate: que el hash
coincida con el de la RPC, la forma del token (basura cortada antes de tocar la
DB), estado ≠ PENDIENTE, vencida, `expires_at` ilegible → **fail-closed**, el
borde exacto de la expiración, y email distinto — que es el punto del gate.

Gates locales: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test:unit` (1395 tests) y
`pnpm build`, los cuatro verdes.

author: terjekv
body: ## Summary - move the event-delivery persistence row, Diesel mappings, SQL cursor mapping, and internal claim token into the PostgreSQL adapter - keep the application-facing delivery DTOs backend-neutral while retaining the mandatory event-delivery administration and worker storage contracts - route platform-suite fixture setup through explicit test-support APIs instead of opening PostgreSQL connections or mutating delivery tables directly - add architectural guards and documentation for the completed event-delivery persistence boundary ## Architecture `EventDeliveryResponse`, `EventDeliveryUpdateResponse`, health projections, IDs, and statuses remain public storage-neutral DTOs. The PostgreSQL adapter now owns `EventDeliveryRow`, including its Diesel/schema integration, SQL cursor behavior, and claim token. Row-returning query helpers are crate-private, and the few fixture-only operations are compiled only with `integration-test-support`. This preserves the required `EventDeliveryAdministrationStorage` and worker capabilities: a backend must still implement the complete lifecycle rather than silently exposing a partial event-delivery feature set. No storage contract version change is needed because the mandatory trait surface and DTO semantics are unchanged. The HTTP behavior is unchanged, including list/filter/cursor responses, retry and dead-letter transitions, fanout, claiming, and health reporting. Internal claim tokens remain absent from API responses and are now physically confined to the adapter. ## Compatibility and operations - PostgreSQL remains behaviorally unchanged. - Platform compatibility tests now exercise delivery behavior through the same application/test boundary available to backend suites. - Adapter-row debug output redacts both claim tokens and recorded delivery errors. - Boundary tests reject future Diesel, schema, SQL cursor, PostgreSQL row, and direct-connection leakage into the public model and platform request tests. ## Changelog and API schema This is an internal architecture refactor with no user-facing behavior change, so no changelog entry is warranted. The HTTP schema is unchanged, so OpenAPI regeneration is not required. ## Verification - `source .env && ./run_tests.sh` - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `npx markdownlint-cli2 --config .markdownlint.json "**/*.md" "!target"` - `scripts/test-classify-ci-changes.sh` - `cargo test --bin hubuum-server dockerfile_copies_every_workspace_manifest --locked` - `docker build --build-arg 'CARGO_BUILD_FLAGS=-F tls-rustls -F tls-openssl --locked --release' --tag hubuum-server:verify .` Stacked above #326. author: yonatanvol
body:
Replaces cream-and-brass with near-black + acid lime. The old palette was heritage-bicycle-shop language; this shop sells electric bikes and scooters.

## Colour

**Lime is brand and action only** — logo, price, primary button, focus. Availability gets its own scale. A page where "in stock" and "buy now" share a colour reads as though everything is on offer.

All eight pairs measured **before** locking:

| | Ratio |
|---|---|
| lime on black | 16.73:1 |
| off-white on black | 16.03:1 |
| grey on black | 5.74:1 |
| in stock / supplier / confirm / out | 8.83 · 9.28 · 10.06 · 6.35 |
| black on lime (button) | 16.73:1 |

Lowest is 5.74:1. Last round I shipped `brass-dark` at 4.22:1 under a plan requiring 4.5:1 — hence checking first this time.

## The larger finding: most of the WooCommerce CSS was dead

Grepped the rendered archive:

| Selector | Occurrences |
|---|---|
| `span.onsale` | **0** |
| `ul.products` | **0** |
| `woocommerce-loop-product__title` | **0** |
| `wc-block-components-product-sale-badge` | 12 |
| `wc-block-components-product-button` | 62 |

Twenty Twenty-Five renders the catalogue through the **Product Collection block**. The classic selectors matched nothing. The cards still looked broadly right — `theme.json` and inherited body styles were doing the work while my rules sat inert, which is exactly why it survived review.

Same mistake as the `loop_shop_columns` filters removed in the previous commit. **Twice now** — writing classic WooCommerce for a block theme. Classic selectors kept as a genuine fallback rather than deleted; they cost nothing.

## Three bugs found by looking rather than assuming

**Cache busting used the theme version**, which doesn't change when the CSS does. Returning visitors keep the cached stylesheet. Cost a confused round of "the palette didn't apply" locally; in production a fix would reach only new visitors. Now keyed to `filemtime()`.

**Two columns at any window size.** Two causes, both mine: a generous gap broke WooCommerce's grid formula (it subtracts the gap *it* assumes), and `theme.json`'s 820px content measure capped the catalogue. Now explicit gap-independent tracks at the wide measure — matched at their specificity rather than reaching for `!important`.

**`overflow: hidden`** on the image well clipped the sale badge to "מבצ".

## Real store details

`דרך חיים ברלב 98, תל אביב-יפו` and `052-487-3436`, verified from the Google Business listing, replacing the invented "רחוב הדוגמה 12".

**Opening hours are marked as unconfirmed rather than guessed.** Only Tuesday is verifiable while logged out of Google. Publishing invented hours for a real shop sends customers to a closed door.

## Tests

- `composer check` — PHPCS, PHPStan L5, HPOS sniff, **64 tests / 117 assertions** ✅
- Contrast: 8/8 pass 4.5:1 ✅
- Archive renders 3 columns at 1440px, badge intact, all 16 images present ✅
- Product images regenerated on the dark ground — old ivory ones read as broken rectangles ✅

**RTL:** verified throughout — logical properties only, badge on the correct inline edge.
**Mobile:** buttons meet the 44px target minimum.

## Not included

Cortez section and video hero — waiting on assets from Eli. The availability model is the next branch and is unaffected by any of this.

* **New Features**
  * Updated homepage messaging for electric bikes and repair services.
  * Added store contact details, phone and WhatsApp buttons, address, and opening hours.
  * Added a notice indicating that store hours require confirmation.
  * Added responsive product collections, sorting controls, sale badges, and add-to-cart styling.

* **Style**
  * Introduced a dark, high-contrast design with lime accents and bold sans-serif typography.
  * Updated buttons, forms, navigation, product cards, notices, and homepage sections.

* **Accessibility**
  * Added automated color-contrast checks for improved readability.

author: charliedowler
body:
## What

The SPK-909 frontend/backend skew guard — invisible by design:

- **Build hash emitted at build time**: the production build writes a build hash consumed both as a meta tag in `index.html` and by the backend module — verified end-to-end against a real build (identical value on both sides).
- **Backend stamps the served hash** on every response; the frontend compares its own baked-in hash.
- **Refresh on the NEXT navigation** on mismatch — never mid-task, no data loss, no error card. The refresher lives on a persistent layout route deliberately (a per-route mount would reset its ref and never fire).
- Complements (doesn't replace) the existing chunk-error boundary.
- react-doctor clean on all touched files (barrel imports converted to direct module imports; one now-unused re-export dropped).

## Verification

New tests 9/9 (6 detection, 3 navigation-deferral); full frontend suite 2,369/2,369 green (verified against a clean main baseline after ruling out a resource-starvation artifact); typecheck clean across common/backend/frontend; real-build hash roundtrip proven.

Part of #27140

Closes: SPK-922
