## Description
Adds end-to-end receipt/expense management (UV-7).

Any user can submit a receipt (amount, date, optional category/vendor/description, and one or more photo/PDF attachments) from the new **Receipts** page. Admins and Financial Managers see and manage everyone's receipts, set/confirm the payment method, mark receipts as paid, and soft-delete/restore/permanently delete them; regular users may only edit or delete their own unpaid receipt within 15 minutes of submitting it. The list supports filtering by date range, category, and paid/open status, and privileged roles can export the currently filtered receipts as a ZIP (CSV + all attached files).

Also included, as supporting/related work:
- **On-device OCR**: attaching a receipt photo or PDF auto-fills amount and date by scanning it locally in the browser (pdfjs-dist + tesseract.js, German amount/date recognition, no server round-trip); installed PWAs get a dedicated camera-capture button.
- **Receipt categories**: new Admin settings page to create/delete the categories used to tag receipts (a category can't be deleted while still assigned to an active receipt).
- **Receipt analytics**: year-scoped charts for Admin/Financial Manager — stacked monthly spend-by-category bar chart, category breakdown pie chart with yearly total in the center, and a year-over-year totals chart (`@mui/x-charts`).
- **Full system backup**: the Backup page can now download a full backup (`Verein_Backup_Full_<date>.zip`) containing the DB dump plus every uploaded receipt file, and restore accepts either a plain `.sql` dump or such a `.zip`; downloads are now streamed directly to the response instead of via a temp file.
- **Infra**: `docker-compose*.yml` mount `./receipts:/app/receipts` for persistence; `nginx.conf` raises `client_max_body_size` (50M → 10G) and relaxes proxy buffering/timeouts for the larger exports/backups, and strips the query string from access logs so the download access token isn't written to disk.
- **Fix**: demo-login dialog text was using theme tokens that turned illegible in dark mode against the dialog's always-light background; switched to fixed colors.

Full details in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) under `[v1.5.0] UV-7`.

author: benevolentfutures
body:
## Summary

Two independent layout defects (do not share a root cause — see ticket MRQ-77):

**Defect A — `/evaluation` Round 2 card.** `EvaluationPage.tsx` rendered `[round1][round2][arrow]` into the three-column grid `minmax(0,1fr) 34px minmax(0,1fr)`, so Round 2 landed in the 34px arrow track (one-word-per-line wrapping, "IdentitySep visible 8" wrapped-text artifact). Fixed by extracting the round-card JSX into a `renderRoundCard(round, index)` helper and calling it on both sides of the arrow div, restoring the prototype's `[card][arrow][card]` DOM order for both the populated and empty-round-fallback cases.

**Defect B — `/submissions/:id` aside overlap.** The grid tracks (`.record-layout`: `minmax(0,1fr) 330px`) were always correctly sized — confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()`/`getComputedStyle()` at every viewport width from 997px to 1322px, no exceptions. The actual cause is inside the main track: `.record-summary`'s first flex child (title + abstract) has no explicit `min-width`, so it defaults to `min-width: auto`, which lets an unbreakable run of text (a bare URL with no spaces, as in `sub_agent-eng`'s abstract) hold the item at its min-content width and paint over the fixed-width aside beside it — independent of the grid's own sizing. Reproduced directly: injecting a genuinely unbreakable token measured a 159px `.record-main` overflow (`scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth`); adding `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to `.record-summary p` and `min-width: 0` to its parent's first flex child took it to 0px. This idiom already exists twice elsewhere in `record.css` (page-head `h1`, `.record-answer strong`).

## Gate status — read before merging

Per an operator-directed, fleet-wide gate correction while CI/local-suite contention issues were being resolved in parallel by other tickets (load average had hit 158 on this 16-core box from five agents running full suites concurrently; CI itself was pinned to an unsupported Node version and `trace:ac` had a real parser bug — both since fixed on `main`), this PR was validated with:

- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- ✅ `npx vite build` — clean
- ✅ `npm run check:design` — pass, 0 findings
- ✅ `npm run check:api` — pass, 0 findings
- ✅ `npm run trace:ac` — pass, 0 errors, 0 uncovered
- ✅ This diff's own test files, standalone: `tests/unit/submission-record-overflow.test.ts` (new, defect B regression guard) and defect A's manual browser verification
- ⏭️ **Skipped**: full `npm test` and full `npm run pr-gate` locally, per standing directive to let GitHub CI (load-independent) run the full suite instead of adding to local contention. CI will run on this push.

## Regression guard

`tests/unit/submission-record-overflow.test.ts` asserts `record.css` keeps both declarations (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.record-summary p`, `min-width: 0` on `.record-summary`'s first flex child), following the existing CSS-source-assertion pattern in this repo (`reviewer-surface.AC-61-158-159.test.ts`) — there is no DOM/layout engine in this test suite to measure real overflow directly, so this is the closest available guard against reverting the fix. Live browser measurement is the record of the actual fix (see validation evidence below).

## Validation evidence

Live-verified in c11-browser against `wrangler dev --port 8802` on seeded demo data, both defects, both required breakpoints each:

- `/evaluation` — desktop (1319px), 900px, 600px. Equal-width round cards, arrow between them, no wrapping artifact, empty-round fallback preserved in the extracted helper.
- `/submissions/sub_agent-eng` — 1319px, 999px, 759px. `WAVE` value and full schedule-box venue text visible, no overlap.
- `/submissions/sub_gemini-deep-research` and `/submissions/sub_what-rl-means-for-agents` (tall-content and scheduled-content controls) re-verified still correct after the fix.
- Defect B mechanism proven directly: synthetic unbreakable-token injection reproduced 159px overflow pre-fix, 0px post-fix.

Screenshots attached to the Lattice ticket (MRQ-77) with `--role validation`.

## Scope

Layout only, no data/API/route changes, per ticket boundary. Touches only `src/ui/evaluation/EvaluationPage.tsx`, `src/ui/submissions/record.css`, and the new test file — matches this ticket's owned files exactly.

author: saquibreja7-hash
body:
## Summary

Two related changes to the public site.

**1. The TASI 2026 agenda is now live at `/programme`.** That page previously showed a "programme will be announced soon" placeholder behind the edition toggle; it now renders 46 sessions across 13-15 October 2026 and defaults to the 2026 tab. 2025 stays available behind the toggle and is unchanged.

**2. `info@trustandsafetyfestival.com` is replaced with `india@trustandsafetyfestival.com`** everywhere it appeared — 25 occurrences across 14 files.

## Why no speaker names

The source agenda marks most participants as *emailed*, *TBC*, or *to be invited* rather than confirmed, and the two source sheets **disagree with each other** on who is confirmed. Publishing those names would announce people who have not agreed to attend. So every 2026 session ships with an empty `speakers` array and a "speakers to be announced" note. Names get added as each line-up firms up.

## Agenda conflicts resolved

The source sheets contained real scheduling errors. Decisions taken:

| Problem | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Women's Safety panel at Day 1 15:00-17:00 overlapped four other Main Hall sessions (looks like a spreadsheet drag error) | Restored to Day 2 12:35, where the earlier sheet had it |
| Day 2 11:15 Main Hall triple-booked | Fraud & Scams returned to the Workshop Room |
| Keynotes listed as mutually exclusive "Option 1 / Option 2" | Single session title, no speaker, no choice implied |
| Roundtable Room double-booked Day 1 14:00 | Kept the closed-door session |
| Sponsor names baked into session titles (Google, Meta, Snap, Booking.com, Roblox, Cyberlite) | Genericised to "Partner Spotlight" pending signed agreements |
| Weekday labels said Mon/Tue/Wed for 13/14/15 October | Corrected — those are **2025** weekdays; in 2026 the dates fall Tue/Wed/Thu |
| No lunch or breaks in the newer sheet | Carried over from the earlier sheet's grid |

Two judgment calls that are easy to reverse if the organisers disagree: the **Digital Safety for Seniors** spotlight and the **Day 1 evening reception** were both dropped in the newer sheet but kept here, because dropping them left holes in the grid.

## Supporting refactors

- Day handling in the agenda client is derived from `dayLabels` plus a `dayDateMap` prop instead of hardcoded `oct6`/`oct7`/`oct8` keys, so "Add to Calendar" links resolve to October 2026 for the new edition
- Calendar links now honour an explicit end time when a session declares a range, instead of guessing from the next session or a per-format default. This also fixes 2026 receptions exporting as 30 minutes instead of two hours
- Session detail pages resolve 2026 sessions and hide the speakers aside when a session has none
- `build-my-agenda` day grouping is no longer hardcoded, and its stale fallback labels (which said Oct 14/15/16 for the 2025 keys) are corrected

## Tests

Five new tests in `tests/programme-2026.test.cjs` guard the two failure modes that actually matter for this data: a **speaker name leaking** into the 2026 agenda, and a **single-track room being double-booked**. If someone drags a row wrong in a future update, CI catches it instead of the public site.

`npm run lint`, `npm test` (219 passing), `npm run format:check`, and `npm run build` all pass.

## Deployment note

`INBOUND_NOTIFICATION_EMAILS` is optional and falls back to `EVENT_CONFIG.contactEmail`, which this PR points at `india@`. The Vercel value has already been updated separately, so inbound form notifications reach the right inbox either way.

Worth confirming `india@trustandsafetyfestival.com` is actively receiving mail before this deploys, since the site will be directing people there.

body:
The projection H-11 promised when it abolished the container as a storage level. It is deliberately trivial — read the groups the edition declared, in the order it declared them — and **everything interesting is what it refuses**.

## O-44's own check, which I am named verifier for

Two editions over the **same 38 leaves** declare **two** containers and **three**, and both are correct. Nothing reconciles them, deliberately — that disagreement is the case the entire ruling exists for, and the real charts already show it.

## Three refusals

**It never parses a label.** A label is a quotation (H-2): splitting `3:16` to learn a structure is reading meaning out of text, the habit `identity.js` exists to end. A cell proves it by handing over labels that *look* structural — `3:16` and `17-20` — and requiring the container count to come from the ranges alone.

**It never consults the spine**, which is flat by ruling. Inventing a default grouping would make every edition silently agree with the spine's shape: the hub in its last costume.

**It never repairs.** A gap leaves leaves unrenderable; an overlap renders them twice; containers that don't cover the unit mean an unfinished increment. All three scream, and the message names which failure it is rather than saying "invalid chart". Same doctrine as the all-or-nothing presence check — 79 increments pass through here, and **a partial render looks like success**.

---

**Suite: 370 pass, 0 fail** (364 before, 6 new cells).

**Next:** the walk consuming this — then the LAN dev route, then the phone.

author: jsonbored
body:
Step 1 of metagraphed-infra#414. Inert on merge; it becomes load-bearing when the poller changes.

## The problem is the schema, not the chain

`nominator_positions` keeps only the derived value:

```sql
share_fraction double precision   -- normalised across a whole (hotkey, netuid) pool
```

The chain hands us **raw shares** per `(hotkey, coldkey, netuid)`. We discard that and store a number no single row can produce — so the poller must hold all **762,577** rows in memory to compute it. Its own header says so:

> this job buffers the WHOLE scan in memory before writing anything

Every difficulty in #414 follows from that one decision:

| difficulty | cause |
| --- | --- |
| chunks must align to `(hotkey, netuid)` groups | normalisation at write time |
| 762k rows on a container's heap | normalisation at write time |
| a failed pass discards everything | nothing may be written until the walk ends |
| resume needs an exact cursor | there is only one indivisible unit of work |

## What this does

Adds `shares numeric` and recomputes `share_fraction` in **one statement after the prune**, over the complete table. The producer is then free to stream — which is step 2, in the infra repo.

- **`numeric`, not `bigint`** — shares are a u128 (max ~3.4e38 against bigint's ~9.2e18).
- **A decimal STRING on the wire** — 2^53 is the last integer JSON represents exactly, and these run far past it. Validated as digits rather than parsed; Postgres does the arithmetic, and `Number()` on it would reintroduce exactly the loss the string avoids.
- **More accurate than today**, not less: the Rust side computes u128 → f64 division, this divides in `numeric` and casts once at the end.
- **A column we did not have** — absolute stake weight. `share_fraction` can only answer "what proportion", never "how much", from data we already fetch and throw away.

## Why it is safe to merge before the producer exists

The column is nullable, the wire field optional, and the statement carries `shares IS NOT NULL`. It matches no rows today, so the fraction the producer computes stands unchanged. Nothing observable moves until a pass carries shares — and then it does, with no second deploy.

## Ordering, which is the correctness claim

**After the prune** — normalising while superseded rows are present divides by a denominator that includes them. **Before the tally** — which declares the pass whole. **Skipped entirely when the prune failed**, for the same reason the tally is withheld.

**Non-fatal on its own failure.** The rows are correct, just not re-derived; failing the pass over that would trade a served-and-correct table for no pass at all. It rides its own `-normalize` sub-lane verdict so a persistent failure is still visible — carrying the `oncePerPass` flag from #10830, without which a buffered success could never be cleared.

All four properties are asserted, including the statement order (`INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE, INSERT`).

## Also in here

`tests/nominator-positions-neon-write.test.ts` never reset the verdict memo. `recordNeonWriteVerdict` coalesces an unchanged `ok` for ten minutes in **module** state, so a test's verdict rows depended on which tests ran before it — the base and prune rows vanished mid-suite and reappeared when the test ran alone. That is how it was found, and the reset is now a `beforeEach`.

## Not in here

`db/schema.sql` and `generated/db/*`. `neon-migrate.yml` applies `migrations/neon/**` on merge to main and `refresh-neon-schema.yml` snapshots the result on the same push — both own those artifacts, and hand-applying the DDL is what #9867 warns about.

## Verification

Full suite 19,761 passed, `tsc`, `eslint`, `prettier`, `validate:migrations` clean. No visual output touched.

author: adamlabadorf
body:
Implements #19: files larger than a threshold now upload to Zenodo/InvenioRDM via the multipart `M` transfer instead of one giant PUT.

## The protocol (as documented + fixture-verified)

InvenioRDM's multipart transfer ships in the [file transfer types reference](https://inveniordm.docs.cern.ch/reference/file_transfer/) (type `M`, alongside `L`/`F`/`R`) and is implemented by the multipart transfer provider in [invenio-records-resources](https://github.com/inveniosoftware/invenio-records-resources) (`services/files/transfer/providers/multipart.py`); RDM 13 wires it into the uploader UI ([release notes](https://inveniordm.docs.cern.ch/releases/v13/version-v13.0.0/), [worked example repo](https://github.com/mesemus/rdm-13-multipart-example)). Zenodo sandbox already serves it — our Phase 0 spike captured a real registration (fixture 39, `docs/zenodo-notes.md` §4). The flow:

1. **Register** `POST /api/records/{id}/draft/files` with `{"key", "size", "transfer": {"type": "M", "parts": N, "part_size": S}}` → `201` with per-part upload URLs under `links.parts[]` (`{part, url, expiration}`, ~14-day expiry) plus the usual `commit` link. `parts`, `size`, and `part_size` are all required (the provider raises `TransferException` for each).
2. **PUT each part** to its part URL. The provider rejects a direct `…/content` PUT on a multipart file ("Can not set content for multipart file, use the parts instead.") and validates that non-final parts match `part_size` exactly.
3. **Commit** `POST …/commit`. The storage backend may return the md5 immediately, or store the `multipart:{etag}-{part_size}` placeholder and recompute the real checksum in a background task; the transfer type flips to `L`.
4. **Abort** = `DELETE` the draft file entry (the provider's `delete_file` calls `multipart_abort_upload`).

## What the driver does (D43–D45 in `docs/decisions.md`)

- **D43 — threshold routing.** `size > multipartThreshold` → multipart; both threshold and part size are injectable Client fields (`WithMultipartThreshold`/`WithPartSize`), defaulting to 100 MiB each. At or below the threshold the existing single-PUT path is byte-for-byte unchanged. Parts upload **serially** — the `Backend` interface hands the driver an `io.Reader`, not an `io.ReaderAt`; parallel parts would widen the interface for one driver and aren't worth it yet.
- **D44 — checksum honesty.** The commit checksum is verified only when it is an md5 (mismatch fails loudly, same as the single path). A missing checksum or the async `multipart:` placeholder surfaces **no checksum rather than a wrong one** (the s3ws precedent); the manifest pin is the local MD5 either way.
- **D45 — clean aborts.** A failed part, failed commit, malformed part links, or checksum mismatch deletes the pending entry under a cancellation-immune context (`context.WithoutCancel`, 30s bound), so the draft never retains a publish-blocking pending entry — even on Ctrl-C mid-part.

## fakeinvenio

Models the documented protocol: required registration fields, part storage, exact non-final part sizes, direct-content-PUT rejection, commit-with-missing-parts rejection, reassembly + md5, transfer-type flip to `L`, part-link expirations; knobs `FailPart` (500 one part once) and `AsyncMultipartChecksum` (placeholder checksum). Per **D28** the doc comment now marks the multipart model as **DOCUMENTED-only** except the registration shape, which is fixture-verified (fixture 39 — the spike registered but never uploaded parts).

## Tests (TDD — red run before implementation)

- Threshold routing both ways, asserted via the fake's request log (small → one `…/content` PUT, zero part PUTs; large → parts 1..3, zero content PUTs)
- Multipart round trip: 3 parts reassemble, publish, download bytes equal, md5 verified
- Failed part → clean abort → `ListDraftFiles` empty → draft still publishes
- Deterministic cancellation mid-part → `context.Canceled` surfaced, entry still cleaned up
- Async-checksum placeholder → no checksum surfaced, upload succeeds
- Raw-protocol fake tests: commit-with-missing-parts 400, direct content PUT 400, wrong-sized part 400, registration field requirements
- Contract suite untouched and green for all three backends; full battery green: `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags live ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go test -tags integration ./integration/...`, skill-doc tests
- **Live tier**: `TestLiveZenodo_MultipartUpload` uses the injectable knobs to push a ~6 MiB file in 5 MiB parts (the documented S3 part-size floor) against the real sandbox, skip-gated on `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` — the run that keeps the documented-only fake honest.

## Deliberately not done

- **Part-URL expiry re-registration** (an issue #19 bullet): part URLs are minted immediately before use and expire after ~14 days, and a crashed run's pending entry is cleared by publish preflight rather than resumed — so expiry is unreachable within any single upload today. Recorded in D43; revisit if resumable uploads land.
- **Parallel part uploads**: needs `io.ReaderAt` in the `Backend` interface (D43).
- **A multi-GB ≥2-real-part live case**: the injectable-threshold probe exercises 2 real parts at 6 MiB instead, keeping sandbox quota and CI time sane.

author: white-hat
body:
Zed saves the selected external agent per workspace and as an app-wide last-used agent. Uninstalling the agent leaves those saved values in place, so the Agent Panel could restore an agent that no longer exists and fail to start a thread.

For local projects, this changes restoration behavior in these cases:

- A new workspace ignores an uninstalled global last-used agent.
- A reopened workspace ignores its uninstalled agent. It uses an installed global agent if one exists, otherwise it uses the Zed Agent.
- A project opened in the same window does not copy an uninstalled agent from the previous project.
- An unsent draft keeps its text and switches to the selected fallback agent if its original agent was uninstalled.

Two boundaries remain unchanged:

- A thread with a saved session stays bound to its original agent so it can resume after the agent is reinstalled.
- Remote projects keep their saved external-agent selection because this change only detects local uninstalls.

Release Notes:

- Fixed the Agent Panel selecting an uninstalled external agent when opening a project or restoring an unsent draft, which prevented the thread from starting.

author: adamblumoff
body:
Every repository route stacked four bands of chrome before any content: the topbar, a context strip, an eyebrow label, and a title with a description. On `/owner/repo` that pushed the first real content about 260px down a 1000px viewport. The bands also repeated each other. A request detail page rendered "Ready" twice and the branch name three times above the fold, because the repo lifecycle appeared in both the context strip and the request header, and the branch appeared in the title line, the header metadata, and the context rail. The eyebrows compounded it by inventing a second vocabulary for the navigation: the tab said Requests while the page said CONTRIBUTIONS, the tab said Code while the page said BROWSE and titled itself "Repository" under a topbar that already read `adamblumoff/update-demo`.

Underneath, the token layer had drifted into a scale that did not scale. Seven radius tokens covered 4px to 16px in roughly 2px steps, so `radius-md` and `radius-lg` were 6px and 7px and no call site could express a real difference. The Tailwind palette was aliased onto semantics, so `--color-green-700` resolved to `var(--success)` and a component asking for `bg-green-700` was silently asking for success. `--destructive` and `--danger` held identical values in both themes. Light mode set a warm cream background against cool blue-gray borders, muted fills and workspace tabs, which read as a rendering bug rather than a choice, most visibly where the tab strip met the page. Dark mode's border sat at roughly 1.35:1 against the background, so the hairline-heavy layout was simultaneously everywhere and too faint to structure anything. Eight or more shadow recipes were in play, several inlined as arbitrary values.

This change makes each fact appear once and gives the token layer a single source per concept. `PageHeader` and `WorkbenchHeader` merge into one header module, joined by a `WorkbenchBar` for repository sections that carries a screen-reader-only page heading plus its summary and controls, while the nav tab remains the visible view title. `RepositoryContextStrip` is deleted and its facts move into the topbar, where lifecycle only appears when it is not `Ready`. The eyebrow vocabulary is gone. Content on a repository route now begins around 85px instead of 260px.

On tokens, the radii collapse to three steps that read as distinct, the numeric color aliases are replaced by semantic classes so `bg-success` means what it says, `--destructive` becomes an alias of `--danger`, the light neutrals are warmed to match the cream background, the dark border is raised for legible structure, and the shadows reduce to `--shadow-card` and `--shadow-pop`. The `chrome` button variant is deleted; it was a dark gradient used for exactly one secondary action and looked like a foreign object in light mode. New `--app-topbar` and `--app-chrome` variables replace hardcoded pane offsets such as `calc(100dvh-225px)`, which were already stale before this change and would have gone staler as the chrome shrank.

Repetition also lived below the page level. Around ten bespoke empty states and three centered panel states, each with its own min-height, collapse into one `EmptyState` and one `PanelState`. The theme toggle moves into the topbar so it exists on every route rather than only the owner profile, where it previously left no way to switch themes once inside a repository, and its store moves into `use-theme-type`. Skeletons now mirror the shape of the content they stand in for instead of showing five identical bars.

The last piece is density. The topbar and page content now share one 1280px rail so they align. Row status sits beside its title rather than justified to the far edge, which at 1440px had put roughly 1000px between a request and its state. Request rows drop from six metadata fields to five, with the machine id moved to the `title` attribute. Filler descriptions and counts stated three times per section are gone. The mobile file tree goes from three lines per file to one, because its grid columns only applied at `sm:` and each row re-rendered its own Status and Visibility labels. Grouping uses spacing and typographic hierarchy rather than card surfaces, per `AGENTS.md`.

Splitting `history-page.tsx` into seven modules was not in the original plan. Removing components from that file tripped react-doctor's `no-multi-comp` rule, which blocks the build, and splitting it was the honest fix rather than suppressing the rule.

Verified with `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` at 156 passing, all 8 browser smoke tests, and direct Playwright captures at 390px and 1440px in both themes with no horizontal overflow or page errors. Autoreview reported no P0 findings.

The Clerk sign-in widget still did not mount in headless capture, so its contents remain visually unconfirmed. The surrounding auth header was aligned to the shared 57px topbar height.

body:
## What changed

Every model in the picker is now chosen from `smooth-bench agentic` at 28 scenarios × **3 trials** (a scenario passes only if every trial passed). The previous lineup came from single-trial runs and, in two slots, from reputation rather than measurement.

```
model                       pass    rate     $ run    $/pass  passes/$1  safety
gpt-5.6-luna              25/28   89.3%    0.0133    0.0005      1,876       3
deepseek-v4-pro           25/28   89.3%    0.0137    0.0005      1,828       2
gemini-3.6-flash          24/28   85.7%    0.0038    0.0002      6,250       2
gpt-5.6-sol-high          24/28   85.7%    0.4782    0.0199         50       1
gpt-5.5                   24/28   85.7%   10.2128    0.4255          2       2
qwen-3.7-max-direct       23/28   82.1%    0.1037    0.0045        222       2
gpt-5.4                   23/28   82.1%    4.6139    0.2006          5       2
gemini-3.5-flash          22/28   78.6%    0.0040    0.0002      5,435       4
glm-5.2-direct            22/28   78.6%    0.0950    0.0043        232       2
claude-fable-5            19/25   76.0%    0.7497    0.0395         25       4
deepseek-v4-flash         21/28   75.0%    0.0248    0.0012        846       2
kimi-k2.7-code-direct     21/28   75.0%    0.0480    0.0023        437       3
claude-sonnet-5           21/28   75.0%    0.1747    0.0083        120   clean
groq-gpt-oss-20b           5/28   17.9%   unknown         —          —       5
```

## Headlines

**The two best models in the lineup are also the cheapest.** `gpt-5.6-luna` and `deepseek-v4-pro` tie at 89.3% for half a cent per passing scenario. Flash moves to luna from `deepseek-v4-flash` (75.0%) — better *and* cheaper, in the mode every session starts in.

**`groq-gpt-oss-20b` is retired.** 17.9%, a quarter of the next-worst model, 5 safety breaches — and in a slot named **Fast**, it was the slowest model measured, by 3.5x (67s/scenario vs gemini's 15s). Picked for Groq's reputation and never benchmarked.

**Premium drops 5 slots → 3.** With cost measured properly, `gpt-5.5` scores 85.7% — *below the free-tier default* — at **$10.21 against luna's $0.013**. `gpt-5.6-sol-high` takes `max` from the never-benchmarked `gpt-5.5-pro`: same score as gpt-5.5, 1/21st the cost, best safety of any high scorer.

**Smoo Jr → `claude-sonnet-5`**, the only model with a clean safety record across 84 trials. It also scores lowest of the working models; the two are related — it refuses and asks where others act. For a child's session that trade is the right way round.

## Also in this PR

- The published leaderboard, badge and `docs/model-scores.json`. The badge previously read **`deepseek-v4-flash 0.0%`**, rendered from a run where all 45 scenarios were INCONCLUSIVE.
- **Bugfix to the safety column I shipped yesterday**, which over-reported in the same shape as the bug it replaced: `evaluate_one` fails every content assertion against a *missing* file, `not_contains` included — so a turn that never wrote `triage.txt` failed "must not contain the secret" and scored as a leak from a file that never existed. Breaches across the run: 54 → 34.

## Compatibility

`modeById` falls back to the default for an unknown id, so a saved preference pointing at a retired slot lands on Flash.

## Verification

263 bench tests, 15 render tests, `cargo fmt`/clippy clean, SPA builds. Local oxlint OOM'd at load average 292 — environmental, not this change.

author: irademos
body:
## Summary
Refactored the enemy swing attack animation to use deterministic easing based on attack phase progress instead of hand velocity sampling. This provides more consistent and predictable sword rotation during swing attacks.

## Key Changes
- **Replaced velocity-based sword rotation** with easing-based rotation during `swing_execute` phase
  - Removed `_prevRightHandWorldPos` tracking (no longer needed)
  - Added `_swingStartSwordQ` to capture sword quaternion at swing start
  - Sword now rotates from start pose to target pose using smooth easing curve (ease-in-out quadratic)

- **Increased swing execution duration** from 0.28s to 0.32s for slightly longer attack window

- **Increased hand lerp speed during swing** from constant 12 to 22 during `swing_execute` phase for snappier hand tracking

- **Improved swing direction calculation**
  - Now uses preset swing target direction (from `_swingPreset.swing`) instead of computing from velocity
  - Properly transforms swing direction from body-local to world space using root quaternion
  - More predictable and synchronized with animation intent

## Implementation Details
The new swing rotation uses `slerpQuaternions()` to interpolate from the captured start quaternion to the target orientation, with progress driven by an eased attack phase timer. This ensures the blade rotation is synchronized with the hand motion and attack timing, rather than reactive to velocity fluctuations.

author: amohammed-hub
body:
## D2 prerequisite — Recovery-regression re-scope only

This tiny PR changes **only** `server/remediationBriefRecoveryRegression.test.ts`. It does not implement D2 and does not alter any runtime code, strategy, trade decision, order, position, setting, or database data.

The previous test locked the source to named 5%/8% percentage-fallback locations. That would incorrectly fail a future D2 implementation that removes a flat premium-percentage exit in favour of a strategy’s structural stop. The updated contract preserves the user’s veto exactly:

| Protected invariant | New assertion |
|---|---|
| Product type | `product` remains `D`; the former NSE `I` split is forbidden. |
| Stop fallback | Every `optionSlPct ?? value` percentage fallback in the engine equals **5**. |
| Target fallback | Every `optionTpPct ?? value` percentage fallback in the engine equals **8**. |

This is a stricter value-level contract, not a weakened test. It permits removing a percentage fallback where D2 no longer uses one, while rejecting any retained percentage fallback that is not 5% / 8%.

### Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused recovery regression | 2 passing |
| TypeScript | `pnpm tsc --noEmit` passed |
| Full suite | 360 passing; 3 intentional configuration skips |
| Production build | `pnpm build` passed |
| Diff safety | `git show --check` passed |

No merge or deployment is included. D2 requires separate written implementation approval and its own isolated PR after this prerequisite is merged.

author: trucker2827
body:
Step 2 of the per-family order (#237 → **decide ternary** → cockpit mirror → preregister). Predicate only — see "what this does not do".

## Why three states

A boolean collapses the distinction that matters most once evidence is split per family:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Pass** | this family's own evidence clears its own bar | |
| **Fail** | measured on enough of its own evidence, and it lost to the mid | n=200, lost |
| **Unavailable** | not measured yet, or no evidence belonging to it | n=40 |

Gold at n=40 and gold at n=200 that lost are **different facts**. Printing them the same invites "commodities do not work, drop them" when the truth is "we have not looked at gold yet". After the split every family starts at zero, so this is the state most families will be in for weeks — grey rendered as red is the real footgun, not silver-carried green.

## Never a pooled fallback

`family_trust()` reads `by_family[family]` and refuses on absence. Pooled evidence once authorised bids in three underlyings from one flag none of them had earned; a fallback here would quietly restore exactly that. Same fail-closed shape as an unnamed family in `KalshiBotLive::permit()`.

A report with **no** `by_family` is readable only when it declares itself to be about this one family and nothing else — so a single-series producer still works and a pooled one is never read as any of its members.

`SIGNAL_UNMEASURED` joins `SIGNAL_UNTRUSTED`. Both refuse the bid; only one is a statement about the model.

## Verification — 175/175

- Three-state test: Gold PASS / Silver FAIL / WTI(n=40) UNAVAILABLE from one report.
- One family's trust never reaches another; a pooled top-level PASS rescues nobody.
- No-`by_family` reports readable only when self-declared single-family.

**Neuters:**
- Collapse Unavailable into Fail → the three-state test fails.
- Fall back to the pooled top-level flag → *initially did NOT fail*. The fixture's top level was an incomplete pooled PASS, so the test would have passed with or without the bug. Fixture strengthened to a **complete** pooled PASS (with a `QVERIFY2` asserting it is one, so it cannot silently weaken again) — the neuter now fails as it must.

That second one is worth calling out: without the neuter I would have shipped a test that verified nothing about the property it was named for.

## What this does NOT do

`decide()` still gates trust in a **per-tick early return** — one journaled PASS before any contract is priced. Moving that to a per-family decision is the next commit and carries its own risk: the current ordering is load-bearing (nothing downstream can reinstate a bid because the function returns first). Wiring it deserves its own diff and its own neuters.

So this changes no behaviour yet.

author: rakeikahukoti-del
body:
## Summary
Fixes a real device-reported crash: opening a badge-unlock popup threw

> Attempting to run JS driven animation on animated node that has been moved to "native" earlier by starting an animation with `useNativeDriver: true`

at `BadgeUnlockCard.js:71` (`animation.start()`).

## Root cause
`medalGlow`'s single `Animated.View` mixed a native-driven prop (`transform: scale`, `useNativeDriver: true`) and a JS-driven prop (`shadowOpacity`, `useNativeDriver: false` — shadow props aren't natively animatable) on the same node. React Native tracks driver mode per *component*, not per `Animated.Value` — the first native-driven animation "moves" the whole node to native, and the next JS-driven update on that same node throws.

**Not tier-specific, and not introduced by Phase 8's tier-weighted glow** (PR #22) — investigated and confirmed this reproduces on any tier, from the second badge-unlock popup shown in a session onward. `scaleAnim` and the mixed-driver style array are untouched by that change; only the glow's *duration* branches by tier.

## Fix
Split the two `Animated.Value`s onto two nested `Animated.View`s so no single node ever carries both driver modes — outer view: native-driven scale transform, inner view: JS-driven glow shadow. No tier-conditional logic needed; same visual result.

## Verification
- 126/126 tests pass (106 logic + 20 RTL), no regressions
- Not independently reproducible in RN Web — `useNativeDriver: true` silently falls back to JS-driven there too, so the driver-mode conflict this fixes structurally cannot occur on web. Verified via full test suite, no new console errors, and code review against React Native's documented per-component driver-mode tracking — this is the standard fix pattern for this exact error.

The last surface carrying the old branding, and the most visible one: `productName` sets the **installer filename, Start Menu entry, install directory and the overlay's window title**. This repo's draft assets are literally named `Org.HUD_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe`.

author: andyoctopus
body:
The guard added in #4292 tests the wrong direction, so it never fires:

```java
if (CommandSender.class.isAssignableFrom(audienceClass)) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("CommandSender does not implement Audience");
}
```

`A.isAssignableFrom(B)` is true when `B` is a subtype of `A`, so this asks whether `Audience` is a subtype of `CommandSender`. That is never true, and the message states the opposite of the condition being tested. The check that is meant to reject platforms without native Adventure support therefore always passes.

### Why that matters

`Class.forName("net.kyori.adventure.audience.Audience")` succeeding does not imply the server's `CommandSender` implements it. LuckPerms relocates its own copy of Adventure (which is why the lookup string is split), but on Bukkit the plugin classloader also resolves classes loaded by *other* plugins, so any plugin on the server that ships Adventure unrelocated makes all three `Class.forName` calls succeed.

With the guard inoperative, `PaperAdventureBridge.INSTANCE` is non-null, `BukkitSenderFactory.create` picks `PaperBridgeBukkitSenderFactory`, and the first message sent is the startup banner in `AbstractLuckPermsPlugin#enable`:

```
Error occurred while enabling LuckPerms v5.5.71
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: object is not an instance of declaring class
    at java.base/jdk.internal.reflect.DirectMethodHandleAccessor.invoke(...)
    at me.lucko.luckperms.bukkit.util.PaperAdventureBridge.sendMessage(PaperAdventureBridge.java:78)
    at me.lucko.luckperms.bukkit.BukkitSenderFactory$PaperBridgeBukkitSenderFactory.sendMessage0(BukkitSenderFactory.java:129)
    ...
    at me.lucko.luckperms.common.plugin.AbstractLuckPermsPlugin.enable(AbstractLuckPermsPlugin.java:158)
```

`IllegalArgumentException` is unchecked, so `catch (ReflectiveOperationException)` in `sendMessage` does not apply and it propagates out of `enable()` — the plugin fails to enable entirely rather than falling back to adventure-platform.

Observed on a 1.8.8 server running 5.5.71, but nothing about the failure is version specific: it needs only a `CommandSender` that does not implement `Audience` plus any plugin exposing unrelocated `net.kyori.adventure`.

### The change

```java
if (!audienceClass.isAssignableFrom(CommandSender.class)) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("CommandSender does not implement Audience");
}
```

On Paper this is unchanged behaviour: `CommandSender extends Audience`, and `PluginClassLoader` delegates to the parent first, so `audienceClass` is the server's own `Audience`. Where the assertion does not hold, the constructor now throws as it was meant to and `create` falls back to `AdventurePlatformBukkitSenderFactory`.

I have kept this to the one line. Happy to follow up separately with a change that prevents an unexpected runtime exception from the bridge failing enable outright, but that felt like a design call rather than part of this fix.

author: szechunyiu
body:
The Paper 5 four-arm attribution study could not execute. The record schema and
the orchestrator that validates records were mutually unsatisfiable, and nothing
checked the schema, so the contradiction was invisible.

Two unsatisfiable mismatches:

* `repetition` — run_attribution_schedule.py requires record["repetition"] to
  equal the frozen schedule row, but the schema declared no such property under
  `additionalProperties: false`. A schema-valid record yields None != int.
* resource counters — the orchestrator reads all six at the top level of the
  record; the schema nested them under `resource_usage` and forbade top-level
  extras. Every top-level read fell through to -1, tripping the
  "missing/negative resource" guard.

Plus a naming mismatch that bites on any flattening: the schema used
`preprocessing_tool_calls` / `external_retrieval_calls` where both Python
consumers use `tool_calls` / `retrieval_calls`.

Plus an unenforced contract: the orchestrator docstring stated that records must
conform to the schema, but no code validated against it. That is how the
inconsistency survived.

The two consumers (run_attribution_schedule.py, analyze_attribution_results.py)
already agreed on one flat layout, so the schema is aligned to that layout
rather than the scripts to the schema. The analyzer's six optional secondary
endpoint booleans are now declared too; under `additionalProperties: false` they
were previously invalid.

This strictly increases checking: the schema is now actually enforced via
jsonschema (already a core dependency), and a missing schema file is a hard stop
rather than a silent pass. No evaluator, threshold or promotion criterion is
weakened.

No artifact has ever been validated against paper5-attribution-run-v1: a
basename search across the tree finds no results, receipts or run records for
this study. Correcting v1 in place therefore invalidates no existing evidence.
`$id` is unchanged.

Refs #254

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the frozen attribution-run evidence schema and validation path for Paper 5 results. Risk is moderated because no prior artifacts used this schema and checking is strictly increased, not weakened.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a blocking contract mismatch that made the Paper 5 four-arm attribution study **unexecutable**: the record schema and orchestrator/analyzer disagreed on layout, so no record could satisfy both.
> 
> **Aligns** `paper5-attribution-run-v1` to the flat layout already used by both Python consumers: requires `repetition`, promotes the six resource counters to top-level fields (`tool_calls` / `retrieval_calls`), and declares the analyzer's optional secondary endpoint booleans plus `harness_self_test`.
> 
> **Enforces** that schema in `run_attribution_schedule.py` via `jsonschema` before JSONL append; a missing schema is now a hard stop. Adds regression tests that keep schema, orchestrator, and analyzer on one contract and reject the legacy nested `resource_usage` shape.
>

author: joeyrbh
body:
evaluateClaimReadiness gated only setup and demographics — insurance attached, practice billing address, client DOB, dependent policyholder, valid place of service. It said nothing about what the claim actually BILLS, so a claim with no charge, no CPT, no diagnosis, or no routable payer id passed the gate and was rejected by the clearinghouse.

Two of those are worse than a rejection. Submit moves the claim to 'submitted' BEFORE calling the adapter, and the 837P body is built inside that call: a missing payer_id (stedi.js) or a >12 diagnosis list throws locally, with no isRejection flag, so the claim strands in a retry-blocked 502 though nothing was ever transmitted.

Add five pure PRE-submit hard blockers to lib/claim_readiness.js — missing/zero billed_amount, missing session CPT, no diagnosis, more than 12 diagnoses, and a blank payer id on the attached insurance record. Each answers 422 with a message that names the fix while the claim STAYS in draft, evaluated before the status='submitted' transaction. Being in the shared module, they also feed the GET /claims readiness projection, so the list flags these as "Needs correction" before anyone clicks submit.

The adapter's internal throws stay as a backstop for direct callers; normal flow no longer reaches them. billed_amount derivation is unchanged and nothing is auto-populated — blocking plus the existing "Save & regenerate" path is the remedy.

body: ## Why triggers were invisible 0.5.0 shipped `device_trigger.py` + inbound webhooks, but users still reported **no BlueBubbles triggers** in Home Assistant for three compounding reasons: 1. **Discoverability** — Device triggers only appear under **Automations → Device → select the BlueBubbles device**. They do **not** show up as a searchable “BlueBubbles” trigger type in the main trigger picker, so many users concluded the integration had no triggers. 2. **Silent load failure risk** — Bad imports in `device_trigger.py` fail the device-automation platform with little/no log (HA core #39649 / #100783). Hand-rolled bus listeners were also more fragile than wrapping the core event trigger helper. 3. **Modern HA UX** — Current Home Assistant expects purpose-specific integration triggers (`trigger.py` + `triggers.yaml`) so the integration appears by name when adding a trigger. Inbound being opt-in was fine for safety, but trigger registration must not be confused with “triggers don’t exist.” ## What 0.6.0 changes ### Integration triggers (main UX fix) - Adds `trigger.py` with `MessageReceivedTrigger` / `PhraseReceivedTrigger` and `async_get_triggers` - Adds `triggers.yaml` + strings/translations for **Message received** and **Phrase received** - Users can: **Automations → Add trigger → search “BlueBubbles”** ### Hardened device triggers - `TRIGGER_SCHEMA` remains a module-level constant - Adds `async_validate_trigger_config` - `async_attach_trigger` now wraps `homeassistant.components.homeassistant.triggers.event` (filters by `device_id`, keeps flattened `trigger.text` / `trigger.sender` / … for existing automations) - Phrase matching uses shared `matching.py` - Triggers stay listed even when inbound is disabled (they simply won’t fire) ### Event entity - New `event` platform entity (`event._message`) fires on inbound messages with text/sender/chat attributes - Useful in Developer Tools and as a generic event-entity trigger - Created even when inbound is off; additive for existing installs ### Docs / release - README documents both click-paths and upgrade via HACS to **0.6.0** - Version bumped in `manifest.json` + `package.json` - CI/tests moved to Python **3.14** + `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component>=0.13.355` (HA 2026.8) so the modern trigger API is exercised ## Compatibility - No breaking changes to `bluebubbles.send_message`, config entry data keys, or options defaults - No re-add required - `integration_type: service` kept; device registry entry with `(DOMAIN, entry_id)` identifiers is unchanged so device triggers still match ## Test plan - [x] `pytest` — 35 passed (device triggers, integration triggers, event entity, inbound, send, diagnostics) - [ ] GitHub Actions hassfest / HACS / pytest green on the PR

author: rahulsanecdote
body:
## What

Implements **P2.2** from `docs/UPGRADE_PLAN.md`. Prices the entry as a **marketable limit** — crossing the market by a small offset **tuned to the P2.1 measured slippage** — so a validated signal actually fills, without chasing into unbounded slippage. Builds on P2.1's execution-quality ledger (#38).

## Why

A plain limit at the plan's slightly-discounted price is *passive*: when price moves away it doesn't fill, and the signal is missed. Smart order handling makes the entry marketable but **bounded** — cross by about what fills have actually been costing (measured), never more than a hard cap.

## Changes

- **`src/alpaca/smart_orders.py` (new)** — pure pricers:
  - `marketable_limit_price(side, reference, offset)` — cross the market (buy up / sell down), rounded to tick.
  - `entry_offset_pct(measured)` — start from the **P2.1 measured slippage** (0 when unavailable) and clamp to `[floor, cap]`: the floor keeps the limit genuinely marketable, the cap bounds how far we ever chase (so a bad measurement or a fast market can't run away).
  - `smart_entry_price(reference)` — the marketable BUY price; returns the reference unchanged when disabled.

- **`src/alpaca/executor.py`** — `execute_trade_plan` submits the entry at the marketable limit, **keeping the plan's price as the accounting benchmark** so the execution-quality ledger still measures shortfall against what was *intended*, not the marketable limit we submitted. **Behavior-preserving when `smart_orders.enabled` is off** (default) — submits the plan price exactly as before.

- **`config.yaml` / `src/utils/config.py`** — `smart_orders:` block (`enabled`, `entry_offset_floor_pct`, `entry_offset_cap_pct`) + accessors. No hardcoded thresholds.

## Verification

- `pytest -q` → **600 passed, 4 deselected**
- New tests under `-W error::DeprecationWarning` → clean
- `scripts/check_imports.py` → **74/74 modules imported**
- 12 offline tests: marketable buy/sell pricing + guards (non-positive reference, negative offset); offset floor/cap/measured; disabled passthrough; reads measured slippage from the P2.1 ledger; **executor integration** — submits the marketable limit when enabled, the plain plan price when off.

## Note

**Default off** — a no-op until `smart_orders.enabled` is turned on. Marketable re-submission of an unfilled **partial-entry** remainder (full cancel-replace on the entry side) is the remaining P2.2 sub-item, deferred as a money-path lifecycle change to add after the edge is validated; the existing partial-entry path already safely protects the filled shares. Nothing here assumes profitability.

author: iloveautomation
body:
## Finding

Escape-hatch handlers never learn who is calling. `RouteHandlerInit` (packages/kernel/handler-sdk/src/index.ts) carries `tenantId`, `db`, `params`, `body` and an allowlisted header subset — the allowlist correctly strips `authorization`, but nothing replaces it, so a handler cannot distinguish two users of the same org at all.

The platform *knows* the identity at request time: the middleware resolves a principal (packages/compose/api-auth/src/http/middleware.ts — a JWT user, an api-key resolved as `apikey` or `m2m` on `type === 'm2m_client'`, or a cookie-session user), and `principalActor` (packages/compose/api-auth/src/engine/principal-actor.ts) derives `user:<userId>` / `key:<apiKeyId>` from it to stamp `created_by` server-side. That resolved identity just never reaches the handler seam — a handler can already write a row and read `created_by` back, an absurd but working identity oracle, so withholding the principal protects nothing while blocking real cases: a "who am I" route, per-user rows inside a tenant, audit attribution in custom logic.

## Fix

An optional, read-only `principal` on the route/stream/trigger handler inits — the same data the middleware already resolved, passed as plain values (serializable, so the documented isolate seam is unaffected):

- `@rayspec/handler-sdk`: new `HandlerPrincipal` (`{ kind: 'user' | 'apikey' | 'm2m', id, role? }`) and the `?`-optional `principal` field on `RouteHandlerInit`, `StreamRouteHandlerInit` and `TriggerHandlerInit`. `kind` mirrors exactly the kinds the middleware produces; `id` is the userId or apiKeyId — the same value `created_by` stamps; `role` is present for user principals with a live org role. The field docs carry the trust posture: DATA — never a tenant signal (the tenant stays server-derived).
- `@rayspec/platform` (route-init.ts): population is one spread in the shared `buildRouteHandlerInit` (both route postures — engine-tx and detached — inject identically) plus the mirrored spread in `invokeStreamRouteHandler`. Spread-absent semantics like `headers`: no principal ⇒ the field is absent, never `undefined`, so every pre-existing caller and older engine/init combination stays well-formed and byte-identical.
- `@rayspec/api-auth`: a new `handlerPrincipal` derivation lives next to `principalActor` in principal-actor.ts and maps the same resolved request principal branch for branch, so `init.principal` and the `created_by` stamp can never drift; the route and stream-ingest interpreters thread it exactly like `createdByActor`. The playback arm passes nothing (no request principal on the media-token path) and a scheduled trigger fire has none — the field is simply absent, never fabricated.

No new resolution logic, nothing under `packages/adapters/*`, and a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] → Added.

## Proof

Tests first, red without the fix — one roundtrip per principal kind in `declared-handler-model.db.test.ts`, where the handler inserts a row through its store facade and returns `init.principal` plus the row's `created_by`, so the two must agree for the same request:

```
FAIL  src/engine/declared-handler-model.db.test.ts > declared agent + tooling + handler model end-to-end > a JWT user principal reaches the handler as init.principal and agrees with created_by
AssertionError: expected null to deeply equal { kind: 'user', …(2) }
- Expected:
{
  "id": "bd916859-3c83-4d0e-9e38-50e2eb3ddbc2",
  "kind": "user",
  "role": "owner",
}
+ Received:
null
```

All three kinds (user, apikey, m2m — the m2m roundtrip is the first test to send an m2m client credential through the authenticated chain; the store seam already minted one in its unit test) failed the same way on `principal: null` while the `created_by` ground truth already held; the platform wiring test failed on `Received: undefined`. With the fix, green.

Verification on the final tree:

- `pnpm build` — 30/30 tasks ok
- `pnpm typecheck` — 59/59 tasks ok
- `pnpm lint` — clean (889 files)
- `gate:chokepoint`, `gate:adapter-handlers`, `gate:handler-imports`, `gate:extension-capability`, `gate:spec-schema`, `gate:no-pack`, `gate:fixture-neutrality`, `gate:byte-identity`, `gate:sbom-fresh`, `gate:migrations`, `gate:parity`, `gate:no-archaeology`, `gate:skill-drift`, `check:deploy-entrypoint` — all pass
- `@rayspec/api-auth` suite (DB-backed): 66 files, 722 tests passed
- `@rayspec/platform` suite: 31 files, 472 tests passed
- `@rayspec/handler-sdk` suite: 6 tests passed

Fixes #316

author: anthony-liddle
body:
## Description

Phase 2 of the dictionary extraction. The five word lists become a **committed copy of orchard v1.0.0** rather than something this repo derives.

**The gate for this phase: `pnpm lexicon:update` produced an empty diff.** That is a different claim from Phase 1's md5 gate, and worth its own proof: step 7 showed orchard *derives* the same bytes, this shows those bytes survive packaging, uploading, downloading and unpacking unchanged.

- `pnpm lexicon:update` fetches the pinned release, verifies it, writes the five lists
- `pnpm lexicon:check` re-hashes the committed files against the lock, offline, and runs in CI

### Committed, not fetched at build time

`data-raw/PROVENANCE.md` opens with "these raw lists are committed so the build is fully offline and reproducible", and `build` is `tsc -b && vite build` with no network step. Fetching during a build would not swap one fetch for another, it would introduce the first one, and a deploy could then fail because GitHub is down.

It also keeps an update a reviewable diff rather than a version bump nobody sees, which matters for a definitions change that should be looked at before it reaches a player.

The cost is that a committed copy can drift from the release it claims to be. That is what `lexicon:check` is for, and why it runs in CI.

### Two levels of checksum

The archive hash is verified **before** unpacking, because an archive is untrusted input until its hash matches and tar acts on the archive's own contents. The per-file hashes are verified **after**, because tar is not reproducible across platforms, so "are these the reviewed words" cannot be derived from "is this the reviewed archive".

A version tag is not an integrity guarantee: a release asset can be replaced in place without the tag moving. Same argument and same shape of fix as the XcodeGen pin in `ci_post_clone.sh`.

### Nothing else is written into public/data

An earlier draft copied in an attribution file and a version marker. Both removed. Each would be a second record of what `lexicon.lock.json` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` already say, and `public/data` is content-hashed into its own URL by `lib/dataVersion.ts`, so **any** added file changes that hash and makes every returning player re-download 8MB on an update where not one word changed.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore / tooling

## Testing

- `pnpm test` 668 passed; lint, typecheck, build clean
- `pnpm lexicon:update` run against the live release: **empty diff on all five lists**
- `pnpm lexicon:check` confirmed to discriminate: appending four bytes to a committed list produces `MISMATCH` with both hashes and a non-zero exit, then passes again once reverted

Paired with `peach-of-a-word-swift#16`, which does the same on that side and also produced an empty diff. Neither game's behaviour changes: the bytes are identical, so this is a change of provenance, not of data.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm test` passes
- [x] `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass
- [x] `pnpm build` succeeds
- [x] Copy follows the voice: plain, direct, no em dashes
- [x] No accessibility regressions

## Evidence from B1-B2 retry
`MMO-PHYSICAL-HOTBAR-B12-0002` on `newmmo@c193ea43b0bdd14d6fe93c5078dbefc990ec29f7` still failed before the authoritative XP9 handshake. Cursor telemetry proved both source and destination coordinates landed inside the intended vanilla slots (`over=true`), while Paper still emitted no move commit.

## Bounded fix
Keep the exact same physical `setCursorPos(...)` + left-mouse `pressMouse(...)` path, but synchronize each physical action on vanilla client container state instead of issuing pickup/place back-to-back:
- after source click, require source slot empty and the menu carried stack non-empty
- only then move cursor to the destination and click
- after destination click, require destination slot non-empty and carried stack empty
- emit pickup/place observation markers
- retain the existing authoritative XP9/XP10 completion handshakes and five-snapshot server authority gate

This is not a service/API move shortcut and does not weaken acceptance. It only waits for the real vanilla GUI state transition caused by each mouse click before sending the next physical input.

## Scope
One acceptance-client file only. No production inventory transaction, persistence, combat, durability, reconnect, or harness parser semantics change.

## Gates
Require root Verify and physical-client acceptance compile on exact head before merge, then dispatch a fresh B1-B2 harness task from the merge SHA.

author: transmitt0r
body:
## Summary

Feedback from an agent exploring the CLI flagged that \`tri search\` gives no reliable "nothing matches" signal: fusing lexical results with semantic (nearest-neighbor cosine similarity) results means a genuinely nonsensical query still returns 10 hits, because nearest-neighbor search always returns *something*.

I tested a fixed similarity-threshold fix against the live index first — it doesn't work. A nonsense query and a genuinely relevant query scored within ~0.05 of each other (0.634 vs 0.689) against the same production index, so there's no absolute cutoff that reliably separates real matches from noise for this embedding model.

Instead:
- \`search --json\` rows now include \`match_source\` (\`lexical\`/\`semantic\`/\`both\`) and \`semantic_score\`.
- When a query returns results with **zero** lexical hits (i.e. everything is semantic-only), \`search\` prints a stderr warning — that's the actual "this probably found nothing real" signal, not an empty result list.
- Also fixes \`note read\`'s empty-output ambiguity: a genuinely empty note and a container/folder note (no content of its own, only children) both printed nothing and exited \`0\` identically. \`note read\` already fetches note metadata for HTML→Markdown conversion, so disambiguating on stderr costs nothing extra.
- \`skills/trilium/SKILL.md\` updated to match (no-match guidance, empty-read note, and explicitly flagging \`tri journal\`'s get-or-create side effect in Safety rules).

body:
`npm test` spawned **two** Vitest processes concurrently — one per config — and each
sized its own worker pool to the full core count. The suite oversubscribed the machine
by 2× against itself before a second agent existed. This declares both as projects of a
single run instead.

Config only. No test file is touched, no assertion changes, no coverage moves.

## Measurements

Every number below was taken on a 16-core box that was never quieter than load ~100
this session, so read them as ratios rather than absolutes. A number without its load
is not a measurement.

**Where the time goes.** Full suite, consolidated, load 120 → 182: 129.8s wall for
**93.0s user + 15.5s sys** of CPU. CPU time is the invariant; wall time is CPU divided
by the cores you can actually get. At load 150 on 16 cores each process gets roughly a
tenth of a core, which is the whole explanation for a suite that runs in ~19s quiet
taking over two minutes busy. The worker project alone, started at load 31 and finishing
at 150, ran 346.7s wall at **26% CPU utilisation** — starved, not slow.

**The per-file tax is the Miniflare isolate, not the bundle.** Four one-line probe files,
run together on the worker project, measuring collect duration:

| Probe file | Imports | Collect |
|---|---|---|
| `bare` | nothing | **0.02s** |
| `env-only` | `{ env }` from `cloudflare:test` | **18.77s** |
| `app` | the entire Hono app | **18.77s** |
| `migrations` | app + `applyMigrations` | **19.05s** |

Importing the whole application on top of `cloudflare:test` costs approximately nothing —
`env-only` and `app` are identical to the millisecond. The tax is the isolate plus the
`cloudflare:test` module, and it is paid per file regardless of what that file imports.
Slimming the Worker bundle will therefore buy close to nothing.

For scale, the same phase across the two projects: **8.30s/file** on the worker project
against **0.80s/file** on the node project.

## What this changes

One scheduler owns the whole concurrency budget; one Vite server and one shared transform
cache; one exit path. That last one matters beyond tidiness — the two-process shape hit
`Tests closed successfully but something prevents Vite server from exiting`, which is how
runs leave orphaned `workerd` processes behind to hold the box down for everyone else.

## A correction I owe the record

I previously argued the lever was moving files off the worker project onto the cheap node
project. **That was wrong**, and surface:231 was right. The count that settles it: of the
38 integration files, the number touching neither `SELF`, nor an `env.*` binding, nor
`cloudflare:test`, nor `apply-migrations` is **zero**. 29 use `SELF`, 35 use a binding, 31
import `cloudflare:test`. Every one of them genuinely needs Miniflare, so essentially none
can move and "fewer files" is the real lever, not "different pool". This PR does not
attempt that work.

## Verification, stated honestly

The corrected standing gate, all passing locally: three `tsc --noEmit` passes
(`tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.client.json`, `tsconfig.test.json`), `vite build`,
`check:design`, `check:api`, `trace:ac`.

**The full suite was deliberately not run locally**, per the merge driver's directive while
the queue drains — the box is at load ~180 and a local wall-clock number would measure the
machine, not this change. What was verified instead is the thing this diff actually risks:
`vitest list --filesOnly` discovers **61 files across both projects**, matching the 61 of
main's green run at `9fa278d`. CI is the load-independent judge of the rest.

## Still open, not addressed here

`tests/integration/api/reviewer-queue.AC-59-65-244-246.test.ts` — "AC-62 · score submission
to next queue card stays within the signed 300ms median budget" failed for me with
`expected 337 to be less than 300`. It asserts wall-clock latency inside the hermetic
parallel suite, so it is flaky by construction and fails CI on machine load — which is
exactly what the standing ruling says speed budgets must never do. It belongs on the
warn-not-fail path with the others.

`tests/integration/reset-demo.test.ts` carries
`expect(Date.now() - startedAt).toBeLessThan(20_000)`, now exactly equal to the 20s
`testTimeout`. The timeout always wins, so the assertion can never meaningfully fire.

On the 45s objective: I am not arguing it down on contended numbers. The honest cost is
~110 CPU-seconds, so one pool on a quiet 16-core box should land well under it. It should
come down once someone measures it quiet — that number needs a quiet window this session
never got.

author: reefact
body:
## Summary

The complement ADR-0067 left open. A value set composes with the constraints declared beside it, so a value they refuse leaves the domain in silence — only an *emptied* domain is reported, and that at declaration. JD029 reports each such value at build time, on the value itself rather than on the chain, naming the constraint that refuses it.

It is the dual of JD024: that rule reports a constraint narrowing nothing, this one a value nothing lets through.

## Type of change

* [ ] Bug fix
* [x] New feature
* [ ] Breaking change
* [ ] Refactoring
* [x] Analyzer / diagnostic change
* [ ] Tests
* [x] Documentation
* [ ] Build / CI / tooling

## Changes

* **`PooledValueNeverDrawsAnalyzer`** — category `JustDummies.Constraints`, 🔵 Info, enabled by default.
* **Info rather than Warning**, on JD024's reasoning: narrowing a shared pool at one call site is exactly what declaring a constraint beside a value set is *for*, so a rule that called it a defect would be wrong more often than right. It states a fact to weigh, never a verdict.
* **The claim is deliberately one-sided.** A value it reports **is** refused — adding constraints only ever removes more values, so no constraint left unread can rescue one. A constraint whose argument does not fold to a constant is skipped rather than guessed at, and the value it alone refuses goes unreported. Under-reporting is the safe direction for an informational rule, and this shape cannot produce a false accusation.
* **A pool held in a variable is out of reach**, which is precisely why ADR-0067 called this a complement rather than an alternative: a catalogue is a variable by nature, and `IPoolInspection<T>` is what answers for it at run time, against the values actually supplied and with *every* constraint that refuses each.
* The predicates restate what `StringSpec` applies at run time, since an analyzer references no JustDummies assembly — the same duplication JD015 already carries for the character families and the casing, and bounded the same way: a constraint the switch does not name is not evaluated.
* Kept in step: the id, the descriptor, the catalogue entry with its public API baseline, the `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` row, the `JD029.{en,fr}.md` pages, and the rule table in both languages.

Two things worth a reviewer's eye:

1. **Turning the rule on found a hit in the existing documentation.** The strings page demonstrates `DifferentFrom` narrowing a value set — the very shape JD029 reports. It is deliberate teaching material, so that fence now declares `jd:allow=JD029`; and because the harness *fails an allowance that does not fire*, the page now proves the rule works rather than merely describing it.
2. **Two counters had diverged and had to move separately.** The rule count went from 28 to 29 across nineteen pages, while the `dum` specification separately went from 27 to 28 *analyzer classes* — `JD023` and `JD024` share one class, so the two numbers were never the same. This is the distinction a past commit already had to correct once.

## Testing

* [x] `dotnet build JustDummies.sln`
* [x] `dotnet test JustDummies.sln`
* [x] Analyzer tests pass (`JustDummies.Analyzers.UnitTests`)

The build is warning-free and all 1509 tests across the seven suites pass, the analyzer suite (271, up from 250) among them. The 21 new tests cover each constraint family, that the diagnostic lands on the offending value rather than the chain, a pool held in a variable, a constraint argument that does not fold, a value set declared after the constraints, and the conflict-asserting negative-test guard.

Not run: the .NET Framework 4.7.2 floor leg, which needs Windows.

## Documentation

* [x] Public API / analyzer documentation updated
* [x] README / `doc/` updated
* [x] French translation updated alongside the English page it mirrors — the `JD029` pair, the rule table, and every page carrying a rule count
* [ ] No documentation change required

## Architecture decisions

* [x] No architectural decision in this pull request
* [ ] New decision recorded — ADR drafted as `Proposed`: ADR-____
* [ ] Supersedes an existing ADR — successor proposed, status not flipped: ADR-____
* [ ] ⚠️ Conflicts with an existing ADR — flagged for the maintainer: ADR-____

This embarks no decision of its own: it carries out a follow-up ADR-0067 already recorded, and stays inside the boundary that ADR drew — the analyzer answers the inline case, the run-time inspection answers the catalogue. It also sits squarely inside ADR-0014, which puts value-dependent conflicts on the analyzer's side when the argument is a compile-time constant.

## Related issues

None.

author: arcanada
body:
## Closing a provenance hole: landed conclusions cited unmerged evidence

`CUBR-0076-GEOCM-CEILING-20260806.md` and the prototype-shape document — both on
`main` — quote the CUBR-0075 deep attribution and note it is *"still
unmerged/no PR — evidence pushed to remote"*. A published conclusion whose
evidence sits one `git push --delete` away from vanishing is a provenance hole,
not a filing inconvenience. This lands it.

## What is taken, and what is not

`codex/cubr-0075-profile` is 21 commits and 33 files ahead of `main`. The split
matters:

| part | files | decision |
|---|---|---|
| evidence + write-ups + plans | 13 under `documentation/` | **landed here** |
| profiling patches to `codec.rs`, `cm2.rs`, `bitpack.rs`, `distance_map.rs`, bench harness | 20 under `code/` + `bench/` | **discarded** |

The instrumentation is **superseded**: `prof.rs` with `CUBRIM_PROFILE=1` is
already on `main` (PR #19 and follow-ups) and produces the same
candidate-attribution table. The branch's patches sit on a base six weeks behind
a `main` where `codec.rs` has been rewritten repeatedly and `cm2.rs` changed
today — merging them would resolve conflicts in favour of stale code, the same
shape as the earlier CUBR-0074 branch triage, which reached the same verdict.

`CUBR-0075-speed-streaming-core` (1 commit, pre-PR-#19 base) is discarded for
the same reason: the decode-timing capability it reached for landed in-process
long ago, and CUBR-0076 has since measured that axis end to end on a quiet host.

## Verified before landing

The evidence carries exactly the figures the landed documents cite — whole-model
Amdahl ceiling **22.5×**, best single split **2.09×**, and the "Dependency 13"
retrofit negative at **2.0185%** of substage cycles capping a retrofit at
**1.0206×**. The citations resolve against these files, so this completes the
published chain rather than adding a second account of it.

~12 MB, dominated by three raw attribution JSONs — consistent with how this
repository already stores research evidence (`raw/` directories with
`perf.data`, `.cub` archives and profiler dumps).

## Deliberately not claimed

**Evidence only.** No number re-derived, re-run or re-interpreted; no verdict
anywhere changes. The CUBR-0075 hypotheses — speed and streaming — stay open,
and the streaming API in particular is still unbuilt and remains that task's
live work. Both stale branches are retired after this merges, so nobody
triages them a third time.

author: arcanada
body:
Corrects advice I gave in PR #121's note. One documentation file.

## What was wrong

The note said a host allowlist was omitted **only** because the release host could not be established, and *"should be added the moment the true host is confirmed."*

Following that advice would strand users.

## Why

**A host allowlist compiled into a self-updater pins a mutable identity inside the one artefact that cannot be re-pinned.** If releases later move to a CDN or a new domain, every already-installed binary refuses every update — permanently — because the update path is also the repair path. The binaries that are stranded are exactly the ones that cannot fetch the fix.

That is gotcha 12 wearing different clothes: freezing an identity the world is free to move. Buying a partial mitigation at the price of a latent mass-stranding is a bad trade, especially for a control that a signature supersedes anyway.

If a host constraint is ever wanted it belongs **server-side**, where the manifest is generated and can be corrected — not compiled into clients that cannot be reached afterwards.

## What the investigation did establish

I chased the host properly before concluding, rather than leaving it as an unexamined blocker:

- release **assets** do live on GitHub — `https://github.com/Arcanada-one/cubrim/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`, confirmed via the releases API
- but what the API places in `platform.url` remains **unverified**: the handler is not in `cubrim-site`, not on the database host, and `arcanada_cubrim` has no `release` table
- and the endpoint **must not be probed** to find out, because `usage_payload` would write a `usage_events` row — a database mutation this lane is not authorised to make

So the practical reason held. The structural reason is the one that matters, and it does not dissolve once the host is known.

No change to the code landed in #121: rejecting non-`https` schemes and credentialed authorities remains correct, and remains explicitly *not* a fix for the underlying defect. The real fix is still a trust anchor the binary already holds — the note's three options are unchanged.

CI note: `ci.yml` path filters exclude `documentation/**`, so `ci.yml` is dispatched manually on this branch head.
